summary: Let F be a totally real field, H/F a finite abelian CM extension with G = Gal(H/F), S ⊇ S_∞ ∪ S_ram and T a disjoint smoothing set satisfying the Deligne–Ribet condition, so that the Stickelberger element Θ_{S,T} lies in Z[G]. The paper proves the Brumer–Stark conjecture away from 2 (Θ_{S,T} annihilates the T-smoothed class group Cl^T(H) after tensoring with Z[1/2], Theorem 1.2), Kurihara's Strong Brumer–Stark conjecture (Θ^#_{S,T} lies in the Fitting ideal over Z[G]^- of the minus part of the Pontryagin dual of Cl^T(H), Theorem 1.3), Kurihara's exact formula Fitt_{Z[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^{∨,-}) = SK^T(H/F)^- for that Fitting ideal in terms of the Sinnott–Kurihara ideal (Theorem 1.4 = 3.5), and the prime-to-2 part of Rubin's higher-rank Brumer–Stark conjecture (Theorem 1.6). Everything is deduced from the keystone Theorem 1.7 = 3.3: for every odd prime p and the depletion/smoothing sets Σ = S_∞ ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v | p}, Σ' = T ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p}, the minus part of the p-completed Burns–Kurihara–Sano Selmer module Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) is quadratically presented with Fitting ideal (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}). The proof is a generalisation of Ribet's method: a divisibility-implies-equality argument from the T-smoothed analytic class number formula (§5), a smoothed Ritter–Weiss module ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H) that is a Jannsen transpose of the Selmer module and whose minus extension class is computed by class field theory (§6, Appendix A), group ring valued Hilbert modular forms in the sense of Wiles and Silliman with a cuspidal family congruent to an Eisenstein series modulo x·Θ^# where the extra factor x records the trivial zeroes at primes above p (§7–8), and the Galois representations of ordinary Hilbert cusp forms, from which a cohomology class and a surjection from ∇ produce the inclusion Fitt_R(B̄_p) ⊆ (Θ^#) (§9, Theorem 9.10). Appendix B bootstraps Kurihara's full conjecture from the partial result by functoriality of ∇ under change of field. The atlas plans the arithmetic side of this in IntegralIwasawaTheory I.6 (Stickelberger elements, ray-class modules, Ritter–Weiss modules) and I.7 (the integral Brumer–Stark theorem with its Hilbert modular congruences and Galois representations), the Deligne–Ribet/Hilbert Eisenstein input in AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 and IntegralIwasawaTheory I.3, and exterior biduals in EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.6; it lacks the theory of group ring valued Hilbert modular forms, the extra-congruence cusp form construction, the smoothed Ritter–Weiss module with its transpose and extension-class properties, the Burns–Kurihara–Sano Selmer module with the divisibility-implies-equality argument, Kurihara's Sinnott–Kurihara-ideal formula and its functoriality proof, and the deduction of Rubin's conjecture, none of which the pinned Mathlib or Tau Ceti contain.

items.name: Artin L-function L(χ, s) of a character of G
items.statement: Standing setting: F is a totally real number field of degree n over ℚ, H a finite abelian extension of F which is a CM field, G = Gal(H/F), Ĝ = Hom(G, ℂ^*), S_∞ the set of infinite places of F. For a character χ: G → ℂ^*, L(χ, s) = ∏_𝔭 (1 − χ(𝔭) N𝔭^{−s})^{−1} for Re(s) > 1, the product over the maximal ideals 𝔭 of O_F, with the convention χ(𝔭) = 0 if χ is ramified at 𝔭 (Euler factor 1 at ramified primes). L(χ, s) has a meromorphic continuation to ℂ, holomorphic if χ ≠ 1, and with a single simple pole at s = 1 if χ = 1.
items.locator: §1 Introduction, lines 250-255 (unnumbered display after line 250, no label)
items.note: Basic analytic object whose values at s = 0 are packaged into the Stickelberger elements; the continuation is a recalled standard fact. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract line 35, verified): "Construct equivariant Artin L-functions for the abelian CM extensions used in the modern proof, their S- and T-modifications, integral Stickelberger elements ..."; audit target "Equivariant Artin L-functions of abelian CM extensions ... | library: absent | Only Dirichlet L-functions over ℚ exist. There are no Hecke or equivariant L-functions of number-field extensions." AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.4 (the layer extract lines 4713-4715, verified): "Connect number-field ideal counting, Hecke characters and completed L-functions to the analytic class-number formula and Chebotarev. Meromorphic continuation via induction is distinguished from Artin holomorphy", with audit target "Artin L-functions: meromorphic continuation by Brauer induction ... | library: absent". Nearest library, read: tauceti MonoidHom.galoisCharacterWeight (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/GaloisCharacter/Weight.lean, `noncomputable def galoisCharacterWeight (χ : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) →* ℂˣ) : TauCeti.MultiplicativeIdealWeight K` for L/K finite Galois; galoisCharacterWeight_apply_of_unramified gives χ(artinSymbol 𝔭) at unramified 𝔭 and galoisCharacterWeight_apply_eq_zero_iff gives 0 exactly at 𝔭 ∈ ramifiedPrimes K L), a completely multiplicative ideal weight whose Dirichlet series/Euler product exists only on Re s > 1. Mathlib NumberField.dedekindZeta (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/DedekindZeta.lean:49) is the χ = 1 Dirichlet series with only the real-variable residue statement tendsto_sub_one_mul_dedekindZeta_nhdsGT (line 77). […]

items.name: Σ-depleted, Σ'-smoothed L-function L_{Σ,Σ'}(χ, s)
items.statement: Let Σ, Σ' be disjoint finite sets of places of F with Σ ⊃ S_∞ (no further condition). For χ ∈ Ĝ, L_{Σ,Σ'}(χ, s) = L(χ, s) · ∏_{𝔭 ∈ Σ ∖ S_∞} (1 − χ(𝔭) N𝔭^{−s}) · ∏_{𝔭 ∈ Σ'} (1 − χ(𝔭) N𝔭^{1−s}).
items.locator: §1 Introduction, unnumbered display lines 257-262
items.note: The L-values L_{Σ,Σ'}(χ, 0) are the coefficients (after χ) of the Stickelberger element Θ_{Σ,Σ'}. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract line 35, verified): "Construct equivariant Artin L-functions for the abelian CM extensions used in the modern proof, their S- and T-modifications, integral Stickelberger elements, ray-class modules, roots-of-unity corrections ..."; audit target "Equivariant Artin L-functions of abelian CM extensions with S- and T-modifications, and integral Stickelberger elements | library: absent". AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 (the layer extract line 169) names "smoothing factors and Euler factors" only for the Deligne–Ribet partial zeta functions/pseudo-measure, not for L(χ,s). Library near misses read: tauceti TauCeti.MultiplicativeIdealWeight.restrict (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/Weight.lean:311, `χ.restrict S hS I = if Ideal.IsPrimeTo I S then χ I else 0`), which realises the Σ-depletion of the Euler product on Re s > 1 only; mathlib DirichletCharacter.LFunction_changeLevel (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/DirichletContinuation.lean:150), Euler-factor removal for imprimitive Dirichlet characters over ℚ. Nothing in either tree implements the smoothing factor (1 − χ(𝔭) N𝔭^{1−s}); rg for 'smooth', 'T-modif', 'depleted' in TauCeti/NumberTheory finds nothing relevant. Confirmed the previous verdict. Neither library has an S-depleted, T-smoothed L-function of a Galois character of a number-field extension, nor L(χ,s) itself beyond Re s > 1 (item 1). I.6's "S- and T-modifications" of the equivariant Artin L-functions is exactly L_{Σ,Σ'}(χ,s); […]

items.name: Stickelberger element Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(s) and Θ_{Σ,Σ'} = Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(0)
items.statement: For Σ, Σ' as above, Θ^{H/F}_{Σ,Σ'}(s) is the unique element of ℂ[G] such that χ(Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(s)) = L_{Σ,Σ'}(χ^{−1}, s) for all χ ∈ Ĝ (χ extended ℂ-linearly to ℂ[G]); the superscript H/F is dropped when unambiguous. Its specialisation at s = 0 is Θ_{Σ,Σ'} := Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(0). Brumer's element is Θ_S := Θ_{S,∅}.
items.locator: §1 Introduction, unnumbered displays lines 263-272 (Θ_{Σ,Σ'}^{H/F}(s) and Θ_{Σ,Σ'} = Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(0)); Θ_S = Θ_{S,∅} at line 313
items.note: The central object of the paper: every main theorem describes annihilators or Fitting ideals of class groups and Selmer modules in terms of Θ_{S,T} and Θ_{Σ,Σ'}. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract line 35, verified): "... their S- and T-modifications, integral Stickelberger elements, ray-class modules ...", audit target "... and integral Stickelberger elements | library: absent". IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 (the layer extract line 7) only consumes "the equivariant Stickelberger normalization" as the finite-level object of its dictionary with the Deligne–Ribet pseudomeasure, and I.8 (areas catalogue) "Prove the relation between the CM Stickelberger element and the totally real Deligne–Ribet pseudomeasure" also consumes it. rg -i stickelberger over both pinned trees hits only TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Stickelberger.lean and TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/LeibnizPart.lean (Stickelberger's discriminant congruence disc ≡ 0,1 mod 4) and nothing in Mathlib; no ℂ[G]-valued L-value exists in either tree. Confirmed the previous verdict. The group-ring-valued function Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(s) ∈ ℂ[G] with χ(Θ) = L_{Σ,Σ'}(χ^{-1}, s) is absent from both libraries (the only Stickelberger in Tau Ceti is the discriminant congruence, a different theorem), and I.6 is the layer that owns the Stickelberger elements; I.3 and I.8 import them. The atlas-wide stage search for 'Stickelberger' returns exactly I.3, I.6, I.8 and the NumberFieldArithmetic discriminant layer.

items.name: Siegel–Klingen–Shintani rationality of Θ_{Σ,Σ'}
items.statement: For any disjoint finite sets Σ ⊃ S_∞ and Σ' of places of F, Θ_{Σ,Σ'} = Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(0) lies in ℚ[G].
items.locator: §1 Introduction, line 272; restated at §2.1, proof of Lemma 2.1 (the source line 602); the general form is stated in §1 before equation (1) (line 272)
items.note: External input (no \cite key at line 272 (attributed to Siegel, Klingen and Shintani); the paper cites \cite{klingen}, \cite{siegel} for the same rationality in §2.1, line 602). Makes Θ_{Σ,Σ'} a rational group-ring element, the prerequisite for the integrality statement (2) and for all Fitting-ideal statements. Evidence: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 (the layer extract lines 167-169, verified): "For a totally real field F construct the Deligne–Ribet p-adic partial zeta functions/pseudo-measure, including the algebraicity of negative critical values, integral congruences, smoothing factors and Euler factors"; audit target: "Only the F = ℚ algebraicity input exists (ζ and Hurwitz ζ at negative integers through Bernoulli numbers and polynomials) ... partial zeta functions of totally real fields, their continuation, Siegel–Klingen values and any pseudo-measure or p-adic zeta function are absent." IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (line 35): "integral Stickelberger elements". Library near miss read: mathlib hurwitzZeta_neg_nat (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/HurwitzZetaValues.lean:189), the F = ℚ case via Bernoulli polynomials; rg for Siegel/Klingen/Shintani over both trees finds nothing about L-values. Confirmed the previous verdict. Rationality of L_{Σ,Σ'}(χ,0), hence Θ_{Σ,Σ'} ∈ ℚ[G], for a general totally real F is the Siegel–Klingen(–Shintani) theorem; the libraries have only the F = ℚ case (Hurwitz/Dirichlet values at non-positive integers), a near miss by the Q-case rule. L3 owns the algebraicity of the non-positive critical values of partial zeta functions of totally real fields (its 'negative critical values' include s = 0 as the k = 1 case in the audit's reading 'Siegel–Klingen values'); I.6 uses it for the Stickelberger elements. […]

items.name: Sets S, T, S_ram, T_H and condition (1) on T
items.statement: S_ram is the set of finite primes of F ramified in H. S and T are disjoint finite sets of places of F with S ⊃ S_∞ ∪ S_ram (so every prime in T is unramified in H). T_H is the set of primes of H above the primes in T. Condition (1): the group of roots of unity ζ ∈ μ(H) such that ζ ≡ 1 (mod 𝔭) for all 𝔭 ∈ T_H is trivial.
items.locator: §1 Introduction, equation (1), label e:drcond (lines 272-281)
items.note: Standing hypotheses on the depletion set S and the smoothing set T under which Θ_{S,T} is integral and the Brumer–Stark conjecture is stated; condition (1) is imposed on T (and later on Σ') throughout the paper. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract line 35, verified): "Construct equivariant Artin L-functions for the abelian CM extensions used in the modern proof, their S- and T-modifications, integral Stickelberger elements, ray-class modules, roots-of-unity corrections, and the archimedean minus construction with the precise convention of DKSW." Library pieces read: tauceti NumberField.Chebotarev.ramifiedPrimes K L (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/RamifiedPrimes.lean:114, `noncomputable def ramifiedPrimes : Finset (HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K))`, the set S_ram); mathlib NumberField.Units.torsion and Ideal.torsionMapQuot (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Ideal/Basic.lean:70, the reduction map μ(K) → (𝓞 K ⧸ I)ˣ) whose kernel-triviality is condition (1) for a single prime. No declaration packages S ⊃ S_∞ ∪ S_ram, T, T_H or the condition that no nontrivial root of unity is ≡ 1 mod every 𝔭 ∈ T_H; rg for 'Deligne', 'smoothing set', 'T_H' in both trees finds nothing. Confirmed the previous verdict. The standing data (S, T, S_ram, T_H, condition (1)) is not in either library as a packaged notion, only its ingredients (ramified primes, torsion units, the reduction map of torsion modulo an ideal). I.6's "S- and T-modifications" with "roots-of-unity corrections" is the containing target for the depletion/smoothing sets and the hypothesis on T under which the T-modification is integral; the atlas-wide search for 'Deligne–Ribet' hits only L3, L5, I.3, I.8 and B.2, none of which names the sets themselves more precisely.

items.name: Sufficient condition for condition (1)
items.statement: If T contains two primes of different residue characteristic, or one prime of residue characteristic larger than [F:ℚ] + 1, then condition (1) holds.
items.locator: §1 Introduction, line 282 (sentence following equation (1))
items.note: External input (none given (standard fact)). Shows condition (1) is mild and gives a criterion for choosing admissible smoothing primes. Evidence: Nearest library, read: mathlib Ideal.torsionMapQuot_injective (Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Ideal/Basic.lean:114): `(hI₁ : absNorm I ≠ 1) (hI₂ : (absNorm I).Coprime (torsionOrder K)) : Function.Injective (torsionMapQuot I)`; Ideal.torsionMapQuot_injective' (line 135): for a prime P with `Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt ℤ P` and `2 < absNorm (under ℤ P)`, `Function.Injective P.torsionMapQuot`; and IsPrimitiveRoot.not_coprime_norm_of_mk_eq_one (line 33): a primitive n-th root of unity (n ≥ 2) with ζ ≡ 1 mod I forces gcd(absNorm I, n) ≠ 1. Tau Ceti has only the local Teichmüller injectivity (TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Teichmuller.lean:152) and cyclotomic prime lemmas. Nearest layer: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract line 35), "their S- and T-modifications ... roots-of-unity corrections"; atlas-wide stage searches for 'roots of unity' near 'congruent/mod' and for 'residue characteristic' find only unrelated stages (MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.3, IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.2, local-field and moduli stages). Confirmed missing, with a corrected nearest-library picture: Mathlib does have the reduction map of μ(H) modulo an ideal and two injectivity criteria, but under different, incomparable hypotheses (norm of the ideal coprime to |μ(H)|; or a prime unramified over ℤ with residue characteristic > 2), not the paper's criterion (two primes of different residue characteristic, or one prime of residue characteristic > [F:ℚ] + 1, with no unramified-over-ℤ or coprimality hypothesis). Those are near misses, not the item. No stage names this sufficient criterion; […]

items.name: Deligne–Ribet / Cassou-Noguès integrality (2)
items.statement: Let S, T be disjoint finite sets of places of F with S ⊃ S_∞ ∪ S_ram and T satisfying condition (1). Then Θ_{S,T} ∈ ℤ[G].
items.locator: §1 Introduction, equation (2), label e:dr (lines 284-285); restated at §2.1, proof of Lemma 2.1 (the source line 602) and §3.3, proof of Lemma 3.4 (line 862–863); stated as equation (2), label e:dr, in §1 (line 284–285); App. B, introduction, line 3575 (citing §1, equation (2), label e:dr, line 284)
items.note: External input (\cite{dr}, \cite{cn}). Integrality of the Stickelberger element, needed to state Conjecture 1.1 and Theorems 1.2–1.4 and used by Kurihara for SK^T(H/F) ⊂ ℤ[G]. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract line 35, verified): "... their S- and T-modifications, integral Stickelberger elements ...", audit target "Equivariant Artin L-functions of abelian CM extensions with S- and T-modifications, and integral Stickelberger elements | library: absent". AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 (the layer extract line 169, verified): "construct the Deligne–Ribet p-adic partial zeta functions/pseudo-measure, including the algebraicity of negative critical values, integral congruences, smoothing factors and Euler factors". IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 (line 7) imports "the Deligne–Ribet pseudomeasure from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3" and I.8 (areas catalogue) proves "the relation between the CM Stickelberger element and the totally real Deligne–Ribet pseudomeasure". rg -i for Deligne, Ribet, Cassou over both pinned trees returns nothing relevant, and no Stickelberger element exists (item 3). Confirmed the previous verdict. The integrality Θ_{S,T} ∈ ℤ[G] under condition (1) cannot even be stated in either library since Θ_{S,T} is absent. I.6 names the integral Stickelberger elements, i.e. statement (2); L3 owns the Deligne–Ribet construction (integral congruences with smoothing factors) from which integrality follows. SpecialValuesBirchTate:B.2 mentions 'an independent Deligne–Ribet integrality result' only as an input, and L5 lists 'Deligne–Ribet and ordinary Katz constructions' as acceptance of L3-level work, so no more foundational owner exists.

items.name: T-smoothed class group Cl^T(H)
items.statement: I_T(H) is the group of fractional ideals of H relatively prime to the primes in T_H; P_T(H) is the subgroup of I_T(H) generated by the principal ideals (α) with α ∈ O_H and α ≡ 1 (mod 𝔭) for all 𝔭 ∈ T_H. Cl^T(H) := I_T(H)/P_T(H), the ray class group of H of conductor the product of the primes in T_H; it is naturally a ℤ[G]-module.
items.locator: §1 Introduction, lines 287-289 (unnumbered display Cl^T(H) = I_T(H)/P_T(H))
items.note: The module whose annihilator (Conjecture 1.1) and whose Pontryagin dual's Fitting ideal (Theorems 1.3, 1.4) the paper determines. Evidence: Read in the pinned Tau Ceti tree: TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/RayClass/Basic.lean:180 `def RayClassGroup (𝔪 : Modulus K) : Type _ := idealsPrimeTo 𝔪 ⧸ ray 𝔪` (namespace TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields), `ray 𝔪 := (rayHom 𝔪).range` (line 139), `mem_ray_iff : I ∈ ray 𝔪 ↔ ∃ x : Kˣ, IsCongrOne 𝔪 x ∧ toPrincipalIdeal (𝓞 K) K x = I` (line 145); TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/RayClass/Modulus.lean:88 `structure Modulus` (finitePart : Ideal (𝓞 K) ≠ ⊥, infinitePart : Finset of real places), line 256 `IsCongrOne 𝔪 x` = v((x:K) − 1) ≤ exp(−exponent v) at each v ∣ finitePart plus positivity at the real places of 𝔪, line 441 `idealsPrimeTo 𝔪` = invertible fractional ideals away from 𝔪.support; RayClass/Integral.lean:196 idealClass_eq_one_iff_exists_integral (denominator-cleared form I·(b) = (a) with a, b ≡ 1). With K = H and 𝔪 = (∏_{𝔭∈T_H} 𝔭, ∅) this is the abelian group I_T(H)/P_T(H). Galois action: rg over both trees for MulAction/MulDistribMulAction/galRestrict on RayClassGroup or ClassGroup finds none (Mathlib's Galois action on ideals in Mathlib/NumberTheory/RamificationInertia/Galois.lean acts on prime ideals only); RayClass/*.lean contain no ≃ₐ, Galois or MulAction. Layer: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract line 35) "ray-class modules", audit target "Ray-class modules ... | library: absent | Tau Ceti has ray class groups as groups, but not their Galois-module structure or minus parts." Changed from library to planned. The item is Cl^T(H) as a ℤ[G]-module (the statement says 'it is naturally a ℤ[G]-module', and every use in the paper is through the ℤ[G]- or ℤ[G]^-–module structure). […]

items.name: S-depleted T-smoothed class group Cl^T_S(H)
items.statement: For a finite set S of primes of F disjoint from T, Cl^T_S(H) is the quotient of Cl^T(H) by the subgroup generated by the classes of the primes of H lying above the primes in S.
items.locator: §1 Introduction, line 291
items.note: Defined 'for later use' (S-class group variant used in the Selmer-module comparisons). Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract lines 33-43; atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json): "Construct equivariant Artin L-functions for the abelian CM extensions used in the modern proof, their S- and T-modifications, integral Stickelberger elements, ray-class modules, roots-of-unity corrections, and the archimedean minus construction with the precise convention of DKSW" and "the comparison to class/ray-class groups"; audit: "Tau Ceti has ray class groups as groups, but not their Galois-module structure or minus parts." Nearest alternative IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.2 (iwasawa-1.json): "Define inverse limits of p-primary class groups, S-class groups, units, S-units ..." (tower-level, p-primary only). Library: tauceti:TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.RayClassGroup, TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/RayClass/Basic.lean:180 `def RayClassGroup (𝔪 : Modulus K) : Type _ := idealsPrimeTo 𝔪 ⧸ ray 𝔪` with Modulus (RayClass/Modulus.lean:88) = nonzero ideal + finset of real places; rg over TauCeti and Mathlib for SClassGroup / S-class / MulAction on ClassGroup finds nothing. Confirmed planned (I.6). The paper (the source lines 286-291) defines Cl^T_S(H) as the quotient of the T-ray class group by the classes of primes above S; it is one of the DKSW ray-class modules and feeds the ray-class/Selmer comparison that I.6 owns. I.2 names S-class groups only as p-primary inverse-limit objects in the Iwasawa tower, so it is shared vocabulary rather than the finite-level T-smoothed S-depleted group. Tau Ceti's RayClassGroup gives Cl^T(H) as an abstract group for the modulus (∏_{𝔮∈T_H} 𝔮, ∅) but has no quotient by classes of primes above S and no ℤ[G]-module structure; […]

items.name: Conjecture 1.1 (Brumer–Stark conjecture, Tate's form)
items.statement: Let S, T be disjoint finite sets of places of F with S ⊃ S_∞ ∪ S_ram and T satisfying (1). Conjecture: Θ_{S,T} ∈ Ann_{ℤ[G]}(Cl^T(H)) (equation (3)). Tate's actual Conjecture IV.6.2 is very slightly stronger: for 𝔭 ∉ S ∪ T split completely in H and 𝔓 | 𝔭 in H, the generator u of 𝔓^{Θ_{S,T}} (see (5)) can be chosen with ū = u^{−1}, where ū is the image of u under the complex conjugation of H. For any generator u the element v = u/ū satisfies v̄ = v^{−1} and generates 𝔓^{2Θ_{S,T}}, so the refinement concerns only a factor of 2 and the discrepancy disappears once 2 is inverted.
items.locator: §1 Introduction, Conjecture 1.1, label c:bs, equation (3) label e:bs (lines 296-301); Tate's refinement at line 329
items.note: External input (\cite{tatebook}*{Conjecture IV.6.2}). The conjecture whose prime-to-2 part is Theorem 1.2. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract lines 46-58): "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem and the stronger module-theoretic statement needed in Kurihara's Theorem 2.12. The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations"; audit target "Integral Brumer–Stark theorem (Dasgupta–Kakde at odd primes, DKSW integrally) | library: absent". I.6 (lines 33-43): "integral Stickelberger elements, ray-class modules" (the two ingredients Θ_{S,T} and Cl^T(H) as ℤ[G]-module). rg -i 'Stickelberger|Brumer|BrumerStark' over Mathlib finds nothing; in Tau Ceti only TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Stickelberger.lean (discriminant congruence). Confirmed planned. The conjecture Θ_{S,T} ∈ Ann_{ℤ[G]}(Cl^T(H)) is the statement whose integral proof I.7 plans (DKSW integrally; Dasgupta–Kakde away from 2) and whose objects I.6 constructs; the KU-brumerstark checkpoint (iwasawa-1.json) aggregates I.6+I.7 as 'Integral Brumer–Stark'. Tate's refinement (generator with ū = u^{-1}) is named by no layer, but the paper discards it after inverting 2. Neither library has Stickelberger elements, equivariant L-values or a Galois action on ray classes, so nothing is library.

items.name: Theorem 1.2 (Brumer–Stark away from 2)
items.statement: Let S, T be disjoint finite sets of places of F with S ⊃ S_∞ ∪ S_ram and T satisfying (1). Then Θ_{S,T} ∈ Ann_{ℤ[G]}(Cl^T(H)) ⊗_ℤ ℤ[1/2] (equation (4)), i.e. 2^m Θ_{S,T} annihilates Cl^T(H) for some m ≥ 0. Proof (lines 357-358): from Theorem 1.3 using (a) Fitt ⊂ Ann, (b) Ann(M^∨) = Ann(M)^# for finite M, (c) σΘ_{S,T} = −Θ_{S,T}, so Θ_{S,T} annihilates a ℤ[1/2][G]-module iff it annihilates its minus part.
items.locator: §1 Introduction, Theorem 1.2, label t:ptt, equation (4) label e:ptt (lines 305-310); deduction from Theorem 1.3 at lines 357-358
items.note: Main corollary: the prime-to-2 part of the Brumer–Stark conjecture. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract line 48): "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations. Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma for residually indistinguishable characters, the Fitting-ideal comparison, and the passage from modified to unmodified data"; audit target "Integral Brumer–Stark theorem (Dasgupta–Kakde at odd primes, DKSW integrally) ... | library: absent". IHG.6 (modular-1.json) explicitly disclaims it: "no arithmetic Brumer–Stark conclusion is part of this abstract supplier." rg for Stickelberger/Brumer/Fitting in both pinned trees: nothing relevant. Confirmed planned. Theorem 1.2 is literally 'the odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde' that I.7 names, and the deduction from Theorem 1.3 (Fitt ⊂ Ann, Ann(M^∨) = Ann(M)^#, σΘ = −Θ) is inside I.7's 'Fitting-ideal comparison'. No more foundational owner: IHG.6 owns only the abstract Ribet lemma and disclaims the arithmetic conclusion. Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Coefficients ζ_{S,T}(σ) and the ideal 𝔓^{Θ_{S,T}} (5)
items.statement: Let 𝔭 ∉ S ∪ T be a prime of F that splits completely in H and 𝔓 a prime of H above 𝔭. Define integers ζ_{S,T}(σ), σ ∈ G, by Θ_{S,T} = Σ_{σ ∈ G} ζ_{S,T}(σ) [σ^{−1}] (integrality by (2)), and set 𝔓^{Θ_{S,T}} := ∏_{σ ∈ G} σ^{−1}(𝔓)^{ζ_{S,T}(σ)} (equation (5)), a fractional ideal of H supported on the primes above 𝔭.
items.locator: §1 Introduction, lines 323-327, equation (5) label e:actual
items.note: The ideal whose principality with a T-congruent anti-unit generator is the content of Tate's conjecture at 𝔓. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract line 35): "Construct equivariant Artin L-functions ..., their S- and T-modifications, integral Stickelberger elements, ray-class modules"; audit: "Tau Ceti has ray class groups as groups, but not their Galois-module structure or minus parts." Nearest Mathlib: Mathlib/NumberTheory/RamificationInertia/Galois.lean:96 `noncomputable instance : MulAction Gal(L/K) (primesOver p B) where smul σ Q := primesOver.mk p (map (galRestrict A K L B σ) Q.1)` and Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Pointwise.lean:42 `protected def pointwiseDistribMulAction : DistribMulAction M (Ideal R) where smul a := Ideal.map (MulSemiringAction.toRingHom _ _ a)` (scoped instance). rg over atlas for 'Galois action on ideals', 'as a Galois module', 'Galois-module structure': no stage names the ℤ[G]-action on ideals of H. Confirmed planned (I.6). The coefficients ζ_{S,T}(σ) are the coefficients of the integral Stickelberger element I.6 constructs, and 𝔓^{Θ} = ∏ σ^{-1}(𝔓)^{ζ(σ)} is the ℤ[G]-module structure on fractional ideals that I.6's 'ray-class modules' require. Mathlib gives σ(𝔓) for σ ∈ Gal(H/F) (action on primesOver, pointwise action on ideals) but no exponentiation of a fractional ideal by a group-ring element and no Θ_{S,T}; Tau Ceti has no Galois action on ideals or ray classes. Not library.

items.name: Conjecture 1.1 implies 𝔓^{Θ_{S,T}} is principal with T-congruent generator
items.statement: Assume Conjecture 1.1 (S ⊃ S_∞ ∪ S_ram, T disjoint from S satisfying (1)). Let 𝔭 ∉ S ∪ T be a prime of F splitting completely in H and 𝔓 a prime of H above 𝔭. Then 𝔓^{Θ_{S,T}} is a principal ideal (u) generated by an element u with u ≡ 1 (mod 𝔮 O_H) for all 𝔮 ∈ T.
items.locator: §1 Introduction, lines 324-328 (sentence containing equation (5))
items.note: External input (\cite{tatebook} (asserted without proof; immediate from the definition of P_T(H))). Connects the annihilation statement to the existence of Brumer–Stark units. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract line 48): "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem and the stronger module-theoretic statement ... A statement about annihilation of a class group is generally weaker than the Fitting or determinant identity needed downstream." I.6 (line 38): "the comparison to class/ray-class groups" and "ray-class modules". Partial library: tauceti:TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.idealClass_eq_one_iff, TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/RayClass/Basic.lean:250 `idealClass 𝔪 I = 1 ↔ ∃ x : Kˣ, IsCongrOne 𝔪 x ∧ ((I : Ideal (𝓞 K)) : FractionalIdeal (𝓞 K)⁰ K) = FractionalIdeal.spanSingleton (𝓞 K)⁰ (x : K)` (integral ideals prime to 𝔪 only; IsCongrOne at RayClass/Modulus.lean:256). Confirmed planned. The implication is the unwinding of Cl^T(H) = I_T(H)/P_T(H) (the source lines 286-289) applied to the class of 𝔓^{Θ}: annihilation ⇒ trivial ray class ⇒ generator ≡ 1 mod T_H. Tau Ceti's idealClass_eq_one_iff supplies the ray-class half for an integral ideal prime to 𝔪 with generator x ∈ Kˣ, IsCongrOne 𝔪 x (so a T-congruence for the modulus ∏_{𝔮∈T_H} 𝔮), but 𝔓^{Θ} is a fractional ideal, needs the Galois action and Θ_{S,T}, and the annihilation hypothesis is absent; hence a near miss, not library. Owner I.7 for the Brumer–Stark-unit form of annihilation, I.6 for the ray-class comparison.

items.name: Brumer–Stark unit
items.statement: For 𝔭 ∉ S ∪ T split completely in H and 𝔓 | 𝔭, the Brumer–Stark unit is the unique u ∈ H^* (existence conjectural: Tate's Conjecture IV.6.2) with (u) = 𝔓^{Θ_{S,T}}, u ≡ 1 (mod 𝔮 O_H) for all 𝔮 ∈ T, and ū = u^{−1} (bar = complex conjugation of H). It is a 𝔭-unit of H whose valuations at the primes above 𝔭 are determined by L-values: Σ_{σ ∈ G} χ(σ) ord_{σ^{−1}(𝔓)}(u) = L_{S,T}(χ, 0) for all χ ∈ Ĝ.
items.locator: §1 Introduction, lines 329-333 (valuation formula in the unnumbered display at line 332)
items.note: Canonical 𝔭-unit predicted by the conjecture; link to explicit class field theory and Hilbert's 12th problem (\cite{dk}). Evidence: rg -i over atlas/areas/*.json, roadmaps/*.json and packets for 'Brumer', 'Stark unit', 'Rubin-Stark', 'Gross-Stark', 'anti-unit', "Hilbert's 12th/twelfth", 'explicit class field': the only Brumer hits are IntegralIwasawaTheory I.6/I.7, the KU-* checkpoints, L4 (Baker–Brumer) and IHG.6; the only Stark hits are EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.6 ("MR 2016 Stark and Kolyvagin systems") and ES.7 ("a conjectural Rubin–Stark element remains a conditional application until its integrality and norm properties are proved"); ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.6 says "general explicit class fields outside proved CM cases remain separately labelled research problems". Libraries: rg -i 'Stickelberger|Brumer|Stark' finds nothing relevant in Mathlib; Tau Ceti only the discriminant Stickelberger file. Confirmed missing. No stage names the Brumer–Stark unit u with (u) = 𝔓^{Θ_{S,T}}, u ≡ 1 mod T, ū = u^{-1}, or its valuation formula Σ χ(σ) ord_{σ^{-1}𝔓}(u) = L_{S,T}(χ,0). Nearest layers: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (proves the annihilation/Fitting theorem, whose consequence is the existence of some generator, but never the anti-unit normalisation, uniqueness or the L-value valuation formula) and ES.7 (conditional Rubin–Stark elements, a different construction not identified with Brumer–Stark units). Nearest library: tauceti:TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.idealClass_eq_one_iff (RayClass/Basic.lean:250) for 'generator congruent to 1 mod the modulus' only.

items.name: Pontryagin dual Cl^T(H)^∨ with contragredient action
items.statement: Cl^T(H)^∨ := Hom_ℤ(Cl^T(H), ℚ/ℤ), endowed with the contragredient G-action (σ f)(c) = f(σ^{−1} c).
items.locator: §1.1 Main Result, lines 337-339
items.note: The Strong Brumer–Stark and Kurihara statements concern the Fitting ideal of this dual rather than of Cl^T(H) itself. Evidence: mathlib:CharacterModule, Mathlib/Algebra/Module/CharacterModule.lean:44 `def CharacterModule : Type uA := A →+ AddCircle (1 : ℚ)`, line 67 `instance : Module R (CharacterModule A) := fast_instance% Module.compHom (A →+ _) (RingEquiv.toOpposite _ |>.toRingHom : R →+* Rᵈᵐᵃ)`, line 71 `lemma smul_apply (c : CharacterModule A) (r : R) (a : A) : (r • c) a = c (r • a) := rfl` (transpose action). mathlib:PontryaginDual, Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/PontryaginDual.lean:37 `def PontryaginDual := A →ₜ* Circle` (no group action). Tau Ceti uses CharacterModule only in TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean (finiteness/cardinality). Atlas 'Pontryagin' hits: ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7 ("derived O-linear or Pontryagin dual and Tate twist" inside duality theorems), SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2 ("Define its compact Pontryagin dual with the contragredient group action" for the Selmer group), CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.3, EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.4; none names the dual of a (ray) class group. Confirmed missing (near miss in the library). Mathlib's CharacterModule is the right group Hom_ℤ(Cl^T(H), ℚ/ℤ), and for R = ℤ[G] it is an R-module, but with (r • f)(c) = f(r • c), i.e. σ f = f ∘ σ, which differs from the paper's contragredient (σ f)(c) = f(σ^{-1} c) by the involution #; the paper's Fitting statements (Θ^# not Θ) depend on this convention, so it is a different convention, not library. No layer names Cl^T(H)^∨ with the contragredient action: I.6/I.7 presuppose it (Kurihara's Theorem 2.12 is about the dual) without naming it; […]

items.name: Involution x ↦ x^# on ℤ[G]
items.statement: x ↦ x^# is the ring involution of ℤ[G] (and of ℚ[G], ℂ[G], ℤ_p[G]) induced by g ↦ g^{−1} for g ∈ G.
items.locator: §1.1 Main Result, line 340
items.note: Θ^#_{S,T} rather than Θ_{S,T} appears in the Fitting-ideal statements because of the contragredient action on the dual. Evidence: Mathlib (commit 082e2d3) Mathlib/Algebra/MonoidAlgebra/MapDomain.lean:362 `def mapDomainRingEquiv (e : M ≃* N) : R[M] ≃+* R[N] := .ofRingHom (MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainRingHom R e) (MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainRingHom R e.symm) ...` (variables [Semiring R] [Monoid M] [Monoid N]); line 372 `mapDomainRingEquiv_single (e : M ≃* N) (r : R) (m : M) : mapDomainRingEquiv R e (single m r) = single (e m) r`; line 381 `symm_mapDomainRingEquiv (e : M ≃* N) : (mapDomainRingEquiv R e).symm = mapDomainRingEquiv R e.symm := rfl`. Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Units/Equiv.lean:195 `def MulEquiv.inv (G : Type*) [DivisionCommMonoid G] : G ≃* G := { Equiv.inv G with toFun := Inv.inv, invFun := Inv.inv, map_mul' := mul_inv }`; line 199 `MulEquiv.inv_symm (G) : (MulEquiv.inv G).symm = MulEquiv.inv G := rfl`. No StarRing/Star instance on MonoidAlgebra in the pinned tree (rg). Atlas I.8 (the layer extract line 61-77): "Construct the involution and cyclotomic twist τ on the coefficient ring ... List S, T, all twists, duals and involutions in each comparison square." Confirmed library. For abelian G, `MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainRingEquiv R (MulEquiv.inv G) : R[G] ≃+* R[G]` is the ring automorphism single g r ↦ single g⁻¹ r (mapDomainRingEquiv_single), uniformly for R = ℤ, ℚ, ℂ, ℤ_p, and it is an involution by rfl: its symm is mapDomainRingEquiv R (MulEquiv.inv G).symm = mapDomainRingEquiv R (MulEquiv.inv G) (symm_mapDomainRingEquiv + MulEquiv.inv_symm). This is an instantiation of a general declaration rather than a named '#'; the Hopf antipode (Mathlib/RingTheory/HopfAlgebra/MonoidAlgebra.lean) is the same map but only R-linear. […]

items.name: Minus part M^- and the rings ℤ[G]^-, ℤ_p[G]^-
items.statement: Let σ ∈ G be the unique complex conjugation of H. For a ℤ[1/2][G]-module M, M^- := M/(σ+1)M ≅ {m ∈ M : σ m = −m}. For a ℤ[G]-module M, M^- := (M ⊗_ℤ ℤ[1/2])^-. In particular ℤ[G]^- = ℤ[1/2][G]/(σ+1); for an odd prime p, ℤ_p[G]^- = ℤ_p[G]/(σ+1) and M_p^- := (M ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p)^-.
items.locator: §1.1 Main Result, lines 341-344
items.note: All Fitting-ideal statements are over ℤ[G]^- or ℤ_p[G]^-; passing to minus parts removes the 2-torsion ambiguity. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract lines 33-36; atlas areas catalogue): "ray-class modules, roots-of-unity corrections, and the archimedean minus construction with the precise convention of DKSW. In characteristic two, do not identify a minus quotient, a minus eigensubmodule and an integral idempotent summand without proof." Audit target: "Ray-class modules, roots-of-unity corrections and the archimedean minus construction in the DKSW convention, including characteristic two | library: absent | Tau Ceti has ray class groups as groups, but not their Galois-module structure or minus parts." Library check: rg for minusPart/minus part/(σ+1)/MonoidAlgebra quotients over Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 finds nothing; the nearest declaration is Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/CMField.lean:143 `noncomputable def complexConj : K ≃ₐ[K⁺] K` (namespace NumberField.IsCMField, with orderOf_complexConj = 2 at line 182), which supplies the complex conjugation of a CM field but no minus quotient M/(σ+1)M, no ℤ[1/2][G]/(σ+1) and no ℤ_p[G]^-. Confirmed the previous verdict (planned, I.6). Re-searched both trees: Mathlib's IsCMField/complexConj (missed by the previous agent) is only the element σ ∈ Gal(K/K⁺), not the minus construction, so it is a near miss and not library. I.6 names the minus construction and the quotient/eigensubmodule/idempotent-summand distinction (i.e. exactly M/(σ+1)M ≅ {σm = −m} after inverting 2), and owns it; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4's 'integral character idempotents for Δ of order prime to p' is shared vocabulary only.

items.name: Theorem 1.3 (Strong Brumer–Stark, conjecture of Kurihara)
items.statement: Let S, T be disjoint finite sets of places of F with S ⊃ S_∞ ∪ S_ram and T satisfying (1). Then Θ^#_{S,T} ∈ Fitt_{ℤ[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^{∨,−}) (equation (6)), where Fitt denotes the 0th Fitting ideal (developed in §2.3, label s:fitting). Deduced from Theorem 1.4 via the identity (7), and independently in §3 from the computation of Fitt_{ℤ_p[G]^-}(Sel_Σ^T(H)_p^-).
items.locator: §1.1 Main Result, Theorem 1.3, label t:sbs, equation (6) label e:sbs (lines 347-351); Fitt convention at line 353; restated at §3.3, Corollary 3.8, label t:sbsc (the source lines 906–909); proof with equation (35), label e:fitsupsk (lines 911–921); restated from §1.1 Theorem 1.3, label t:sbs, equation (6)
items.note: Corollary of the main theorem; implies Theorem 1.2 and (in §3.4) Theorem 1.6. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract lines 46-56): "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem and the stronger module-theoretic statement needed in Kurihara's Theorem 2.12. The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations. Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma ..., the Fitting-ideal comparison, and the passage from modified to unmodified data." Audit target: "Integral Brumer–Stark theorem (Dasgupta–Kakde at odd primes, DKSW integrally) and the module-theoretic statement for Kurihara's Theorem 2.12 | library: absent". Checkpoint IntegralIwasawaTheory:KU-brumerstark aggregates I.6+I.7 ("Integral Brumer–Stark, Ritter–Weiss and generalised Ribet theorem"). Library: rg -i 'brumer|stickelberger|fitting' over both pinned trees: only TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Stickelberger.lean (discriminant theorem) and Fitting decompositions of endomorphisms/Lie modules (Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean:314, Algebra/Lie/Weights). Confirmed the previous verdict. Theorem 1.3 (Θ^#_{S,T} ∈ Fitt_{ℤ[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^{∨,-}) for odd primes) is the 'odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde' of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem that I.7 names explicitly; nothing in either library states it or its ingredients (no Fitting ideals, no Stickelberger elements, no Galois-module Cl^T).

items.name: (a) Fitting ideal is contained in the annihilator
items.statement: For a finitely generated module M over a commutative ring R, Fitt_R(M) ⊂ Ann_R(M).
items.locator: §1.1 Main Result, line 358, observation (a)
items.note: External input (none given (standard; cf. §2.3, label s:fitting)). Step (a) in deducing Theorem 1.2 from Theorem 1.3 (and used throughout to pass from Fitting ideals to annihilation). Evidence: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6 (the layer extract lines 235-245): "Supply Fitting ideals, projective presentations, exterior powers and exterior bidual base-change/denominator lemmas under their finiteness/reflexivity hypotheses, reusing the generic Fitting algebra of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants"; audit target "Fitting ideals, projective presentations, exterior powers and exterior-bidual base-change/denominator lemmas | library: absent | Finite presentations and exterior powers exist; Fitting ideals and exterior biduals do not." Catalogue check: no IHG stage defines Fitting ideals (IHG.6 only says "Reuse existing homological/Fitting-ideal APIs" and "Do not ... replace the Fitting ideal by an annihilator"); IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.1 only imports "Fitting ideals of finitely presented modules" from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras; StableReduction Layer 0 names Fitting ideals of sheaves only. Library: rg -i 'fittingIdeal|Fitt_|Fitting ideal' over both trees: nothing; Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Maps.lean:860 `def Module.annihilator : Ideal R := RingHom.ker (Module.toAddMonoidEnd R M)` exists but there is no Fitting ideal to compare it with. Confirmed planned but narrowed the owner: I.1 is an importer, not the owner (PROTOCOL §15), so it is dropped; L6 is the only stage in the whole catalogue that supplies the generic Fitting-ideal API, and Fitt_R(M) ⊂ Ann_R(M) is its first basic lemma. Not library: neither pinned tree defines Fitting ideals at all. Medium confidence because no stage states the containment verbatim.

items.name: (b) Annihilator of the Pontryagin dual
items.statement: For a finite ℤ[G]-module M, with M^∨ = Hom_ℤ(M, ℚ/ℤ) carrying the contragredient G-action, Ann_{ℤ[G]}(M^∨) = Ann_{ℤ[G]}(M)^#.
items.locator: §1.1 Main Result, line 358, observation (b)
items.note: External input (none given (standard)). Step (b) in deducing Theorem 1.2 from Theorem 1.3; converts Θ^# into Θ. Evidence: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6 (the layer extract lines 235-245): "For a nonzero element of O prove the appropriate Artinian quotient is self-injective ... Develop the exact R-dual on finite modules over these zero-dimensional Gorenstein quotients, biduality, annihilator duality, length comparisons"; audit target "Exact R-dual on finite modules over zero-dimensional Gorenstein quotients: biduality, annihilator duality ... | library: absent | No Matlis-type duality in either library." SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L2 (areas catalogue): "Define its compact Pontryagin dual with the contragredient group action and prove the involution convention." Library: Mathlib/Algebra/Module/CharacterModule.lean (`def CharacterModule : Type uA := A →+ AddCircle (1 : ℚ)`, line 44, with dual/dual_injective_of_surjective etc.) and Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/PontryaginDual.lean contain no annihilator statement and no contragredient group-ring action (rg 'annihilator' in those files: none); TauCeti's CharacterOrthogonality and FiniteBilinearModule files likewise. Confirmed the previous verdict. The item is Ann_{ℤ[G]}(M^∨) = Ann_{ℤ[G]}(M)^# for finite M with contragredient action; Mathlib's CharacterModule is the underlying ℚ/ℤ-dual but carries no G-action or annihilator lemma, so not library. L6's 'annihilator duality' for the exact dual on finite modules over zero-dimensional Gorenstein quotients (ℤ_p[G]/p^k is such a quotient and Hom(M,ℚ/ℤ) is that dual up to the involution #) together with L2's 'contragredient ... involution convention' plan it; neither states it in the paper's ℤ[G] form, hence medium.

items.name: (c) Complex conjugation acts as −1 on Θ_{S,T}
items.statement: With S ⊃ S_∞ ∪ S_ram and T as above, σΘ_{S,T} = −Θ_{S,T} for the complex conjugation σ ∈ G. Consequently Θ_{S,T} annihilates a ℤ[1/2][G]-module M if and only if it annihilates M^-.
items.locator: §1.1 Main Result, line 358, observation (c)
items.note: External input (none given (standard: L_{S,T}(χ, 0) = 0 for even χ)). Step (c): reduces annihilation statements to minus parts. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract lines 33-36): "Construct equivariant Artin L-functions for the abelian CM extensions used in the modern proof, their S- and T-modifications, integral Stickelberger elements, ray-class modules, roots-of-unity corrections, and the archimedean minus construction with the precise convention of DKSW." Audit target: "Equivariant Artin L-functions of abelian CM extensions with S- and T-modifications, and integral Stickelberger elements | library: absent | Only Dirichlet L-functions over ℚ exist." Catalogue search for 'even character|odd character|complex conjugation' finds no Iwasawa-area stage; 'minus' hits in the area are I.6 and I.9 only. Library: no Stickelberger element Θ_{S,T} of a CM extension in either tree (rg stickelberger: TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Stickelberger.lean and LinearAlgebra/Matrix/LeibnizPart.lean only). Confirmed the previous verdict. σΘ_{S,T} = −Θ_{S,T} (vanishing of L_{S,T}(χ,0) for even χ) is a basic property of the integral Stickelberger elements and the minus construction that I.6 owns (I.3/AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 own the p-adic/Deligne–Ribet side, not the complex group-ring element); it is not stated verbatim anywhere, hence medium.

items.name: Inertia I_v, decomposition G_v, idempotent e_v and the element 1 − σ_v e_v
items.statement: For v ∈ S_ram let I_v ⊂ G_v ⊂ G be the inertia and decomposition groups at v, N I_v := Σ_{σ ∈ I_v} σ ∈ ℤ[G], and e_v := (1/#I_v) N I_v ∈ ℚ[G], the idempotent projecting onto the characters unramified at v. Let σ_v ∈ G_v be any representative of the Frobenius coset of v; the element 1 − σ_v e_v ∈ ℚ[G] is independent of the choice of representative.
items.locator: §1.1 Main Result, lines 361-362
items.note: Ingredients of the Sinnott–Kurihara ideal and of the Euler-factor identity (7). Evidence: NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 1 (areas catalogue, §1.4): "Let `D = MulAction.stabilizer G Q` for a prime `Q` of `M` over `p`, and let `I = Q.inertia G`"; Layer 2 (§2.2): "At a ramified `Q` the honest statement is Mathlib's `mul_inv_mem_inertia`: the Frobenius is well defined only modulo `Q.inertia`", (§2.3) "`𝔭` ramified, where the symbol is not defined and only the coset modulo inertia exists". IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6: "equivariant Artin L-functions ..., their S- and T-modifications" (the S-modification at v ∈ S_ram is the Euler-factor element built from σ_v and e_v). Library near misses read in the pinned tree: Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Defs.lean:154 `abbrev inertia : Subgroup G := I.toAddSubgroup.inertia G` (mem_inertia: σ•x − x ∈ I); Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation/RamificationGroup.lean:30 `abbrev decompositionSubgroup (A : ValuationSubring L) : Subgroup (L ≃ₐ[K] L) := MulAction.stabilizer (L ≃ₐ[K] L) A`; Mathlib/RingTheory/Frobenius.lean:183 `abbrev IsArithFrobAt`, :200 `lemma mul_inv_mem_inertia`, :260 `def _root_.arithFrobAt`; Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Invariants.lean:39 `noncomputable def average : k[G] := ⅟(Fintype.card G : k) • ∑ g : G, of k G g` (whole-group idempotent only, no subgroup version). No declaration builds N I_v ∈ ℤ[G], e_v ∈ ℚ[G] or 1 − σ_v e_v. […]

items.name: Sinnott–Kurihara ideal SK^T(H/F)
items.statement: With S = S_ram ∪ S_∞ and T disjoint from S satisfying (1), SK^T(H/F) := (Θ^#_{S_∞,T}) · ∏_{v ∈ S_ram} (N I_v, 1 − σ_v e_v), the product of the ℤ[G]-submodules of ℚ[G] generated by the indicated elements; a priori a fractional ideal of ℤ[G].
items.locator: §1.1 Main Result, unnumbered display line 364
items.note: The right-hand side of Kurihara's conjecture (Theorem 1.4). Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract lines 46-56): "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem and the stronger module-theoretic statement needed in Kurihara's Theorem 2.12 ... the Fitting-ideal comparison, and the passage from modified to unmodified data"; audit target "Integral Brumer–Stark theorem (Dasgupta–Kakde at odd primes, DKSW integrally) and the module-theoretic statement for Kurihara's Theorem 2.12 | library: absent". items.name: Theorem 1.4 (Kurihara's conjecture: exact Fitting ideal of Cl^T(H)^{∨,−})
items.statement: Let S = S_ram ∪ S_∞ and T disjoint from S satisfying (1). Then Fitt_{ℤ[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^{∨,−}) = SK^T(H/F)^- (the image of SK^T(H/F) in ℤ[G]^-). Proved in Appendix B (label s:kurihara) from Theorem 1.7. Conductor-1 proof sketch (absorbed, §1.3 lines 435-446): if H/F is unramified at all finite primes then Cl^T(H)^- is quadratically presented over ℤ[G]^-, so Fitt_{ℤ[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^-) is principal; Ribet's method gives Fitt_{ℤ[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^-) ⊂ (Θ_{S_∞,T}) (equation (11), label e:fct); the class number formula (12) and an elementary argument (§2.3) force equality; and Fitt_{ℤ[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^{∨,−}) = Fitt_{ℤ[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^-)^# in this case.
items.locator: §1.1 Main Result, Theorem 1.4, label t:sk (lines 368-371); conductor-1 sketch §1.3 lines 435-446 with equation (11) label e:fct; restated at §3.3, Theorem 3.5, label t:sk0 (the source lines 869–872); restated from §1.1 Theorem 1.4, label t:sk
items.note: The paper's main theorem; implies Theorems 1.3, 1.2 and 1.6. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract lines 46-56): "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem and the stronger module-theoretic statement needed in Kurihara's Theorem 2.12. The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations. Include ... the Fitting-ideal comparison, and the passage from modified to unmodified data. ... Prove the finite-level equivariant Tamagawa-number/Brumer–Stark comparison actually used by Kurihara. A statement about annihilation of a class group is generally weaker than the Fitting or determinant identity needed downstream." Audit targets: "Integral Brumer–Stark theorem (Dasgupta–Kakde at odd primes, DKSW integrally) and the module-theoretic statement for Kurihara's Theorem 2.12 | absent", "Fitting-ideal comparison and passage from modified to unmodified data | absent". Catalogue: 'Kurihara' occurs only in IntegralIwasawaTheory I.6–I.9 and SpecialValuesBirchTate:B.6 (the 2-primary K-theory route, not this theorem). Library: no Fitting ideals, no Galois-module Cl^T(H), no Stickelberger elements in either pinned tree (rg as above). Confirmed the previous verdict. Theorem 1.4 (Fitt_{ℤ[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^{∨,−}) = SK^T(H/F)^-) is the exact Fitting-ideal identity of the dual minus class group that I.7 names as the Dasgupta–Kakde odd-prime module-theoretic statement feeding Kurihara's Theorem 2.12, with its Appendix-B derivation from Theorem 1.7 covered by 'the Fitting-ideal comparison, and the passage from modified to unmodified data'; the absorbed conductor-1 sketch (quadratic presentation, class number formula) falls under I.7/I.6. Medium because the layer does not spell out the SK^T right-hand side.

items.name: Euler-factor identity (7): Θ^#_{S,T} ∈ SK^T(H/F)
items.statement: With S = S_ram ∪ S_∞ and T as above: Θ^#_{S,T} = Θ^#_{S_∞,T} · ∏_{v ∈ S_ram} (1 − σ_v e_v) in ℚ[G]; hence Θ^#_{S,T} ∈ SK^T(H/F). Consequently Theorem 1.4 implies Theorem 1.3 and hence Theorem 1.2.
items.locator: §1.1 Main Result, equation (7), label e:tstd (lines 375-377)

The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... the Fitting-ideal comparison, and the passage from modified to unmodified data" and its audit target "Finite-level equivariant Tamagawa-number / Brumer–Stark comparison used by Kurihara". items.name: T-congruent elements H_T^*
items.statement: H_T^* := {h ∈ H^* : ord_w(h − 1) > 0 for all w ∈ T_H}.
items.locator: §1.2 The Rubin–Stark Conjecture, line 388; restated at §3.1, first paragraph (the source lines 755–756)
items.note: Ambient group of T-congruent elements in which the (S',T)-units U_{S',T} live. Evidence: Verified in tauceti-f790474/TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/RayClass/Modulus.lean (git HEAD f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369): line 82 `namespace TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields` (the inner `namespace Modulus` closes at line 224 and `namespace IsCongrOne` at line 303, so the declaration at line 307 is `TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.congruenceSubgroup`); line 88 `structure Modulus (K) ... finitePart : Ideal (𝓞 K); finitePart_ne_bot : finitePart ≠ ⊥; infinitePart : Finset {w : InfinitePlace K // w.IsReal}`; line 150 `noncomputable def exponent (𝔪 : Modulus K) (v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K)) : ℕ` = multiplicity of v in finitePart (line 155); line 256 `def IsCongrOne (𝔪 : Modulus K) (x : Kˣ) : Prop := (∀ v : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K), v.asIdeal ∣ 𝔪.finitePart → v.valuation K ((x : K) - 1) ≤ WithZero.exp (-(𝔪.exponent v : ℤ))) ∧ ∀ w ∈ 𝔪.infinitePart, 0 < InfinitePlace.embedding_of_isReal w.2 (x : K)`; line 307 `def congruenceSubgroup (𝔪 : Modulus K) : Subgroup Kˣ where carrier := {x | IsCongrOne 𝔪 x} ...`; line 336 `mem_congruenceSubgroup : x ∈ congruenceSubgroup 𝔪 ↔ IsCongrOne 𝔪 x`. Confirmed the previous verdict. The library declaration is the congruence subgroup of Kˣ for an arbitrary modulus, so the item is the instance K = H, 𝔪 = (∏_{w∈T_H} w, ∅) (finite part the squarefree product of the primes of T_H, exponent 1 at each, = ⊤ ≠ ⊥ when T_H = ∅; empty infinite part). For that modulus IsCongrOne says v.valuation(x−1) ≤ exp(−1), i.e. ord_w(x−1) ≥ 1 > 0 for every w ∈ T_H, with no archimedean condition: exactly H_T^* = {h ∈ H^* : ord_w(h−1) > 0 ∀ w ∈ T_H} as a subgroup of Hˣ (the paper's H^* excludes 0, as does Kˣ). Hypotheses are weaker (any modulus) and the convention is the same; […]

items.name: Split primes {v_1,…,v_r}, chosen w_j, and the unit group U_{S,T} (8)
items.statement: Choose r finite primes v_1, …, v_r of F that split completely in H; §1.2 writes S = {v_1, …, v_r} for this set (in §3.4 it is called S' while S ⊃ S_∞ ∪ S_ram keeps its earlier meaning, and Θ_{S,T} in the definition of u_RBS is the Stickelberger element of that S). S_H denotes the primes of H above these v_j, and a prime w_j of H above each v_j is chosen. U_{S,T} := {u ∈ H_T^* : |u|_w = 1 for all finite primes w ∉ S_H} (equation (8)), and ℚU_{S,T} := U_{S,T} ⊗_ℤ ℚ.
items.locator: §1.2, equation (8), label e:udef (lines 390-395)
items.note: The (S,T)-unit group underlying Rubin's conjecture. Evidence: Nearest declarations (read): Mathlib RingTheory/DedekindDomain/SInteger.lean:108 `def unit : Subgroup Kˣ := (⨅ (v) (_ : v ∉ S), (v.valuation K).valuationSubring.unitGroup).copy {x : Kˣ | ∀ (v) (_ : v ∉ S), (v : HeightOneSpectrum R).valuation K x = 1} ...` (S-units, no T-congruence); tauceti-f790474/.../RayClass/Modulus.lean:307 `congruenceSubgroup` (T-congruence, no S-unit condition) and :380 `def unitsCongruenceSubgroup (𝔪 : Modulus K) : Subgroup (𝓞 K)ˣ := (congruenceSubgroup 𝔪).comap (Units.map (algebraMap (𝓞 K) K).toMonoidHom)` (= U_{∅,T}, the r = 0 special case). rg for 'SUnit|sUnit|S-unit|TUnit' over both trees finds no (S,T)-unit group. Atlas: I.2 (the layer extract:29) "Define inverse limits of p-primary class groups, S-class groups, units, S-units"; MordellLawrenceVenkatesh:LV.6 "The S-unit theorem" (Diophantine S-unit equations); ES.7 (the layer extract:214) names only "a conjectural Rubin–Stark element"; no stage in areas/*.json or roadmaps/*.json mentions (S,T)-units or T-smoothed S-units. Confirmed missing. U_{S,T} = {u ∈ H_T^* : |u|_w = 1 for finite w ∉ S_H} is the meet `Set.unit S_H H ⊓ congruenceSubgroup 𝔪_T` of two library subgroups, but neither tree defines it (and the special case with S = ∅, `unitsCongruenceSubgroup`, is a near miss, not the item), nor ℚU_{S,T} as a ℚ[G]-module; the choice of split primes v_j and of w_j | v_j is also unrepresented. No layer names (S,T)-units: I.2's S-units are Iwasawa-theoretic inverse limits without T-smoothing, LV.6 is about S-unit equations, and I.6's 'S- and T-modifications' are of L-functions.

items.name: The map ord_G on the r-th exterior power (9),(10)
items.statement: ord_G: ∧^r_{ℚ[G]} ℚU_{S,T}^- → ℚ[G]^- is the ℚ[G]-linear map induced by ord_G(u_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ u_r) = det( Σ_{σ ∈ G} [σ^{−1}] ord_{w_j}(σ(u_i)) )_{i,j = 1,…,r}.
items.locator: §1.2, equations (9) label e:ordg and (10) label e:ordgdef (lines 396-403)
items.note: Equivariant regulator of valuations used to define the Rubin–Brumer–Stark element. Evidence: Nearest declaration (read): Mathlib LinearAlgebra/ExteriorPower/Pairing.lean:64 `noncomputable def pairingDual (n : ℕ) : ⋀[R]^n (Module.Dual R M) →ₗ[R] Module.Dual R (⋀[R]^n M)` with :70 `pairingDual R M n (ιMulti _ _ f) (ιMulti _ _ v) = Matrix.det (n := Fin n) (.of (fun i j ↦ f j (v i)))`, and :44 `alternatingMapToDual`. No declaration in either tree for an equivariant valuation functional u ↦ Σ_σ [σ⁻¹] ord_w(σu), for minus parts of ℤ[G]- or ℚ[G]-modules, or for a group-ring-valued regulator. Atlas: ES.6 (the layer extract:194,196) "Construct the exterior bidual ..., its determinant evaluation map" and "prove the Stark regulator, rank-one freeness and structure control" (the Mazur–Rubin 2016 regulator of Stark systems over Artinian rings/DVRs); PS.5 (the layer extract:297) "regulator, functional-equation and duality normalization" for ETNC statements. rg -i 'equivariant regulator|Stark regulator|ord_G' over the layer extract, the layer extract, areas/*.json, roadmaps/*.json finds no valuation regulator. Confirmed missing. ord_G would be `pairingDual ℚ[G] (ℚU_{S,T}^-) r` applied to the wedge of the r equivariant valuation functionals, so Mathlib supplies the abstract determinant pairing, but the functionals ord_{w_j}^G, the minus part ℚU_{S,T}^- and the map ord_G are absent, and ES.6's 'Stark regulator' is the Mazur–Rubin regulator of a Stark system over an Artinian coefficient ring, not the valuation regulator of (S,T)-units; PS.5's regulator is the ETNC regulator normalisation. Shared vocabulary only.

items.name: ord_G is a ℚ[G]-module isomorphism
items.statement: The map ord_G: ∧^r_{ℚ[G]} ℚU_{S,T}^- → ℚ[G]^- of (9)-(10) is an isomorphism of ℚ[G]-modules.
items.note: External input (none given at line 404 (standard; cf. \cite{rubin})). Guarantees existence and uniqueness of u_RBS. Evidence: Library: Mathlib NumberTheory/NumberField/Units/DirichletTheorem.lean (`unitLattice` line 174, rank card(InfinitePlace K) − 1 per the module doc at lines 58-59) is Dirichlet's theorem for 𝒪_H^× only, not for S-units, not Galois-equivariant, no minus parts; Mathlib SInteger.lean:108 `Set.unit` carries no rank/freeness statement; TauCeti has no S-unit theorem (rg 'S-unit|SUnit|sUnit' over TauCeti/ returns nothing). Atlas: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/GlobalNumberFields layer 6 (the layer extract:1854) "recover class-group finiteness and Dirichlet's unit theorem as agreement corollaries"; ClassFieldTheory layer 10 (the layer extract:1265) "the Herbrand quotient of the relevant S-idele and S-unit modules" and layer 13 (the layer extract:1461) "Develop the S-idele and unit-lattice Herbrand calculations"; KTheoryLowDegrees:U.4 uses "Dirichlet's S-unit theorem" O_{F,S}^× ≅ μ(F) ⊕ ℤ^{r₁+r₂+|S|−1}; MordellLawrenceVenkatesh:LV.6 is the Diophantine S-unit theorem. None states the G-module structure ℚU_S ≅ ker(ℚ[S_H] → ℚ) or the minus-part isomorphism. Confirmed missing. The statement is the equivariant (Dirichlet–Herbrand) S-unit theorem for the minus part: ℚU_{S,T}^- ≅ (ℚ[G]^-)^r via the valuations at the r completely split primes, the archimedean and T-parts dropping out. Neither library has any S-unit theorem, let alone a G-equivariant one; the CFT layers only plan Herbrand-quotient computations of S-unit modules (which use such a structure theorem but do not name it), and the GlobalNumberFields/KTheory layers only reuse the non-equivariant rank statement.

items.name: Rubin–Brumer–Stark element u_RBS
items.statement: u_RBS ∈ ∧^r_{ℚ[G]} ℚU_{S,T}^- ⊂ ∧^r_{ℚ[G]} ℚU_{S,T} is the unique element with ord_G(u_RBS) = Θ_{S,T} (Θ_{S,T} for S ⊃ S_∞ ∪ S_ram as in §1). It depends on the choice of the w_j only up to multiplication by an element of G.

I.6 (the layer extract:35) plans the Stickelberger element but does not mention Rubin–Stark; other 'rubin' hits (ES.3, ES.4, ES.8, EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture L0–L3, HE.*, BSD.6) refer to Rubin's Euler-system bounds or Mazur–Rubin. ES.7's sentence names the Rubin–Stark element only to disclaim it: it is a 'conditional application', i.e. an input the layer may assume once its integrality and norm relations are proved elsewhere, not a construction ES.7 owns; no layer plans the definition u_RBS := ord_G^{-1}(Θ_{S,T}) (which is unconditional, needing items 28-29 and I.6's Θ_{S,T}) or its dependence on the w_j up to G. Applying the rule that a mention as shared vocabulary/conditional input is not planning, and defaulting to the stricter status, this is missing; nearest layers are ES.7 (name only) and I.6 (Stickelberger side).

items.name: r-th exterior power bidual ∩^r_{ℤ[G]} U_{S,T}
items.statement: For ℤ[G]-module homomorphisms φ_i: U_{S,T} → ℤ[G], i = 1,…,r, let φ: ∧^r_{ℚ[G]} ℚU_{S,T} → ℚ[G] be the ℚ[G]-linear map induced by φ(u_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ u_r) = det(φ_i(u_j)). The r-th exterior power bidual ∩^r_{ℤ[G]} U_{S,T} is the set of u ∈ ∧^r_{ℚ[G]} ℚU_{S,T} such that φ(u) ∈ ℤ[G] for all r-tuples (φ_1,…,φ_r) ∈ Hom_{ℤ[G]}(U_{S,T}, ℤ[G])^{⊕r}.

items.name: Lemma 2.1, integrality of L_{S_∞,T}(H/H^+, ε, 0)
items.statement: Let F be totally real, H/F a finite abelian CM extension with G = Gal(H/F), H^+ the maximal totally real subfield of H and ε the nontrivial character of Gal(H/H^+). Let T be a finite set of finite primes of F, unramified in H, satisfying condition (1) (no nontrivial root of unity of H is ≡ 1 mod every prime of H above T). Then L_{S_∞,T}(H/H^+, ε, 0) ∈ ℤ. (Proof: ε is ±1-valued so the value is rational by Klingen/Siegel; it is integral by Cassou-Noguès/Deligne–Ribet because L_{S_∞,T}(H/H^+,ε,0) = L_{S_ram(H/H^+),T}(H/H^+,ε,0) and (S_ram(H/H^+) ∪ S_∞, T) is an admissible pair for the quadratic extension H/H^+.)

items.name: Lemma 2.1, equation (22): T-smoothed analytic class number formula for the minus part
items.statement: With F, H, G, H^+, ε as in Lemma 2.1 and T a finite set of finite primes of F unramified in H satisfying condition (1): #Cl^T(H)^- ≐ L_{S_∞,T}(H/H^+, ε, 0), where ≐ means equality up to a power of 2 and Cl^T(H)^- = (Cl^T(H) ⊗ ℤ[1/2])^-. Proof (absorbed): (24) L_{S_∞,T}(H/H^+,ε,0) = ζ^*_{H,S_∞,T}(0)/ζ^*_{H^+,S_∞,T}(0), leading terms at s = 0, both zeta functions vanishing there to order rank O_H^* = rank O_{H^+}^* = [H^+:ℚ] − 1; (25) this ratio equals #Cl^T(H)R_T(H)/(#Cl^T(H^+)R_T(H^+)) by the T-smoothed Dedekind class number formula; (26) it is ≐ #Cl^T(H)^- because Cl^T(H) ⊗ ℤ[1/2] ≅ (Cl^T(H^+) ⊗ ℤ[1/2]) ⊕ Cl^T(H)^- and R_T(H) = 2^{[H^+:ℚ]−1} R_T(H^+), the latter since O^*_{H,S_∞,T} = O^*_{H^+,S_∞,T} by condition (1). Without T-smoothing this is [nickel, Proposition 2].

items.name: T-smoothed Dedekind class number formula at s = 0 (equation (25))
items.statement: Let K be a number field and T a finite set of finite primes of K such that the T-unit group O^*_{K,S_∞,T} = {u ∈ O_K^* : u ≡ 1 mod every prime of K above T} is torsion-free (guaranteed by condition (1)). Then the leading term ζ^*_{K,S_∞,T}(0) of the T-smoothed Dedekind zeta function ζ_{K,S_∞,T}(s) = ζ_K(s)∏_{𝔮∈T}(1 − N𝔮^{1−s}) at s = 0 equals, up to sign, #Cl^T(K)·R_T(K), where R_T(K) is the regulator of O^*_{K,S_∞,T}; the order of vanishing is rank O_K^*. As used: ζ^*_{H,S_∞,T}(0)/ζ^*_{H^+,S_∞,T}(0) = #Cl^T(H)R_T(H)/(#Cl^T(H^+)R_T(H^+)) for K = H and K = H^+.

items.name: Artin formalism for L-functions (induction and quadratic extensions)
items.statement: Artin L-functions are invariant under induction and additive in the character: L_{Σ,Σ'}(H/H^+, ε, s) = L_{Σ,Σ'}(H/F, Ind_{G_{H^+}}^{G_F} ε, s), and L(H/F, ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2, s) = L(H/F,ψ_1,s)L(H/F,ψ_2,s). As used: (a) Ind_{G_{H^+}}^{G_F} ε = ⊕_{ψ∈Ĝ odd} ψ, giving L_{S_∞,T}(H/H^+, ε, 0) = ∏_{ψ odd} L_{S_∞,T}(H/F, ψ, 0) (equation (23)); (b) for the quadratic extension H/H^+, ζ_{H,S_∞,T}(s) = ζ_{H^+,S_∞,T}(s)·L_{S_∞,T}(H/H^+, ε, s), giving (24) as a ratio of leading terms.

items.name: Coefficient ring O, the G-modules O_ψ and the ψ-component M_ψ
items.statement: Fix an odd prime p and a finite extension O of ℤ_p containing all values of all characters G → ℚ̄_p^*; K denotes its fraction field (used in §3.1). For ψ ∈ Ĝ, O_ψ is the ring O endowed with the G-action in which g ∈ G acts by multiplication by ψ(g). There is an O-algebra embedding O[G] ↪ ∏_{ψ∈Ĝ} O_ψ, x ↦ (ψ(x))_ψ. For a ℤ[G]-module M, M_ψ := M ⊗_{ℤ[G]} O_ψ.

items.name: Character group ring R_Ψ
items.statement: For a subset Ψ ⊂ Ĝ, R_Ψ is the image of the O-algebra map O[G] → ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O_ψ, x ↦ (ψ(x))_{ψ∈Ψ} (equivalently O[G]/∩_{ψ∈Ψ} ker ψ). Quotients of O[G] of this form are called character group rings. Each R_Ψ is a finite index subring of the finite product of DVRs ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O_ψ.
items.locator: §2.2, unnumbered definition (the source lines 629–631)
items.note: The class of rings over which the size lemmas 2.4, 2.5 and Lemma 3.2 are formulated; used throughout §5. Evidence: rg -i 'character group ring|characterGroupRing|charGroupRing|finite index subring|product of DVR|Pi.*DiscreteValuationRing' over pinned Mathlib/ and TauCeti/ → no relevant hit (one TauCeti valuation lemma in FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/OfValuationSubring.lean). Atlas: rg -i 'character group ring|finite.index subring' over atlas/areas/*.json, roadmaps/*.json and packets/ → no hits. Nearest layer texts read: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4 (idempotents for prime-to-p Δ only) and PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6 (iwasawa-1.json): 'Own the ring-level algebra required by Burns–Sakamoto–Sano: a commutative O-order R (finite torsionfree over a complete DVR O, with its specified finite-dimensional semisimple fraction algebra), including semilocal products ... Tests include O, a finite product of DVRs, a nonmaximal Gorenstein order'. Confirmed missing. Neither library defines R_Ψ = image of O[G] in ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O_ψ (= O[G]/∩ ker ψ) or the class of character group rings. L6 is the nearest layer, since every R_Ψ is a commutative O-order with fraction algebra ∏_Ψ K and L6 lists 'a finite product of DVRs' as a test case, but L6 never names group rings, characters or quotients of O[G] by character kernels; L4's idempotent decomposition yields the full product ∏ O_ψ only for prime-to-p characters, not the non-split subrings R_Ψ for arbitrary Ψ. Shared vocabulary, not planning.

items.name: Local components R_χ = O[G_p]_χ of O[G] and characters belonging to χ
items.statement: Write G = G_p × G' with G_p the p-Sylow subgroup and G' the subgroup of elements of prime-to-p order. For χ ∈ Ĝ', R_χ = O[G_p]_χ is the O-algebra O[G_p] with G acting by g ↦ χ(g)·ḡ, ḡ the image of g under G → G_p. O[G] decomposes as the product of the local rings R_χ, χ ∈ Ĝ' (its connected components). Each R_χ is the character group ring R_Ψ for Ψ = {ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ|_{G'} = χ}; the ψ ∈ Ψ are said to belong to χ. O[G]^- is the product of the R_χ with χ odd.

items.name: Norm element N I of a subgroup
items.statement: For a subgroup I ⊂ G, N I = Σ_{σ∈I} σ ∈ ℤ[G] ⊂ O[G]. (When #I is invertible, e_I = N I/#I is the idempotent projecting onto the characters trivial on I; e_v = N I_v/#I_v in ℚ[G].)

items.name: Lemma 2.2: O[G]/(N I) is a character group ring
items.statement: Let I ⊂ G be a subgroup and N I = Σ_{σ∈I} σ ∈ O[G]. Then O[G]/(N I) ≅ R_Ψ where Ψ = {ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ(I) ≠ 1}; more precisely the canonical surjection α: O[G] ↠ R_Ψ has kernel exactly the ideal (N I). (Proof: ψ(N I) = 0 for ψ(I) ≠ 1 gives N I ∈ ker α; conversely if x ∈ ker α then ψ(gx) = ψ(x) for all g ∈ I and all ψ ∈ Ĝ, so gx = x for all g ∈ I and x ∈ (N I).)

items.name: Corollary 2.3: R_χ/(N I) is a character group ring

items.name: Quadratically presented module
items.statement: Let R be a commutative ring. An R-module N is quadratically presented over R if there exist a positive integer m and an exact sequence R^m →^φ R^m → N → 0, i.e. a finite presentation with the same number m of generators and relations.

items.name: Fitting ideal of a quadratically presented module is principal, generated by det φ
items.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and N an R-module with a quadratic presentation R^m →^φ R^m → N → 0. Then the 0th Fitting ideal Fitt_R(N) is principal, generated by the determinant of φ: Fitt_R(N) = (det φ).

items.name: Lemma 2.4: order of a quadratically presented module over a finite index subring of a product of PIDs
items.statement: Let B be a finite index subring of a finite product of PIDs (for example any character group ring R_Ψ, Ψ ⊂ Ĝ). Let N be a quadratically presented B-module such that Fitt_B(N) = (x) for some non-zerodivisor x ∈ B, and suppose B/(x) is finite. Then N is finite and #N = #(B/(x)). Proof (absorbed): for B a PID, N ≅ B^m/AB^m ≅ ⊕ B/x_iB with x_i the Smith normal form entries of a relation matrix A, (x) = (det A) = (∏x_i), and #N = ∏#(B/x_iB) = #(B/(x)); the statement for B and B' implies it for B × B'; and it descends from B' to a finite index subring B ⊂ B' via (27) #(B'/det(A)B')/#(B/det(A)B) = #(B'/B)/#(det(A)B'/det(A)B) = 1 and (28) #((B')^m/A(B')^m)/#(B^m/AB^m) = #((B')^m/B^m)/#(A(B')^m/AB^m) = 1, multiplication by det A resp. by A being isomorphisms of the indicated quotients (injectivity for A via the adjugate: Av ∈ AB^m ⇒ det(A)v ∈ det(A)B^m ⇒ v ∈ B^m).

items.name: Smith normal form over a PID
items.statement: Let B be a principal ideal domain and A an m×m matrix over B. There are invertible matrices P, Q over B with PAQ diagonal with entries x_1, …, x_m; consequently B^m/A·B^m ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^m B/x_iB and (det A) = (∏_{i=1}^m x_i). As used in the proof of Lemma 2.4: if det A = x is a non-zerodivisor with B/(x) finite, each B/x_iB is finite (a quotient of B/xB) and #(B^m/AB^m) = ∏#(B/x_iB) = #(B/(x)).

items.name: Lemma 2.5: order of R_Ψ/(x) via character values
items.statement: Let Ψ ⊂ Ĝ, let R_Ψ be the associated character group ring over O, and let x ∈ R_Ψ be a non-zerodivisor. Then #(R_Ψ/(x)) = #(O/(∏_{ψ∈Ψ} ψ(x))). (Proof: R_Ψ ↪ O_Ψ := ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O, y ↦ (ψ(y))_ψ, has finite index; #(O_Ψ/R_Ψ) = #(xO_Ψ/xR_Ψ) since multiplication by x is an isomorphism of these quotients; hence #(R_Ψ/xR_Ψ) = #(O_Ψ/xO_Ψ) = ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} #(O/ψ(x)) as O_Ψ is a product ring.)

items.name: Elementary argument: the inclusion (11) plus the class number formula (12) force equality (conductor-1 case)
items.statement: Work over O[G]^- (p odd, O as in §2.2). Assume H/F is unramified at all finite primes, so that (as the paper asserts, 'one can show') Cl^T(H)^-_O := Cl^T(H)^- ⊗ O is a quadratically presented O[G]^- -module. If Fitt_{O[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^-_O) ⊂ (Θ_{S_∞,T}) (the inclusion (11)), then Fitt_{O[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^-_O) = (x·Θ_{S_∞,T}) for some x ∈ O[G]^-, and Lemmas 2.4 and 2.5 give #Cl^T(H)^-_O = #(O[G]^-/(xΘ_{S_∞,T})) = #(O/∏_{ψ odd} ψ(xΘ_{S_∞,T})). The class number formula (12), #Cl^T(H)^- ≐ ∏_{ψ odd} ψ(Θ_{S_∞,T}), then forces ψ(x) ∈ O^* for all odd ψ, hence x ∈ (O[G]^-)^*, so Fitt_{O[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^-_O) = (Θ_{S_∞,T}).

items.name: Lemma 2.6, first assertion: multiplicativity of Fitting ideals for a quadratically presented quotient

items.name: Lemma 2.6, second assertion: extensions of quadratically presented modules are quadratically presented
items.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and 0 → A → B → C → 0 a short exact sequence of R-modules. If A and C are both quadratically presented over R, then so is B. (Proof in [northcott, Theorem 22].)

items.name: Lemma 2.7: Fitting ideals of two extensions with a common quotient
items.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and B, B' quadratically presented R-modules fitting into exact sequences 0 → A → B → C → 0 and 0 → A' → B' → C → 0 of R-modules. Then Fitt_R(A)·Fitt_R(B') = Fitt_R(A')·Fitt_R(B). (Proof: the fibre product M = B ×_C B' of pairs (b,b') with the same image in C sits in 0 → A' → M → B → 0 and 0 → A → M → B' → 0; computing Fitt_R(M) both ways with Lemma 2.6 gives the result. A more general statement is [kataoka, Theorem 2.6].)

items.name: The Burns–Kurihara–Sano Selmer module Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H), equation (29)
items.statement: With Σ ⊇ S_∞ and Σ' disjoint finite sets of places of F, Σ' satisfying condition (1): Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) = Hom_ℤ(H^*_{Σ'}, ℤ) / ∏_{w ∉ Σ_H ∪ Σ'_H} ℤ, the product over the primes w of H not above Σ ∪ Σ', the implicit map sending a tuple (x_w)_w to the function Σ_w x_w ord_w. It is given the contragredient G-action (gφ)(x) = φ(g^{−1}x). Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_p := Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p and Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R := base change to a component R of O[G]^-.
items.locator: §3.1, equation (29), label e:selmerdef (the source lines 757–760)
items.note: External input (\cite{bks} D. Burns, M. Kurihara, T. Sano, On zeta elements for G_m, Doc. Math. 21; \cite{burns} D. Burns, On derivatives of p-adic L-series at s = 0, J. Reine Angew. Math. 762). The module whose minus part is quadratically presented with Fitting ideal (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) (Theorem 3.3); it replaces Cl^T(H)^∨ in the general ramified case. items.name: Y_{H,Σ}: free abelian group on the places of H above Σ
items.statement: For a set Σ of places of F, Y_{H,Σ} is the free abelian group on the places of H above Σ, with its canonical G-action (a ℤ[G]-module ≅ ⊕_{v∈Σ} ℤ[G/G_v]). Y_{H,S_∞}^- = 0, since complex conjugation fixes every infinite place of H.
items.locator: §3.1, sentence before Lemma 3.1 (the source line 763); Y^-_{H,S_∞} = 0 at line 779
items.note: Kernel term of Lemma 3.1, of the trivial-zero computation, and of the exact sequence (44) in §3.4. Evidence: Read Mathlib Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Over.lean:376 `def primesOver : Set (Ideal B) := { P : Ideal B | P.IsPrime ∧ P.LiesOver p }` and NumberTheory/RamificationInertia/Galois.lean:77 `instance : MulAction G (primesOver p B)`, :95 `noncomputable instance : MulAction Gal(L/K) (primesOver p B)`, :132 `isPretransitive_of_isGaloisGroup`; Tau Ceti TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/PrimesAbove.lean:78 `def primesAbove (S : Set (HeightOneSpectrum R)) : Set (HeightOneSpectrum B)` (primes of B above a set of primes of R, finite when S is). These give the set of finite places above Σ with its Galois action, but rg -in 'free abelian.*place|placesAbove|PlacesOver|Z\[G/G_v\]|ofMulAction' in Tau Ceti and Mathlib finds no ℤ[G]-module on the places (infinite places included), no minus part and no Y^-_{H,S_∞} = 0. Atlas: rg -io 'Y_\{H|Y_S|free abelian group on the places|places above S|permutation module' over areas/*.json and roadmaps/*.json returns only modular-curve Y_{H,k} and Fargues–Fontaine Y_S hits; I.6's description (read in full) names 'ray-class modules' and 'Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations' but not the place module. Confirmed missing. The set of primes above Σ with Galois action is in both libraries (Mathlib primesOver + MulAction, Tau Ceti primesAbove), but Y_{H,Σ} as a ℤ[G]-module (including infinite places), its decomposition ⊕ ℤ[G/G_v] and the vanishing of the minus part at S_∞ are absent, and no layer names it; I.6's Ritter–Weiss constructions would need it as a kernel term but the description does not say so.

items.name: Lemma 3.1: Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^- is an extension of Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-} by Y^-_{H,Σ}
items.statement: With Σ ⊇ S_∞ and Σ' disjoint finite sets of places of F, Σ' satisfying condition (1), there is a canonical short exact sequence of ℤ[G]^- -modules 0 → Y^-_{H,Σ} → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^- → Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-} → 0. Proof (absorbed): the canonical exact sequence 0 → Y_{H,Σ∖S_∞} → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → Sel_{S_∞}^{Σ'}(H) → 0 of ℤ[G]-modules, first map induced by w ↦ ord_w; Y^-_{H,S_∞} = 0; and the isomorphism (30) Sel_{S_∞}^{Σ'}(H)^- ≅ Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-}.
items.locator: §3.1, Lemma 3.1, label l:ysc (the source lines 766–772); proof lines 774–789

The nearest layer is IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6, whose 'comparison to class/ray-class groups' concerns the Ritter–Weiss modules ∇ and whose 'archimedean minus construction' is the minus-part convention; neither phrase names the Selmer module or Lemma 3.1, so it is not a clearly containing target. items.name: Burns's exact sequence (5) for Sel_{S_∞}^{Σ'}(H)
items.statement: For Σ = S_∞ and Σ' a finite set of finite primes of F satisfying condition (1), there is a canonical short exact sequence of ℤ[G]-modules 0 → Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨ → Sel_{S_∞}^{Σ'}(H) → Hom_ℤ(O^*_{H,S_∞,Σ'}, ℤ) → 0, where O^*_{H,S_∞,Σ'} = {u ∈ O_H^* : u ≡ 1 mod every prime of H above Σ'} is the group of Σ'-units and Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨ = Hom(Cl^{Σ'}(H), ℚ/ℤ).
items.locator: §3.1, proof of Lemma 3.1 (the source lines 784–787), citing [burns, sequence (5)]
items.note: External input (\cite{burns}, sequence (5): D. Burns, On derivatives of p-adic L-series at s = 0, J. Reine Angew. Math. 762 (going back to \cite{bks})). Yields (30) after taking minus parts. Evidence: Library: only the unit term exists, as TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.unitsCongruenceSubgroup (Modulus.lean:380, read: `(congruenceSubgroup 𝔪).comap (Units.map (algebraMap (𝓞 K) K).toMonoidHom)`, i.e. O^*_{H,Σ'} at the modulus ∏_{w∈Σ'_H} w); no Selmer module, no Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨ as ℤ[G]-module (item 58/60 searches; rg 'Burns' in both trees hits only Burnside). items.name: Equation (30): Sel_{S_∞}^{Σ'}(H)^- ≅ Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-}
items.statement: For H/F a finite abelian CM extension and Σ' a finite set of finite primes of F satisfying condition (1): Sel_{S_∞}^{Σ'}(H)^- ≅ Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-}. (Proof: take minus parts of Burns's sequence (5); since H is CM, (O^*_{H,S_∞,Σ'})^- is trivial.)

Evidence: Mathlib Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/CMField.lean:71 `class IsCMField (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K] : Prop`, :263 `unitsComplexConj : (𝓞 K)ˣ ≃* (𝓞 K)ˣ`, :270 `def realUnits : Subgroup (𝓞 K)ˣ`, :277 `unitsComplexConj_eq_self_iff` — the CM unit ingredients that would show (O^*_{H,S_∞,Σ'})^- is torsion — but no Selmer module, no minus part (rg 'minus part|minusPart' none), no class-group dual. the layer extract I.6 audit: 'archimedean minus construction in the DKSW convention ... | library: absent'.
