items.name: Equation (31): alternative presentation of Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) via S'-units (BKS)
items.statement: Let S' be any finite set of places of F containing Σ and disjoint from Σ', chosen so that the S'-class group Cl^{Σ'}_{S'}(H) is trivial. Then there is a canonical isomorphism Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) ≅ Hom_ℤ(O^*_{H,S',Σ'}, ℤ) / ∏_{w∈S'_H − Σ_H} ℤ, with the implicit map (x_w) ↦ Σ_w x_w ord_w as in (29), where O^*_{H,S',Σ'} is the group of S'-units of H congruent to 1 modulo all primes above Σ'.
items.locator: §3.1, equation (31), label e:sels (the source lines 792–798), citing [bks, equation (12)]
items.note: External input (\cite{bks}, equation (12): D. Burns, M. Kurihara, T. Sano, On zeta elements for G_m, Doc. Math. 21). Finite presentation of Sel in terms of S'-units, used in §4 (line 1180) and Appendix A (lines 3458, 3506) to compare Sel with the Ritter–Weiss module. Evidence: Library: Tau Ceti's S-units and S-class group (TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/SInteger/Unit.lean, SInteger/ClassGroup.lean, `ClassGroup (S.integer K)` per the SelmerGroup/Basic.lean docstring) and unitsCongruenceSubgroup (Modulus.lean:380) exist as inputs; rg -in 'Hom.*ord|S-units.*congruent|Cl_S.*trivial' in both trees finds no presentation Hom_ℤ(O^*_{H,S',Σ'},ℤ)/∏_{w∈S'_H−Σ_H} ℤ and no BKS Selmer module (item 58). Nearest library objects: Tau Ceti's S-units/S-class group of a Dedekind domain and units congruent to one modulo a modulus, which are inputs, not the isomorphism (31).

items.name: Vanishing of Fitt_{O_ψ}(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_ψ) at a non-trivial character with a trivial zero
items.statement: Let ψ ∈ Ĝ with ψ ≠ 1 and suppose ψ(G_v) = 1 for some v ∈ Σ, G_v ⊂ G the decomposition group at v. With Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_ψ = Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) ⊗_{ℤ[G]} O_ψ, one has Fitt_{O_ψ}(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_ψ) = 0. (Proof: it suffices that the finitely generated O_ψ-module Sel_ψ is infinite, i.e. that Sel_ψ ⊗_{O_ψ} K = (Sel ⊗ K)^ψ ≠ 0; by Lemma 3.1 and ψ ≠ 1, (Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) ⊗ K)^ψ ≅ (Y_{H,Σ} ⊗ K)^ψ ⊇ (Y_{H,{v}} ⊗ K)^ψ = (Ind_{G_v}^G K)^ψ ≅ K by Frobenius reciprocity since ψ(G_v) = 1.)
items.locator: §3.1, unnumbered claim before Lemma 3.2 (the source lines 800–805)
items.note: Character-wise input to Lemma 3.2: trivial zeroes force the Fitting ideal of the Selmer module to vanish. Evidence: rg -in 'fitting' over Mathlib and Tau Ceti: only Fitting's lemma (TauCeti/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Indecomposable.lean:76, KrullSchmidt/*), Lie-algebra Fitting decomposition (Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/TraceForm.lean) and Artinian modules; no Fitting ideal (the layer extract I.6 audit: 'neither library has Fitting ideals'). No Selmer module (item 58). Tau Ceti does have character-level Frobenius reciprocity: TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Induction/FrobeniusReciprocity.lean:151 `theorem frobenius_reciprocity [Fintype G] (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : k)) (A : FDRep k S) (B : FDRep k G) : (Nat.card G : k)⁻¹ * ∑ g, (indFDRep A).character g * B.character g⁻¹ = (Nat.card S : k)⁻¹ * ∑ s : S, A.character s * B.character (s⁻¹)` and :109 `finrank_hom_indFDRep` — an ingredient for (Ind_{G_v}^G K)^ψ ≅ K, not the item. Atlas: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6 'Supply Fitting ideals, projective presentations, exterior powers ... reusing the generic Fitting algebra of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants' plans a generic Fitting API; rg -io 'trivial zero' over areas/*.json hits only Dirichlet L-function trivial zeros (AnalyticNumberTheory) and a quadratic-form 'nontrivial zero'; NE.5 mentions 'exceptional-zero behavior' of zeta elements only. No stage names the vanishing of Fitt_{O_ψ}(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_ψ) when ψ(G_v) = 1. Confirmed missing. Fitting ideals are planned only generically (L6 / IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants), the Selmer module and its ψ-components are absent and unplanned, and the trivial-zero mechanism is not named by any layer; Tau Ceti's frobenius_reciprocity (characters of FDRep over a field with |G| invertible) is the only library ingredient found.

items.name: Frobenius reciprocity for the place module Y_{H,{v}}
items.statement: For a place v of F with decomposition group G_v ⊂ G, Y_{H,{v}} ⊗ K ≅ Ind_{G_v}^G K, and for ψ ∈ Ĝ the ψ-isotypic part (Ind_{G_v}^G K)^ψ is ≅ K if ψ(G_v) = 1 and 0 otherwise.

items.name: Fitting ideals commute with base change (functoriality for quotients)
items.statement: For a homomorphism of commutative rings R → R' and a finitely presented R-module M, Fitt_{R'}(M ⊗_R R') = Fitt_R(M)·R'. As used: if Fitt_{O_ψ}(M ⊗_{ℤ[G]} O_ψ) = 0 for every ψ ∈ Ψ then Fitt_{R_Ψ}(M ⊗_{ℤ[G]} R_Ψ) = 0 (since R_Ψ ↪ ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O_ψ); and Fitting ideals over ℤ_p[G]^- may be computed after extending scalars to O and projecting to each component R = O[G_p]_χ.
items.locator: §3.1, proof of Lemma 3.2 ('Fitting ideals are functorial with respect to quotients', the source line 811); also the reduction at the start of the proof of Theorem 3.7 (line 925); restated at §5.2, equation (67), label e:fitpsi (the source lines 1398–1402), proof of Lemma 5.7 (line 1561) and line 1571
items.note: External input (standard (cf. \cite{northcott}; no citation given)). Passes Fitting-ideal statements between ℤ_p[G]^-, O[G]^-, the components R_χ, and the O_ψ. Evidence: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6 (the layer extract line 234ff; atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json): "Supply Fitting ideals, projective presentations, exterior powers and exterior bidual base-change/denominator lemmas under their finiteness/reflexivity hypotheses, reusing the generic Fitting algebra of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants." Ownership corroborated by IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.1: "import from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras the characteristic ideals ..., Fitting ideals of finitely presented modules, ..." and EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.7: "Import PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L6's Gorenstein-order, self-injective Artinian reduction, exact-duality and Fitting APIs". IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6: "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality." Library: `rg -il 'fittingIdeal|fitting ideal|Fitt_'` over the pinned Mathlib tree returns nothing; in the pinned Tau Ceti tree the only 'Fitting' hits are Fitting's lemma / Krull–Schmidt files (TauCeti/RingTheory/KrullSchmidt/*.lean, TauCeti/RingTheory/PrimitiveIdempotent.lean, TauCeti/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Indecomposable.lean). IHG.6 only says "Reuse existing homological/Fitting-ideal APIs and export these general algebraic subresults independently"; no IHG stage defines Fitting ideals. Confirmed the previous verdict. Neither pinned library has a Fitting ideal at all, so Fitt_{R'}(M ⊗_R R') = Fitt_R(M)R' cannot be library. […]

items.name: Lemma 3.2, first equality: Fitt_{R_Ψ}(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) ⊗ R_Ψ) = 0 on trivial-zero components
items.statement: Let Ψ ⊂ Ĝ with 1 ∉ Ψ and let R_Ψ be the associated character group ring. Suppose that for each ψ ∈ Ψ there exists v ∈ Σ with ψ(G_v) = 1. Then Fitt_{R_Ψ}(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) ⊗_{ℤ[G]} R_Ψ) = 0. (Immediate from the character-wise vanishing and functoriality of Fitting ideals for quotients.)
items.locator: §3.1, Lemma 3.2, label l:trivial, first equality (the source lines 808–811)

The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations. Include ... the Fitting-ideal comparison, and the passage from modified to unmodified data." Paper: the source 808–811 (Lemma 3.2, label l:trivial): "The first equality follows immediately from the fact that Fitt_{O_ψ}(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_ψ) = 0 since Fitting ideals are functorial with respect to quotients." The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde'), so the containing target is clear; the lemma, the Selmer module Sel_Σ^{Σ'} and the character group rings R_Ψ are named by no layer, hence medium confidence. items.name: Euler-factor identities for Stickelberger elements under depletion and smoothing
items.statement: Let Σ ⊇ S_∞ and Σ' be disjoint finite sets of places of F and v a finite prime of F not in Σ ∪ Σ', with I_v ⊂ G_v the inertia and decomposition groups, e_v = N I_v/#I_v and σ_v a Frobenius representative in G_v. Then in ℚ[G]: Θ^#_{Σ∪{v},Σ'} = (1 − σ_v e_v)·Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} and Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'∪{v}} = (1 − σ_v e_v N v)·Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}; character-wise, ψ(Θ^#_{Σ∪{v},Σ'}) = L_{Σ∪{v},Σ'}(ψ,0) = (1 − ψ(v))L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0) (ψ(v) := ψ(σ_v) if ψ is unramified at v, 0 otherwise). Instances used in the range: ψ(Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) = (1 − ψ(v))L_{Σ−{v},Σ'}(ψ,0) for v ∈ Σ (Lemma 3.2); Θ^#_{Σ,T} = Θ^#_{S_∞,T}∏_{v∈S_ram, v|p}(1 − σ_v e_v) and Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} = Θ^#_{Σ,T}∏_{v∈S_ram, v∤p}(1 − σ_v e_v N v) (Remark 3.6, proof of Theorem 3.7); Θ^#_{S,T} = Θ^#_{Σ,T}∏_{v∈S_ram, v∤p}(1 − σ_v e_v) for S = S_∞ ∪ S_ram (proof of Corollary 3.8); (1 − σ_v e_v)Θ^#_{J,T} = Θ^#_{J∪{v},T} (proof of Lemma 3.4).

items.name: Lemma 3.2, second equality: Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} R_Ψ = 0 on trivial-zero components
items.statement: Let Ψ ⊂ Ĝ with 1 ∉ Ψ and suppose that for each ψ ∈ Ψ there exists v ∈ Σ with ψ(G_v) = 1. Then Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} R_Ψ = 0, i.e. the image of Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} in R_Ψ vanishes, because for each ψ ∈ Ψ, ψ(Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) = L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0) = (1 − ψ(v))L_{Σ−{v},Σ'}(ψ,0) = 0.

items.name: J̄, the subfield H^{J̄}, and the map ℤ[Gal(H^{J̄}/F)] → ℤ[G]
items.statement: For S_∞ ⊂ J ⊂ S_∞ ∪ S_ram write J̄ = S_ram ∖ J. H^{J̄} is the maximal subextension of H/F unramified at all primes in J̄, i.e. the subfield of H fixed by the subgroup of G generated by the inertia groups I_v, v ∈ J̄. Multiplication by ∏_{v∈J̄} N I_v defines a homomorphism ℤ[Gal(H^{J̄}/F)] → ℤ[G] (ℤ[G/⟨I_v : v ∈ J̄⟩] → ℤ[G], coset sum ↦ product of the norm elements times a lift).

items.name: Lemma 3.4 (Kurihara, Proposition 3.1): SK^T(H/F) is an ideal of ℤ[G]
items.statement: Let S = S_ram ∪ S_∞ and T a finite set of primes of F unramified in H satisfying condition (1). The Sinnott–Kurihara ideal SK^T(H/F) = (Θ^#_{S_∞,T})∏_{v∈S_ram}(N I_v, 1 − σ_v e_v), a priori a fractional ideal of ℤ[G], is contained in ℤ[G] and hence is an ideal of ℤ[G]. (Proof: by the alternative description (34), SK^T is generated by the elements ∏_{v∈J̄} N I_v·(Θ_{J,T}^{H^{J̄}/F})^#, each of which lies in ℤ[G] by Deligne–Ribet/Cassou-Noguès applied to H^{J̄}/F.)

items.name: Equation (34): generators of the Sinnott–Kurihara ideal from subextensions
items.statement: With S = S_ram ∪ S_∞ and T as in Lemma 3.4: expanding the product, SK^T(H/F) = (∏_{v∈J̄} N I_v·(Θ_{J,T}^{H/F})^# : S_∞ ⊂ J ⊂ S_∞ ∪ S_ram) (using (1 − σ_v e_v)Θ^#_{J,T} = Θ^#_{J∪{v},T}), and by the norm compatibility (33), ∏_{v∈J̄} N I_v·(Θ_{J,T}^{H^{J̄}/F})^# = ∏_{v∈J̄} N I_v·(Θ_{J,T}^{H/F})^# in ℚ[G] (left side via the map ℤ[Gal(H^{J̄}/F)] → ℤ[G]), one has SK^T(H/F) = (∏_{v∈J̄} N I_v·(Θ_{J,T}^{H^{J̄}/F})^# : S_∞ ⊂ J ⊂ S_∞ ∪ S_ram), where each (Θ_{J,T}^{H^{J̄}/F})^# ∈ ℤ[Gal(H^{J̄}/F)]^- by (2).

items.name: Tame inertia at v ∤ p is a quotient of (O_F/v)^* (class field theory)
items.statement: Let v be a finite prime of F ramified in H with v ∤ p, I_v ⊂ G its inertia group and I_{v,p} the p-Sylow subgroup of I_v. By class field theory I_{v,p} is a quotient of (O_F/v)^*; hence I_{v,p} is cyclic, N v ≡ 1 (mod #I_{v,p}), and #I_v divides N v − 1 in ℤ_p.
items.locator: §3.3, Remark 3.6 (the source lines 883–884) and proof of Theorem 3.7 (line 945)
items.note: External input (standard (local class field theory, tame inertia; no citation given)). items.name: Remark 3.6, second part: Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} ∈ SK_p^T(H/F) ⊂ ℤ_p[G]
items.statement: For an odd prime p and Σ, Σ' as in (32): since #I_v divides N v − 1 in ℤ_p for v ∈ S_ram, v ∤ p, one has Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} = Θ^#_{Σ,T}∏_{v∈S_ram, v∤p}(1 − σ_v e_v N v) = Θ^#_{Σ,T}∏_{v∈S_ram, v∤p}[(1 − σ_v e_v) + σ_v·N I_v·(1 − N v)/#I_v] ∈ SK_p^T(H/F) ⊂ ℤ_p[G]. items.name: Theorem 3.7: Fitting ideal of Sel_Σ^T(H)_p^- equals SK_p^T(H/F)^- (partial Kurihara)
items.statement: For every odd prime p, with Σ as in (32) and T a finite set of primes of F unramified in H satisfying condition (1): Fitt_{ℤ_p[G]^-}(Sel_Σ^T(H)_p^-) = SK_p^T(H/F)^-. Proved assuming the keystone Theorem 3.3. Proof (absorbed): reduce to a component R = O[G_p]_χ, χ odd, where (36) Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R) = (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}); put S' = {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p}; (37) 0 → Cl^T(H)^{∨,-} → Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-} → ∏_{w∈S'_H}((O_H/w)^*)^{∨,-} → 0; for v ∈ S' write I_v = I_{v,p} × I_v', τ_v a generator of the cyclic group I_{v,p}, e_{v,p} = N I_{v,p}/#I_{v,p}, e_v' = N I_v'/#I_v'; the base change of (O_H/w)^* to R is 0 unless χ(I_v') = 1; (38) ∏_{w∈S'_H}((O_H/w)^*)^∨_R ≅ ∏_{v∈S', χ(I_v')=1} R/(τ_v − 1, σ_v^{−1} − N v) from ℤ[G_v]/(τ_v − 1, σ_v − N v, τ − 1 : τ ∈ I_v') ≅ (O_H/w)^*, x ↦ u^x; the snake lemma on the two Lemma 3.1 sequences gives (39) 0 → Sel_Σ^T(H)^- → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^- → ∏_{w∈S'_H}((O_H/w)^*)^{∨,-} → 0 and, over R, (40); (41) 0 → R/(N I_{v,p}, σ_v^{−1} − N v) →^{τ_v − 1} R/(σ_v^{−1} − N v) → R/(τ_v − 1, σ_v^{−1} − N v) → 0 is exact (injectivity via R/(τ_v − 1) ≅ O[G_p/I_{v,p}] in which σ_v^{−1} − N v is a non-zerodivisor); Lemma 2.7 gives (42) Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^T(H)_R)∏_{v∈S', χ(I_v')=1}(σ_v^{−1} − N v) = Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R)∏_{v∈S', χ(I_v')=1}(N I_{v,p}, σ_v^{−1} − N v); the σ_v^{−1} − N v are non-zerodivisors, e_v = 0 in Frac(R) if χ(I_v') ≠ 1 and e_v = e_{v,p} if χ(I_v') = 1 (N I_v = #I_v'·N I_{v,p}, #I_v' a p-adic unit), so Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} = Θ^#_{Σ,T}∏_{v∈S', χ(I_v')=1}(1 − σ_v e_v N v) and Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^T(H)_R) = (Θ^#_{Σ,T})∏_{v∈S', χ(I_v')=1}(N I_{v,p}, 1 − σ_v e_{v,p} N v) = (Θ^#_{Σ,T})∏_{v∈S', χ(I_v')=1}(N I_v, 1 − σ_v e_v) (using N v ≡ 1 mod #I_{v,p}) = (Θ^#_{Σ,T})∏_{v∈S'}(N I_v, 1 − σ_v e_v N v) since (N I_v, 1 − σ_v e_v) = (1) in R when χ(I_v') ≠ 1; this is the projection of SK_p^T(H/F) to R.

items.name: Fitting ideal grows under surjections
items.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M ↠ M' a surjection of finitely presented R-modules. Then Fitt_R(M) ⊂ Fitt_R(M'). As used: the surjection Sel_Σ^T(H)^- ↠ Cl^T(H)^{∨,-} of Lemma 3.1 gives Fitt_{ℤ_p[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)_p^{∨,-}) ⊇ Fitt_{ℤ_p[G]^-}(Sel_Σ^T(H)_p^-), and the surjection Cl^T(H)^{∨,-} ↠ A^∨ gives Fitt_{ℤ[G]^-}(Cl^T(H)^{∨,-}) ⊂ Fitt_{ℤ[G]^-}(A^∨).

items.name: Lemma 3.9: Fitt(M/N) annihilates the cokernel of ⋀^r N → ⋀^r M
items.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and N ⊂ M R-modules with N finitely generated and M finitely presented. For each positive integer r, the ideal Fitt_R(M/N) annihilates the cokernel of the canonical map ⋀^r_R N → ⋀^r_R M. Proof (absorbed): choose a surjection R^m ↠ M and a finite presentation R^n → R^m → M/N → 0, lift R^n → N; right exactness of ⋀^r gives a commutative diagram ⋀^r R^n → ⋀^r R^m ↠ C_2 over ⋀^r N → ⋀^r M ↠ C_1 with C_2 ↠ C_1, so it suffices that Fitt(M/N), generated by the maximal minors det(A') of the m×n matrix A of R^n → R^m (n ≥ m), annihilates C_2; for x ∈ ⋀^r R^m and x̃ ∈ ⋀^r R^n obtained by inserting zeros in the coordinates of the columns deleted from C_r(A) to obtain C_r(A'), C_r(A)x̃ = C_r(A')x and adj_r(A')·C_r(A)x̃ = adj_r(A')·C_r(A')x = det(A')x, so det(A')x lies in the image.

items.name: Right exactness of exterior powers
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and each r ≥ 1, the functor ⋀^r_R is right exact: a surjection M' ↠ M of R-modules induces a surjection ⋀^r M' ↠ ⋀^r M, and a commutative square of R-modules with surjective vertical maps induces a surjection between the cokernels of the horizontal maps after applying ⋀^r (as in the diagram of Lemma 3.9).
items.locator: §3.4, proof of Lemma 3.9 (the source line 1044)
items.note: External input (standard (no citation given)). Reduces Lemma 3.9 to free modules. Evidence: Read Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/ExteriorPower/Basic.lean: variables at line 43 `variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) {M N N' : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] ...`, `namespace exteriorPower` at line 47; line 260 `noncomputable def map (f : M →ₗ[R] N) : ⋀[R]^n M →ₗ[R] ⋀[R]^n N`; lines 326-328: docstring "If a linear map is surjective, then the map it induces on exterior powers is surjective." and `lemma map_surjective {f : M →ₗ[R] N} (hf : Surjective f) : Surjective (map n f)`. Hypotheses: any commutative ring R, any R-modules, any n — no extra hypotheses, same convention (⋀[R]^n M as the functorial n-th exterior power). Confirmed the previous verdict. The mathematical content of 'right exactness of ⋀^r' — a surjection M' ↠ M induces a surjection ⋀^r M' ↠ ⋀^r M — is exactly `exteriorPower.map_surjective` in full generality. The item's second clause (a commutative square with surjective vertical maps gives a surjection C_2 ↠ C_1 on the cokernels of the horizontal maps after applying ⋀^r, as in the diagram of Lemma 3.9) is not a separate named Mathlib lemma; it is a two-line diagram chase from `map_surjective` and surjectivity of the quotient map (Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective), which is why confidence is not maximal. PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6 also lists 'exterior powers' in its supply, but that is unnecessary here.

items.name: Compound matrices and the higher adjugate identity
items.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, A an m×n matrix over R and r ≥ 1. The r-th compound matrix C_r(A) is the C(m,r)×C(n,r) matrix of r×r minors of A; it represents ⋀^r A: ⋀^r R^n → ⋀^r R^m in the standard bases. For a square m×m matrix A' there is an r-th higher adjugate matrix adj_r(A') with adj_r(A')·C_r(A') = det(A')·Id. If A' is an m×m submatrix of A then C_r(A') is the submatrix of C_r(A) obtained by deleting the C(n,r) − C(m,r) columns indexed by r-subsets not contained in the chosen columns.

items.name: The smoothing set Σ'' = Σ' minus the p-adic primes of T
items.statement: With Σ' = {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p} ∪ T as in (32), define Σ'' = Σ' ∖ {v ∈ T : v | p}; equivalently Σ'' = {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p} ∪ {v ∈ T : v ∤ p}. The primes of T above p are unramified in H (T is disjoint from S_ram by definition), Σ'' ⊂ Σ', and Σ'' is still disjoint from Σ.

items.name: Lemma 4.1, first assertion: Selmer R-component unchanged by removing p-adic primes from T
items.statement: Let Σ, Σ' be as in (32), let χ be a character of G' and R = R_χ, and let Σ'' = Σ' ∖ {v ∈ T : v | p}. Then Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R ≅ Sel_Σ^{Σ''}(H)_R; the isomorphism is the R-component of the natural map Sel_Σ^{Σ''}(H) → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) induced by restriction of functionals along H^*_{Σ'} ⊂ H^*_{Σ''}. (Proof, as in (40): there is a short exact sequence of R-modules 0 → Sel_Σ^{Σ''}(H)_R → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R → [∏_{v ∈ T, v | p} ∏_{w | v} (𝒪_H/w)^*]^∨_R → 0, and the bracketed finite group has prime-to-p order ∏_w (Nw − 1), so its tensor product with the ℤ_p-algebra R vanishes.)

items.name: Lemma 4.1, second assertion: Stickelberger ideal in R unchanged by removing p-adic primes from T
items.statement: With Σ, Σ', Σ'', χ, R as in the first assertion of Lemma 4.1, the principal ideals of R generated by the images of Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} and Θ^#_{Σ,Σ''} coincide: (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) = (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ''}) in R. (Proof: Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} = Θ^#_{Σ,Σ''} · ∏_{v ∈ T, v | p} (1 − σ_v N v), where σ_v ∈ G is the Frobenius of the unramified prime v, because L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0) = L_{Σ,Σ''}(ψ,0) ∏_{v ∈ Σ'∖Σ''} (1 − ψ(v) N v) and ψ(Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) = L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0); and for v | p the image of 1 − σ_v N v in the local ring R is a unit, since N v is a power of p and p lies in the maximal ideal of R.)

There are no Hecke or equivariant L-functions of number-field extensions." IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7: "the Fitting-ideal comparison, and the passage from modified to unmodified data". items.name: The field H_χ cut out by χ
items.statement: For a character χ of G' ⊂ G = Gal(H/F), H_χ ⊂ H denotes the subfield of H fixed by ker(χ) ⊂ G'. Then [H : H_χ] = #ker(χ) is prime to p, Gal(H_χ/F) = G/ker(χ) ≅ G_p × G'/ker(χ), and χ induces a faithful character of G'/ker(χ), the maximal prime-to-p subgroup of Gal(H_χ/F); the local component of 𝒪[Gal(H_χ/F)] attached to this character is again R = R_χ = 𝒪[G_p]_χ, so M_R makes sense for ℤ[Gal(H_χ/F)]-modules M (compatibly with pullback along G ↠ Gal(H_χ/F)). H_χ/F is abelian, and CM when χ is odd (complex conjugation lies outside ker χ).

items.name: Lemma 4.2 (descent of the Selmer R-component to H_χ)
items.statement: Let χ be a character of G' and R = R_χ. Let H_χ ⊂ H be the subfield of H fixed by the kernel of χ inside G'. Let Σ ⊃ S_∞ and Σ' be finite disjoint sets of places of F whose union contains the set S_ram of finite primes ramified in H/F. Then there is a canonical isomorphism of R-modules Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R ≅ Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_χ)_R, namely the R-component of the map Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_χ) induced by the inclusion H_χ ⊂ H (restriction of ℤ-linear functionals from H^*_{Σ'} to H_{χ,Σ'}^*). (Proof: choose S' ⊇ Σ disjoint from Σ' with Cl_{S'}^{Σ'}(H) trivial and use the presentation (31) for both fields; since 𝒪^*_{H,S',Σ'} ⊗ 𝒪 is a free 𝒪-module of finite rank, (Hom_ℤ(𝒪^*_{H,S',Σ'}, ℤ) ⊗_ℤ 𝒪)_R = Hom_𝒪(𝒪^*_{H,S',Σ'} ⊗ 𝒪, 𝒪)_R = Hom_𝒪((𝒪^*_{H,S',Σ'} ⊗ 𝒪)^{G'=χ}, 𝒪), where N^{G'=χ} is the sub-𝒪-module on which g ∈ G' acts by χ(g); this gives the commutative diagram (50) with right-exact rows (Y_{H,S'−Σ})_R → Hom_𝒪((𝒪^*_{H,S',Σ'} ⊗ 𝒪)^{G'=χ}, 𝒪) → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R → 0 and (Y_{H_χ,S'−Σ})_R → Hom_𝒪((𝒪^*_{H_χ,S',Σ'} ⊗ 𝒪)^{G'=χ}, 𝒪) → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_χ)_R → 0; the middle vertical arrow is an isomorphism by Galois theory (ker χ acts trivially on the χ-eigenspace and the ker χ-invariants of 𝒪^*_{H,S',Σ'} ⊗ 𝒪 are 𝒪^*_{H_χ,S',Σ'} ⊗ 𝒪), hence the right vertical arrow is surjective; the left vertical arrow is surjective because the primes in S' − Σ lie outside Σ ∪ Σ' ⊇ S_ram and so are unramified in H_χ (and in H), hence the right vertical arrow is injective.)

items.name: Images of Θ^{H/F}_{Σ,Σ'} and Θ^{H_χ/F}_{Σ,Σ'} in R agree
items.statement: Let χ be a character of G', R = R_χ, H_χ the fixed field of ker χ, and Σ, Σ' finite disjoint sets of places of F with Σ ⊃ S_∞ (e.g. the sets (32)). The images in R of the Stickelberger elements Θ^{H/F}_{Σ,Σ'} ∈ ℚ[G] and Θ^{H_χ/F}_{Σ,Σ'} ∈ ℚ[Gal(H_χ/F)] are equal (R is a component of both 𝒪[G] and 𝒪[Gal(H_χ/F)], compatibly with G ↠ Gal(H_χ/F)); consequently the same holds for Θ^# and the ideals (Θ^{H/F,#}_{Σ,Σ'}) = (Θ^{H_χ/F,#}_{Σ,Σ'}) of R coincide. This is clear from the definitions: every ψ ∈ Ĝ belonging to χ is trivial on ker χ, so factors through Gal(H_χ/F), and ψ(Θ^{H/F}_{Σ,Σ'}) = L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ^{-1},0) = ψ(Θ^{H_χ/F}_{Σ,Σ'}) since both sides are the same (primitive) Hecke L-value; R is reduced, so agreement at all ψ belonging to χ gives equality in R.

items.name: The sets Σ(χ) and Σ'(χ) attached to H_χ
items.statement: Standing convention (from §4.1, after Lemma 4.1): Σ' is replaced by Σ'' and hereafter T, and hence Σ' = {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p} ∪ T, contain no primes above p. Define Σ(χ) = {v | p : v is ramified in H_χ} ∪ S_∞ and Σ'(χ) = {v ∤ p : v is ramified in H_χ} ∪ T. Since a prime ramified in H_χ is ramified in H and T ∩ S_ram = ∅, one has Σ(χ) ⊂ Σ and Σ'(χ) ⊂ Σ', with Σ − Σ(χ) = {v | p : v ramified in H but unramified in H_χ} and Σ' − Σ'(χ) = {v ∤ p : v ramified in H but unramified in H_χ}; Σ(χ) ∩ Σ'(χ) = ∅, and Σ(χ), Σ'(χ) are exactly the sets of recipe (32) for the extension H_χ/F and the same set T.

items.name: Equation (51): Euler-factor relation between Θ_{Σ,Σ'} and Θ_{Σ(χ),Σ'(χ)} for H_χ/F
items.statement: With Σ, Σ' the sets (32) for H/F (T containing no primes above p) and Σ(χ), Σ'(χ) as defined for H_χ, one has in ℚ[Gal(H_χ/F)]: Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(H_χ/F)^# = Θ_{Σ(χ),Σ'(χ)}(H_χ/F)^# · ∏_{v ∈ Σ − Σ(χ)} (1 − σ_v) · ∏_{v ∈ Σ' − Σ'(χ)} (1 − σ_v N v), where σ_v ∈ Gal(H_χ/F) is the Frobenius at v (well defined since every such v is unramified in H_χ). (It follows from L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0) = L_{Σ(χ),Σ'(χ)}(ψ,0) ∏_{v ∈ Σ−Σ(χ)} (1 − ψ(v)) ∏_{v ∈ Σ'−Σ'(χ)} (1 − ψ(v) N v) and ψ(Θ^#) = L(ψ,0) for all ψ ∈ Gal(H_χ/F)^.)

items.name: Lemma 4.3 (adding unramified primes to the depletion and smoothing sets)
items.statement: Let χ be a character of G', R = R_χ, H_χ the fixed field of ker χ, Σ, Σ' the sets (32) for H/F with T containing no primes above p, and Σ(χ), Σ'(χ) the sets attached to H_χ. Suppose that the R-module Sel_{Σ(χ)}^{Σ'(χ)}(H_χ)_R is quadratically presented. Then Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_χ)_R is quadratically presented over R as well, and Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_χ)_R) = Fitt_R(Sel_{Σ(χ)}^{Σ'(χ)}(H_χ)_R) · ∏_{v ∈ Σ − Σ(χ)} (1 − σ_v) · ∏_{v ∈ Σ' − Σ'(χ)} (1 − σ_v N v), σ_v ∈ Gal(H_χ/F) the Frobenius at v. (Both conclusions are proved simultaneously. Proof: expand the smoothing set first, then the depletion set, using Lemma 3.1 for H_χ base-changed to R in both steps. Diagram (52): rows (Y_{H_χ,Σ(χ)})_R ↪ Sel_{Σ(χ)}^{Σ'(χ)}(H_χ)_R ↠ Cl^{Σ'(χ)}(H_χ)^∨_R and (Y_{H_χ,Σ(χ)})_R ↪ Sel_{Σ(χ)}^{Σ'}(H_χ)_R ↠ Cl^{Σ'}(H_χ)^∨_R, left vertical arrow the identity; the right vertical arrow is injective with cokernel (53) = ∏_{v ∈ Σ'−Σ'(χ)} ∏_{w | v} ((𝒪_{H_χ}/w)^*)^∨_R, which, the primes of Σ' − Σ'(χ) being unramified in H_χ, is quadratically presented over R with Fitting ideal (∏_{v ∈ Σ'−Σ'(χ)} (1 − σ_v N v)) (as in (38): ∏_{w|v}(𝒪_{H_χ}/w)^* ≅ ℤ[Gal(H_χ/F)]/(σ_v − N v), whose dual R-component is R/(σ_v^{-1} − N v) = R/(1 − σ_v N v)); the snake lemma gives 0 → Sel_{Σ(χ)}^{Σ'(χ)}(H_χ)_R → Sel_{Σ(χ)}^{Σ'}(H_χ)_R → (53) → 0 and Lemma 2.6 gives Sel_{Σ(χ)}^{Σ'}(H_χ)_R quadratically presented with Fitting ideal Fitt_R(Sel_{Σ(χ)}^{Σ'(χ)}(H_χ)_R) ∏_{v ∈ Σ'−Σ'(χ)} (1 − σ_v N v). Diagram (54): rows (Y_{H_χ,Σ})_R ↪ Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_χ)_R ↠ Cl^{Σ'}(H_χ)^∨_R and (Y_{H_χ,Σ(χ)})_R ↪ Sel_{Σ(χ)}^{Σ'}(H_χ)_R ↠ Cl^{Σ'}(H_χ)^∨_R, right vertical arrow the identity, left vertical arrow the projection for the canonical decomposition Y_{H_χ,Σ} = Y_{H_χ,Σ(χ)} ⊕ Y_{H_χ,Σ−Σ(χ)}; the left and middle vertical arrows are surjective with kernel (Y_{H_χ,Σ−Σ(χ)})_R = ⊕_{v ∈ Σ−Σ(χ)} R/(1 − σ_v) (v unramified in H_χ, so Y_{H_χ,{v}} ≅ ℤ[Gal(H_χ/F)]/(σ_v − 1)), which is quadratically presented over R with Fitting ideal (∏_{v ∈ Σ−Σ(χ)} (1 − σ_v)); Lemma 2.6 applied to 0 → (Y_{H_χ,Σ−Σ(χ)})_R → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_χ)_R → Sel_{Σ(χ)}^{Σ'}(H_χ)_R → 0 gives the result.)

items.name: Σ, Σ_p, Σ' for the component R = O[G_p]_χ
items.statement: Setting: F totally real, H/F finite abelian CM, G = Gal(H/F) = G_p × G' (G_p the p-Sylow subgroup, G' of prime-to-p order), p an odd prime, O a finite extension of Z_p containing the values of all characters of G, R = O[G_p]_χ the connected component of O[G] attached to an odd character χ of G', H_p the fixed field of G' in H (so Gal(H_p/F) ≅ G_p, Gal(H/H_p) ≅ G'). By the reductions of §4, χ is assumed FAITHFUL on G', and T satisfies the Deligne–Ribet condition (1). With S_ram the set of finite primes of F ramified in H and G_v ⊂ G the decomposition group at v, G_v' = G' ∩ G_v, define Σ = {v ∈ S_ram : v | p} ∪ S_∞ (57, e:bigsigmadef); Σ_p = {v ∈ S_ram : v | p and χ(G_v') = 1} ⊂ Σ (58, e:sigmasub); Σ' = {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p} ∪ T (59, e:sigmapdef). Since χ is faithful, χ(G_v') = 1 ⟺ G_v' = 1 ⟺ G_v is a p-group.

items.name: Theorem 5.1 (t:include): divisibility implies equality
items.statement: Suppose that in EVERY situation with notation as above (every totally real F, every finite abelian CM extension H/F, every odd prime p, every faithful odd character χ of G', T satisfying the Deligne–Ribet condition, Σ and Σ' as in (57), (59), R = O[G_p]_χ), the R-module Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R = Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) ⊗_{Z[G]} R is quadratically presented over R and (60, e:include) Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R) ⊂ (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) holds. Then each such inclusion is an equality: Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R) = (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}). (The proof uses the hypothesis for the extensions H/H_p, H_α/H_p, H_ψ/F and H_ψ^I/F, so a single inclusion is not shown to be an equality on its own.) Proof structure (absorbed): the hypotheses give x ∈ R with Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R) = (x·Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) (principal Fitting ideal of a quadratically presented module), and one shows x ∈ R^*. Case Σ_p = ∅: Θ_{Σ,Σ'} is a non-zerodivisor in R; by (62) Fitt_R(Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨_R) = (x·Θ^#), so Lemmas 2.4, 2.5 give (65, e:clxl) #Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨_R = #O/∏_{ψ|_{G'}=χ} ψ(x)·L_{Σ,Σ'}(H/F,ψ,0); by (66) and the unit Euler factors, comparison with Lemma 5.3 gives ∏_ψ ψ(x) ∈ O^*, so each ψ(x) ∈ O^* and x ∈ R^*. Case Σ_p ≠ ∅: for each ψ belonging to χ, base change gives (67, e:fitpsi) Fitt_O(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_ψ) = (ψ(x)·L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0)) ⊂ (L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0)); if equality holds for one ψ with L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0) ≠ 0 then ψ(x) ∈ O^* and x ∈ R^*; if every ψ belonging to χ has a trivial zero, Lemma 3.2 gives Fitt_R(Sel_R) = 0 = (Θ^#); so it suffices to prove (68, e:fitpsieq) Fitt_O(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_ψ) = (L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0)) for every ψ belonging to χ, which follows by projecting the equality of Lemma 5.7 (for H_ψ, with Σ, Σ' replaced by Σ(H_ψ), Σ'(H_ψ) via Lemma 5.4, (51) and Lemma 4.3) from R_I to O_ψ.

items.name: R-component of Y_{H,{v}} vanishes when χ(G_v') ≠ 1
items.statement: Let Y_{H,S} denote the free abelian group on the places of H above a set S of places of F with its G-action. If v is a place of F with χ(G_v') ≠ 1 (where G_v' = G' ∩ G_v), then (Y_{H,{v}})_R = Y_{H,{v}} ⊗_{Z[G]} R = 0: choosing σ ∈ G_v' with χ(σ) ≠ 1, 1 − σ acts trivially on the places above v while its image in R = O[G_p]_χ is a unit. Consequently (Y_{H,Σ})_R ≅ (Y_{H,Σ_p})_R.
items.locator: §5, sentence after equation (61) (the source line 1311); the same argument is repeated in the proof of Lemma 5.5 (lines 1449–1450)
items.note: Shows only the primes of Σ_p contribute to the Y-term of the R-component of the exact sequence (61) of Lemma 3.1; gives (62) and the first reduction in Lemma 5.5. Evidence: Paper: the source line 1311: "(Y_{H,Σ})_R ≅ (Y_{H,Σ_p})_R since (Y_{H,{v}})_R = 0 when χ(G'_v) ≠ 1". The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... the Fitting-ideal comparison"; IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (line 37): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups" (Y_{H,S} is the places module entering the Ritter–Weiss/BKS sequence (61)). Library: TauCeti primesAbove (RingTheory/DedekindDomain/PrimesAbove.lean:78) is a set of primes; the only FreeAbelianGroup use in TauCeti is contour cycles (Analysis/Contour/Cycle/Basic.lean:183); no free Z[G]-module on places nor its tensor with a group-ring component in either tree; the atlas search for 'places module'/'free abelian group on places' returns no number-theoretic stage. items.name: Equation (62): Selmer module equals class group dual on R when Σ_p = ∅
items.statement: If Σ_p = ∅, then Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R ≅ (Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨)_R, where the isomorphism is induced by the surjection Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^- → Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-} of the exact sequence (61) of Lemma 3.1 (0 → Y_{H,Σ}^- → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^- → Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-} → 0), whose kernel term has vanishing R-component.
items.locator: §5, equation (62), label e:selcl (the source lines 1312–1314)
items.note: Converts the Fitting ideal of the Selmer module into that of the class group dual in Lemma 5.3 (for H/H_p) and in the case Σ_p = ∅ of Theorem 5.1. Evidence: Paper: the source lines 1305-1314 (sequence (61) and equation (62)). IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract line 48): "the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... Dasgupta–Kakde ... the Fitting-ideal comparison"; IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (line 37): "Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups"; I.6 AUDIT TARGET "Ray-class modules ... | library: absent | Tau Ceti has ray class groups as groups, but not their Galois-module structure or minus parts." items.name: Lemma 5.2 (l:alpha): descent of the α-component of the class group dual to H_α
items.statement: Let α be any character of G', O_α and H_α as above. Then Cl^{Σ'}(H_α)^∨_{O_α} ≅ Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨_{O_α}. Proof (absorbed): since [H:H_α] is prime to p, the maps 𝔞 ↦ 𝔞·O_H (extension of ideals) and 𝔞 ↦ (1/[H:H_α])·N_{H/H_α}(𝔞) are explicit mutually inverse isomorphisms between Cl^{Σ'}(H_α)_{O_α} and Cl^{Σ'}(H)_{O_α}; the isomorphism of the lemma is the Pontryagin dual of this with α replaced by α^{-1}.
items.locator: §5, Lemma 5.2, label l:alpha (the source lines 1317–1330)
items.note: Lets the divisibility hypothesis (60) applied to the field H_α (where α is faithful) be transported to the α-component of Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨, giving (63). Evidence: Paper: the source lines 1317-1330 (Lemma 5.2 and proof). IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract line 48): "the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... the Fitting-ideal comparison"; IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (line 37): "the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality". items.name: Lemma 5.3 (l:gptriv), first equality: size of (Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨)_R
items.statement: Assume the running hypothesis of Theorem 5.1 (inclusion (60) in every situation; in particular for H/H_p and for H_α/H_p for every odd character α of Gal(H/H_p)). Then #(Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨)_R = #O/(L), where L = L_{S_∞,Σ'}(H/H_p, χ, 0) is the S_∞-depleted, Σ'-smoothed L-value at 0 of χ regarded as a character of Gal(H/H_p) ≅ G'. Proof (absorbed): H_p is totally real (odd degree over F); for H/H_p one has G_v = G_v', so by faithfulness of χ the set Σ_p attached to H/H_p is empty and the component ring is O_χ; hence (60) and (62) give Fitt_{O_χ}(Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨_{O_χ}) ⊂ (L_{S_∞,Σ'}(H/H_p,χ,0)), i.e. #O/L_{S_∞,Σ'}(H/H_p,χ,0) divides #Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨_{O_χ}. Applying this to H_α/H_p for every odd α of Gal(H/H_p) and using Lemma 5.2 gives (63, e:alpha): #O/L_{S_∞,Σ'}(H/H_p,α,0) | #Cl^{Σ'}(H_α)^∨_{O_α} = #Cl^{Σ'}(H)^∨_{O_α}. The product over all odd α gives (64, e:divprod): #O/L_{S_∞,Σ'}(H/H^+,ε,0) | #Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-}_O, H^+ the maximal totally real subfield, ε the nontrivial character of Gal(H/H^+) (left side by Artin formalism, right side because O[Gal(H/H_p)]^- = ∏_{α odd} O_α). By the analytic class number formula (Lemma 2.1) (64) is an equality, hence each (63) is an equality; α = χ gives the claim.
items.locator: §5, Lemma 5.3, label l:gptriv, equations (63), (64), labels e:alpha, e:divprod (the source lines 1336–1363)

items.name: Euler factor 1 − ψ(v) is a p-adic unit when χ(G_v') ≠ 1
items.statement: Let π_E ∈ O be a uniformizer, ψ a character of G belonging to χ, and v a finite prime of F with χ(G_v') ≠ 1 (equivalently v ∉ Σ_p when v ∈ Σ − S_∞). Then ψ(v) = 0 if ψ is ramified at v, and ψ(v) ≡ χ(v) ≢ 1 (mod π_E) if ψ is unramified at v; in both cases 1 − ψ(v) ∈ O^*. In particular, if Σ_p = ∅ then ∏_{v ∈ Σ − S_∞}(1 − ψ(v)) ∈ O^* for every ψ belonging to χ, so L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0) and L_{S_∞,Σ'}(ψ,0) generate the same ideal of O.
items.locator: §5.1 (the source lines 1381–1387); the same fact is used for v ∈ Σ − Σ_p in the proof of Lemma 5.6 (lines 1507–1509)
items.note: Removes the Euler factors so that (65) and Lemma 5.3 can be compared directly, and so that L_I in Lemma 5.6 can be rewritten with S_∞-depleted L-values. items.name: Units of R (or of a character group ring quotient) are detected by characters
items.statement: Let R = O[G_p]_χ, or a character group ring quotient R_Ψ of it with Ψ ≠ ∅ (e.g. R_I = R/N I). R is a local ring and the O-algebra maps R → O induced by each character ψ ∈ Ψ are local homomorphisms of local rings; hence x ∈ R is a unit as soon as ψ(x) ∈ O^* for one (equivalently every) ψ ∈ Ψ. Moreover ∏_{ψ ∈ Ψ} ψ(x) ∈ O^* implies ψ(x) ∈ O^* for each ψ.
items.locator: §5.1 (the source line 1390); reused in §5.2 (line 1409) and in the proof of Lemma 5.7 (line 1568)
items.note: Final step of each case of Theorem 5.1 and of Lemma 5.7: a unit product of L-value ratios gives a unit x. items.name: Trivial zero of a character ψ
items.statement: A character ψ of G (belonging to χ) has a trivial zero if there exists v ∈ Σ with ψ(G_v) = 1; then the Euler factor 1 − ψ(v) vanishes and L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ, 0) = 0, equivalently ψ(Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) = 0.
items.locator: §5 preamble (the source line 1275) and §5.2 (line 1411)
items.note: Determines whether the component ψ carries information: if every ψ belonging to χ has a trivial zero, both sides of (60) vanish (Lemma 3.2); otherwise a ψ with L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0) ≠ 0 detects that x is a unit. Evidence: rg 'trivial zero|trivialZero' over Mathlib/ and TauCeti/: nothing about Artin/Hecke L-functions. Atlas stage search for 'trivial zero' hits only AnalyticNumberTheory:AN.1/AN.3 (trivial zeros of ζ and Dirichlet L-functions at negative integers) and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/QuadraticFormInvariants layer 6/6c (nontrivial zero of a conic), none the Gross-type notion ψ(G_v)=1 for v ∈ Σ killing L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0) (the source line 1411). items.name: Lemma 5.4 (l:descend): descent of ψ-coinvariants of the Selmer module to H_ψ
items.statement: Let ψ be a character of G and H_ψ ⊂ H the subfield of H fixed by the kernel of ψ, with Σ ⊃ S_∞ and Σ' finite disjoint sets of places of F whose union contains S_ram (as in Lemma 4.2). There is a canonical isomorphism Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_ψ ≅ Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_ψ, induced by the inclusion H_ψ ⊂ H. The proof is that of Lemma 4.2 (l:descendchi) with (H_χ, R) replaced by (H_ψ, O_ψ); details omitted in the source.
items.locator: §5.2, Lemma 5.4, label l:descend (the source lines 1423–1430)
items.note: Allows H to be replaced by the cyclic extension H_ψ/F in the proof of (68). items.name: Minimal inertia group I, e = #I, N I and R_I (normalised setting for Lemmas 5.5–5.7)
items.statement: Standing normalisation (absorbed): ψ is a character of G belonging to χ; by Lemma 5.4 one takes H = H_ψ (so H_ψ/F is cyclic), and by (51) (e:thetachi) and Lemma 4.3 one replaces Σ, Σ' by Σ(H_ψ) = {v | p : v ramified in H_ψ} ∪ S_∞ and Σ'(H_ψ) = {v ∤ p : v ramified in H_ψ} ∪ T (the extra Euler factors ∏(1 − σ_v)∏(1 − σ_v N v) multiply both the Fitting ideal and Θ^# equally), so that ψ is ramified at every prime of Σ_p; Σ_p ≠ ∅ is assumed (the case Σ_p = ∅ being §5.1). Each v ∈ Σ_p satisfies ψ(G_v') = χ(G_v') = 1, so its decomposition group in Gal(H_ψ/F) is a p-group; the subgroups of the cyclic p-group being linearly ordered by inclusion, there is v ∈ Σ_p whose inertia group I_v satisfies I_v ⊂ I_w for all w ∈ Σ_p. Definition: I = this minimal I_v; I ≠ 1 since ψ is ramified at all v ∈ Σ_p and Σ_p ≠ ∅; e = #I; N I = Σ_{σ ∈ I} σ ∈ O[G] (the norm element of Lemma 2.2); R_I = R/N I, which by Corollary 2.3 is the character group ring R_Ψ with Ψ = {α : α|_{G'} = χ, α(I) ≠ 1}.
items.locator: §5.2 (the source lines 1432–1435); e = #I line 1468; R_I in Lemma 5.7 line 1558
items.note: The quotient by N I kills exactly the characters trivial on I; H_ψ/H_ψ^I is totally ramified at every prime of Σ_p, which drives Lemmas 5.5 and 5.6. Evidence: New library check: tauceti:TauCeti.subgroupCharSum (TauCeti/Algebra/MonoidAlgebra/SubgroupCharSum.lean:49, `noncomputable def subgroupCharSum : MonoidAlgebra k G := ∑ h : H, χ (h : G) • MonoidAlgebra.of k G (h : G)`, docstring lines 18-19: with χ = 1 it is 'the norm element ∑_{h ∈ H} h of a subgroup') provides the norm element N I ∈ O[G] of a finite subgroup, but nothing else of the item: no quotient R/N I, no identification with the character group ring R_Ψ (rg 'characterGroupRing|character group ring' in Tau Ceti: none), no minimal-inertia-group choice (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Inertia.lean has inertia groups of one prime only; Mathlib/GroupTheory/SpecificGroups/ZGroup.lean:53 gives cyclicity of p-subgroups of Z-groups, and no 'subgroups of a cyclic p-group are totally ordered' lemma exists: rg 'le_or_le|le_total' with Subgroup in Mathlib/GroupTheory: none). Atlas: 'norm element', 'character group ring', 'linearly ordered' return no stage; 'cyclic p-group' hits only PerfectoidSpaces:P8. Confirmed missing, with a corrected nearest-library pointer: tauceti:TauCeti.subgroupCharSum (χ = 1) is the norm element N I, a single component of this normalisation bundle (minimal inertia group I among Σ_p, e = #I, N I, R_I = R/N I ≅ R_Ψ, replacement of Σ, Σ' by Σ(H_ψ), Σ'(H_ψ)); the bundle as a whole is in neither tree and no layer (I.6/I.7 or the ClassFieldTheory/NumberFieldArithmetic roadmaps, which cover inertia groups generally) names it.

items.name: Lemma 5.5 (l:selcl): Selmer module and class group dual agree modulo N I
items.statement: With H = H_ψ, Σ = Σ(H_ψ), Σ' = Σ'(H_ψ), Σ_p ≠ ∅ and I the minimal inertia group as above: Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_R / N I ≅ (Cl^{Σ'}(H_ψ)^∨)_R / N I. Proof (absorbed): (i) from 0 → Y_{H_ψ,Σ−Σ_p} → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_ψ) → Sel_{Σ_p}^{Σ'}(H_ψ) → 0 and (Y_{H_ψ,Σ−Σ_p})_R = 0 (for w above v ∈ Σ − Σ_p pick σ ∈ G_v' with χ(σ) ≠ 1: 1 − σ fixes the image of w and is a unit in R), Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_R ≅ Sel_{Σ_p}^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_R, so one may take Σ = Σ_p. (ii) Tensoring (61) with R/N I over R, it suffices that (Y_{H_ψ,Σ_p})_R/N I → Sel_{Σ_p}^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_R/N I vanishes; one proves (69, e:xs) that already Y^-_{H_ψ,Σ_p}/N I → Sel_{Σ_p}^{Σ'}(H_ψ)^-/N I vanishes on the full minus side over Z[1/2]. (iii) Let M = Cl^{Σ'}(H_ψ)^-/N I = I_{Σ'}(H_ψ)^-/⟨H^{*,-}_{ψ,Σ'}, N I·I_{Σ'}(H_ψ)^-⟩. The primes 𝔓 ∈ (Σ_p)_{H_ψ} come in pairs (𝔓, 𝔓̄) exchanged by complex conjugation with 𝔓 ≠ 𝔓̄ (χ(G_v') = 1 while χ is odd); J is a set of representatives. Claim: if ∏_{𝔓∈J}(𝔓/𝔓̄)^{a_𝔓} is trivial in M then e | a_𝔓 for all 𝔓: write it as (x)·𝔞^{N I} (70, e:fP) with x ∈ H^{*,-}_{ψ,Σ'}, 𝔞 ∈ I_{Σ'}(H_ψ)^-; all terms but (x) are I-invariant so (x) is; the generator in H^{*,-}_{ψ,Σ'} of a principal ideal on the minus side is unique, so x ∈ (H_ψ^I)^*_{Σ'}; the 𝔓 are totally ramified over H_ψ^I, so ord_𝔓(x) ∈ eZ and e | a_𝔓. (iv) Fix 𝔓 ∈ J; by the claim there is φ̃: M → Q/Z[1/2] with φ̃(𝔓 − 𝔓̄) = 1/e and φ̃(𝔓' − 𝔓̄') = 0 for 𝔓' ∈ J, 𝔓' ≠ 𝔓; since I_{Σ'}(H_ψ)^- is a free Z[1/2]-module, φ̃ lifts to a Z[1/2]-homomorphism φ: I_{Σ'}(H_ψ)^- → Q with φ(𝔓 − 𝔓̄) = 1/e, φ(𝔓' − 𝔓̄') = 0; φ is Z[1/2]-valued on H^{*,-}_{ψ,Σ'}, hence Φ = Σ_{w ∉ Σ'_{H_ψ}} φ(w) ord_w = (1/e)(ord_𝔓 − ord_𝔓̄) + Σ_{w ∉ (Σ_p ∪ Σ')_{H_ψ}} φ(w) ord_w is a class in Sel_{Σ_p}^{Σ'}(H_ψ)^-. (v) (71, e:nip): N I·Φ = (ord_𝔓 − ord_𝔓̄) + Σ_{w ∉ (Σ_p ∪ Σ')_{H_ψ}} φ(N I·w) ord_w; since φ∘N I is Z[1/2]-valued by definition of M, the last sum is trivial in Sel_{Σ_p}^{Σ'}(H_ψ)^- by definition of the Selmer module, so ord_𝔓 − ord_𝔓̄ = N I·Φ, proving (69).

items.name: Lemma 5.6 (l:clsize): size of the class group dual modulo N I
items.statement: With H = H_ψ, Σ = Σ(H_ψ), Σ' = Σ'(H_ψ), Σ_p ≠ ∅ and I the minimal inertia group, under the running hypothesis of Theorem 5.1 (used through Lemma 5.3 for H_ψ/F and H_ψ^I/F): #((Cl^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_R)^∨ / N I) = #O/L_I, where L_I = ∏_{α(I) ≠ 1, α|_{G'} = χ} L_{Σ,Σ'}(H_ψ/F, α, 0), the product over the characters α of Gal(H_ψ/F) belonging to χ with α(I) ≠ 1. Proof (absorbed): each such α is ramified at every v ∈ Σ_p (I ⊂ I_v) and 1 − α(v) is a p-adic unit for finite v ∈ Σ − Σ_p, so L_{Σ,Σ'}(H_ψ/F,α,0) = L_{S_∞,Σ'}(H_ψ/F,α,0) (as ideals of O). Write M = Cl^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_R; by Lemma 5.3, #M^∨ = #O/L with L = ∏_{α|_{G'}=χ} L_{S_∞,Σ'}(H_ψ/F,α,0); so it suffices to show (72, e:nimv) #(N I·M^∨) = #O/L_I', where L_I' = ∏_{α(I)=1, α|_{G'}=χ} L_{S_∞,Σ'}(H_ψ/F,α,0) = ∏_{α ∈ Gal(H_ψ^I/F)^∧, α|_{G'}=χ} L_{S_∞,Σ'}(H_ψ^I/F,α,0) (73–76, e:lip). Since M is finite, the exact sequence 0 → M^∨[N I] → M^∨ →(N I) M^∨ → M^∨/N I → 0 gives #M^∨/N I = #M^∨[N I] = #(M/N I)^∨ = #(M/N I), so #(N I·M^∨) = #(N I·M) and (72) is equivalent to (77, e:nim) #(N I·M) = #O/L_I'. Let N = Cl^{Σ'}(H_ψ^I)_R; Lemma 5.3 for H_ψ^I/F and (76) give (78, e:nin) #N = #O/L_I'. It remains to show the canonical map N → M^I, 𝔞 ↦ 𝔞·O_{H_ψ}, is injective with image N I·M. Injectivity: snake lemma on the diagram with exact rows 0 → (H^{I,*}_{ψ,Σ'})_R → I_{Σ'}(H_ψ^I)_R → N → 0 and 0 → ((H^*_{ψ,Σ'})^I)_R → (I_{Σ'}(H_ψ)^I)_R → M^I → 0 (the final 0 of the bottom row comes from Hilbert's Theorem 90 but is not needed); the left vertical arrow is an isomorphism by Galois theory and the middle one is an injection. Surjectivity of the norm M → N: by class field theory M and N are Galois groups of extensions of H_ψ and H_ψ^I unramified outside Σ', the norm is restriction of Galois groups, and restriction is surjective because H_ψ/H_ψ^I is totally ramified at the primes in Σ_p by the choice of I. Since extension∘norm = N I, the image of N in M is N I·M, giving (77).

items.name: Class field theory for Σ'-ray class groups: norm = restriction, surjective under total ramification (external)
items.statement: Statement as used: for a number field K and a finite set Σ' of finite primes of F, the Σ'-smoothed class group Cl^{Σ'}(K) (and its R-component) is, via the Artin map, the Galois group of an abelian extension of K unramified outside Σ' (the ray class field of conductor supported on Σ'_K). For an extension L/K of such fields, the norm map Cl^{Σ'}(L) → Cl^{Σ'}(K) is identified with the restriction map between these Galois groups. If L/K (here H_ψ/H_ψ^I, a cyclic p-extension) is totally ramified at primes outside Σ' (here the primes of Σ_p), then L is linearly disjoint from the ray class field of K, so restriction, hence the norm map on Σ'-class groups, is surjective.

The Galois/class-group isomorphisms (`gal_rayClassField_equiv_rayClassGroup`, ...) ... items.name: Lemma 5.7 (l:ri): Fitting ideal equals Stickelberger ideal over R_I = R/N I
items.statement: Let R_I = R/N I. With H = H_ψ, Σ = Σ(H_ψ), Σ' = Σ'(H_ψ), Σ_p ≠ ∅, I the minimal inertia group, and under the running hypothesis of Theorem 5.1 (Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_R quadratically presented with (60) for H_ψ/F, and (60) in the situations needed for Lemmas 5.3 and 5.6): Fitt_{R_I}(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_{R_I}) = (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) as ideals of R_I, where Θ_{Σ,Σ'} = Θ_{Σ,Σ'}(H_ψ/F). Proof (absorbed): projecting (60) from R to R_I gives Fitt_{R_I}(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_{R_I}) ⊂ (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}); by Corollary 2.3, R_I is the character group ring R_Ψ, Ψ = {α : α|_{G'} = χ, α(I) ≠ 1}, so Lemmas 2.4 and 2.5 apply (the image of Θ^# in R_I is a non-zerodivisor: no α ∈ Ψ has a trivial zero, as α is ramified at every v ∈ Σ_p and 1 − α(v) is a unit for v ∈ Σ − Σ_p); writing Fitt_{R_I}(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_{R_I}) = (x·Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) with x ∈ R_I, they give #Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_{R_I} = #O/∏_{α(I)≠1, α|_{G'}=χ} α(x)·L_{Σ,Σ'}(H_ψ/F,α,0); comparing with Lemmas 5.5 and 5.6 yields ∏ α(x) ∈ O^*, hence each α(x) ∈ O^* and x ∈ R_I^*.

Include ... the Fitting-ideal comparison, and the passage from modified to unmodified data." Lemma 5.7 (Fitt_{R_I}(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_{R_I}) = (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) over R_I = R/N I) is the concluding step of the Σ_p ≠ ∅ case of Theorem 5.1 inside that proof. items.name: Remark 5.8: reduction to Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} ∈ m_R
items.statement: The remainder of the paper proves the inclusion Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R) ⊂ (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}). If the image of Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} in the local ring R = O[G_p]_χ does not lie in the maximal ideal m_R, then it is a unit of R, (Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'}) = R, and the inclusion holds trivially. Hence from here on it is assumed that the image of Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} in R lies in m_R.
items.locator: §5, Remark 5.8 (no label) (the source lines 1576–1580)
items.note: Standing assumption for §§6–9 (Ribet's method), where Θ^# must lie in m_R for the congruences to be nontrivial. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract l.46–52): "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma ..., the Fitting-ideal comparison". Remark 5.8 is the reduction (Θ^# ∉ m_R ⇒ Θ^# a unit of the local ring R ⇒ (Θ^#) = R ⇒ Fitt_R(Sel) ⊂ (Θ^#) trivially) that fixes the standing assumption Θ^# ∈ m_R for the Ribet-method sections §§6–9 of that proof. items.name: Contragredient dual M^* of a ℤ[G]-module
items.statement: For a ℤ[G]-module M, M^* := Hom_{ℤ[G]}(M, ℤ[G]) endowed with the contragredient action (r·φ)(x) = φ(r^#·x) for r ∈ ℤ[G], φ ∈ M^*, x ∈ M (eq (82)), where # is the involution of ℤ[G] with g ↦ g^{-1}. If M is a module over a character group ring R = R_Ψ, M^* is viewed as an R^#-module via the same rule.
items.locator: §6.1 Transpose, eq (82) label e:rpd (the source l.1637–1640)

For lattices and torsionfree modules over positive-dimensional orders distinguish Hom_R(−,R), O-linear duals and derived duals; prove the change-of-rings maps"; audit: "Hom_R(−,R), O-linear and derived duals of lattices over positive-dimensional orders | library: absent | Only the generic linear dual exists." DK's convention (82) (r·φ)(x) = φ(r^# x), making M^* an R^#-module, is a different module structure (the restriction of scalars of the plain dual along the involution # of item 120, which is absent). items.name: Transpose of a module with a finite projective presentation (Jannsen)
items.statement: Let M be a ℤ[G]-module (or a module over a character group ring R) with a presentation P_0 → P_1 → M → 0 (eq (83)) by projective ℤ[G]-modules (resp. R-modules) of finite rank. Each P_i^* = Hom_{ℤ[G]}(P_i, ℤ[G]) (contragredient action) is again projective, and the transpose of M with respect to this presentation is M^{tr} := coker(P_1^* → P_0^*), naturally an R^#-module when M is an R-module.

Pure Math. 17)). ∇ is a transpose of the Selmer module; its Fitting ideal is compared with that of Sel by Lemma 6.1. items.name: Transpose is well defined up to projective summands
items.statement: If M' and M'' are transposes of M arising from two different finite projective presentations (83), then there exist projective modules P and Q with M' ⊕ P ≅ M'' ⊕ Q (the transpose is well defined up to homotopy).
items.locator: §6.1 Transpose, text after eq (83) (the source l.1647)

items.name: The ring R^# and the involution # on character group rings
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime, 𝒪 a finite extension of ℤ_p containing all values of characters of G, and R = R_Ψ the character group ring (image of 𝒪[G] in ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} 𝒪_ψ) attached to Ψ ⊂ Ĝ. Define R^# := R_{Ψ^#}, Ψ^# = {ψ^{-1} : ψ ∈ Ψ}. The involution # of 𝒪[G] (g ↦ g^{-1}) induces mutually inverse 𝒪-algebra maps #: R → R^# and #: R^# → R. For an R-module M, M^* and any transpose of M are naturally R^#-modules via (82).
items.locator: §6.1 Transpose, text after eq (83) (the source l.1649–1654)
items.note: Needed to state Lemma 6.1 and Corollary 6.2, since transposing swaps R and R^#. items.name: Lemma 6.1: transpose of a quadratically presented module and its Fitting ideal
items.statement: Let R be a character group ring and M a quadratically presented R-module. Let M^{tr} be the transpose of M associated with any quadratic presentation R^m →(φ) R^m → M → 0 of M. Then M^{tr} is a quadratically presented R^#-module and Fitt_{R^#}(M^{tr}) = Fitt_R(M)^#. (Proof: if (a_{ij}) is the square matrix of φ over R, then (a_{ji}^#) is the matrix of the corresponding quadratic presentation of M^{tr} over R^#.)

items.name: Corollary 6.2: Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R is quadratically presented with Fitting ideal Fitt_{R^#}(∇_{R^#})^#
items.statement: Let F be totally real, H/F finite abelian CM with G = Gal(H/F), p an odd prime, S_ram the finite primes of F ramified in H, T a finite set of primes of F unramified in H, disjoint from S_ram, satisfying condition (1); put Σ = {v ∈ S_ram : v | p} ∪ S_∞ and Σ' = {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p} ∪ T (eqs (57),(59)). Let R be any character group ring quotient R_Ψ of 𝒪[G]. Then the R-module Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R := Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) ⊗_{ℤ[G]} R has a quadratic presentation; its Fitting ideal over R is principal and Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R) = Fitt_{R^#}(∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#})^#. (Follows from (P3), (P4) and Lemma 6.1; proved in bks Lemma 2.8 when Σ ⊃ S_ram.) Notation of §6: Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) is the Σ'-ray class group of H modulo the classes of the primes above Σ, Y_{H,Σ} the free abelian group on the places of H above Σ, X_{H,Σ} = ker(Y_{H,Σ} → ℤ), N^- the minus part of N ⊗ ℤ[1/2], N_p = N ⊗ ℤ_p.

items.name: The module M = Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^- and its class field L/H
items.statement: Work over ℤ[1/2] with Σ, Σ' as in §6. Set M := Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^- and let L/H be the abelian extension corresponding to M by class field theory: the maximal abelian extension of H of odd degree, unramified outside the places of Σ'_H and at most tamely ramified at Σ'_H, in which every prime of Σ_H splits completely, and such that the conjugation action of complex conjugation on Gal(L/H) is inversion. rec_{L/H}: M ≅ Gal(L/H) is the Artin reciprocity isomorphism.

items.name: L/F is Galois and 1 → M → Gal(L/F) → G → 1 splits
items.statement: With M = Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^- and L as above, L/F is Galois (any σ ∈ G_F sends L to a field with the same defining properties), and the short exact sequence of groups 1 → M ≅ Gal(L/H) → Gal(L/F) → G → 1 splits, i.e. Gal(L/F) ≅ M ⋊ G; the splitting holds because H^2(G, M) = 0 for the minus module M with 2 inverted.

items.name: Vanishing of H^i(G, N) for minus modules with 2 inverted
items.statement: Let N be any ℤ[G]^- -module (a ℤ[1/2][G]-module on which complex conjugation c ∈ G acts as −1). Then H^i(G, N) = 0 for all i ≥ 0. Proof: for any g ∈ G, the G-module map N → N given by the action of g induces the identity on H^i(G, N) (Cassels–Fröhlich, Proposition 3, p. 99); for g = c this map is −1, so 2 kills H^i(G, N), which is a ℤ[1/2]-module.

items.name: Lemma 6.3: restriction H^1(G_F, N) → H^1(G_H, N)^G is an isomorphism for minus modules
items.statement: Let N be any ℤ[G]^- -module (2 inverted; e.g. N = M = Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^-), regarded as a G_F-module through G_F → G. Then the restriction map res^{G_F}_{G_H}: H^1(G_F, N) → H^1(G_H, N)^G is an isomorphism. (Proof: the neighbouring terms of the inflation–restriction sequence are H^1(G, N) and H^2(G, N), which vanish.)

items.name: The local classes λ_v ∈ H^1(G_v, M), v ∈ Σ (eq (84))
items.statement: For v ∈ Σ let G_{F,v} ⊂ G_F be the decomposition group of v for a chosen embedding F̄ ⊂ F̄_v, G_{H,v} = G_{F,v} ∩ G_H, and G_v ⊂ G the decomposition group of v in G. The restriction of λ to G_{H,v} is the restriction of ϖ to the decomposition group of a prime of H above v, hence trivial because the primes of Σ_H split completely in L. By inflation–restriction, res^{G_F}_{G_{F,v}} λ is the inflation of a unique class λ_v ∈ H^1(G_v, M) (eq (84)).

items.name: The cocycles γ_v(g) = gx − x attached to ∇^- (eq (86))
items.statement: Let v ∈ Σ, w ∈ Σ_H above v, and w̄ the complex conjugate place; ½(w − w̄) ∈ X_{H,Σ}^-. Let x ∈ ∇_Σ^{Σ',-} be any lift of ½(w − w̄) under the surjection ∇_Σ^{Σ',-} → X_{H,Σ}^- of (80). For g ∈ G_v define γ_v(g) := gx − x ∈ M = Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^-. This is a cocycle whose class in H^1(G_v, M) does not depend on the choice of x, and the tuple (γ_v)_{v∈Σ} is the image of the extension class of (80) under (85).
items.locator: §6.2, eq (86) label e:alphadef and surrounding text (the source l.1712–1718)

Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality"; audit: "Ritter–Weiss modules, their presentations ... | library: absent | Absent". No declaration in either tree mentions ∇, minus parts, or the element ½(w − w̄) (rg 'ritter|minus part|tate sequence' in both trees: none). No more exact atlas owner exists (atlas search for 'extension class' hits only unrelated stages).

items.name: Lemma 6.4 = Lemma A.9 = Property (P2): the extension class of ∇^- equals (λ_v)_{v∈Σ}
items.statement: Assume (A1): Σ ∪ Σ' ⊃ S_ram (satisfied by the sets of §6), work over ℤ[1/2], and let M = Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^-. The minus part 0 → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^- → ∇_Σ^{Σ',-} → X_{H,Σ}^- → 0 (eq (80)) of the sequence (79) defines a class in Ext^1_{ℤ[G]^-}(X_{H,Σ}^-, M) ≅ ⊕_{v∈Σ} H^1(G_v, M) (eqs (81),(85)); this class equals the tuple of canonical classes (λ_v)_{v∈Σ} of eq (84). Proof: enlarge S' by a place v' unramified in H with Frobenius c (S' may be enlarged, and the G_{v'} cover G); the lift x̃ ∈ B^{θ,-} of ½(w − w̄) with coordinate (1−c)/2 at v, 1/2 at v', 0 elsewhere gives γ_v(g) = (g−1)x̃ ∈ W^{θ,-}; the Ritter–Weiss map ρ sends 2(g−1)x̃ to g̃c̃ − c̃g̃ = (g̃c̃g̃^{-1}c̃^{-1} − 1)(c̃g̃), which corresponds to g̃c̃g̃^{-1}c̃^{-1} ∈ M under (164), so γ_v(g) = (g̃c̃g̃^{-1}c̃^{-1})^{1/2} = λ_v(g) by (163).

items.name: Auxiliary set S' for the construction of ∇ (with the standing hypotheses of Appendix A)
items.statement: Throughout Appendix A, Σ, Σ' are finite disjoint sets of places of F with Σ ⊃ S_∞ and Σ' satisfying condition (1) (no nontrivial root of unity of H is ≡ 1 modulo every prime of H above Σ'); no further assumption is made until (A1), (A2), (A2') are imposed. An auxiliary set S' is a finite set of places of F with: (i) S' ⊃ Σ and S' ∩ Σ' = ∅; (ii) S' ∪ Σ' ⊃ S_ram; (iii) Cl_{S'}^{Σ'}(H) = 1; (iv) ∪_{w ∈ S'_H} G_w = G, where G_w ⊂ G is the decomposition group at w. For each place v of F a place w of H above v is fixed.

items.name: Local Weil group extensions (eq (135))
items.statement: For a finite place w of H over v, let H_w^{ab} ⊃ H_w^{nr} be the maximal abelian and maximal unramified extensions of H_w. There are canonical short exact sequences 0 → W(H_w^{ab}/H_w) ≅ H_w^* → W(H_w^{ab}/F_v) →(π_V) G_w → 0 and 0 → W(H_w^{nr}/H_w) ≅ ℤ → W(H_w^{nr}/F_v) →(π_W) G_w → 0, where W denotes the Weil group and the identifications are local class field theory.
items.locator: App. A.1, eq (135) label e:whw (the source l.3103–3111)
items.note: External input (rw — Ritter, Weiss, A Tate sequence for global units, Compositio Math.). Source of the (relative) augmentation ideals used to define V_w and W_w. Evidence: ClassFieldTheory Layer 9 (the layer extract l.1177–1224; atlas/areas/classical-1.json): "localWeilGroup K ≤ G_K, the preimage of ℤ ⊆ Ẑ under the imported surjection G_K → Gal(K^ur/K) ≅ Ẑ"; "For L/K finite Galois, restriction weilRestrict : W_K → Gal(L/K) is surjective with kernel the image of weilTransfer"; "weilDegree : W_K → ℤ is surjective with kernel inertia, giving 1 → I_K → W_K → ℤ → 1"; "localWeilArtinEquiv : Kˣ ≃ₜ* W_K^ab onto the topological abelianization W_K / closure ⁅W_K, W_K⁆"; "Global Weil groups are outside this roadmap." Audit: "No Weil group, maximal unramified extension or G_K -> Z-hat surjection exists." Atlas: LanglandsParameterStacks:LP0 only "Use the local-field Weil-group carrier, inertia and wild inertia with their topologies" (imports Layer 9); no stage names relative Weil groups W(L/K) (search 'relative Weil', 'W(L/K)': none). Confirmed the previous verdict. The two sequences of (135) are the quotients of Layer 9's 1 → W_{H_w} → W_{F_v} → Gal(H_w/F_v) → 1 by the closure of the commutator subgroup of W_{H_w} (kernel identified with H_w^* by localWeilArtinEquiv) and by I_{H_w} (kernel ℤ by weilDegree); Layer 9 names every ingredient but not the relative Weil groups W(H_w^ab/F_v), W(H_w^nr/F_v) themselves, and I.6 owns their Ritter–Weiss use. Not library: neither tree has any Weil group.

items.name: Ritter–Weiss local module V_w (eqs (133),(136))
items.statement: Let ΔV be the augmentation ideal of ℤ[W(H_w^{ab}/F_v)] and Δ(V, H_w^*) the relative augmentation ideal, the kernel of ℤ[W(H_w^{ab}/F_v)] → ℤ[G_w] induced by π_V. Define V_w = V_w(H_w) := ΔV/(ΔV)·Δ(V, H_w^*). It is a ℤ[G_w]-module sitting in the exact sequence 0 → H_w^* → V_w → ΔG_w → 0 (eq (133)), ΔG_w ⊂ ℤ[G_w] the augmentation ideal.
items.locator: App. A.1, eq (133) label e:vseq and eq (136) (the source l.3088–3096, 3113–3118)

No other layer names it.

items.name: Ritter–Weiss local module W_w (eqs (134),(137))
items.statement: For w finite, let ΔW be the augmentation ideal of ℤ[W(H_w^{nr}/F_v)] and Δ(W, ℤ) the relative augmentation ideal for π_W. Define W_w = W_w(H_w) := ΔW/(ΔW)·Δ(W, ℤ). It sits in an exact sequence of ℤ[G_w]-modules 0 → 𝒪_w^* → V_w → W_w → 0 (eq (134)).

items.name: Semi-local modules J, V, W and the sequence 0 → J → V → W → 0 (eq (138))
items.statement: Define J = ∏~_{v ∉ Σ∪Σ'} 𝒪_w^* × ∏~_{v∈Σ} H_w^* × ∏~_{v∈Σ'} U_w^1; V = ∏~_{v ∉ S'∪Σ'} 𝒪_w^* × ∏~_{v∈S'} V_w × ∏~_{v∈Σ'} U_w^1; W = ∏~_{v ∈ S'−Σ} W_w × ∏~_{v∈Σ} ΔG_w. Using (133) at v ∈ Σ, (134) at v ∈ S' − Σ and the identity elsewhere, there is an exact sequence of G-modules 0 → J → V → W → 0.

items.name: Lemma A.1: θ: V → 𝔒 is surjective
items.statement: With S' satisfying the four conditions of the auxiliary set and V, 𝔒, θ as in (140), the map θ is surjective. Proof (Ritter–Weiss p. 162): in (141), θ_{J'} is surjective since its cokernel is Cl_{S'}^{Σ'}(H) = 1, and θ_{W'}: ∏~_{v∈S'} ΔG_w → ΔG is surjective because the decomposition groups G_w, w ∈ S'_H, cover G; hence θ is surjective.
