Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups". The class-field-theory input coker(θ_{J'}) = Cl_{S'}^{Σ'}(H) is the ray-class dictionary of atlas/areas/classical-1.json GlobalNumberFields Layer 7: "`rayClassQuotient : IdeleClassGroup K →* RayClassGroup 𝔪` with surjectivity and kernel `RaySubgroup 𝔪`" (conductor 𝔪 only; the S'-inverted, Σ'-smoothed group Cl_{S'}^{Σ'} is not named). Library: rg over both pinned trees for ritter|tate sequence finds nothing; TauCeti rg RayClassGroup|SUnit|TSmooth hits no number-theory file (only unrelated knot-theory/linear-algebra matches). Confirmed the previous verdict (planned, I.6). Lemma A.1 (surjectivity of θ via the auxiliary diagram (141), Cl_{S'}^{Σ'}(H) = 1 and the covering of G by decomposition groups) is a property of the Ritter–Weiss presentation and is planned only under I.6's Ritter–Weiss target; GlobalNumberFields Layer 7 supplies the ray-class dictionary it uses but does not plan the lemma. No library declaration.

items.name: Snake sequence 0 → 𝒪_{H,Σ,Σ'}^* → V^θ → W^θ → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → 0 (eq (142))
items.statement: Set V^θ = ker θ and W^θ = ker θ_W. By class field theory ker θ_J = 𝒪_{H,Σ,Σ'}^* (Σ-units of H congruent to 1 modulo Σ'_H) and coker θ_J = Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H). Applying the snake lemma to (140) and using surjectivity of θ (Lemma A.1) yields an exact sequence of ℤ[G]-modules 0 → 𝒪_{H,Σ,Σ'}^* → V^θ → W^θ → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → 0. The connecting map W^θ → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) sends w̄ ∈ W^θ to the class of x ∈ C_H whenever θ(y) = image of x in 𝔒 for a lift y ∈ V of w̄; it is described explicitly by Ritter–Weiss Theorem 5.
items.locator: App. A.1, eq (142) label e:snake (the source l.3183–3190)
items.note: Provides the class group as a submodule of ∇ and the unit group as the kernel of the presentation (150). Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups"; GlobalNumberFields Layer 7 (classical-1.json): "Define one `IdeleCongruenceSubgroup 𝔪`. At a finite divisor of `𝔪` it uses principal units of the specified level; at other finite places it uses local units ... `rayClassQuotient : IdeleClassGroup K →* RayClassGroup 𝔪` with surjectivity and kernel `RaySubgroup 𝔪`". Abstract snake lemma verified in Mathlib: Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/SnakeLemma.lean:385 `lemma snake_lemma : S.composableArrows.Exact` in namespace CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.SnakeInput (six-term exactness `S.L₀.X₁ ⟶ S.L₀.X₂ ⟶ S.L₀.X₃ ⟶ S.L₃.X₁ ⟶ S.L₃.X₂ ⟶ S.L₃.X₃`). No declaration for V^θ, W^θ, 𝒪_{H,Σ,Σ'}^* or Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) in either tree. Confirmed the previous verdict (planned). The four-term sequence is I.6's 'comparison to class/ray-class groups' of the Ritter–Weiss modules; its class-field-theory input (ker θ_J = Σ-units ≡ 1 mod Σ', coker θ_J = Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) as a quotient of the idele class group) is the ray-class dictionary of GlobalNumberFields Layer 7, which plans the conductor-𝔪 version only. Mathlib's CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.SnakeInput.snake_lemma gives the abstract snake lemma but not the specific modules or the Ritter–Weiss Theorem 5 description of the connecting map, so the item is not library.

items.name: Ritter–Weiss Lemma 5: embedding of W_w into ℤ[G_w]^2 (eq (143))
items.statement: Write W_w^* = Hom_ℤ(W_w, ℤ). There is a commutative diagram of ℤ[G_w]-modules with exact rows 0 → W_w →((α_w, β_w)) ℤ[G_w]^2 → W_w^* → 0 over 0 → ΔG_w → ℤ[G_w] → ℤ → 0, with vertical maps α_w: W_w → ΔG_w, the first projection π_1: ℤ[G_w]^2 → ℤ[G_w], and an induced map W_w^* → ℤ. When v is unramified in H, β_w: W_w → ℤ[G_w] is an isomorphism (so Ind_{G_w}^G W_w ≅ ℤ[G]) and α_w = (σ_w − 1)·β_w.
items.locator: App. A.1, eq (143) label e:ww2 (the source l.3191–3200), and text on l.3238, 3258, 3323
items.note: External input (rw Lemma 5 — Ritter, Weiss, A Tate sequence for global units). Embeds W into the free module B so that ∇ = coker(V^θ → B^θ) has a projective presentation. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations"; audit l.42 "Ritter–Weiss modules, their presentations, comparison with class and ray-class groups, and Fitting-ideal functoriality | library: absent". Foundation only: classical-1.json ClassFieldTheory Layer 9 plans "`localWeilGroup K ≤ G_K` ... `weilRestrict : W_K → Gal(L/K)` is surjective with kernel the image of `weilTransfer` ... `1 → I_K → W_K → ℤ → 1`" and says "Global Weil groups are outside this roadmap", but never names W_w = ΔW/(ΔW)Δ(W,ℤ), W_w^*, or the embedding (α_w, β_w). rg over both pinned trees for ritter|WeilGroup|weil group: no hits; Mathlib's Rep/Representation files have no relative augmentation ideal of a Weil group. Confirmed the previous verdict (planned, I.6). Ritter–Weiss Lemma 5 (W_w ↪ ℤ[G_w]^2 with cokernel W_w^*, compatible with ΔG_w ⊂ ℤ[G_w] → ℤ, and β_w an isomorphism with α_w = (σ_w − 1)β_w at unramified v) is the local input to the projective presentation of ∇ and is planned only as part of I.6's 'Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations'. ClassFieldTheory Layer 9 is the most foundational supplier of the Weil group W(H_w^nr/F_v) but does not own W_w or this embedding.

items.name: The map α_w: W_w → ΔG_w and the sequence 0 → ℤ → W_w → ΔG_w → 0 (eq (144))
items.statement: α_w is induced by the canonical projection π_W: ΔW → ΔG_w (from (135) and (137)); it sits in the short exact sequence of ℤ[G_w]-modules 0 → ℤ → W_w →(α_w) ΔG_w → 0 (Ritter–Weiss Lemma 5(b); also obtained by combining (133) and (134)).
items.locator: App. A.1, eq (144) label e:alphaw (the source l.3201–3208); also l.3399–3401
items.note: External input (rw Lemma 5(b) — Ritter, Weiss, A Tate sequence for global units). Defines the component of θ_W at v ∈ S' − Σ, gives dim(Ind W_w^*)_χ = 1 in Lemma A.4 and the sequence (161) in Lemma A.8. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups". ClassFieldTheory Layer 9 (classical-1.json stage 137) plans the local Weil group with "`weilDegree : W_K → ℤ` is surjective with kernel inertia, giving `1 → I_K → W_K → ℤ → 1`" and `weilRestrict : W_K → Gal(L/K)`, the objects behind π_W : W(H_w^nr/F_v) → G_w, but not the augmentation quotient W_w or α_w. Library: rg over both pinned trees for ritter|WeilGroup|augmentation (outside TauCeti's DG/A∞ augmentation ideals) finds no relevant declaration; TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/Formation/Basic.lean has only abstract formations and Tate cohomology of layers. Confirmed the previous verdict (planned, I.6). α_w : W_w → ΔG_w and 0 → ℤ → W_w → ΔG_w → 0 (Ritter–Weiss Lemma 5(b), equivalently (133) composed with (134)) belong to the local Ritter–Weiss module package that I.6 names; no other layer of the atlas (areas/*.json, roadmaps/*.json) mentions W_w, α_w or Ritter–Weiss local modules, and neither library has a declaration for them.

items.name: The maps β_w^0: W_w → ℤ[G_w/I_w] and β_w = N I_w·β_w^0 (eqs (145),(146))
items.statement: Let σ ∈ W(H_w^{nr}/F_v), σ̄ its image in G_w/I_w = Gal(H_w^{I_w}/F_v), and n ∈ ℤ defined by σ|_{F_v^{nr}} = σ_v^n with σ_v ∈ W(F_v^{nr}/F_v) ≅ ℤ the Frobenius; σ_w = σ̄_v ∈ G_w/I_w the Frobenius. For x = σ − 1, β_w^0(x) ∈ ℤ[G_w/I_w] is the unique element with augmentation n such that ᾱ_w(x) = σ̄ − 1 = (σ_w − 1)β_w^0(x) in ℤ[G_w/I_w] (eq (145)); explicitly β_w^0(σ−1) = 1 + σ_w + ⋯ + σ_w^{n−1} if n > 0, 0 if n = 0, −(σ_w^{-1} + ⋯ + σ_w^{n}) if n < 0. Define β_w(x) := N I_w·β_w^0(x) ∈ ℤ[G_w], N I_w = Σ_{τ∈I_w} τ (eq (146)).
items.locator: App. A.1, eqs (145),(146) labels e:iwred, e:betawdef (the source l.3209–3225)
items.note: Second coordinate of the embedding W_w → ℤ[G_w]^2, and the whole embedding at unramified places of S'. Evidence: the layer extract l.37 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6, also atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality." Audit l.42: "AUDIT TARGET: Ritter–Weiss modules, their presentations ... | library: absent". the source l.3209–3225 (eqs (145),(146)) define β_w^0 and β_w = N I_w·β_w^0 as the second coordinate of the Ritter–Weiss embedding (α_w,β_w): W_w → ℤ[G_w]^2 of (143) (rw Lemma 5), a local building block of the presentation of ∇ that I.6 names. Library check: rg -il 'ritter|weiss|Tate sequence|Brumer' over Mathlib finds only PoissonSummation.lean (Weierstrass-type hit) and over TauCeti only LeibnizPart.lean and Discriminant/Stickelberger.lean (Stickelberger's discriminant congruence, l.13, unrelated); rg 'WeilGroup|weilGroup|Weil group' in TauCeti hits only Mordell–Weil files; Mathlib has no inertia-norm element N I_w or Frobenius geometric-series map on ΔW_w. Verdict changed in one respect: the previous secondary citation tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-9-the-local-weil-group is removed from `planned`. Its description (classical-1.json) plans only the carrier `localWeilGroup K`, `weilDegree : W_K → ℤ` and `weilRestrict : W_K → Gal(L/K)`; these are inputs (the Frobenius exponent n and σ ↦ σ̄) already consumed by the earlier definition of W_w, and the layer does not name β_w, N I_w or any Ritter–Weiss map, so listing it is shared vocabulary, not planning (its audit is also 'not built'). Status planned with owner I.6 confirmed; […]

items.name: The set S'_ram and the free module B
items.statement: S'_ram := S_ram ∖ (Σ ∪ Σ') ⊂ S' (ramified primes not in Σ ∪ Σ'). B := ∏_{v ∈ S'∖S'_ram} ℤ[G] × ∏_{v ∈ S'_ram} ℤ[G]^2, a free ℤ[G]-module of rank #S' + #S'_ram.
items.locator: App. A.1, text after eq (146) (the source l.3226–3230)
items.note: Free target of the embedding γ; B^θ is the free module of the presentation of ∇. Evidence: the layer extract l.37 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality." Audit l.42: "AUDIT TARGET: Ritter–Weiss modules, their presentations, comparison with class and ray-class groups, and Fitting-ideal functoriality | library: absent". the source l.3226–3230: S'_ram = S_ram ∖ (Σ ∪ Σ') and B = ∏_{S'∖S'_ram} ℤ[G] × ∏_{S'_ram} ℤ[G]^2, the free target of the Ritter–Weiss embedding γ. Library check: rg over both trees for Ritter/Weiss/Tate sequence/Brumer/Stickelberger elements finds nothing (TauCeti's Stickelberger.lean is the discriminant congruence); Mathlib's free-module API (Module.Free, Finsupp) is generic and has no declaration for this place-indexed module or the set S'_ram. Confirmed previous verdict. The paper-specific data (abelian CM extension H/F, S', Σ, Σ', S_ram) is absent from both libraries, and I.6 is the only atlas stage naming Ritter–Weiss presentations, of which B is the free target.

items.name: The injection γ: W → B
items.statement: γ is defined componentwise: for v ∈ Σ, γ_v is induced by the inclusion ΔG_w ⊂ ℤ[G_w]; for v ∈ S'_ram, γ_v is induced by (α_w, β_w): W_w → ℤ[G_w]^2 of (143); for v ∈ S' ∖ (Σ ∪ S'_ram), γ_v is induced by β_w: W_w → ℤ[G_w], an isomorphism since v is unramified in H. γ is injective.
items.locator: App. A.1, itemised definition of γ (the source l.3231–3239)
items.note: Realises W^θ inside the free module B^θ; ∇ is the cokernel of V^θ → B^θ. Evidence: the layer extract l.37 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations"; audit l.42 "Ritter–Weiss modules, their presentations ... | library: absent". the source l.3231–3239: γ: W → B defined componentwise (ΔG_w ⊂ ℤ[G_w] at Σ; (α_w,β_w) at S'_ram; β_w, an isomorphism at unramified places by rw Lemma 5), injective. Library check: rg -il 'ritter|weiss|Tate sequence|TateSequence|Brumer' over Mathlib and TauCeti finds no relevant file; no W_w, ΔW or induced-module-over-places objects exist in either tree. Confirmed previous verdict. γ is the embedding of W into the free module of the Ritter–Weiss presentation that I.6 plans; its injectivity at unramified places uses rw Lemma 5, also absent from both libraries. No more foundational owner names Tate sequences (the only atlas 'Tate sequence' is the Bass–Tate sequence in K2SymbolsBrauer:T.4, unrelated).

items.name: The module Z and the diagram (147) with vertical maps θ_W, θ_B, θ_Z
items.statement: Z := ∏~_{v∈Σ} ℤ × ∏~_{v ∈ S'_ram} W_w^*. There is a commutative diagram with exact rows 0 → W →(γ) B → Z → 0 over 0 → ΔG → ℤ[G] → ℤ → 0, with vertical maps defined componentwise: for v ∈ Σ, θ_W and θ_B are the identity (ΔG_w ⊂ ΔG, ℤ[G_w]-component → ℤ[G]) and θ_Z is the augmentation; for v ∈ S'_ram, θ_W, θ_B, θ_Z are induced from the vertical maps of (143); for v ∈ S' ∖ (Σ ∪ S'_ram), θ_W is induced by α_w = (σ_w − 1)·β_w and θ_B is multiplication by σ_w − 1 (the component of Z is 0).
items.locator: App. A.1, eq (147) label e:wbdiagram and following itemisation (the source l.3240–3261)
items.note: Its kernels give the sequence (148) and hence the quotient Z^θ (= X_{H,Σ} under (A1)) of ∇. Evidence: the layer extract l.37 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups". the source l.3240–3261: Z = ∏~_Σ ℤ × ∏~_{S'_ram} W_w^*, diagram (147) label e:wbdiagram with rows 0→W→B→Z→0 over 0→ΔG→ℤ[G]→ℤ→0 and vertical maps θ_W, θ_B, θ_Z given componentwise (identity/augmentation at Σ, from (143) at S'_ram, α_w = (σ_w−1)β_w and multiplication by σ_w−1 at unramified places). Library check: rg over both trees for Ritter/Weiss/Weil group/Tate sequence finds nothing relevant; Mathlib's 'augmentation' hits are singular-homology augmentations and TauCeti's are DG/A∞ augmentations. Confirmed previous verdict. The diagram is the middle step of the Ritter–Weiss presentation of ∇ and of its comparison with the class group (quotient Z^θ), both named by I.6; no library declaration and no other atlas stage plans it.

items.name: Short exact sequence 0 → W^θ → B^θ → Z^θ → 0 (eq (148))
items.statement: Since θ_W: W → ΔG is surjective, taking kernels of the vertical maps in (147) yields a short exact sequence of ℤ[G]-modules 0 → W^θ → B^θ → Z^θ → 0, where B^θ = ker θ_B and Z^θ = ker θ_Z.
items.locator: App. A.1, eq (148) label e:wbx (the source l.3262–3267)
items.note: Combined with (142) it produces the two exact sequences (150),(151) characterising ∇. Evidence: the layer extract l.37 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations". the source l.3262–3267, eq (148) label e:wbx: since θ_W is surjective, taking kernels in (147) gives 0 → W^θ → B^θ → Z^θ → 0. Generic tool verified in the pinned Mathlib: Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/SnakeLemma.lean l.210 `lemma L₀_exact : S.L₀.Exact` (exactness of the kernel row of a `SnakeInput`), l.222 `L₃_exact`; but these give exactness of the kernel row for an abstract snake input, not the specific statement about W^θ, B^θ, Z^θ, whose objects (items 147–148) are absent from both trees, and right-exactness needs the surjectivity of θ_W (Ritter–Weiss input). Confirmed previous verdict. Mathlib's snake lemma (CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.SnakeInput.L₀_exact) is a general tool, not a declaration providing this item; the item is the specific short exact sequence in the Ritter–Weiss presentation planned by I.6.

items.name: B^θ is free of rank #S' + #S'_ram − 1 (eq (149))
items.statement: Since θ_B is the identity on each ℤ[G]-component with v ∈ Σ and Σ ⊃ S_∞ is nonempty, B^θ = ker(θ_B: B → ℤ[G]) is a free ℤ[G]-module of rank #S' + #S'_ram − 1.
items.locator: App. A.1, eq (149) label e:bfree (the source l.3268–3271)
items.note: Provides the free module of the presentation of ∇; its rank equals rank V^θ = #S' − 1 exactly when S'_ram = ∅, i.e. under (A1). Evidence: the layer extract l.37 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations"; audit l.42 "Ritter–Weiss modules, their presentations ... | library: absent". the source l.3268–3271, eq (149) label e:bfree: B^θ = ker θ_B is a free ℤ[G]-module of rank #S' + #S'_ram − 1, because θ_B is the identity on each Σ-component and Σ ⊃ S_∞ ≠ ∅. Library check: rg in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Prod.lean and FreeModule/Basic.lean for 'ker_fst|Free.*ker' finds no lemma that the kernel of a map from a finite free module which is the identity on one free coordinate is free of rank one less; Mathlib/RingTheory/Finiteness/Cardinality.lean l.116 `kerRepr` merely names the kernel of a surjection from a finite free module. B, θ_B, S'_ram are absent from both trees. Confirmed previous verdict. The generic linear algebra (kernel of a split projection is the complementary summand) is elementary but not a Mathlib declaration in this form, and the item is the paper-specific freeness/rank statement of the free module of the Ritter–Weiss presentation, owned by I.6.

items.name: Definition A.2: the Ritter–Weiss module ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)
items.statement: ∇_Σ^{Σ'} = ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H) is the cokernel of the composite ℤ[G]-module map V^θ → W^θ → B^θ, where V^θ = ker(θ: V → 𝔒), W^θ = ker(θ_W: W → ΔG), B^θ = ker(θ_B: B → ℤ[G]), the first map is induced by V → W in (138) and the second by γ.
items.locator: App. A.1, Definition A.2 (no label; the source l.3272–3277)
items.note: The central object of §6 and Appendix A: a transpose of the Selmer module with a locally quadratic presentation. Evidence: the layer extract l.37 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6, iwasawa-1.json): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality." Audit l.42: "AUDIT TARGET: Ritter–Weiss modules, their presentations, comparison with class and ray-class groups, and Fitting-ideal functoriality | library: absent | Absent: neither library has Fitting ideals." the source l.3272–3277, Definition A.2: ∇_Σ^{Σ'} = coker(V^θ → W^θ → B^θ). Library check: rg -il 'ritter|weiss|nabla|Tate sequence|Brumer|Stickelberger' over Mathlib and TauCeti finds only unrelated files (PoissonSummation.lean, LeibnizPart.lean, Discriminant/Stickelberger.lean = discriminant congruence); rg -il 'fitting' hits only Lie-theory Fitting decompositions and category-theory images. Confirmed previous verdict. This is precisely the 'Ritter–Weiss module' the I.6 description names. IntegralIwasawaTheory:KU-brumerstark ('Integral Brumer–Stark, Ritter–Weiss and generalised Ribet theorem') is an aggregation checkpoint of I.6/I.7, and NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.6 ('Kakde and Ritter–Weiss routes') is the noncommutative main conjecture, so neither is an alternative owner.

items.name: Tate-type sequence 0 → 𝒪_{H,Σ,Σ'}^* → V^θ → B^θ → ∇_Σ^{Σ'} → 0 (eq (150))
items.statement: Comparing (142) and (148), there is an exact sequence of ℤ[G]-modules 0 → 𝒪_{H,Σ,Σ'}^* → V^θ → B^θ → ∇_Σ^{Σ'} → 0.
items.locator: App. A.1, eq (150) label e:tate (the source l.3278–3283)
items.note: The presentation of ∇ used for projectivity (Lemma A.4), local quadraticity (Lemma A.5) and the transpose (Lemma A.8); also shows V^θ is ℤ-torsion-free. Evidence: the layer extract l.37 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups". the source l.3278–3283, eq (150) label e:tate: 0 → 𝒪_{H,Σ,Σ'}^* → V^θ → B^θ → ∇_Σ^{Σ'} → 0, obtained by comparing the snake sequence (142) (l.2967–2972) with (148). Library check: rg over both pinned trees for 'Tate sequence|TateSequence|ritter|weiss|Brumer' finds nothing relevant; Mathlib's 'Tate' material is Tate cohomology (RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology), Tate modules and Tate's thesis, none of which gives a Tate sequence for global units. Atlas: the only other 'Tate sequence' stage is K2SymbolsBrauer:T.4 (Bass–Tate sequence for F(t)), unrelated; new roadmaps/*.json and packets contain no Ritter/Tate-sequence hits. Confirmed previous verdict. The four-term exact sequence is the Tate-type presentation of the Ritter–Weiss module (Ritter–Weiss, 'A Tate sequence for global units'), part of 'their presentations' in I.6; no library declaration and no more foundational owner.

items.name: Property (P1): 0 → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → ∇_Σ^{Σ'} → Z^θ → 0 (eq (151)), and = X_{H,Σ} under (A1) (eqs (79),(152))
items.statement: Comparing (142) and (148), there is a short exact sequence of ℤ[G]-modules 0 → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → ∇_Σ^{Σ'} → Z^θ → 0 (eq (151)), where Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → ∇ is induced by the snake map of (142) (the image in W^θ ⊂ B^θ of a lift y ∈ V of the image in 𝔒 of x ∈ C_H representing the class) and ∇ → Z^θ is induced by B^θ → Z^θ. If (A1) holds (Σ ∪ Σ' ⊃ S_ram), then S'_ram = ∅, Z = Y_{H,Σ}, Z^θ = X_{H,Σ}, and the sequence reads 0 → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → ∇_Σ^{Σ'} → X_{H,Σ} → 0 (eq (152) = eq (79), property (P1) for the sets of §6).
items.locator: App. A.1, eqs (151),(152) labels e:seltr, e:seltr2 (the source l.3284–3303); stated as §6 property (P1), eq (79) label e:nablaext (l.1595–1601)
items.note: Realises ∇ as an extension of X_{H,Σ} (carrying the trivial-zero data) by the class group whose Fitting ideal is to be bounded; used in §9 and Appendix B. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.32–41; atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality." Audit note under it: "Ritter–Weiss modules, their presentations, comparison with class and ray-class groups, and Fitting-ideal functoriality | library: absent". Paper: the source l.3288–3303 (eqs (151),(152)), l.1595–1601 (eq (79)). rg -il 'Ritter|Weiss|Tate sequence|TateSequence' over Mathlib/ and TauCeti/ at the pinned commits: only an unrelated hit in Mathlib/Analysis/Fourier/PoissonSummation.lean. Confirmed the previous verdict. The sequence 0 → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → ∇_Σ^{Σ'} → Z^θ → 0 (and its (A1) form with X_{H,Σ}) is exactly the 'comparison to class/ray-class groups' of the Ritter–Weiss module that I.6 names; no more foundational layer mentions ∇ or Ritter–Weiss (KU-brumerstark in iwasawa-1.json is only an aggregation checkpoint of I.6/I.7). Neither library has ∇, X_{H,Σ} as a G-module, or the T-smoothed ray class group with Galois action.

items.name: Assumption (A1)
items.statement: (A1): Σ ∪ Σ' ⊃ S_ram, i.e. every finite prime of F ramified in H lies in Σ or Σ'. (Under (A1), S'_ram = ∅, Z = Y_{H,Σ}, Z^θ = X_{H,Σ} and B^θ is free of rank #S' − 1.)
items.locator: App. A.1, text after eq (151) (the source l.3290–3298)
items.note: Hypothesis of (152), Lemma A.5 and Lemma A.9; satisfied by the sets (57),(59). Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups". Paper: (A1) introduced at the source l.3294–3298 solely so that S'_ram = ∅, Z = Y_{H,Σ}, Z^θ = X_{H,Σ} in (152); S_ram defined at l.272 as the finite primes of F ramified in H. Library search: Mathlib has the predicates Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt / Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (used in TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/AuxiliaryPrime.lean:48 and FrobeniusPrimeSet.lean:95), and GlobalNumberFields 1.2 (the layer extract l.2113–2120) says to state unramified-outside-a-set conditions directly with them. Confirmed the previous verdict. (A1) is 'H/F unramified at every finite prime outside Σ ∪ Σ'', a hypothesis of the Ritter–Weiss comparison sequence rather than an independent object; the containing target is I.6. Mathlib's Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt/IsUnramifiedIn supply only the vocabulary for expressing it (no declaration packages S_ram or this condition), so not library.

items.name: Lemma A.3: enlarging S' by one place gives an equivalent extension
items.statement: Let ∇ and ∇' be constructed as in §A.1 with the same Σ, Σ' but auxiliary sets S' and S' ∪ {v} (v a place not in S' ∪ Σ', hence unramified in H). Then there is an equivalence of the extensions (151): an isomorphism ∇ → ∇' making the diagram with rows 0 → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → ∇ → Z^θ → 0 and 0 → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → ∇' → Z^θ → 0 and identity outer vertical maps commute (eq (153)). Proof: 0 → V → V' → Ind_{G_v}^G W_w ≅ ℤ[G] → 0 induces 0 → V^θ → (V')^θ → ℤ[G] → 0 (θ surjective on V and V'), and similarly (split) for (W, W') and (B, B'); the induced maps on the ℤ[G]-quotients are the identity, so ∇ ≅ ∇'; commutativity is an arrow chase using the snake-map description of Cl → ∇.
items.locator: App. A.2 Independence of S', Lemma A.3, eq (153) label e:nnp (the source l.3308–3341)
items.note: Shows ∇ and its extension class are canonical (independent of S'); not used elsewhere in the paper. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups". Paper: Lemma A.3, the source l.3313–3341, eq (153) (equivalence of the extensions (151) for auxiliary sets S' and S' ∪ {v}, proof via 0 → V → V' → Ind_{G_v}^G W_w ≅ ℤ[G] → 0 and the snake-map description of Cl → ∇). Library: rg for Ritter/Weiss/Tate sequence finds nothing; Tau Ceti Formation/Basic.lean has only Formation/NormalLayer carriers and Tate-cohomology abbreviations. Confirmed the previous verdict. Lemma A.3 is the well-definedness (independence of the auxiliary set S') of the Ritter–Weiss module and of its extension class, which belongs to the construction I.6 owns; the layer does not name the independence statement itself, hence the containing-target reading and medium confidence. Nothing in either library.

items.name: Independence of ∇ and of its extension class from S'
items.statement: The module ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H) and the extension class it defines via (151) are independent, up to equivalence of extensions, of the auxiliary set S' used in the construction (identify the constructions for S_1', S_2' with that for S_1' ∪ S_2' by iterating Lemma A.3).
items.locator: App. A.2, opening paragraph label s:indep (the source l.3308–3311)
items.note: Canonicity of ∇ (stated as not used in this work). Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups". Paper: §A.2 opening paragraph label s:indep, the source l.3308–3311 (independence 'by identifying the construction for two different sets S_1' and S_2' with the one for S_1' ∪ S_2'' from Lemma A.3). Confirmed the previous verdict. Canonicity of ∇_Σ^{Σ'} and its class in Ext^1(Z^θ, Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)) is the iterated form of Lemma A.3 and part of constructing the Ritter–Weiss module (I.6); no layer names the independence statement explicitly and no library declaration exists.

items.name: Assumption (A2)
items.statement: (A2): Σ' contains no primes of wild ramification, i.e. for every v ∈ Σ' the inertia group I_v ⊂ G_v ⊂ G has order prime to ℓ, where ℓ is the residue characteristic of v.
items.locator: App. A.3 Projectivity of Presentation, label s:pp (the source l.3343–3349)
items.note: Ensures U_w^1 is cohomologically trivial for v ∈ Σ', hence V^θ projective over ℤ[G] (Lemma A.4(i)). Evidence: LocalFieldsRamification Layer 3 (the layer extract l.7565–7590; atlas/areas/classical-1.json stages[168]): "**Tame and wild.** Define `IsTamelyRamified K L` by `p ∤ e` and `IsWildlyRamified K L` by `p ∣ e`, where `p` is the residue characteristic." The global-to-local transfer is NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 6.4 (the layer extract from l.3373; classical-1.json stages[179]): "`v_P(𝔡) = e − 1` if and only if the completed local extension is tamely ramified" via the Layer 5 completion dictionary. IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations" — (A2) is the hypothesis of Lemma A.4(i) (the source l.3345–3349, l.3358–3361). Library: Mathlib/NumberTheory/RamificationInertia/Galois.lean:317 `Ideal.card_inertia_eq_ramificationIdxIn : Nat.card (P.inertia G) = Ideal.ramificationIdxIn p S` gives #I_v = e_v, but no tame/wild predicate exists in either pinned tree (rg -il 'tamely|IsTame|TamelyRamified|wildly|IsWild': no relevant hits). Changed the previous verdict's owners: the mathematical content of (A2) is the notion of wild/tame ramification at a prime (I_v of order prime to ℓ ⇔ ℓ ∤ e_v ⇔ H_w/F_v tamely ramified, using #I_v = e_v), which is owned by LocalFieldsRamification Layer 3 (definition of IsTamelyRamified/IsWildlyRamified) with NumberFieldArithmetic Layer 5/6 transporting it to primes of a number field; I.6 is retained for the hypothesis role in the Ritter–Weiss presentation. Status remains planned; not library since no tameness predicate is defined in either pinned tree.

items.name: Assumption (A2')
items.statement: (A2'): one works over a ℤ[G]-algebra R such that for every v ∈ Σ' ∩ S_ram the rational prime ℓ below v is invertible in R.
items.locator: App. A.3, text after (A2) (the source l.3351–3356)
items.note: Alternative to (A2) used in the main body over ℤ_p[G]-algebras, for Lemmas A.4(ii), A.5(ii), A.8(ii). Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations". Paper: (A2') at the source l.3351–3356 (R a ℤ[G]-algebra with the residue characteristic ℓ of every v ∈ Σ' ∩ S_ram invertible in R), used in Lemma A.4 second clause (l.3359–3361) and its proof (l.3377–3379). Confirmed the previous verdict. (A2') is a coefficient-ring hypothesis for projectivity of V^θ_R (the ℤ_p[G]-algebra case of the main body) and is part of the Ritter–Weiss presentation I.6 plans; it is trivially expressible (IsUnit (ℓ : R)) but no library declaration or other layer packages this condition.

items.name: Cohomologically trivial G-module
items.statement: A G-module M is cohomologically trivial if the Tate cohomology groups Ĥ^i(H', M) vanish for all subgroups H' ⊂ G and all integers i.
items.locator: App. A.3, proof of Lemma A.4 (the source l.3365)
items.note: External input (nak — Nakayama, On modules of trivial cohomology over a finite group II, Nagoya Math. J.). Property of V^θ that, with ℤ-torsion-freeness, implies projectivity by Nakayama's theorem. Evidence: rg -il 'cohomologically ?trivial|CohomologicallyTrivial|cohomTrivial|IsCohomologicallyTrivial' over Mathlib and tauceti-f790474/TauCeti: no hits. Atlas: rg over atlas/areas/*.json, research/blueprint/roadmaps/*.json and packets for 'cohomologically', 'trivial cohomology', 'Nakayama' (projectivity), 'Shapiro/coinduced/acyclic': the only cohomology hits are ProfiniteCohomology Layer 7 ('Coind_1^G A ... has vanishing H^i for i = 1, 2', 'coindAcyclic in every positive degree' in Layer 10) and ClassFieldTheory Layer 0 (the layer extract l.686–740: Tate-cohomology suppliers, restriction/corestriction in every degree, Tate's theorem cup-product criterion), none of which names cohomologically trivial modules. Nearest library: Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/Basic.lean:145 `abbrev tateCohomology (n : ℤ) : ModuleCat R := (tateCohomologyFunctor n).obj M`; Tau Ceti TateCohomology/Restriction.lean (restriction to subgroups in degrees 0, −1 only). Confirmed the previous verdict after a wider search. The notion 'Ĥ^i(H', M) = 0 for all H' ≤ G and all i ∈ ℤ' is definable from Mathlib's tateCohomology but is not defined, and no layer plans it (or Nakayama's criterion 'cohomologically trivial + ℤ-torsion-free ⇒ projective'); the closest planned material is acyclicity of coinduced modules in positive ordinary degrees (ProfiniteCohomology Layer 7/10), which is neither all Tate degrees nor all subgroups.

items.name: 𝔒 is cohomologically trivial
items.statement: The middle term 𝔒 of the global Tate extension (139) (the extension of ΔG by C_H attached to the global fundamental class) is a cohomologically trivial G-module.
items.locator: App. A.3, proof of Lemma A.4 (the source l.3366)
items.note: External input (nsw Theorem 3.1.4(i) — Neukirch, Schmidt, Wingberg, Cohomology of number fields). With V cohomologically trivial and θ surjective, gives V^θ = ker θ cohomologically trivial. Evidence: ClassFieldTheory Layer 3 (the layer extract l.848–884; classical-1.json stages[131]): "State the generic theorem `tateTheorem` ... obtain tateIso (r : ℤ) : Ĥ^r(U/V,ℤ) ≃ Ĥ^{r+2}(U/V,A^V) as that theorem applied to the fundamental class"; Layer 0 audit (l.735): "No Tate's theorem in any form exists in either library." Layer 2 (l.815–846): "Define `ClassFormation` ... existence and uniqueness of the class of invariant 1/[U:V]; `fundamentalClass` generates H²". Layer 11 (l.1327–1370): "Package `globalInv` into `globalClassFormation`", audit: 'globalClassFormation ... | library: absent'. Paper: the source l.3140–3147 (extension (139) 0 → C_H → 𝔒 → ΔG → 0 'associated to the global fundamental class in H^2(G, C_H)') and l.3366 ('it is known that 𝔒 is cohomologically trivial [nsw, Theorem 3.1.4(i)]'). Tau Ceti NumberTheory/ClassFieldTheory/Formation/Basic.lean:361–371 only says the class-formation axioms and fundamental class 'are read here' and defines TateH/TrivialTateH abbreviations; no fundamental class or extension module exists. Confirmed planned, adding Layer 2 (which constructs the fundamental class that defines 𝔒). NSW 3.1.4(i) is Tate's theorem for a class formation in module form: cohomological triviality of the extension 𝔒 of ΔG by C_H attached to the fundamental class is equivalent, via the connecting maps of 0 → C_H → 𝔒 → ΔG → 0 and 0 → ΔG → ℤ[G] → ℤ → 0, to the cup-product isomorphisms tateIso in all degrees that Layer 3 plans; the global class formation supplying the fundamental class is Layer 11. […]

items.name: Ind_{G_w}^G 𝒪_w^* is cohomologically trivial for v unramified; (U_w^1)^{I_w} cohomologically trivial over G_w/I_w
items.statement: If v is a finite place of F unramified in H (in particular any v ∉ S' ∪ Σ', since S' ∪ Σ' ⊃ S_ram), then 𝒪_w^* is a cohomologically trivial G_w-module and hence Ind_{G_w}^G 𝒪_w^* is a cohomologically trivial G-module. The same argument shows that for any finite w, (U_w^1)^{I_w} is cohomologically trivial as a G_w/I_w-module.
items.locator: App. A.3, proof of Lemma A.4 (the source l.3368, 3371)
items.note: External input (cf §VI.1.2 Proposition 1 — Cassels–Fröhlich, Algebraic number theory (Serre, Local class field theory)). Cohomological triviality of the components of V away from S' ∪ Σ', and a step for U_w^1 at v ∈ Σ'. Evidence: Re-searched both pinned trees: rg -i 'cohomologically|CohomologicallyTrivial|cohomological triviality' over Mathlib and TauCeti returns only A∞ 'CohomologicallyUnital' and Frobenius 'nakayamaAut' hits. Mathlib has Tate cohomology only as a carrier (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/Basic.lean:145 `abbrev tateCohomology (n : ℤ) : ModuleCat R`) and Shapiro only for ordinary group (co)homology (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/Shapiro.lean), not Tate; Tau Ceti's TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/TateCohomology/{Restriction,Inflation,Periodic,HerbrandQuotient,...}.lean have res/cor/infl/periodicity but no vanishing theorem for unit modules, and TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/UnitFiltration/Basic.lean:88 `def unitFiltration (i : ℕ) : Subgroup Kˣ` is the carrier only. Atlas: a full scan of all 2001 stage descriptions in atlas/areas/*.json and roadmaps/*.json for 'cohomologically trivial', 'trivial cohomology', 'cohomology of units', 'Ĥ…unit' finds no stage. Nearest: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification#layer-2-unramified-extensions-and-frobenius (classical-1.json): 'For L/K unramified prove N_{L/K}(𝒪[L]ˣ) = 𝒪[K]ˣ, named map_norm_unitFiltration_zero … consumed by … the finite-Tate package ClassFieldTheory.tateH' (only Ĥ^0 = 0); tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-6-… (the layer extract l.1015-1068): 'Units are norms in this case'. Confirmed the previous verdict (missing). […]

items.name: Ind_{G_w}^G V_w is cohomologically trivial (Ritter–Weiss §3, Proposition 2)
items.statement: For every place v of F, the G-module Ind_{G_w}^G V_w, with V_w the Ritter–Weiss module of (136), is cohomologically trivial.
items.locator: App. A.3, proof of Lemma A.4 (the source l.3368)
items.note: External input (rw §3 Proposition 2 — Ritter, Weiss, A Tate sequence for global units). Cohomological triviality of the components of V at v ∈ S'. Evidence: atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json, stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): 'Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality.' Audit (the layer extract l.42): 'Ritter–Weiss modules, their presentations, comparison with class and ray-class groups, and Fitting-ideal functoriality | library: absent'. The only other atlas stages naming Ritter–Weiss are IntegralIwasawaTheory:KU-brumerstark (an aggregation checkpoint of I.6/I.7, 'not a new proof construction') and NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa:NE.6 (the noncommutative Ritter–Weiss main-conjecture route, unrelated to the local modules V_w). rg -i 'Ritter|Weiss' over both Lean trees: no hits. Confirmed the previous verdict. Ritter–Weiss §3 Prop 2 (Ind_{G_w}^G V_w cohomologically trivial) is a basic property of the local Ritter–Weiss module V_w of (136), which falls under 'the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations' owned by I.6; no more foundational owner exists (ClassFieldTheory Layer 0 supplies only generic Tate cohomology and names no local Tate-sequence module, and no stage mentions Tate sequences for units). Nothing in either library.

items.name: Nakayama's theorem: cohomologically trivial and ℤ-torsion-free implies projective
items.statement: A finitely generated ℤ[G]-module that is cohomologically trivial and ℤ-torsion-free is projective over ℤ[G].
items.locator: App. A.3, proof of Lemma A.4 (the source l.3375)
items.note: External input (nak Theorem 1 — Nakayama, On modules of trivial cohomology over a finite group II, Nagoya Math. J.). Deduces projectivity of V^θ from its cohomological triviality and torsion-freeness (from (150)). Evidence: Mathlib: Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Rep/Iso.lean:178 `Projective (free k G α)`, :193 `Projective (leftRegular k G)` (projectivity of free representations only); Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Coinduced.lean:315 `(resFunctor S.subtype).PreservesProjectiveObjects` (restriction preserves projectives). No declaration links Tate cohomology to projectivity; rg -i 'cohomologically' over both trees gives no Galois-module hit. Atlas: every 'Nakayama' occurrence in the 2001 stage descriptions is Tate–Nakayama (ClassFieldTheory Layer 0/4, EndoscopicTransfer ET.0), Murnaghan–Nakayama (SchurWeyl), the Nakayama automorphism (StablePeriodicCurved Layer 0), or Nakayama's lemma (KTheoryLowDegrees Z.2, PadicHodgeRegulators D.3, IntegralIwasawaTheory L2/L3, PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L5, ModularCurves Layer 8, P7, QW.2); none is the projectivity criterion. ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.7 plans 'group-ring modules for rings of integers, normal-basis maps, locally free class groups' (tame normal integral bases), not this theorem. Confirmed the previous verdict (missing). Nakayama's theorem (finitely generated, ℤ-torsion-free, cohomologically trivial ℤ[G]-module ⇒ ℤ[G]-projective; Nakayama 1957 Thm 1 / Serre LF IX §5 Thm 7) is absent from both libraries, which do not even define cohomological triviality, and no atlas stage names it: the nearest are ClassFieldTheory Layer 0 (generic Tate suppliers, Tate's theorem, Tate–Nakayama) and CA.7 (integral Galois modules), neither of which plans the projectivity criterion.

items.name: U_w^1 contains a cohomologically trivial open subgroup of ℓ-power index
items.statement: For a finite place w of H with residue characteristic ℓ, U_w^1 contains an open subgroup U_w' that is cohomologically trivial as a G_w-module (Cassels–Fröhlich Ch. VI, Prop. 3), and the index [U_w^1 : U_w'] is a power of ℓ. Hence if ℓ is invertible in R then (U_w^1)_R ≅ (U_w')_R.
items.locator: App. A.3, proof of Lemma A.4, adaptation to (A2') (the source l.3377–3378)
items.note: External input (cf Chapter VI Proposition 3 — Cassels–Fröhlich, Algebraic number theory). Replaces (A2) by (A2') in Lemma A.4(ii) when working over R with ℓ invertible. Evidence: atlas/areas/classical-1.json, stage tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-6-the-local-class-formation-and-finite-local-reciprocity (the layer extract l.1015-1068, sentence at l.1034): 'For local units, use a scaled normal-basis element to obtain an open stable lattice that is free over the group ring, then pass through the finite quotient into the unit filtration; do not assume that 𝒪_L itself is free over 𝒪_K[Γ], which holds only in the tame case.' Audit (l.1068): 'Local units: scaled normal-basis lattice, unit filtration, solvability … | library: partial | Unit filtration and its graded pieces are in Tau Ceti; the lattice argument … absent.' Tau Ceti: TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/UnitFiltration/Basic.lean:88 `def unitFiltration (i : ℕ) : Subgroup Kˣ` (carrier only; no Galois-cohomology statement). No stage mentions 'cohomologically trivial' anywhere in the atlas. Confirmed the previous verdict (planned), with a caveat. The Layer 6 sentence is exactly the Cassels–Fröhlich Ch. VI Prop 3 construction: a scaled normal-basis element x gives an open G_w-stable subgroup U_w' = exp/1+ of 𝒪_K[G]·x inside U_w^1 that is free over the group ring, hence induced and cohomologically trivial. The layer does not spell out 'cohomologically trivial', the ℓ-power index [U_w^1 : U_w'] (automatic since U_w^1 is pro-ℓ and U_w' open), or the consequence (U_w^1)_R ≅ (U_w')_R for ℓ invertible in R; these are immediate corollaries of the named construction, so I keep planned rather than missing, but at medium confidence. Nothing in either library beyond the unit-filtration carrier.

items.name: Lemma A.4(i): V^θ is projective of constant rank #S' − 1 under (A2)
items.statement: Assume the standing hypotheses of Appendix A, S' an auxiliary set, and (A2). Then the ℤ[G]-module V^θ = ker(θ: V → 𝔒) is projective with constant rank #S' − 1, i.e. dim_{Q̄} V^θ ⊗_{ℤ[G]} Q̄(χ) = #S' − 1 for every character χ: ℤ[G] → Q̄^*. Proof: (a) V is a product of cohomologically trivial modules: Ind 𝒪_w^* for v ∉ S' ∪ Σ', Ind V_w for v ∈ S', and Ind U_w^1 for v ∈ Σ', where under (A2) U_w^1 is G_w-cohomologically trivial because (U_w^1)^{I_w} is G_w/I_w-cohomologically trivial and multiplication by #I_w is invertible on the pro-ℓ group U_w^1; since 𝔒 is cohomologically trivial and θ surjective, V^θ is cohomologically trivial; (b) V^θ is ℤ-torsion-free by (150) since 𝒪_{H,Σ,Σ'}^* (by condition (1)) and B^θ are; Nakayama gives projectivity; (c) rank: by (151) dim(∇)_χ = dim(Z^θ)_χ = dim(X_{H,Σ})_χ + Σ_{v∈S'_ram} dim(Ind W_w^*)_χ, the Dirichlet unit theorem gives dim(𝒪_{H,Σ,Σ'}^*)_χ = dim(X_{H,Σ})_χ, so (150) yields dim V^θ_χ = dim B^θ_χ − Σ_{v∈S'_ram} dim(Ind W_w^*)_χ (eq (154)), each summand being 1 by (144), whence dim V^θ_χ = (#S' + #S'_ram − 1) − #S'_ram = #S' − 1.
items.locator: App. A.3, Lemma A.4 label l:projective, first statement (the source l.3358–3362); proof l.3364–3404, eq (154) label e:vbw
items.note: Makes (150) a projective presentation of ∇, so the Jannsen transpose is defined and, with (A1), the presentation is locally quadratic. Evidence: atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json, stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): 'Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality. This is also where the finitely generated module and finite-presentation hypotheses required by Kurihara's finite-level theorems are proved.' Audit (l.42): 'library: absent | Absent: neither library has Fitting ideals.' A scan of all atlas stage descriptions for 'V^θ', 'B^θ', '∇/nabla', 'projective … ℤ[G]/group ring' finds no other owner (∇ hits are gradients in OptimalTransport/HopfRinow). rg -i 'Ritter|Weiss|nabla|cohomologically' over both Lean trees: nothing relevant; Mathlib's only projectivity results for representations are free/regular ones (Rep/Iso.lean:178,193). Confirmed the previous verdict. Lemma A.4(i) (V^θ is ℤ[G]-projective of constant rank #S' − 1 under (A2)) is the projectivity input for the Ritter–Weiss presentation (150)/(155) of ∇ and so belongs to 'the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations' of I.6; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6 owns only generic 'Fitting ideals, projective presentations' over coefficient orders, not this module. Its inputs (items 161, 163) are missing and 162, 164 are planned elsewhere, so the item is planned but its proof route has unplanned ingredients.

items.name: Lemma A.4(ii): V^θ_R is projective of constant rank #S' − 1 under (A2')
items.statement: Assume the standing hypotheses of Appendix A, S' an auxiliary set, and (A2') for a ℤ[G]-algebra R. Then V^θ_R := V^θ ⊗_{ℤ[G]} R is a projective R-module of constant rank #S' − 1. (Proof as in (i), replacing U_w^1 for v ∈ Σ' by a cohomologically trivial open subgroup U_w' of ℓ-power index, which does not change the module after ⊗ R.)
items.locator: App. A.3, Lemma A.4 label l:projective, second statement (the source l.3358–3362, 3377–3378)
items.note: Version used in the main body over ℤ_p[G]-algebras. Evidence: atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json, stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): 'Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality.' Audit (l.42): 'Ritter–Weiss modules, their presentations … | library: absent'. No library declaration: rg for Ritter/Weiss/nabla/cohomologically in both trees finds nothing relevant; Mathlib has generic base change of projective modules (Module.Projective under tensor) but nothing about V^θ. Confirmed the previous verdict. Lemma A.4(ii) is the base-changed statement (V^θ ⊗_{ℤ[G]} R projective of constant rank #S' − 1 under (A2')), the form used over ℤ_p[G]-algebras; it is part of the Ritter–Weiss presentations planned in I.6. Its extra ingredient (item 164) is planned in ClassFieldTheory Layer 6.

items.name: Lemma A.5(i): locally quadratic presentation of ∇ over ℤ[G] under (A1),(A2)
items.statement: Assume (A1) and (A2). Then the exact sequence V^θ → B^θ → ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → 0 (eq (155)) is a locally quadratic presentation of ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H) over ℤ[G]: V^θ is projective of constant rank #S' − 1 (Lemma A.4(i)) and B^θ is free of rank #S' − 1 (by (149), since S'_ram = ∅), so after localising at any prime of ℤ[G] both become free of the same rank.
items.locator: App. A.3, Lemma A.5, eq (155) label e:pp (the source l.3406–3414)
items.note: Integral form of (P4). Evidence: atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json, stage IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.37): 'Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality.' Audit (l.42): 'library: absent | Absent: neither library has Fitting ideals.' Atlas scan for 'locally quadratic|quadratic presentation|quadratically presented' hits only tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ZigzagPreprojective#layer-1 (an unrelated algebra presentation). rg over both Lean trees for 'quadratic presentation|LocallyQuadratic|QuadraticPresentation|Fitting' (module sense): no hits (Mathlib's 'Fitting' hits are the Fitting decomposition in RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean:314 and Lie theory). Confirmed the previous verdict. items.name: Lemma A.5(ii): locally quadratic presentation of ∇_R over R under (A1),(A2')
items.statement: Assume (A1) and (A2') for a ℤ[G]-algebra R. Then the exact sequence V^θ_R → B^θ_R → ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R → 0 (eq (156)) is a locally quadratic presentation of ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R over R: V^θ_R is projective of constant rank #S' − 1 (Lemma A.4(ii)) and B^θ_R is free of rank #S' − 1.

items.name: Remark A.7 / Property (P4): over a ℤ_p[G]-algebra, V^θ_R is free and (∇)_R is quadratically presented
items.statement: Let R be a ℤ_p[G]-algebra and let Σ = {v ∈ S_ram : v | p} ∪ S_∞, Σ' = {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p} ∪ T be the sets (57),(59) of the main body. These sets satisfy (A1) and (A2') (every v ∈ Σ' ∩ S_ram has residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p, invertible in R). Since ℤ_p[G] is a product of local rings, the projective module of constant rank V^θ_R is free (of rank #S' − 1); hence (156) is a quadratic presentation R^{#S'−1} → R^{#S'−1} → ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R → 0. In particular (P4): the ℤ_p[G]-module (∇_Σ^{Σ'})_p = ∇_Σ^{Σ'} ⊗ ℤ_p is quadratically presented.
items.locator: App. A.3, Remark A.7 (the source l.3430–3432); stated as §6 property (P4) label i:qp (l.1621–1622)

items.name: The transpose ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^{tr} (eq (157))
items.statement: Assume (A2) (not necessarily (A1)). The transpose of ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H) associated to the projective presentation (155) is ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^{tr} := coker((B^θ)^* → (V^θ)^*), with (·)^* = Hom_{ℤ[G]}(·, ℤ[G]) carrying the contragredient action (82). Under (A2') the transpose ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^{tr}_R of ∇_R is defined likewise from (156).
items.locator: App. A.4 Transpose of ∇, eq (157) label e:ntdef (the source l.3434–3445)
items.note: The canonical transpose whose identification with Sel is (P3). Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.32-44): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups" — ∇^{tr} is the transpose of the projective presentation (155) of the Ritter–Weiss module and is property (P3)'s carrier. Library near miss verified: TauCeti/Algebra/Module/AuslanderReiten/Transpose.lean:94 `def AuslanderReitenTranspose (p₁ : P₁ →ₗ[A] P₀) : Type _ := Module.Dual A P₁ ⧸ LinearMap.range (p₁.lcomp Aᵐᵒᵖ A)` for an arbitrary ring A: the generic cokernel of Hom_A(P₀,A) → Hom_A(P₁,A) with the natural Aᵐᵒᵖ-module structure, not the ℤ[G]-module Hom_{ℤ[G]}(·,ℤ[G]) with the contragredient action (82) applied to V^θ → B^θ. rg -i 'jannsen|ritter' in both trees: no hits. No atlas stage names Jannsen's transpose (rg 'Jannsen' hits only MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.1/MC.3/MC.7, on motives). Confirmed planned. AuslanderReitenTranspose exists as stated but is a different convention (Aᵐᵒᵖ action rather than the #-twisted ℤ[G]-action) and the input presentation (155)/(156) of ∇ is absent, so it is a near miss, not library. I.6 is the only layer naming the Ritter–Weiss module and its presentations; no more foundational owner names the transpose over ℤ[G].

items.name: Lemma A.8(i): ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^{tr} ≅ Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) under (A2)
items.statement: Assume the standing hypotheses of Appendix A, S' an auxiliary set, and (A2) (but not necessarily (A1)). With ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^{tr} defined by (157), there is an isomorphism of ℤ[G]-modules ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^{tr} ≅ Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H), where Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) = Hom_ℤ(H_{Σ'}^*, ℤ)/∏_{w ∉ Σ_H ∪ Σ'_H} ℤ (eq (29)) ≅ Hom_ℤ(𝒪_{H,S',Σ'}^*, ℤ)/∏_{w ∈ S'_H − Σ_H} ℤ (eq (31), bks eq (12)) with contragredient action. Proof: using the natural isomorphism Hom_ℤ(−, ℤ) ≅ Hom_{ℤ[G]}(−, ℤ[G]), φ ↦ (m ↦ Σ_g φ(gm)[g^{-1}]), write 𝓕 = Hom_ℤ(−, ℤ); applying 𝓕 to (148) (Z^θ ℤ-free) gives 𝓕(B^θ) ↠ 𝓕(W^θ), so 0 → 𝓕(W^θ) → 𝓕(V^θ) → ∇^{tr} → 0 (eq (158), left injectivity since Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) is finite); the snake lemma on (141) with Cl_{S'}^{Σ'}(H) = 1 gives 0 → 𝒪_{H,S',Σ'}^* → V^θ → (W')^θ → 0 (eq (159)) and dually 0 → 𝓕((W')^θ) → 𝓕(V^θ) → 𝓕(𝒪_{H,S',Σ'}^*) → 0 (eq (160)); V^θ → (W')^θ factors through W^θ → (W')^θ (α_w at v ∈ S' − Σ, identity at v ∈ Σ), which by (144) sits in 0 → Y_{H,S'−Σ} → W^θ → (W')^θ → 0 (eq (161)); the snake lemma on the resulting diagram yields ∇^{tr} ≅ coker(α: 𝓕(Y_{H,S'−Σ}) → 𝓕(𝒪_{H,S',Σ'}^*)) (eq (162)) with α(φ)(x) = φ((ord_w(x))_{w ∈ (S'−Σ)_H}), which is exactly (31). (A version when Σ ⊃ S_ram is in bks.)

items.name: Lemma A.8(ii) / Property (P3): ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^{tr}_R ≅ Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R under (A2')
items.statement: Assume the standing hypotheses of Appendix A, S' an auxiliary set, and (A2') for a ℤ[G]-algebra R. The transpose of ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R associated to the projective presentation (156) satisfies ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^{tr}_R ≅ Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R := Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) ⊗_{ℤ[G]} R as R^#-modules (proof as in (i)). In particular (P3): for the sets (57),(59) of §6 and R = ℤ_p[G], the ℤ_p[G]-module (∇_Σ^{Σ'})_p has the canonical transpose (∇_Σ^{Σ'})_p^{tr} (from (156)) and (∇_Σ^{Σ'})_p^{tr} ≅ Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_p.

items.name: Explicit cocycle for λ (eq (163))
items.statement: Assume (A1), 2 inverted, M = Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^-, ϖ: G_H → Gal(L/H) ≅ M the reciprocity homomorphism, and c ∈ G_F a fixed complex conjugation. The function λ(g) = ϖ(g c g^{-1} c^{-1})^{1/2} (m^{1/2} the unique square root of m in the finite abelian group M of odd order) is a well-defined 1-cocycle on G_F with values in M representing the unique class λ ∈ H^1(G_F, M) with res^{G_F}_{G_H} λ = ϖ; indeed for g ∈ G_H, since c acts as inversion on M, ϖ(c g^{-1} c^{-1}) = ϖ(g) and λ(g) = ϖ(g^2)^{1/2} = ϖ(g).
items.locator: App. A.5 Extension class via Galois cohomology, eq (163) label e:kappadef2 (the source l.3513–3528)
items.note: Used in Lemma A.9 to identify the snake-map computation with λ_v. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.32-44): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups" — the cocycle λ(g) = ϖ(gcg^{-1}c^{-1})^{1/2} with res λ = ϖ is the device of Lemma A.9 establishing (P2), the extension-class comparison of ∇ with Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^-. Library check: Mathlib/GroupTheory/OrderOfElement.lean:1255 `noncomputable def powCoprime {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : (Nat.card G).Coprime n) : G ≃ G` (square root in odd-order group, generic); Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/LowDegree.lean:276 `def cocycles₁ : Submodule k (G → A)`, l.961 `abbrev H1 := groupCohomology A 1`, l.964 `def H1π` (generic k-linear 1-cocycles/H^1, no continuity, no Galois-group reciprocity map ϖ, no minus part). Atlas: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.6 (motivic/modular catalogue) constructs cocycles for the DKSW extension theorem "a continuous class in H¹(G,M(chi/psi)) whose every representative cocycle generates M", a different object; no stage mentions a commutator-with-complex-conjugation cocycle (rg 'complex conjugation' hits are unrelated: PS.0, G7, R12.6, HE.0). Confirmed planned with low confidence: I.6 names the comparison of ∇ with the class group (whose proof is Lemma A.9), not this explicit cocycle; no library declaration gives ϖ, M = Cl^- or the well-definedness of λ.

items.name: Ritter–Weiss augmentation sequence for G̃ = Gal(L/F) (eq (164))
items.statement: Let G̃ = Gal(L/F) (an extension of G by M), ΔG̃ the augmentation ideal of ℤ[G̃] and Δ(G̃, M) the kernel of ℤ[G̃] → ℤ[G]. There is a canonical short exact sequence 0 → M ≅ Δ(G̃,M)/Δ(G̃,M)ΔG̃ → ΔG̃/Δ(G̃,M)ΔG̃ → ΔG → 0, where the explicit isomorphism M ≅ Δ(G̃,M)/Δ(G̃,M)ΔG̃ (Ritter–Weiss p. 155) sends m ∈ M to the class of m̃ − 1; in particular the class of (g̃c̃g̃^{-1}c̃^{-1} − 1)(c̃g̃) corresponds to g̃c̃g̃^{-1}c̃^{-1} ∈ M.
items.locator: App. A.5, eq (164) label e:rw (the source l.3541–3550), and l.3563–3566
items.note: External input (rw p. 155 — Ritter, Weiss, A Tate sequence for global units). Target of the map ρ that computes the snake map W^θ → M explicitly. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.32-44): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups" — the sequence (164) is the target of the Ritter–Weiss map ρ that computes the snake map W^θ → Cl of the Ritter–Weiss sequence. These give ΔG̃ and Δ(G̃,M) with generators but no quotient ΔG̃/Δ(G̃,M)ΔG̃, no isomorphism M ≅ Δ(G̃,M)/Δ(G̃,M)ΔG̃ (m ↦ m̃−1) and no exact sequence. Mathlib: only Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/IsAugmentation.lean:31 `def IsAugmentation ... : Prop := IsCompl 1 (I.restrictScalars R)`, a predicate. Atlas: rg -i 'augmentation' over areas/*.json and roadmaps/*.json: group-ring hits are PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1/L3 (augmentation of O[[G]], pseudo-measures), NE.0 (restriction/induction and augmentation for Iwasawa algebras), ES.3 (norm/derivative identities); none names the relative augmentation ideal Δ(G̃,M) or the sequence (164). items.name: Explicit description of the snake map W^θ → M via ρ (Ritter–Weiss Theorem 5)
items.statement: Ritter–Weiss associate to each w ∈ W an element ρ(w) ∈ ΔG̃/Δ(G̃,M)ΔG̃; when w ∈ W^θ the image of ρ(w) in ΔG is trivial, so ρ(w) lies in M ≅ Δ(G̃,M)/Δ(G̃,M)ΔG̃, and w ↦ ρ(w) is the connecting (snake) map W^θ → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → M of (142) composed with projection to the minus part. On components: for v ∈ Σ, where the component of W is Ind_{G_v}^G ΔG_v = ℤ[G] ⊗_{ℤ[G_v]} ΔG_v ⊂ ℤ[G], ρ_v((1 − c) ⊗ (g − 1)) = (1 − c̃)(g̃ − 1); for v' ∈ S' − Σ unramified with component ℤ[G] ⊗_{ℤ[G_{v'}]} ℤ[G_{v'}] = ℤ[G], ρ_{v'}((g − 1) ⊗ 1) = (g̃ − 1)(c̃ − 1), where g̃, c̃ ∈ G̃ are lifts of g and of c = Frob_{v'} lying in the decomposition groups at v and v' respectively. Consequently ρ(2(g−1)x̃) = g̃c̃ − c̃g̃ for the lift x̃ of Lemma A.9.
items.locator: App. A.5, proof of Lemma A.9 (the source l.3540–3562)
items.note: External input (rw Theorem 5 — Ritter, Weiss, A Tate sequence for global units). Computes γ_v(g) for the explicit lift x̃ and yields γ_v = λ_v in Lemma A.9. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract l.32-44): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality"; audit note "Ritter–Weiss modules, their presentations, comparison with class and ray-class groups ... | library: absent". Ritter–Weiss Theorem 5 is the explicit description of the connecting map W^θ → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) via ρ. Readiness checkpoint ... verify completion and map-level compatibility of IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6, I.7. This is an aggregation of those owners, not a new proof construction" — so I.6 is the owner. items.name: Trivial-zero-free character set Ψ and quotient R_Ψ
items.statement: Setting: p an odd prime, O a finite extension of Z_p containing all character values, G = Gal(H/F) = G_p × G' (G_p the p-Sylow subgroup, G' the prime-to-p part), χ a totally odd character of G', R = O[G_p]_χ the corresponding connected component of O[G], Σ, Σ' as in §5, Θ = Θ_{Σ,Σ'}. Define Ψ = { ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ|_{G'} = χ and ψ(v) ≠ 1 for all v ∈ Σ } (the characters belonging to χ without a trivial zero, i.e. with L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ, 0) ≠ 0), and let R_Ψ be the character group ring quotient of R associated to Ψ (§2.2): the image of O[G] → ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O_ψ, x ↦ (ψ(x))_ψ. By construction the map R_Ψ ↪ ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O, x ↦ (ψ(x))_{ψ∈Ψ}, is an injective ring homomorphism (equation (96), label e:rembed). Convention (line 1761): for the rest of the paper R denotes R_Ψ.
items.locator: §7.1 (label s:replacer), displayed definition of Ψ before Lemma 7.1; the embedding (96) (label e:rembed) in the proof of Lemma 7.2
items.note: Replaces the component O[G_p]_χ by the quotient in which Θ^# is a non-zerodivisor; all constructions of §8–§9 are over this ring and elements of it are recognised through their specialisations (96). Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract l.45-59): "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma ..., the Fitting-ideal comparison" — R_Ψ is the coefficient ring over which §§7–9 of that proof run. PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4 (the layer extract l.251-258): "For Delta finite abelian of order prime to p, construct integral character idempotents after adjoining character values and prove componentwise comparisons" — plans the decomposition O[G] = ∏_χ O[G_p]_χ into components R = O[G_p]_χ over characters χ of the prime-to-p part G'. IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.1 was checked as a possible more foundational owner: it only constructs Z_p[[G∞]] and warns "If p divides the finite group order, integral character idempotents need not exist", so it does not plan the component decomposition. Library: Mathlib/GroupTheory/Sylow.lean:912 `noncomputable def directProductOfNormal [Finite G] (hn : ∀ {p} [Fact p.Prime] (P : Sylow p G), P.Normal) : (∀ p : (Nat.card G).primeFactors, ∀ P : Sylow p G, P) ≃* G` gives G ≅ ∏ Sylow subgroups only; no character-group-ring quotient, no trivial-zero condition ψ(v) ≠ 1 for v ∈ Σ, no embedding (96). Atlas: rg -i 'trivial[ -]zero' hits only AN.1/AN.3 (Dirichlet L-functions) and QuadraticFormInvariants (Hilbert symbol); rg -i 'character group ring|group[ -]ring quotient|components? of the group ring' returns nothing. […]

items.name: Θ^# is a non-zerodivisor in R_Ψ
items.statement: With R = R_Ψ the trivial-zero-free character group ring quotient of O[G_p]_χ and Θ = Θ_{Σ,Σ'}, the image of Θ^# in R_Ψ is a non-zerodivisor. (Asserted without proof; it follows from the injectivity of R_Ψ ↪ ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O and ψ(Θ^#) = L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ, 0) ≠ 0 for every ψ ∈ Ψ.)
items.locator: §7.1, sentence following the proof of Lemma 7.1 (line 1761: "The image of Θ^# is a non-zerodivisor in R")
items.note: Allows the argument of §8–§9 to divide by Θ^# (e.g. Θ^# divides p^m in R, the modules R/xΘ^#, the constant-term computations); it is the reason for passing to R_Ψ. Evidence: Catalogue atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json, IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7: "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations. Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, ... the Fitting-ideal comparison"; IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6: "Construct equivariant Artin L-functions for the abelian CM extensions used in the modern proof, their S- and T-modifications, integral Stickelberger elements". items.name: Lemma 7.1: reduction to the trivial-zero-free quotient
items.statement: Let R = O[G_p]_χ and let R_Ψ be the character group ring quotient of R associated to Ψ = { ψ : ψ|_{G'} = χ, ψ(v) ≠ 1 for all v ∈ Σ }. Suppose Fitt_{R_Ψ}(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R_Ψ}) ⊂ (Θ^#) in R_Ψ (equation (87), Θ = Θ_{Σ,Σ'}). Then Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R) ⊂ (Θ^#) in R (equation (88)). Proof: let Ψ' = { ψ : ψ|_{G'} = χ, ψ(v) = 1 for some v ∈ Σ } and R_Ψ' the associated character group ring quotient; since Ψ ⊔ Ψ' is the set of characters belonging to χ, the canonical map ι = (ι_1, ι_2) : R → R_Ψ × R_Ψ' is injective. By Corollary 6.2, Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R) = (x) is principal; by Lemma 3.2, ι_2(x) = 0 = ι_2(Θ^#); by (87), ι_1(x) = y·ι_1(Θ^#) for some y ∈ R_Ψ; for any lift ỹ ∈ R of y, x − ỹΘ^# is killed by ι_1 and ι_2, hence x = ỹΘ^#.
items.locator: §7.1, Lemma 7.1, equations (87) (label e:rpsi) and (88) (label e:rpsipsi)
items.note: Shows that the inclusion of Theorem 5.1 may be proved over the trivial-zero-free quotient R_Ψ, where Ribet's method is run in §8–§9. The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... Include ... the Fitting-ideal comparison, and the passage from modified to unmodified data." Library re-search: rg -il 'fitting ?ideal|FittingIdeal|Fitt_' over both pinned trees returns no file (the layer extract line 42/249/269 audits: "neither library has Fitting ideals"); no Selmer module Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) or character group ring quotient exists. Checked PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6 (generic Fitting ideals over O-orders, "reusing the generic Fitting algebra of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants") and IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.6 (abstract Ribet lemma, "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses"): neither names the reduction to the trivial-zero-free quotient. Confirmed the previous verdict (planned). Lemma 7.1 is a proof step of the Dasgupta–Kakde theorem (reduction of Fitt_R(Sel) ⊂ (Θ^#) from R = O[G_p]_χ to R_Ψ using the principal Fitting ideal of Cor. 6.2, Lemma 3.2 and injectivity of R → R_Ψ × R_Ψ'); I.7 plans the whole proof and its Fitting-ideal comparison. The generic Fitting-ideal algebra it uses is owned by IHG/L6 but those layers do not plan this lemma. Not library: no Fitting ideals in either pinned tree.

items.name: GL_2^+(F) and its action on H^n
items.statement: H is the complex upper half plane with the usual action of GL_2^+(R) (real 2×2 matrices of positive determinant) by linear fractional transformations. GL_2^+(F) is the group of 2×2 matrices over F with totally positive determinant. A fixed ordering of the n = [F:Q] real embeddings F ↪ R gives an embedding GL_2^+(F) ↪ GL_2^+(R)^n and hence an action of GL_2^+(F) on H^n, componentwise.
items.locator: §7.2.1 Hilbert modular forms, first paragraph (line 1769)
items.note: Basic setting for Hilbert modular forms (following Shimura, shim, and ddp §2.1). Evidence: Catalogue atlas/areas (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H0): "Construct the restriction-of-scalars group and the scalar-determinant subgroup. ... Identify the conjugacy domains: for `G` all independent upper/lower half-plane choices occur, while the standard `G*` conjugacy class has the common-sign components." Library near misses read in the pinned trees: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Defs.lean:343 `def GLPos : Subgroup (GL n R) := (Units.posSubgroup R).comap GeneralLinearGroup.det` (positive determinant over one linearly ordered ring, giving GL(2,ℝ)⁺ only); Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/UpperHalfPlane/MoebiusAction.lean (GL(2,ℝ) acting on the single ℍ); TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/TotallyPositive.lean:36 `NumberField.IsTotallyPositive` (totally positive elements of a number field, no matrix group). rg for 'Fin .* → ℍ', 'ℍ ^', 'Hilbert modular' in both trees: only Mathlib SlashActions.lean:223/245 `prod_slash` lemmas for finite products of one-variable slashes, not an action on ℍ^n. Confirmed the previous verdict (planned). No library declaration gives GL₂⁺(F) (totally positive determinant over a totally real F) or its componentwise action on ℍ^n via the real embeddings; Mathlib's GLPos and Möbius action are the single-real-place case. H0 plans the Hilbert Shimura datum Res_{F/ℚ}GL₂ with domain (ℍ^±)^n, a clearly containing target; no more exact owner names GL₂⁺(F) acting on ℍ^n (OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O2 has Hilbert automorphy factors only on the p-adic anticanonical tower).

items.name: Congruence subgroup Γ_λ(n)
items.statement: For each class λ of the narrow class group Cl^+(F) fix a representative fractional ideal t_λ. Let d be the different of F and n ⊂ O_F an ideal. Then Γ_λ(n) = { (a b; c d) ∈ GL_2^+(F) : a, d ∈ O_F, c ∈ t_λ d n, b ∈ (t_λ d)^{-1}, ad − bc ∈ O_F^*, d ≡ 1 (mod n) }.
items.locator: §7.2.1, displayed definition of Γ_λ(n) (lines 1772–1778)
items.note: The level-n groups whose invariants form the λ-components of Hilbert modular forms of level n. Evidence: Catalogue (HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H1): "Define a `𝔠`-polarization through an ordered invertible `𝒪_F`-module `𝔠` ... Construct the moduli problem with tame level `µ_N` and the variants needed for `K`, `K₀`, and `K₁` level. ... Keep the fractional-ideal labels, their changes by totally positive elements, and their effect on pairings visible. Prove the trace/different dictionary"; H3: "Construct the maps associated with changing `𝔠`, and the disjoint union over polarization classes needed for Hecke operators. Compare different lists of ideal representatives using explicit comparison isomorphisms." Library near misses read: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CongruenceSubgroups.lean (Gamma0/Gamma1 of SL(2,ℤ) only); TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/NarrowClassGroup/Basic.lean:83 `def NarrowClassGroup : Type _` (carrier only, no chosen representatives t_λ); rg for 'Gamma_λ|Γ_λ|Gamma1.*𝔫|congruence subgroup.*number field' in both trees: nothing over a general totally real field. Confirmed the previous verdict (planned). Γ_λ(n) is the arithmetic group of the K₁(n)-level component attached to the polarization class t_λ (with the different 𝔡 in the lattice); H1 plans the K₁-level Hilbert moduli with fractional-ideal labels and the trace/different dictionary, and H3 the components indexed by ideal-class representatives, so it is planned as a containing target. Not library: the only congruence subgroups are Γ₀(N), Γ₁(N) ⊂ SL(2,ℤ), and the narrow class group exists only as an abstract carrier.

items.name: Weight-k slash action f|_{α,k}
items.statement: For k a positive integer, f : H^n → C holomorphic and α = (a b; c d) ∈ GL_2^+(F), f|_{α,k}(z_1, …, z_n) = N(det α)^{k/2} ∏_{i=1}^n (c_i z_i + d_i)^{-k} f((a_1 z_1 + b_1)/(c_1 z_1 + d_1), …, (a_n z_n + b_n)/(c_n z_n + d_n)), where a_i, b_i, c_i, d_i are the images of a, b, c, d under the i-th real embedding of F and N is the norm F → Q.
items.locator: §7.2.1, displayed formula for f_λ|_{α,k} (line 1782)
items.note: Defines modularity and the Fourier expansions at cusps. Evidence: Catalogue (AutomorphicBundles:B4): "Define classical modular and cuspidal forms as sections of the canonical and subcanonical extensions. Prove the analytic transformation-law comparison, including the growth condition and the actual cocycle identity `j(γ₁γ₂,z)=j(γ₁,γ₂z)j(γ₂,z)` for a left action. Derive the appropriate right-action formula ... For Hilbert varieties over a splitting coefficient field, identify the factors `ω_τ`, determinant twists, and the parity/central-character condition for arithmetic weights." Library near miss read: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/SlashActions.lean:36 `class SlashAction (β G α : Type*) [Monoid G] [AddMonoid α]` and line 91–92 `private def privateSlash (k : ℤ) (γ : GL (Fin 2) ℝ) (f : ℍ → ℂ) (x : ℍ) : ℂ := σ γ (f (γ • x)) * |γ.det.val| ^ (k - 1) * UpperHalfPlane.denom γ x ^ (-k)` (one variable, GL(2,ℝ), normalisation |det|^{k-1}); lines 223/245 `prod_slash_sum_weights`/`prod_slash` are products of one-variable slashes over an index type, not an n-variable action of GL₂⁺(F). OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O2 ("Hilbert automorphy factors and domains") is the p-adic anticanonical-tower factor κ(cz+d), not the analytic slash. Confirmed the previous verdict (planned). The Hilbert weight-k slash f|_{α,k} = N(det α)^{k/2} ∏(c_i z_i+d_i)^{-k} f(α z) on ℍ^n is planned by B4 through the analytic transformation law with per-embedding factors ω_τ and determinant twists for Hilbert varieties; Mathlib's SlashAction is the F = ℚ case with a different determinant normalisation, hence a near miss, not library.

items.name: Hilbert modular forms M_k(n)
items.statement: For a positive integer k and an ideal n ⊂ O_F, M_k(n) is the space of Hilbert modular forms for F of level n and weight k: tuples f = (f_λ)_{λ ∈ Cl^+(F)} of holomorphic functions f_λ : H^n → C such that f_λ|_{α,k} = f_λ for all λ ∈ Cl^+(F) and all α ∈ Γ_λ(n). (The definition follows Shimura, shim, see also ddp §2.1; for F = Q the holomorphy-at-cusps condition of the reference is understood.)
items.locator: §7.2.1, definition of M_k(n) (lines 1780–1781)
items.note: External input (shim (Shimura); ddp §2.1). The ambient space in which the Eisenstein series and cusp forms of §8–§9 live. Evidence: Catalogue (AutomorphicBundles:B4): "Define classical modular and cuspidal forms as sections ... Prove the analytic transformation-law comparison ... For Hilbert varieties over a splitting coefficient field, identify the factors `ω_τ`, determinant twists, and the parity/central-character condition for arithmetic weights" (the layer extract line 4598 audit: "Hilbert modular forms are not defined in either library"). These general Hilbert modular constructions must be imported from a verified supplier or implemented as the Iwasawa proof's explicit prerequisite". items.name: Hecke operators T_q, U_q and diamond operators S(m)
items.statement: M_k(n) carries the action of the Hecke algebra generated by the operators T_q for primes q ∤ n, U_q for primes q | n, and the diamond operators S(m) for each class m ∈ G_n^+, the narrow ray class group of F of conductor n. The operators are those of Shimura, shim §2.
items.locator: §7.2.2 Hecke Operators (lines 1787–1795)
items.note: External input (shim §2). The Hecke algebra of §9 is generated by these operators; the eigenvalue, nebentypus and preservation statements of §7.2.6, §7.2.9 and §7.3 refer to them. Evidence: Catalogue (AutomorphicBundles:B5): "Construct pullback, coefficient identification, and trace along Hecke correspondences. State all scalar normalizations and prove composition against the existing abstract Hecke algebra." OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O6: "Construct tame Hecke and diamond operators and the p-level correspondences, including the operators at primes `𝔭|p`. Define them as pullback, coefficient identification, and trace. ... `U_p=∏_{𝔭|p}U_𝔭^{e_𝔭}`". HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H3: "the disjoint union over polarization classes needed for Hecke operators ... A Hecke correspondence can move between polarization components". Other catalogue hits for 'diamond operator' (ModularSymbolsPadicLFunctions:L0, ModularCurvesPartII:R12.6/R14.1, tauceti ModularForms layers 0/2) are GL₂/ℚ only. Confirmed the previous verdict (planned). […]

items.name: Cusps of Γ_λ(n), equation (89)
items.statement: cusps(Γ_λ(n)) = Γ_λ(n) \ GL_2^+(F) / { (a b; 0 d) ∈ GL_2^+(F) }, a finite set, in bijection with Γ_λ(n) \ P^1(F) via (a b; c d) ↦ (a : c).
items.locator: §7.2.3 Cusps, q-expansions and cusp forms, equation (89) (label e:cuspsdef)
items.note: Index set for the constant terms of Hilbert modular forms at each λ-component. Evidence: Catalogue (AutomorphicBundles:B5): "Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps and Fourier–Jacobi expansions at the relevant higher-dimensional boundary components. ... Identify cuspidality with the appropriate boundary vanishing condition." ShimuraCompactifications:C6: "Construct the Hilbert toroidal and minimal models used around the ordinary locus, with their cusp lattice, positivity cone, and unit quotient ... For `g>1`, prove the precise Koecher extension theorem needed for Hilbert sections." (Also ShimuraVarieties:V2 "rational boundary components and their incidence" and HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H5 "zero-dimensional rational boundary components" for a real quadratic field.)
