Confirmed the previous verdict (planned) but corrected the evidence: `IsCusp`/`CuspOrbits` live in Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps.lean (lines 58/168), not BoundedAtCusp.lean. […]

items.name: cusps(n) and the cusp [𝒜] of a pair 𝒜 = (A, λ), equation (90)
items.statement: cusps(n) = ⨆_{λ ∈ Cl^+(F)} cusps(Γ_λ(n)). A pair 𝒜 = (A, λ) with A ∈ GL_2^+(F) and λ ∈ Cl^+(F) determines the cusp [𝒜] ∈ cusps(n), the image of A in cusps(Γ_λ(n)) placed in the λ-component of the disjoint union.
items.locator: §7.2.3, equation (90) (label e:disjoint) and the following sentence
items.note: Cusps of level n; the constant terms of all forms in §8 are indexed by these. Evidence: ShimuraCompactifications:C6 (atlas/areas/modular-1.json): "Construct the Hilbert toroidal and minimal models used around the ordinary locus, with their cusp lattice, positivity cone, and unit quotient" — the cusps of Γ_λ(n) are the boundary points of the minimal model. HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H3: "Construct the maps associated with changing 𝔠, and the disjoint union over polarization classes needed for Hecke operators. Compare different lists of ideal representatives using explicit comparison isomorphisms" (audit the layer extract:4311: the indexing set is the narrow class group, built in TauCeti, but the components do not exist). AutomorphicBundles:B5: "Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps". Library check: rg -i 'hilbert modular|HilbertModular' over Mathlib/ and TauCeti/ is empty; Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps.lean:58 `IsCusp (c : OnePoint ℝ) (𝒢 : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ))` and TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps/Basic.lean are cusps of subgroups of GL(2,ℝ) on the single upper half-plane; TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/NarrowClassGroup/Basic.lean:83 `NumberField.NarrowClassGroup K` gives only the index set Cl⁺(F). Confirmed planned; reordered owners. The set cusps(Γ_λ(n)) = Γ_λ(n)\P¹(F) is the boundary of the minimal compactification owned by C6, the disjoint union over λ ∈ Cl⁺(F) is H3's disjoint union over polarization classes, and B5 consumes these as 'Hilbert cusps'. No stage names Γ_λ(n)\P¹(F) or the pair-to-cusp map [𝒜] literally, but the boundary of the minimal Hilbert model plus the class-indexed components clearly contain it. Not library: only the ℚ-case cusps and the bare narrow class group exist.

items.name: Fourier expansion at a pair 𝒜 and raw coefficients a_𝒜(b), equation (91)
items.statement: For f = (f_λ) ∈ M_k(n) and a pair 𝒜 = (A, λ), the function f_λ|_{A,k} has a Fourier expansion f_λ|_{A,k}(z) = a_𝒜(0) + Σ_{b ∈ a, b ≫ 0} a_𝒜(b) e_F(bz), where a is a certain lattice in F depending on 𝒜, b ≫ 0 means b totally positive, and e_F(bz) = exp(2πi(b_1 z_1 + ⋯ + b_n z_n)) with b_i the i-th real embedding of b. When A = 1 the lattice a is the ideal t_λ.
items.locator: §7.2.3, equation (91) (label e:fourier); the identification a = t_λ for A = 1 is in §7.2.4 (line 1843)
items.note: External input (shim). Defines the raw Fourier coefficients a_𝒜(b), which are then normalised to c_𝒜(b, f). Evidence: AutomorphicBundles:B5: "Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps and Fourier–Jacobi expansions at the relevant higher-dimensional boundary components. Prove the expansion principle with the necessary connectedness, base, and coefficient assumptions." AutomorphicBundles:B4: "Define classical modular and cuspidal forms as sections of the canonical and subcanonical extensions. Prove the analytic transformation-law comparison, including the growth condition and the actual cocycle identity" (the analytic f_λ|_{A,k} side). ShimuraCompactifications:C6: "with their cusp lattice, positivity cone, and unit quotient" (the lattice 𝔞 and the totally positive cone b ≫ 0 over which (91) is summed). Library: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/QExpansion.lean:162 `UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion (f : ℍ → ℂ) : PowerSeries ℂ` (namespace UpperHalfPlane opened at line 156) is a one-variable power series in q = exp(2πiτ/h) for functions on the single upper half-plane; TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/QExpansion/Basic.lean:63 `ModularForm.qExpansionLinearMap` likewise for Γ ≤ GL(2,ℝ). Confirmed planned; owners corrected. The previous note cited `ModularForm.qExpansion` — the declaration at QExpansion.lean:162 is `UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion`; still only the F = ℚ, one-variable case, so a near miss. The n-variable expansion f_λ|_{A,k}(z) = a_𝒜(0) + Σ_{b∈𝔞, b≫0} a_𝒜(b) e_F(bz) over the totally positive cone of the cusp lattice is B5's q-expansion at a Hilbert cusp, compared with the analytic form by B4, with the cusp lattice/positivity cone from C6. […]

items.name: Ideal b_𝒜 attached to a pair
items.statement: For 𝒜 = (A, λ) with A = (a *; c *), the fractional ideal b_𝒜 = a O_F + c (t_λ d)^{-1}, where d is the different of F.
items.locator: §7.2.3, displayed definition of b_𝒜 (line 1822)
items.note: Enters the normalisation of Fourier coefficients and the definition of the integral ideal c_𝒜. Evidence: ShimuraCompactifications:C6: "Construct the Hilbert toroidal and minimal models used around the ordinary locus, with their cusp lattice, positivity cone, and unit quotient." AutomorphicBundles:B5: "Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps". Paper (the source line 1822): b_𝒜 = a𝒪_F + c(t_λ𝔡)^{-1} for A = (a *; c *), the ideal invariant of the cusp (a:c) that fixes the lattice 𝔞 of (91) and normalises the coefficients. Library: Mathlib has `FractionalIdeal` and `differentIdeal` as raw material; rg for 'cusp' in Mathlib/NumberTheory and TauCeti/NumberTheory finds only the GL(2,ℝ)/OnePoint ℝ cusps (Cusps.lean:58), nothing attaching an ideal of a number field to a cusp. Confirmed planned, low confidence, with C6 promoted to owner. No stage names b_𝒜 itself; but the lattice at a Hilbert cusp (the 'cusp lattice' C6 names) is exactly the datum b_𝒜 encodes for the cusp A·∞ of Γ_λ(n), and any construction of B5's q-expansion at a Hilbert cusp has to fix this ideal to state the coefficient normalisation. Strictly a containing target, not a named object, hence low confidence rather than missing.

items.name: Normalised Fourier coefficients c_𝒜(b, f)
items.statement: For f ∈ M_k(n) and a pair 𝒜 = (A, λ), c_𝒜(b, f) = a_𝒜(b) · (N t_λ)^{-k/2} · (N b_𝒜)^{-k} · (N det A)^{k/2}, for b = 0 and for b ∈ a totally positive.
items.locator: §7.2.3, displayed definition of c_𝒜(b, f) (line 1825)
items.note: The normalised constant term c_𝒜(0, f) is what is computed at each cusp in §8 and what defines cuspidality. Evidence: AutomorphicBundles:B5: "Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps ... Prove the expansion principle with the necessary connectedness, base, and coefficient assumptions. Identify cuspidality with the appropriate boundary vanishing condition. These expansions provide normalization tests for the p-adic comparison". AutomorphicBundles:B4: "Prove the analytic transformation-law comparison, including the growth condition and the actual cocycle identity j(γ₁γ₂,z)=j(γ₁,γ₂z)j(γ₂,z) for a left action. Derive the appropriate right-action formula" — the factors (N det A)^{k/2}, (N b_𝒜)^{-k}, (N t_λ)^{-k/2} are the automorphy-factor bookkeeping of the slash action at a cusp. Library: `UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion` (Mathlib QExpansion.lean:162) has no cusp-dependent normalisation and is ℚ-only. Confirmed planned. The normalised coefficients c_𝒜(b,f) = a_𝒜(b)(N t_λ)^{-k/2}(N b_𝒜)^{-k}(N det A)^{k/2} are the paper's (Shimura's) normalisation of B5's q-expansion at a Hilbert cusp; the specific factors are not spelled out in any layer, but B5 explicitly plans the normalisations of the Hilbert cusp expansions and B4 the transformation law they come from. Dropped KU-hilberteisenstein (aggregation checkpoint, consumer).

items.name: Cusp forms S_k(n)
items.statement: S_k(n) ⊂ M_k(n) is the subspace of f = (f_λ) ∈ M_k(n) such that c_𝒜(0, f) = 0 for all pairs 𝒜 = (A, λ) with A ∈ GL_2^+(F), λ ∈ Cl^+(F). This subspace does not depend on the choice of the ideal class representatives t_λ.
items.locator: §7.2.3, definition of S_k(n) (lines 1830–1832)
items.note: Target space of the cusp form constructions of §8 (Theorem 8.17 etc.). Evidence: AutomorphicBundles:B4: "Define classical modular and cuspidal forms as sections of the canonical and subcanonical extensions. Prove the analytic transformation-law comparison ... For Hilbert varieties over a splitting coefficient field, identify the factors ω_τ, determinant twists, and the parity/central-character condition for arithmetic weights." AutomorphicBundles:B5: "Identify cuspidality with the appropriate boundary vanishing condition." OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O6: "Define cusp forms by the subcanonical coefficient/boundary ideal and prove compatibility with the classical and AIP definitions. In degree one use the compactified cusp calculation; in higher Hilbert degree use the proved Koecher statement". C6 also: "Cusp forms are still distinguished by their boundary ideal". Library: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Basic.lean:82 `structure CuspForm extends SlashInvariantForm Γ k` with `zero_at_cusps' {c : OnePoint ℝ} (hc : IsCusp c Γ)` and :100 `class CuspFormClass` — Γ : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ), functions ℍ → ℂ, i.e. F = ℚ only; audit the layer extract:4347 confirms 'there is no Hilbert modular form of any kind'. Confirmed planned. S_k(n) ⊂ M_k(n), cut out by c_𝒜(0,f) = 0 at every pair, is the classical Hilbert cusp space that B4 defines/compares analytically, B5 identifies with boundary vanishing and O6 proves compatible with the classical definition. Mathlib's CuspForm is the ℚ-case near miss.

items.name: Dependence of the normalised constant term on the cusp (parity of k)
items.statement: Let f ∈ M_k(n). If k is even, c_𝒜(0, f) depends only on the cusp [𝒜] ∈ cusps(n) determined by 𝒜. If k is odd, c_𝒜(0, f) is invariant under replacing A by γA with γ ∈ Γ_λ(n), and for A' = (a b; 0 d) ∈ GL_2^+(F) one has c_{(AA', λ)}(0, f) = sgn(N_{F/Q}(a)) · c_{(A, λ)}(0, f); so for odd k the constant term is well defined on the cusp up to sign.
items.locator: §7.2.3, paragraph after the definition of S_k(n) (lines 1834–1835)
items.note: Justifies speaking of constant terms at a cusp (up to sign for odd weight); the sgn(N a) factors reappear in the constant-term formulas of §8. Evidence: AutomorphicBundles:B5: "Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps ... Identify cuspidality with the appropriate boundary vanishing condition." AutomorphicBundles:B4: "Prove the analytic transformation-law comparison ... and the actual cocycle identity ... Derive the appropriate right-action formula rather than reusing it unchanged." Paper lines 1834–1835: c_𝒜(0,f) depends only on [𝒜] for k even; for k odd it is Γ_λ(n)-invariant and c_{(AA',λ)}(0,f) = sgn(N_{F/ℚ}(a))·c_{(A,λ)}(0,f) for upper-triangular A'. Library: the ℚ-analogue is Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CuspFormSubmodule.lean:142 `ModularForm.isCuspForm_iff_coeffZero_eq_zero (f : ModularForm 𝒮ℒ k)` (SL(2,ℤ) only) and `CuspFormClass.qExpansion_coeff_zero` (QExpansion.lean:436); no Hilbert analogue and no sgn(N a) parity statement anywhere. Confirmed planned, low confidence. A q-expansion 'at a Hilbert cusp' (B5) must be attached to the cusp rather than to a representative matrix, and identifying cuspidality with boundary vanishing requires the constant term's vanishing to be a condition on the cusp; so the even-k statement is contained in B5, and the odd-k sign is the right-action transformation-law bookkeeping B4 plans. The explicit sgn(N a) formula is stated in no layer, hence low confidence; not missing because the well-definedness on the cusp is an unavoidable part of B5's construction.

items.name: Constant term c_λ(0, f) at the pair (1, λ), equation (92)
items.locator: §7.2.4 q-expansions, equation (92) (label e:constantdef)
items.note: The constant terms at the cusps above infinity that appear in the q-expansion and in the Eisenstein constant-term formulas of §7.3. Evidence: AutomorphicBundles:B5: "Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps". AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3: "Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof" — the constant-term argument is stated in terms of the constant terms c_λ(0,f) at the cusps (1,λ) above infinity. IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 ("Hilbert modular Eisenstein series, their algebraic Fourier coefficients, q-expansion principles") is a consumer that 'must import from a verified supplier'. Library: `UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion_coeff_zero` (Mathlib QExpansion.lean:169) gives the constant coefficient at ∞ for a function on the single upper half-plane — the F = ℚ, one-component case. Confirmed planned; I.3 dropped as consumer-only, L3 kept because its 'constant-term argument' names these constant terms. c_λ(0,f) = a_{(1,λ)}(0)(N t_λ)^{-k/2} is the constant term of B5's q-expansion at the cusp ∞ of the λ-component, with the (1,λ) specialisation of item 188's normalisation.

items.name: Normalised Fourier coefficient c(m, f) at an integral ideal and the q-expansion, equation (93)
items.statement: Any nonzero integral ideal m of O_F can be written m = (b) t_λ^{-1} with b ∈ t_λ totally positive for a unique λ ∈ Cl^+(F); then c(m, f) = a_{(1,λ)}(b) · (N t_λ)^{-k/2}. The collection { c_λ(0, f) (λ ∈ Cl^+(F)), c(m, f) (m ≠ 0 integral) } is called the q-expansion of f.
items.locator: §7.2.4, equation (93) (label e:positivedef) and the following sentence
items.note: The coefficients indexed by ideals on which the Hecke operators act by (100) and by which group ring valued forms are specified (Lemma 7.2). Evidence: AutomorphicBundles:B5: "Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps ... Prove the expansion principle with the necessary connectedness, base, and coefficient assumptions." AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3: "Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument" — the integral q-expansion principle is formulated on the ideal-indexed coefficients {c_λ(0,f), c(m,f)}. HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H3 supplies the class-indexed components and 'Compare different lists of ideal representatives' (the choice of t_λ in m = (b)t_λ^{-1}). Library: `UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion` (Mathlib QExpansion.lean:162) and TauCeti `ModularForm.qExpansionLinearMap` (QExpansion/Basic.lean:63) are ℕ-indexed one-variable expansions for Γ ≤ GL(2,ℝ), i.e. F = ℚ where integral ideals are (m), m ∈ ℕ, and Cl⁺(ℚ) is trivial — a near miss. Confirmed planned; trimmed KU-hilberteisenstein and I.3 (aggregation checkpoint and consumer). The ideal-indexed normalised coefficients c(m,f) = a_{(1,λ)}(b)(N t_λ)^{-k/2}, m = (b)t_λ^{-1} with b ∈ t_λ totally positive, and the q-expansion {c_λ(0,f), c(m,f)} are the standard Hilbert q-expansion datum that B5 constructs and on which L3's integral q-expansion principle is stated. Previous note's `ModularForm.qExpansion` corrected to `UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion`.

items.name: q-expansion determines the form
items.statement: For f ∈ M_k(n), the q-expansion { c_λ(0, f), c(m, f) } determines f: the map M_k(n) → C^{Cl^+(F)} × C^{ {nonzero integral ideals} }, f ↦ (c_λ(0, f), c(m, f)), is injective.
items.locator: §7.2.4, last sentence (line 1849)
items.note: External input (shim (asserted without explicit citation)). Uniqueness in Lemma 7.2 and throughout §8, where forms are defined by their coefficients. Evidence: Verified in atlas/areas/modular-1.json stage 21 (AutomorphicBundles:B5): "Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps and Fourier–Jacobi expansions ... Prove the expansion principle with the necessary connectedness, base, and coefficient assumptions." atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json stage 22 (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3): "Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof." stage 90 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3): "This includes Hilbert modular Eisenstein series, their algebraic Fourier coefficients, q-expansion principles ..."; stage 18 (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:KU-hilberteisenstein): "Owns any missing modular-form and q-expansion prerequisites". Library check: Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/QExpansion.lean (pinned tree) has `def qExpansion (f : ℍ → ℂ) : PowerSeries ℂ` at line 162 and `qExpansion_coeff_unique` (header line 42) for functions on the single upper half-plane ℍ; Tau Ceti uses it in TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Degeneracy.lean:986 for GL₂(ℝ)-subgroups only. rg -il 'hilbert ?modular|HilbertModular' over both TauCeti/ and Mathlib/ returns nothing. Confirmed the previous verdict. The item is injectivity of f ↦ (c_λ(0,f), c(𝔪,f)) on M_k(𝔫) for Hilbert forms over a totally real F (Shimura's tuple-of-components convention); the ℚ-case q-expansion uniqueness in Mathlib/Tau Ceti is a near miss. B5 is the owner (it constructs q-expansions at Hilbert cusps and proves the expansion principle, which contains injectivity of the coefficient map); […]

items.name: Integral ideal c_𝒜 of a cusp
items.statement: For 𝒜 = (A, λ) with A = (a b; c d), c_𝒜 = (c)(t_λ d b_𝒜)^{-1} ⊂ O_F, an integral ideal depending only on the cusp [𝒜]. For F = Q and 𝒜 representing the cusp a/c ∈ P^1(Q) with gcd(a, c) = 1, c_𝒜 = (c) ⊂ Z. (Notation from dka.)
items.locator: §7.2.5 Cusps above infinity and zero, displayed definition of c_𝒜 (line 1854)
items.note: External input (dka). Measures how close a cusp is to ∞ relative to the level; used to define C_∞ and C_0 and appears in the constant-term formulas of §8 via ψ(c_𝒜). Evidence: Searched atlas/areas/*.json and roadmaps/*.json for 'Hilbert ... cusp', 'cusps above', 'C_∞', 'denominator', 'diamond ... cusp': only hits are AutomorphicBundles:B5 ("Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps"), ShimuraCompactifications:C6 ("Construct the Hilbert toroidal and minimal models used around the ordinary locus, with their cusp lattice, positivity cone, and unit quotient"), HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:R18.2 ("Compact quaternionic curves carry no Hilbert cusp boundary"), ModularCurves R12.6 ("chosen rational cusp", F = ℚ). None defines an ideal attached to a Hilbert cusp. Library: tauceti `Subgroup.integerCuspWidth (𝒢 : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ)) : ℕ` at TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps/Basic.lean:143 and Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps.lean are for subgroups of GL₂(ℝ) acting on ℍ (F = ℚ); rg -il 'hilbert ?modular' in TauCeti/ and Mathlib/ is empty. Confirmed missing. 𝔠_𝒜 = (c)(𝔱_λ 𝔡 𝔟_𝒜)^{-1} is the DK/dka-specific level-relative invariant of a cusp of Γ_λ(𝔫); no layer names it (B5 and C6 only mention Hilbert cusps and their toroidal lattice data, shared vocabulary), and the nearest library notion, the integer cusp width over ℚ, is a different invariant of a different object.

items.name: Cusps above infinity C_∞(n), C_∞(b, n)
items.statement: C_∞(n) ⊂ cusps(n) is the set of cusps [𝒜] with n | c_𝒜. More generally, for b | n, C_∞(b, n) = { [𝒜] ∈ cusps(n) : b | c_𝒜 } (so C_∞(n) = C_∞(n, n)).
items.locator: §7.2.5, displayed definition of C_∞(b, n) (lines 1858–1859)
items.note: External input (dka). The constant terms of the group ring forms in §8 are controlled at C_∞(𝔓, n) and C_∞(n). Evidence: Same atlas search as 194 (patterns 'cusps above', 'C_∞', 'C_\\infty', 'Hilbert.{0,80}cusp'): the only 'C_∞' hits are the patching complex C_∞ in foundations-1.json (unrelated); Hilbert-cusp hits are B5 ("q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps ... Identify cuspidality with the appropriate boundary vanishing condition"), C6 ("cusp lattice, positivity cone, and unit quotient") and O6 ("Define cusp forms by the subcanonical coefficient/boundary ideal"). Library: no Hilbert cusps in either tree (rg empty); Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps.lean and TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Cusps/*.lean treat cusps of subgroups of GL₂(ℝ) on ℍ only. Confirmed missing. C_∞(𝔟,𝔫) = {[𝒜] ∈ cusps(𝔫) : 𝔟 | 𝔠_𝒜} rests on the unplanned ideal 𝔠_𝒜 (item 194); no layer names the divisibility partition of Hilbert cusps by the level. Nearest planned objects are the Hilbert cusps themselves (B5, C6).

items.name: Cusps above zero C_0(n), C_0(b, n)
items.statement: C_0(n) is the set of cusps [𝒜] ∈ cusps(n) with gcd(c_𝒜, n) = 1, and for b | n, C_0(b, n) = { [𝒜] ∈ cusps(n) : gcd(b, c_𝒜) = 1 }.
items.locator: §7.2.5, displayed definition of C_0(b, n) (lines 1863–1864)
items.note: External input (dka). Support of the constant terms of the modified Eisenstein series of §8. Evidence: Same search as 194/195 (adding 'C_0(', 'coprime ... cusp'): no atlas stage or new roadmap names cusps 'above zero' or a coprimality condition on a Hilbert cusp; nearest are AutomorphicBundles:B5 ("q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps") and ShimuraCompactifications:C6 ("cusp lattice, positivity cone, and unit quotient"). Library: rg -il 'hilbert ?modular' in TauCeti/ and Mathlib/ is empty; the cusp files in both trees are for GL₂(ℝ)-subgroups on ℍ. Confirmed missing. C_0(𝔟,𝔫) = {[𝒜] : gcd(𝔟, 𝔠_𝒜) = 1} depends on 𝔠_𝒜 (item 194), which nothing plans.

items.name: C_∞(b, n) and C_0(b, n) are stable under diamond operators
items.statement: For b | n, the sets C_∞(b, n) and C_0(b, n) are stable under the action of the diamond operators S(m), m ∈ G_n^+, on cusps(n). These sets are enumerated explicitly in dka.
items.locator: §7.2.5, last two sentences (line 1865)
items.note: External input (dka). Ensures the constant-term conditions imposed in §8 are compatible with nebentypus and lets constant terms at C_∞ and C_0 be computed cusp by cusp. Evidence: Atlas: OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O6 (modular-1.json stage 207): "Construct tame Hecke and diamond operators and the p-level correspondences, including the operators at primes 𝔭|p. Define them as pullback, coefficient identification, and trace ... compare q-expansions with B5" (operators on overconvergent Hilbert forms; no action on cusps). Search for 'diamond.{0,80}cusp|cusp.{0,80}diamond' over areas/*.json and roadmaps/*.json finds only ModularCurves R12.6 ("diamond operators, complex conjugation and the chosen rational cusp", F = ℚ) and ShimuraCompactifications C7 ("prime N≥5 diamond quotients", F = ℚ). Library: tauceti `diamondOp (k : ℤ) (d : (ZMod N)ˣ) : ModularForm ((Gamma1 N).map (mapGL ℝ)) k →ₗ[ℂ] ModularForm ((Gamma1 N).map (mapGL ℝ)) k` at TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/DiamondOperators.lean:148 (Γ₁(N) over ℚ); no diamond action on any set of cusps in either tree. Confirmed missing. The stability of C_∞(𝔟,𝔫), C_0(𝔟,𝔫) under S(𝔪), 𝔪 ∈ G_𝔫^+, acting on cusps(𝔫), and the enumeration of these sets in [dka], are unplanned: no layer names an action of diamond operators on Hilbert cusps, and the sets themselves (items 194–196) are unplanned.

items.name: Characters of G_n^+ of sign (k, …, k)
items.statement: G_n^+ is the narrow ray class group of F of conductor n and h_n^+ = #G_n^+. A character ψ : G_n^+ → C^* has associated sign congruent to (k, …, k) ∈ (Z/2Z)^n if for every α ∈ O_F with α ≡ 1 (mod n) one has ψ((α)) = sgn(N_{F/Q}(α))^k.
items.locator: §7.2.6 Forms with Nebentypus, first paragraph (lines 1869–1870)
items.note: Parity condition on a nebentypus character; totally odd characters satisfy it for odd k. Evidence: Verified in atlas/areas/classical-1.json stage 152 (Layer 9): "`RayClassCharacter 𝔪 := RayClassGroup 𝔪 →* ℂˣ`. Construct `HeckeCharacter.ofRayClassCharacter` as pullback along `rayClassQuotient`"; stage 153 (Layer 10, the layer extract line 1964ff): "`FiniteOrderInfinityType K` is a sign at each real place, and nothing else ... Prove `HeckeCharacter.exists_finiteOrderInfinityType` for a character of finite order" and "a real place contributes its exponent as modulus exponent and, mod 2, as sign parity", audit verdict for the infinity-type carriers: "Absent; grep for `InfinityType` returns nothing in either library." modular-1.json stage 20 (AutomorphicBundles:B4): "For Hilbert varieties over a splitting coefficient field, identify the factors `ω_τ`, determinant twists, and the parity/central-character condition for arithmetic weights." Library (object only): `def RayClassGroup (𝔪 : Modulus K) : Type _ := idealsPrimeTo 𝔪 ⧸ ray 𝔪` at TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/RayClass/Basic.lean:180, `structure Modulus` at Modulus.lean:88 (finite part + set of real places), `instance finite_rayClassGroup` at Finite.lean:154; rg for 'RayClassCharacter|HeckeCharacter|InfinityType' in TauCeti/ returns nothing, and Mathlib has no ray class groups. Confirmed the previous verdict. The item's substance is the sign condition ψ((α)) = sgn(N(α))^k for α ≡ 1 mod 𝔫, i.e. the sign vector at the real places of the finite-order Hecke character attached to ψ being constant (k,…,k). G_𝔫^+ and h_𝔫^+ are available as RayClassGroup of the modulus (𝔫, all real places) and its cardinality, but no declaration defines the sign of a character of it, so not library. […]

items.name: Forms with nebentypus ψ: M_k(n, ψ), S_k(n, ψ)
items.statement: For ψ : G_n^+ → C^* of sign (k, …, k), a form f ∈ M_k(n) has nebentypus ψ if f|_{S(a)} = ψ(a) f for all a ∈ G_n^+. M_k(n, ψ) is the space of such forms and S_k(n, ψ) = M_k(n, ψ) ∩ S_k(n).
items.locator: §7.2.6, displayed definition of nebentypus (lines 1870–1872)
items.note: Eisenstein series E_k(ψ_S, 1) and the specialisations of group ring valued forms live in these spaces. Evidence: Atlas: rg over areas/*.json and roadmaps/*.json for 'nebentypus' finds only ℚ-level stages (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms Layer 0 with `modFormCharSpace k χ` for (ZMod N)ˣ; ModularCurves R29.x; R20.4; PadicFamilies:L0 "specialization to the correct classical ordinary space, with nebentypus" over ℚ) and AutomorphicCongruences R12 ("Generalized Eisenstein series with tame nebentypus", GL₁ input). Hilbert-side stages read: OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O6 ("Construct tame Hecke and diamond operators" on overconvergent forms), AutomorphicBundles:B4 (classical Hilbert forms as bundle sections, "parity/central-character condition"), PadicFamilies:L5 ("central-character and torsion-unit restrictions" on ordinary Hilbert modules), H3 ("totally positive unit action on polarizations"). None defines M_k(𝔫,ψ). Library: tauceti `modFormCharSpace (k : ℤ) (χ : (ZMod N)ˣ →* ℂˣ) : Submodule ℂ (ModularForm ((Gamma1 N).map (mapGL ℝ)) k) := ⨅ d, Module.End.eigenspace (diamondOpHom k d) (χ d)` at TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/DiamondOperators.lean:315 and `cuspFormCharSpace` at line 279, Γ₁(N) over ℚ only. Confirmed missing. M_k(𝔫,ψ) and S_k(𝔫,ψ) for Hilbert forms with ψ a character of G_𝔫^+ have the exact ℚ-analogue in Tau Ceti (a near miss); no layer names character/nebentypus spaces of classical Hilbert modular forms — O6's diamond operators are on overconvergent Hilbert forms and B4/L5 only mention central-character conditions, shared vocabulary.

items.name: Nebentypus decomposition of M_k(n) and S_k(n)
items.statement: M_k(n) = ⊕_ψ M_k(n, ψ) and S_k(n) = ⊕_ψ S_k(n, ψ), the direct sums running over the characters ψ of G_n^+ as above.
items.locator: §7.2.6, displayed decompositions (lines 1873–1875)
items.note: External input (shim (asserted without explicit citation)). Standard eigenspace decomposition under the diamond operators. Evidence: Library verified: `theorem isInternal_modFormCharSpace (k : ℤ) [DecidableEq ((ZMod N)ˣ →* ℂˣ)] : DirectSum.IsInternal (fun χ : (ZMod N)ˣ →* ℂˣ ↦ modFormCharSpace k χ)` at TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/CharacterDecomp.lean:131 and `isInternal_cuspFormCharSpace` at line 154 (Γ₁(N) ⊂ SL₂(ℤ), F = ℚ); abstract engine `iSup_iInf_eigenspace_unitHom_eq_top_of_commGroup (hcard : IsUnit (Nat.card G : K)) : (⨆ χ₀ : G →* Kˣ, ⨅ g, (ρ g).eigenspace (χ₀ g)) = ⊤` at TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Eigenspace/JointEigenvector/Basic.lean:376. Atlas: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms Layer 0 (modular-2.json stage 0): "The nebentypus decomposition of `M_k(Γ₁(N))` — already proved in AINTLIB; migrate" (ℚ only); no stage names a character decomposition of Hilbert modular forms (same 'nebentypus'/'diamond' search as 199; O6 constructs diamond operators on overconvergent Hilbert forms without naming eigenspace decomposition). Confirmed missing. The decomposition M_k(𝔫) = ⊕_ψ M_k(𝔫,ψ), S_k(𝔫) = ⊕_ψ S_k(𝔫,ψ) over characters of G_𝔫^+ is proved in Tau Ceti precisely over ℚ (a near miss), and the abstract joint-eigenspace theorem would yield it once a G_𝔫^+-action by S(𝔞) on M_k(𝔫) exists; that action and the spaces (item 199) are in neither library and are named by no layer.

items.name: Raising the level: f|q ∈ M_k(nq), equation (94)
items.statement: For f ∈ M_k(n) and an integral ideal q of F there is a form f|q ∈ M_k(nq) characterised by: for nonzero integral ideals a, c(a, f|q) = c(a/q, f) if q | a and c(a, f|q) = 0 if q ∤ a; and c_λ(0, f|q) = c_{λq}(0, f) for all λ ∈ Cl^+(F) (equation (94)). Construction: Shimura, shim Prop. 2.3.
items.locator: §7.2.7 Raising the level (label sss:level), equation (94) (label eq:levelconstant)
items.note: External input (shim Prop 2.3). Used in §8 to modify Eisenstein series (the operators V and the forms W_k) and to change level. Evidence: AutomorphicBundles:B5 (atlas/areas/modular-1.json; the layer extract:4602): "Construct pullback, coefficient identification, and trace along Hecke correspondences. State all scalar normalizations ... Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps ... Prove the expansion principle with the necessary connectedness, base, and coefficient assumptions." Shimura's f|q is the pullback along the degeneracy correspondence X(nq)→X(n), and (94) is its effect on the coefficients c(a,·) and the constant terms c_λ(0,·) at the Hilbert cusps. Audit (the audit extract:2146): B5 verdict not built; "Hilbert cusps and the sheaf-theoretic expansion do not exist". Library check (my own rg): `rg -il 'hilbert ?modular|HilbertModular'` over Mathlib/ and TauCeti/ at the pinned commits returns nothing. The only level-raising declaration is TauCeti.ModularForm.levelRaise, TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Degeneracy.lean:278, `def levelRaise [𝒢'.HasDetOne] (d : ℕ) [NeZero d] (h : 𝒢' ≤ ConjAct.toConjAct (scaleGL d)⁻¹ • 𝒢) (f : ModularForm 𝒢 k) : ModularForm 𝒢' k` with `levelRaise_apply : levelRaise d h f τ = f (scaleGL d • τ)` at line 291 — elliptic forms for subgroups of GL₂(ℝ) on a single ℍ, ℂ-valued. Confirmed planned, with the planned list narrowed. The library near miss (Tau Ceti's V_d = levelRaise, ℚ-case, one cusp, no ideal-indexed coefficients or narrow-class-indexed constant terms) is verified and is not the item. […]

items.name: Integral forms M_k(n, Z)
items.statement: M_k(n, Z) ⊂ M_k(n) is the subgroup of forms f such that c(m, f) ∈ Z for all nonzero integral ideals m ⊂ O_F and c_λ(0, f) ∈ Z for all λ ∈ Cl^+(F).
items.locator: §7.2.9 Group ring valued Hilbert modular forms, first display (lines 1905–1906)
items.note: Base lattice from which forms over any coefficient ring are defined by base change. Evidence: AutomorphicBundles:B4 (the layer extract:4580): "Define classical modular and cuspidal forms as sections of the canonical and subcanonical extensions ... after the specified level, coefficient, and cusp conditions. For Hilbert varieties over a splitting coefficient field, identify the factors ω_τ ... Before splitting, define the same coefficient using 𝒪_F⊗𝒪-linear tensors and descent"; audit target "For Hilbert varieties ... the O_F ⊗ O-linear tensor before splitting | library: absent". items.name: Forms with coefficients in an abelian group: M_k(n, A) = M_k(n, Z) ⊗ A, and S_k(n, A)
items.statement: For any abelian group A, M_k(n, A) = M_k(n, Z) ⊗_Z A. "These definitions generalize in the obvious way" to S_k(n, A): S_k(n, Z) = S_k(n) ∩ M_k(n, Z) and S_k(n, A) = S_k(n, Z) ⊗_Z A. The coefficients c(m, f), c_λ(0, f) ∈ A of f ∈ M_k(n, A) are the A-linear extensions of the Z-valued coefficient maps (implicit in the source).
items.locator: §7.2.9, second display (line 1908) and the sentence "These definitions generalize in the obvious way" (line 1912)
items.note: Defines Hilbert modular forms over the coefficient rings O, ∏_ψ O and R = R_Ψ used throughout §8–§9. Evidence: AutomorphicBundles:B4 (the layer extract:4580): "Define classical modular and cuspidal forms as sections of the canonical and subcanonical extensions ... after the specified level, coefficient, and cusp conditions ... Before splitting, define the same coefficient using 𝒪_F⊗𝒪-linear tensors and descent" — Hilbert forms with coefficients in a ring 𝒪. AutomorphicBundles:B5: "Prove the expansion principle with the necessary connectedness, base, and coefficient assumptions" — the q-expansion principle over a base ring, which is what compares the geometric forms over A with M_k(n,ℤ)⊗A. Library: no Hilbert modular forms in either tree; no modular forms over a coefficient ring even for F=ℚ (Mathlib ModularForm is ℂ-valued, Basic.lean:74; Tau Ceti's spaces are ℂ-submodules, e.g. `modFormCharSpace ... : Submodule ℂ (ModularForm ((Gamma1 N).map (mapGL ℝ)) k)`, TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/DiamondOperators.lean:315). Confirmed planned, with the caveat retained: no Hilbert layer names the base-change statement M_k(n,A) = M_k(n,ℤ)⊗_ℤ A explicitly; the explicit "finite-generation/base-change statements for spaces of forms" occur only in AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights:R15.2 (modular-1.json), which is the modular-curve, F=ℚ roadmap and so is not the owner for a totally real F. The item is credited to B4/B5 as the containing target 'Hilbert forms over a coefficient ring with q-expansions and expansion principle over a base'. Both layers are unbuilt for Hilbert targets per the audit (B4 partly built, only the GL₂(ℝ) cocycle identity; B5 not built).

items.name: Forms of nebentypus ψ over a ring A: M_k(n, A, ψ), S_k(n, A, ψ)
items.statement: For a ring A and a character ψ : G_n^+ → A^*, M_k(n, A, ψ) = { f ∈ M_k(n, A) : f|_{S(a)} = ψ(a) f for all a ∈ G_n^+ }, and (obvious generalisation) S_k(n, A, ψ) = S_k(n, A) ∩ M_k(n, A, ψ).
items.locator: §7.2.9, third display (line 1910) and line 1912
items.note: The coefficient-ring version of nebentypus; with A = R and ψ = 𝛙 it gives the group ring valued forms. Evidence: OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O6 (modular-1.json; the layer extract:2302): "Define cusp forms ... prove compatibility with the classical and AIP definitions ... Construct tame Hecke and diamond operators and the p-level correspondences ... Define them as pullback, coefficient identification, and trace ... compare q-expansions with B5" — the tame diamond operators S(a) for Hilbert forms. The Tau Ceti roadmap stage tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms#layer-0 ("diamond operators and modular forms with character (nebentypus)") is likewise the ℚ-case. rg over areas/*.json and roadmaps/*.json for 'nebentypus' finds no Hilbert/totally real stage. Confirmed planned, but at low confidence and borderline: the item's only content beyond item 203 is the diamond operators S(a), a ∈ G_n^+, on Hilbert forms over a ring A and their joint ψ-eigenspace. O6 names the Hilbert tame diamond operators explicitly (as correspondences, with comparison to the classical definition) and B5 owns the underlying Hecke correspondences; the ψ-eigenspace is then a one-line definition, so the item is credited by containment. items.name: Canonical character 𝛙 : G_n^+ → G → R^* and group ring valued forms M_k(n, R, 𝛙)
items.statement: Let R = R_Ψ be as in §7.1 and suppose the conductor of H/F divides n, so that G = Gal(H/F) is canonically a quotient of G_n^+. The canonical character 𝛙 : G_n^+ → G → R^* is the composite of the quotient map with the tautological map G → O[G] → R. The space of group ring valued Hilbert modular forms is M_k(n, R, 𝛙) (first considered by Wiles, wiles); similarly S_k(n, R, 𝛙).
items.locator: §7.2.9, displayed definition of 𝛙 (lines 1914–1919) and the following sentence
items.note: The central objects of Ribet's method in this paper: the Eisenstein family and the cusp forms of §8 are elements of these spaces. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (iwasawa-1.json; the layer extract:46): "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations. Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation"; audit target "Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations ... for the Hilbert/Eisenstein representation | library: absent". AutomorphicBundles:B4: "Before splitting, define the same coefficient using 𝒪_F⊗𝒪-linear tensors and descent" (Hilbert forms over a coefficient ring, the underlying M_k(n,R)). Catalogue search: rg over all 2001 stage descriptions (areas/*.json + roadmaps/*.json) for 'group[- ]ring[- ]valued' gives 0 hits; 'group ring' hits only Iwasawa-algebra and class-field stages; 'Wiles' hits Taylor–Wiles/Skinner–Wiles stages and I.5, none naming group-ring-valued forms; 'Λ-adic' hits only HE.8 and L6. Library: rg -i 'group.?ring.?valued' over both trees is empty; no Hilbert modular forms at all. Confirmed planned. The canonical character 𝛙: G_n^+ → G → R^* and Wiles's space M_k(n,R,𝛙) are the precise vehicle of the 'Hilbert modular congruences' that I.7 names as part of the Dasgupta–Kakde proof (Remark 7.3), so the item is planned by that containing target; B4 supplies the underlying Hilbert forms over the coefficient ring R. […]

items.name: Specialisation ψ(f) of a group ring valued form
items.statement: For ψ ∈ Ψ the ring map ψ : R → O induces ψ : M_k(n, R) = M_k(n, Z) ⊗ R → M_k(n, Z) ⊗ O = M_k(n, O); for f ∈ M_k(n, R, 𝛙) the specialisation ψ(f) lies in M_k(n, O, ψ) and has coefficients c(m, ψ(f)) = ψ(c(m, f)), c_λ(0, ψ(f)) = ψ(c_λ(0, f)). Remark 7.3: f thus encodes the family {ψ(f)}_{ψ∈Ψ}, and R-integrality of its coefficients (rather than ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O-integrality) expresses p-adic congruences among the forms ψ(f).
items.locator: §7.2.9, statement of Lemma 7.2 (the notation ψ(f)) and Remark 7.3 (lines 1952–1954)
items.note: Every group ring form in §8 is constructed and checked through its specialisations; Remark 7.3 records the family viewpoint used throughout. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract:46): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation". AutomorphicBundles:B5 (the layer extract:4602): "Construct pullback, coefficient identification, and trace" and "Prove the expansion principle with the necessary connectedness, base, and coefficient assumptions" — functoriality of the forms in the coefficient ring and its compatibility with q-expansions. Library: no Hilbert modular forms in either tree; no coefficient-change map on modular forms over rings even for F=ℚ (Mathlib forms are ℂ-valued, Basic.lean:74). PadicFamilies:L0 ("At arithmetic characters prove specialization to the correct classical ordinary space, with nebentypus") is the F=ℚ Hida-family specialisation, read and rejected as owner. Confirmed planned by containment. The specialisation ψ(f) = (id⊗ψ)(f) with c(m,ψ(f)) = ψ(c(m,f)), c_λ(0,ψ(f)) = ψ(c_λ(0,f)) is coefficient-ring functoriality of M_k(n,−) plus compatibility with q-expansions (B5's coefficient identification), and Remark 7.3's family/congruence reading is I.7's 'Hilbert modular congruences'. No layer names the specialisation map of group-ring-valued forms itself.

items.name: Silliman's characterisation of M_k(n, R) inside M_k(n, ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O), equation (97)
items.statement: For R = R_Ψ ⊂ ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O via (96): M_k(n, R) = { f ∈ M_k(n, ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O) : c(m, f) ∈ R and c_λ(0, f) ∈ R for all nonzero integral m and all λ ∈ Cl^+(F) }, where M_k(n, R) → M_k(n, ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O) is induced by the inclusion R ⊂ ∏ O. (Stated as implied by Silliman, dks Corollary 7.28 and Remark 7.29.)
items.locator: §7.2.9, proof of Lemma 7.2, equation (97) (label e:jinject)
items.note: External input (dks Corollary 7.28 and Remark 7.29 (Silliman)). The key input that a tuple of forms with all coefficients in R is itself an R-valued form; it is what makes Lemma 7.2, and hence every construction of §8, work. Evidence: AutomorphicBundles:B5 (the layer extract:4602): "Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps ... Prove the expansion principle with the necessary connectedness, base, and coefficient assumptions"; audit: "there is no version over a base ring". AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 (the layer extract:167): "Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof"; audit (line 175): "any integral q-expansion principle [is] absent". Confirmed planned. Equation (97) — a form over ∏_ψ O all of whose coefficients c(m,·) and constant terms c_λ(0,·) at every cusp lie in the subring R is an R-valued form — is the integral q-expansion principle over a base for Hilbert forms (Silliman/DKS Cor. items.name: Lemma 7.2: group ring valued forms from compatible families
items.statement: Let R = R_Ψ and 𝛙 be as above (cond(H/F) | n). Let c(m) ∈ R for nonzero integral ideals m ⊂ O_F and c_λ(0) ∈ R for λ ∈ Cl^+(F) be elements such that for every ψ ∈ Ψ there exists a form f_ψ ∈ M_k(n, O, ψ) with c(m, f_ψ) = ψ(c(m)) and c_λ(0, f_ψ) = ψ(c_λ(0)) for all m, λ. Then there exists a unique f ∈ M_k(n, R, 𝛙) such that ψ(f) = f_ψ for all ψ ∈ Ψ. Proof: M_k(n, ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O) = ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} M_k(n, O) (canonically, coefficients being tuples of coefficients); let f be the form corresponding to (f_ψ)_ψ; then c(m, f) = (ψ(c(m)))_ψ and c_λ(0, f) = (ψ(c_λ(0)))_ψ (equations (98), (99)) are the images of c(m), c_λ(0) under (96), so f ∈ M_k(n, R) by (97), and f ∈ M_k(n, R, 𝛙) since ψ(f) = f_ψ ∈ M_k(n, O, ψ) for all ψ.
items.locator: §7.2.9, Lemma 7.2 (lines 1923–1950), with equations (98) (label e:cmdef) and (99) (label e:cldef) in its proof
items.note: The tool by which all group ring valued forms in §8 (Eisenstein families, W_k(𝛙,1), G_k(𝛙), H_k(𝛙), F_k(𝛙)) are defined by specifying Fourier coefficients in R. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract:46): "The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences" — Lemma 7.2 is the mechanism producing every group-ring-valued form of §8 from a compatible family of specialisations, i.e. the constructive core of those congruences. AutomorphicBundles:B5: "Prove the expansion principle with the necessary connectedness, base, and coefficient assumptions" — the proof of Lemma 7.2 is (97) applied to (f_ψ)_ψ ∈ M_k(n,∏O) = ∏_ψ M_k(n,O). Library: no Hilbert modular forms in either pinned tree (rg empty); nothing gluing forms over a product ring exists even for F=ℚ; the nearest material is Mathlib's complex elliptic qExpansion_injective (QExpansion.lean:661). Catalogue: no stage names Lemma 7.2, compatible families of specialisations, or existence/uniqueness of group-ring-valued forms (rg over all stage descriptions for 'group ring valued', 'Λ-adic', 'Silliman' as above). Confirmed planned by containment. Lemma 7.2 is a direct corollary of item 207's integral q-expansion principle plus the finite-product base change M_k(n,∏O) = ∏ M_k(n,O); no layer names it, but it is the constructive core of I.7's explicitly named 'Hilbert modular congruences' in the Dasgupta–Kakde proof, and B5 owns the q-expansion input. Not library: different generality (F=ℚ, ℂ-coefficients) for the nearest declaration.

items.name: Hecke action on M_k(n, R, 𝛙): formulas (100) and preservation
items.statement: The operators T_q (q ∤ n prime), U_q (q | n prime) and S(m) ((m, n) = 1) preserve M_k(n, R, 𝛙). S(m) acts by the scalar 𝛙(m) ∈ R^*. For a prime q ∤ n and f ∈ M_k(n, R, 𝛙): c(m, f|_{T_q}) = Σ_{a | (m, q)} 𝛙(a) N a^{k−1} c(mq/a^2, f) (equation (100)) and c_λ(0, f|_{T_q}) = c_{λq^{-1}}(0, f) + 𝛙(q) N q^{k−1} c_{λq}(0, f). The same formulas hold for U_q, q | n, with the convention 𝛙(q) = 0, i.e. c(m, f|_{U_q}) = c(mq, f) and c_λ(0, f|_{U_q}) = c_{λq^{-1}}(0, f). Since the right-hand sides lie in R, T_q and U_q preserve M_k(n, R, 𝛙).
items.locator: §7.2.9, paragraph after Remark 7.3, equation (100) (label e:heckec) and the unnumbered second row of the align (lines 1956–1962)
items.note: Makes M_k(n, R, 𝛙) and S_k(n, R, 𝛙) Hecke modules; formula (100) also defines the Hecke action on the coefficient module in §9 and underlies the ordinary projector. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation" — the group-ring-valued forms M_k(n,R,𝛙) as Hecke modules are the framework of these congruences. AutomorphicBundles:B5 "Hecke action and Fourier expansions" (atlas/areas/modular-1.json): "Construct pullback, coefficient identification, and trace along Hecke correspondences. State all scalar normalizations ... Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps ... Prove the expansion principle with the necessary connectedness, base, and coefficient assumptions", with B4 identifying classical Hilbert modular forms ("For Hilbert varieties over a splitting coefficient field, identify the factors ω_τ ..."). Library: rg -i 'Hilbert ?modular|HilbertModular' over Mathlib/ and TauCeti/ at the pinned commits: no hits. Nearest: tauceti HeckeRing.GL2.heckeRingHomCharSpace (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/HeckeSlash/Nebentypus/Action.lean:293, integral Γ₀(N) Hecke ring acting on modFormCharSpace k χ over ℂ) and heckeUNat_eq_heckeTNat (HeckeSlash/BadPrime/Basic.lean:65) — elliptic forms over ℚ with ℂ-coefficients only. […]

items.name: R_Ψ is a complete local Z_p-algebra
items.statement: The ring R = R_Ψ (a quotient of the local ring O[G_p]_χ, finite over Z_p) is a complete local Z_p-algebra.
items.locator: §7.2.10 Ordinary forms, first sentence (line 1966)
items.note: Needed for the limit lim U_𝔭^{n!} defining Hida's ordinary projector to converge on M_k(n, R, 𝛙). Evidence: Verified in the pinned Mathlib tree: RingTheory/LocalRing/Basic.lean:117 `theorem of_surjective' [Ring S] [Nontrivial S] (f : R →+* S) (hf : Function.Surjective f) : IsLocalRing S` (quotients of local rings are local); NumberTheory/Padics/PadicIntegers.lean:539 `instance : IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal ℤ_[p]) ℤ_[p]`; RingTheory/AdicCompletion/LocalRing.lean:49 `isLocalRing_of_isAdicComplete_maximal` and :127 completeness of the adic completion of a Noetherian local ring. rg 'IsLocalRing' over Mathlib/Algebra/MonoidAlgebra and rg 'MonoidAlgebra.*Local|Local.*MonoidAlgebra' over Mathlib: no hits (no 'O[G] is local for a p-group'); rg 'Module.Finite' in RingTheory/AdicCompletion: only Exactness/AsTensorProduct lemmas, no 'a finite Z_p-algebra is p-adically complete'. Atlas: rg over areas/*.json and roadmaps/*.json for 'complete local Z_p', 'O[G]', 'character group ring', 'p-group ... local': no stage names R_Ψ or the locality/completeness of a finite character group-ring quotient; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1 ("Complete local coefficient categories") and PadicFamilies:L0a ("A finite module over a complete noetherian local ring with finite residue field ... is a standard sufficient instance") only take such rings as the ambient category/hypothesis. Confirmed missing. […]

items.name: p-part 𝔓 of the level
items.statement: 𝔓 = gcd(p^∞, n) is the p-part of the level n, i.e. the product of the prime-power factors of n at the primes of F above p.
items.locator: §7.2.10, first paragraph (line 1966)
items.note: Indexes the ordinary operator e_𝔓^ord and the cusp set C_∞(𝔓, n) used in §8. Evidence: Verified: Mathlib RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Factorization.lean:72 `def IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.maxPowDividing (I : Ideal R) : Ideal R := v.asIdeal ^ (Associates.mk v.asIdeal).count (Associates.mk I).factors` — exact power of a single prime v dividing I. rg -i 'pPart|primePart|gcd.*pow|primesOver.*prod' over Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain, RingTheory/Ideal and TauCeti/: no declaration for the p-part of an ideal. Atlas rg 'p-part of (the )?(level|ideal)|gcd\(p': no hits in areas/*.json or roadmaps/*.json. Confirmed missing. 𝔓 = ∏_{𝔭 | p} maxPowDividing 𝔭 n is composable from maxPowDividing and Ideal.primesOver but no single declaration gives it and no layer names it (PadicFamilies:L0/L5 and OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O6 speak of p-power level and operators at 𝔭 | p, not of this bookkeeping definition).

items.name: Hida's ordinary operators e_𝔭^ord, e_𝔓^ord, e_p^ord
items.statement: For a prime 𝔭 | 𝔓 (so that U_𝔭 is defined on M_k(n, R, 𝛙)), following Hida, e_𝔭^ord = lim_{n→∞} U_𝔭^{n!} (the limit exists since R is a complete local Z_p-algebra); e_𝔓^ord = ∏_{𝔭 | 𝔓} e_𝔭^ord and e_p^ord = ∏_{𝔭 | p} e_𝔭^ord (the source writes e_𝔭 for e_𝔭^ord; the latter product requires U_𝔭 to be defined for every prime 𝔭 of F above p, i.e. 𝔭 | n).
items.locator: §7.2.10, displayed definition of the ordinary operators (lines 1967–1968)
items.note: Projects onto the ordinary part; in §8 the cusp form is obtained by applying e_𝔓^ord, and Hida theory is applied to ordinary forms. Evidence: PadicFamilies:L0a (atlas/areas/modular-1.json): "For an endomorphism U of a finite underlying module, prove the Fitting decomposition ... Prove that U^(n!) is eventually constant with value the projector e onto the invertible summand; identify e by this decomposition, prove e²=e ... For a complete separated module M presented as an inverse limit of finite discrete quotient modules M/J with compatible U, construct e as the inverse limit of these finite projectors. Prove pointwise convergence of U^(n!) ... A finite module over a complete noetherian local ring with finite residue field ... is a standard sufficient instance". PadicFamilies:L5: "Instantiate L0a on the integral Hilbert automorphic/cohomology modules ... Nearly ordinary filtrations at each place above p are distinct data". Library: rg -in 'ordinary projector|ordinaryProjector|e_ord|Hida' over both pinned trees: no relevant hits. Confirmed planned. L0a owns the abstract e = lim U^{n!} (its convergence hypothesis is exactly R = R_Ψ complete local with finite residue field, cf. item 210) and L5 instantiates it on Hilbert modules over totally real F; the products e_𝔓, e_p over primes above p are the multi-place instance. Dropped OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.1, which only consumes ("Consume ... PadicFamilies for ordinary projectors") and is not the owner.

items.name: p-ordinary forms M_k(n, R, 𝛙)^{p-ord}, S_k(n, R, 𝛙)^{p-ord}
items.statement: For the canonical character 𝛙 (the source says "for any character ψ : G_n^+ → R^*" and then writes 𝛙): M_k(n, R, 𝛙)^{p-ord} = e_p^ord M_k(n, R, 𝛙) and S_k(n, R, 𝛙)^{p-ord} = e_p^ord S_k(n, R, 𝛙).
items.locator: §7.2.10, displayed definition of the p-ordinary spaces (lines 1969–1970)
items.note: The spaces on which the Hecke algebra of §9 is defined and to which Hida's control theorems apply. Evidence: PadicFamilies:L5 (atlas/areas/modular-1.json): "Instantiate L0a on the integral Hilbert automorphic/cohomology modules furnished by the Shimura and general automorphic owners ... Establish Hida control on the actual ordinary loci and integral weight algebras"; PadicFamilies:L0a: "image/kernel decomposition, invertibility of U on eM, and topological nilpotence on (1−e)M". the layer extract audit under L5: "Instantiation of the ordinary projector on integral Hilbert automorphic/cohomology modules | library: absent". Library: no Hilbert modular forms and no ordinary subspace in either pinned tree (rg 'Hilbert ?modular', 'ordinary' in TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms: no declarations). Confirmed planned: the p-ordinary spaces are the image eM of L0a's projector on the Hilbert modules of L5 ('ordinary loci'). One caveat kept from the previous verdict: L5's modules are the automorphic/cohomology modules of the Shimura owners, whereas the paper's M_k(n,R,𝛙) are q-expansion-defined group-ring-valued forms; the identification is a containing-target reading, not verbatim.

items.name: U_𝔭 is invertible on p-ordinary forms
items.statement: By construction of e_p^ord, for each prime 𝔭 | p the operator U_𝔭 acts invertibly on M_k(n, R, 𝛙)^{p-ord} and on S_k(n, R, 𝛙)^{p-ord}.
items.locator: §7.2.10, last sentence (line 1971)
items.note: Used in §8–§9 when working with U_𝔭-eigenvalues of ordinary forms and the Hecke algebra. Evidence: PadicFamilies:L0a (atlas/areas/modular-1.json): "construct e as the inverse limit of these finite projectors. Prove pointwise convergence of U^(n!) in the specified inverse-limit topology, continuity, image/kernel decomposition, invertibility of U on eM, and topological nilpotence on (1−e)M." PadicFamilies:L5: "Instantiate L0a on the integral Hilbert automorphic/cohomology modules". Library: rg for ordinary projectors / Hilbert modular forms in both pinned trees: nothing. Confirmed planned: 'U_𝔭 acts invertibly on e_p^ord M' is literally L0a's 'invertibility of U on eM' (applied for each 𝔭 | p, where e_p^ord = ∏ e_𝔭 factors through e_𝔭), instantiated on Hilbert forms by L5.

items.name: S-depleted character ψ_S and the level n
items.statement: Let k ≥ 1 be odd, ψ : G → O^* a totally odd character, and S a finite set of places of F. ψ_S denotes ψ viewed as having modulus divisible by all finite primes in S, i.e. ψ_S(a) = ψ(a) if a is coprime to S and ψ_S(a) = 0 if a is divisible by a prime in S. The level n is the product of cond(ψ) and the primes in S not dividing cond(ψ).
items.locator: §7.3 Eisenstein series (label s:eisenstein), first paragraph (line 1982)
items.note: Depleting at S removes Euler factors, producing the S-stabilised Eisenstein series whose constant terms involve L_S-values and the S-depleted Stickelberger element. Evidence: GlobalNumberFields Layer 9 (atlas/areas/classical-1.json): "`RayClassCharacter 𝔪 := RayClassGroup 𝔪 →* ℂˣ` ... Define local components and the finite conductor ideal ... Define `RayClassCharacter.induced` against `classMap` and `RayClassCharacter.IsPrimitive`; prove that the trivial character of a nontrivial modulus is imprimitive." IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract line 35): "Construct equivariant Artin L-functions for the abelian CM extensions used in the modern proof, their S- and T-modifications, integral Stickelberger elements". Library: mathlib DirichletCharacter.changeLevel (Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean:66, `changeLevel {n m : ℕ} (hm : n ∣ m) : DirichletCharacter R n →* DirichletCharacter R m`) and IsPrimitive (line 292) are the ℚ-case only; Tau Ceti has RayClassGroup (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/RayClass/Basic.lean:180) but rg 'RayClassCharacter|HeckeCharacter' over TauCeti/: no hits. Confirmed planned with a change of second owner: ψ_S is ψ (a character of Gal(H/F), i.e. by reciprocity a ray-class character of conductor cond ψ) induced to the modulus n = cond(ψ)·∏_{𝔮∈S, 𝔮∤cond ψ} 𝔮 and extended by zero on ideals meeting S; Layer 9 owns the induced (imprimitive) ray-class character with modulus/conductor, and I.6 owns the S-modification of the equivariant L-functions/Stickelberger elements that ψ_S implements at character level. Replaced AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors:AL.5 (Euler-factor removal for GL_2/Rankin automorphic families, shared vocabulary only). Near miss in Mathlib (changeLevel, ℚ only, ℂ/ring-valued Dirichlet characters); […]

items.name: S-stabilised Eisenstein series E_k(ψ_S, 1)
items.statement: For k ≥ 1 odd, ψ : G → O^* totally odd, S and n as above, there is an S-stabilised Eisenstein series E_k(ψ_S, 1) ∈ M_k(n, Frac O, ψ) with normalised Fourier coefficients c(m, E_k(ψ_S, 1)) = Σ_{r | m} ψ_S(m/r) N r^{k−1} for all nonzero integral ideals m. (Existence asserted without citation in §7.3; the introduction of §7.2 refers the reader to dka and dkv, and §8 cites dka for its constant terms at all cusps.)
items.locator: §7.3, first paragraph and the displayed Fourier coefficient formula (lines 1982–1984)
items.note: External input (shim; dka; dkv (no explicit citation at this point)). The Eisenstein series whose Hecke eigenvalues and constant terms drive Ribet's method; its family over R is E_k(𝛙, 1). Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof." IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3: "This includes Hilbert modular Eisenstein series, their algebraic Fourier coefficients, q-expansion principles, the relevant congruences". Confirmed planned; L3 is the owner of the Hilbert Eisenstein series with Euler factors removed (the S-stabilised E_k(ψ_S,1) with coefficients Σ_{r|m} ψ_S(m/r) N r^{k−1}), I.3 imports it into the Stickelberger normalisation. Dropped AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:KU-hilberteisenstein, which is declared "an aggregation of those owners, not a new proof construction". Library only has the ℚ-case pieces (elliptic Eisenstein series, twisted divisor sums), so not library.

items.name: Constant terms of E_k(ψ_S, 1) at the pairs (1, λ) for k > 1
items.statement: If k > 1 and n ≠ 1 then c_λ(0, E_k(ψ_S, 1)) = 0 for all λ ∈ Cl^+(F). If k > 1 and n = 1 then c_λ(0, E_k(ψ_S, 1)) = 2^{−n} ψ^{−1}(λ) L(ψ^{−1}, 1−k), where n in 2^{−n} is [F:Q].
items.locator: §7.3, the two sentences after the Fourier coefficient formula (lines 1985–1987)
items.note: External input (dka (constant terms; no citation given in §7.3 itself)). Gives the k > 1 rows of the constant-term formula for the group ring form E_k(𝛙, 1). Evidence: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 (the layer extract lines 167–181; atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json stages[22]): "Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof." IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 (the layer extract 3–17; iwasawa-1.json stages[90]): "This includes Hilbert modular Eisenstein series, their algebraic Fourier coefficients, q-expansion principles, the relevant congruences and the distribution/bounded-denominator theorem." L3 audit: "Hilbert modular forms, Hilbert Eisenstein series and any integral q-expansion principle are absent." The aggregation checkpoint AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:KU-hilberteisenstein (iwasawa-1.json stages[18]) confirms L3/I.3 as owners: "Owns any missing modular-form and q-expansion prerequisites". Confirmed planned. Re-ran rg for 'Hilbert ?modular|HilbertModular|totally real.*modular form' over the pinned TauCeti and Mathlib trees: no hits. Mathlib's Mathlib/NumberTheory/ModularForms/EisensteinSeries/*.lean is the Γ(N) ⊂ SL₂(ℤ) series over ℚ only, and TauCeti/NumberTheory/ArithmeticFunction/TwistedDivisorSum.lean:52 `twistedDivisorSum` gives only the non-constant coefficients for Dirichlet characters over ℚ; neither carries a totally real base, a ray-class character ψ, or a constant term c_λ(0,·) at the cusps (1,λ). The higher-weight constant-term formula is part of the 'constant-term argument' of the Deligne–Ribet construction that L3 names and the 'Hilbert modular Eisenstein series, their algebraic Fourier coefficients' of I.3.

items.name: Constant terms of E_1(ψ_S, 1), equation (101)
items.statement: If k = 1: c_λ(0, E_1(ψ_S, 1)) = 2^{−n} L(ψ_S, 0) if n ≠ 1, and c_λ(0, E_1(ψ_S, 1)) = 2^{−n} (L(ψ, 0) + ψ^{−1}(λ) L(ψ^{−1}, 0)) if n = 1, for all λ ∈ Cl^+(F), where L(ψ_S, s) is the L-function of ψ with the Euler factors at the primes of S removed and 2^{−n} has n = [F:Q].
items.locator: §7.3, equation (101)
items.note: External input (dka (no citation given in §7.3 itself)). Weight-one constant terms are the L-values L_S(ψ, 0) that specialise the Stickelberger element; they give the k = 1 rows of the constant terms of E_1(𝛙, 1). Evidence: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 (the layer extract 167–181): "Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof." IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 (the layer extract 3–17): "This includes Hilbert modular Eisenstein series, their algebraic Fourier coefficients, q-expansion principles, the relevant congruences". I.6 audit note (the layer extract 33–45): "Only Dirichlet L-functions over ℚ exist. There are no Hecke or equivariant L-functions of number-field extensions." Confirmed planned. The weight-one constant terms 2^{-n}L(ψ_S,0) (resp. 2^{-n}(L(ψ,0)+ψ^{-1}(λ)L(ψ^{-1},0)) at level 1) are the constant-term argument of the Deligne–Ribet construction that L3 names. Library search: no Hilbert modular forms in either tree; rg 'depleted|Euler factors removed' finds nothing, so the S-depleted L-value L(ψ_S,0) of a ray-class character of a totally real field has no carrier (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/Weight.lean gives only `MultiplicativeIdealWeight K` as a coefficient carrier, no L-function values at 0). Mathlib's Γ(N) Eisenstein series constant terms are the ℚ-case near miss only.

items.name: E_k(ψ_S, 1) is a Hecke eigenform with eigenvalues given by its Fourier coefficients
items.statement: E_k(ψ_S, 1) is an eigenvector for the Hecke operators with eigenvalues the corresponding Fourier coefficients: T_l acts by ψ(l) + N l^{k−1} for primes l ∤ n, and U_l acts by N l^{k−1} for primes l | n.
items.locator: §7.3, itemised list after (101) (lines 1995–1999)
items.note: External input (shim (asserted without explicit citation)). Provides the Eisenstein Hecke eigenvalues, which define the Eisenstein ideal and the homomorphism from the Hecke algebra in §9. Evidence: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 (the layer extract 167–181): "Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof." Checkpoint AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:KU-hilberteisenstein (iwasawa-1.json stages[18]): "Hilbert Eisenstein theory and p-adic interpolation ... Owns any missing modular-form and q-expansion prerequisites; no weight-two shortcut." Consumer: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences" (the layer extract 46–60). Changed: dropped IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.5 from the planned list. I.5 ("Prove Wiles's totally real main conjecture at odd primes. The proof programme includes Hecke algebras ..., Eisenstein ideals") names Eisenstein ideals for Wiles's main conjecture, which is shared vocabulary rather than a plan for the Hecke-eigenvalue formula of E_k(ψ_S,1) used by this paper's §9; the paper's Eisenstein ideal and congruences are under I.7. The eigenform property with eigenvalues ψ(l)+Nl^{k-1} (T_l, l ∤ n) and Nl^{k-1} (U_l, l | n) is a basic property of the Hilbert Eisenstein series that L3 (via the KU-hilberteisenstein checkpoint 'Hilbert Eisenstein theory ... modular-form prerequisites') owns; no layer states the eigenvalue formula itself, so confidence stays medium. Library: TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Eigenform.lean, HeckeSlash/Nebentypus/EigenFromPrimes.lean and Eigenvector.lean are for classical forms on SL₂(ℤ) congruence subgroups (F = ℚ) and do not treat Eisenstein series; […]

items.name: Group ring Eisenstein series E_k(𝛙, 1), equation (102)
items.statement: Let R be a character group ring associated to G (§2.2), let n be divisible by cond(H/F), 𝛙 : G_n^+ → G → R the canonical character, and S the set of primes dividing n. There is an Eisenstein series E_k(𝛙, 1) whose specialisation at each character ψ of G through R is E_k(ψ_S, 1); its q-expansion coefficients are c(m, E_k(𝛙, 1)) = Σ_{r | m, (m/r, n) = 1} 𝛙(m/r) N r^{k−1} ∈ R (equation (102)). Its non-constant coefficients lie in R, but its constant terms only lie in Frac(R) (so it is regarded as a form over Frac(R) of nebentypus 𝛙; cf. §8.3, line 2324: E_k(𝛙^m, 1) ∈ M_k(n/m, Frac(O[G/I_m]), 𝛙^m)).
items.locator: §7.3, equation (102) (label e:ekgp) and surrounding paragraph (lines 2008–2014)
items.note: The Eisenstein family that Ribet's method compares with a cusp form; §8.3 uses E_k(𝛙^m, 1) for the various sub-conductors. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 (the layer extract 3–17): "import the Deligne–Ribet pseudomeasure from AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 and prove its dictionary with the equivariant Stickelberger normalization. This includes Hilbert modular Eisenstein series, their algebraic Fourier coefficients, q-expansion principles, the relevant congruences and the distribution/bounded-denominator theorem." AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3: "Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof." IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract 46–60): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations ...". Confirmed planned. rg -i 'group[- ]ring[- ]valued|group ring Eisenstein|Λ-adic|Silliman' over atlas/areas and roadmaps finds only IHG.6 (the DKSW Ribet lemma), Λ-adic Heegner classes and BSS hypotheses; no layer names group-ring-valued Hilbert modular forms explicitly. The Eisenstein family E_k(𝛙,1) with coefficients Σ_{r|m,(m/r,n)=1} 𝛙(m/r)Nr^{k-1} ∈ R is the Deligne–Ribet group-ring Eisenstein family whose q-expansion/congruence properties I.3 and L3 name ('Hilbert modular Eisenstein series, their algebraic Fourier coefficients, q-expansion principles, the relevant congruences'), and it is the object of I.7's 'Hilbert modular congruences'; hence medium confidence. Library: rg 'group ring valued|GroupRing.*ModularForm|Λ-adic|LambdaAdic' over both trees finds nothing; no Hilbert modular forms exist; Mathlib's Eisenstein series are complex-valued on Γ(N) ⊂ SL₂(ℤ).

items.name: Narrow ray class field H_n and the image Θ_S of the S-depleted Stickelberger element in Frac(R)
items.statement: H_n is the narrow ray class field of F of conductor n, so Gal(H_n/F) ≅ G_n^+. Θ_S^{H_n/F}(s) ∈ C[G_n^+] is the S-depleted Stickelberger element of H_n/F (in the notation of §1: Θ_{S,∅} with depletion set S ∪ S_∞, defined by ψ(Θ_S(s)) = L_S(ψ^{−1}, s) for all characters ψ of G_n^+); its values Θ_S^{H_n/F}(0) and Θ_S^{H_n/F}(1−k) lie in Q[G_n^+] (Siegel–Klingen–Shintani). Θ_S denotes the image in Frac(R) of Θ_S^{H_n/F} ∈ Q[G_n^+] under Q[G_n^+] → Q[G] → Frac(R), and Θ_S^# its image under the involution induced by g ↦ g^{−1}.
items.locator: §7.3, the two sentences after equation (102) (lines 2015–2016)
items.note: Packages the constant terms of E_k(𝛙, 1) as elements of Frac(R); at k = 1 and n ≠ 1 the constant term 2^{−n} Θ_S^#(0) is the quantity Ribet's method exploits. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract 33–45; iwasawa-1.json stages[93]): "Construct equivariant Artin L-functions for the abelian CM extensions used in the modern proof, their S- and T-modifications, integral Stickelberger elements, ray-class modules ..."; audit: "Only Dirichlet L-functions over ℚ exist. There are no Hecke or equivariant L-functions of number-field extensions." ClassFieldTheory Layer 13 (classical-1.json stages[141], id tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ClassFieldTheory#layer-13-norm-theorems-and-class-fields): "define `rayClassField 𝔪` as its class field; ... `narrowHilbertClassField` is `rayClassField` at `GlobalNumberFields.narrowModulus`. ... The Galois/class-group isomorphisms (`gal_rayClassField_equiv_rayClassGroup`, `gal_hilbertClassField_equiv_classGroup`)". AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 (the layer extract 167–181): "the Deligne–Ribet p-adic partial zeta functions/pseudo-measure, including the algebraicity of negative critical values". Confirmed planned; added L3 for the rationality clause. Three parts: (a) the narrow ray class field H_n with Gal(H_n/F) ≅ G_n^+ is planned by ClassFieldTheory Layer 13 (`rayClassField 𝔪` at the modulus n·∞ and `gal_rayClassField_equiv_rayClassGroup`); (b) the S-depleted Stickelberger element Θ_S^{H_n/F}(s) ∈ ℂ[G_n^+] with ψ(Θ_S(s)) = L_S(ψ^{-1},s) is owned by I.6 ('integral Stickelberger elements' with 'S- and T-modifications'); (c) the assertion Θ_S(0), Θ_S(1−k) ∈ ℚ[G_n^+] (Siegel–Klingen–Shintani) is L3's 'algebraicity of negative critical values'. […]

items.name: Constant terms of the group ring Eisenstein series E_k(𝛙, 1)
items.statement: With R, 𝛙, S = primes dividing n, and Θ_S as above, the constant terms of E_k(𝛙, 1) lie in Frac(R) and are, for every λ ∈ Cl^+(F): c_λ(0, E_k(𝛙, 1)) = 2^{−n} · { 0 if k > 1 and n ≠ 1; 𝛙^{−1}(λ) Θ_S(1−k) if k > 1 and n = 1; Θ_S^#(0) if k = 1 and n ≠ 1; Θ_S^#(0) + 𝛙^{−1}(λ) Θ_S(0) if k = 1 and n = 1 }, where 2^{−n} has n = [F:Q]. (Asserted; it interpolates the formulas for E_k(ψ_S, 1) and (101) through the specialisations ψ and the embedding of R into a product of copies of O.)
items.locator: §7.3, final display of §7 (constant terms of E_k(𝛙, 1), lines 2017–2025)
items.note: These constant terms are what §8 must cancel (up to Θ^#) to produce a cusp form congruent to the Eisenstein series. Evidence: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 (the layer extract 167–181): "Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof." IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 (the layer extract 3–17): "prove its dictionary with the equivariant Stickelberger normalization. This includes Hilbert modular Eisenstein series, their algebraic Fourier coefficients, q-expansion principles, the relevant congruences". IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract 46–60): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations ...". Confirmed planned. The four-case formula c_λ(0,E_k(𝛙,1)) = 2^{-n}·{0; 𝛙^{-1}(λ)Θ_S(1−k); Θ_S^#(0); Θ_S^#(0)+𝛙^{-1}(λ)Θ_S(0)} is the group-ring interpolation of items 217–218 (L3's 'constant-term argument') expressed through the Stickelberger element, i.e. the 'dictionary with the equivariant Stickelberger normalization' of I.3, and it is the input to I.7's Hilbert modular congruences (§8 cancels these constant terms). rg over atlas/areas and roadmaps for 'constant[- ]term' finds no stage stating this formula (the other hits are Langlands-style parabolic constant terms and the ℚ-case cusp–Eisenstein decomposition), so medium confidence. Library: no Hilbert modular forms, no Stickelberger element and no group-ring-valued forms in either pinned tree (searches in items 217, 220, 221).

items.name: Lemma 8.1: Θ^# divides p^m in R for m large
items.statement: Let R be the trivial-zero-free character group ring quotient fixed in §7.1 (a quotient of the connected component 𝒪[G_p]_χ in which Θ^# = Θ^#_{Σ,Σ'} is a non-zerodivisor; from §8 on an unadorned Θ denotes the Stickelberger element Θ_{Σ,Σ'} and Θ^# its image under the involution σ ↦ σ^{-1}). Then for all sufficiently large positive integers m there is z ∈ R with Θ^#·z = p^m, i.e. Θ^# divides p^m in R. (Proof: Frac(R) = R ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p, so z = p^m(Θ^#)^{-1} ∈ R once m is large.) Standing choices for the rest of the paper: m is a positive integer satisfying this lemma, enlarged later as needed (m ≥ ord_p(#G_p) for Theorem 8.15; #G_p·Θ^# | p^m for Theorem 8.17; p^m/Θ_{S_∞}(0) ∈ R, plus one more, for Lemma 8.16); k is a positive integer with k ≡ 1 (mod (p−1)p^N) for a sufficiently large integer N > m, and from §8.2.1 on k > 1 is imposed.
items.locator: §8 introduction, Lemma 8.1 (label l:largem), the source 2031–2044 (convention Θ = Θ_{Σ,Σ'} at 2031, choice of m, N, k at 2042–2044; k > 1 at §8.2.1, 2214)
items.note: Fixes the modulus p^m used throughout §8 so that p^m/Θ^# and p^m/(#G_p·Θ^#) lie in R (Theorems 8.17, 8.23, Lemma 8.16). Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract 46–60; iwasawa-1.json stages[94]): "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations. Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma ..."; audit: "Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations and the hypotheses of the generalised Ribet lemma ... | library: absent". Confirmed planned. Lemma 8.1 (Θ^# divides p^m in R for m large, because Θ^# is a non-zerodivisor of the trivial-zero-free quotient R and Frac(R) = R ⊗_{ℤ_p} ℚ_p) is the opening step of the §8 congruence construction, a clearly contained piece of I.7's 'proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... Hilbert modular congruences'; no layer names the lemma, hence medium confidence. Library: the algebraic engine is generic — Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/Defs.lean:133 `IsLocalization.surj` (∀ z : S, ∃ x : R × M, z * algebraMap R S x.2 = algebraMap R S x.1) would give p^m·(Θ^#)^{-1} ∈ R once Frac(R) is identified with R[1/p] — but there is no Stickelberger element, no character group ring quotient R and no statement of this divisibility in either tree, so not library; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6's O-order ring class is only the ambient ring type.

items.name: Definition 8.2: modified Eisenstein series W_k(ψ_𝔓,1)
items.statement: Setting: ψ a totally odd (finite order, 𝒪^*-valued) character of G_F, k ≥ 1 an odd integer, 𝔠_0 = cond(ψ); T a finite nonempty set of primes of F not dividing 𝔠_0, 𝔱 = ∏_{𝔩∈T} 𝔩; 𝔓 an integral ideal coprime to 𝔱; 𝔠 = lcm(𝔠_0, 𝔓) and 𝔫 = 𝔠𝔱; ψ_𝔓 the 𝔓-depleted character (ψ_𝔓(𝔞) = 0 when 𝔞 shares a prime with 𝔓, as in §7.2). Definition: W_k(ψ_𝔓,1) := Σ_{𝔪 | 𝔱} μ(𝔪) ψ(𝔪) N𝔪^k · E_k(ψ_𝔓,1)|_𝔪 ∈ M_k(𝔫, ψ), where μ is the Möbius function on ideals, E_k(ψ_𝔓,1) is the Eisenstein series of §7.2 with Fourier coefficients c(𝔪) = Σ_{𝔯|𝔪} ψ_𝔓(𝔪/𝔯) N𝔯^{k−1}, and f|_𝔪 is the level-raising operator of §7.2.
items.locator: §8.1, Definition 8.2 (unlabelled), the source 2071–2076; notation of §8.1 at 2050–2054
items.note: Central construction: its constant term at ∞ carries L_{S_𝔓,T}(ψ,0), its constant terms at p-unramified cusps vary in weight by the cusp-independent constant L(ψ^{-1},1−k)/L(ψ^{-1},0), and the forms interpolate into a single group ring form (Proposition 8.14). Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract 46–60): "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma for residually indistinguishable characters, the Fitting-ideal comparison, and the passage from modified to unmodified data." AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 (the layer extract 167–181): "the Deligne–Ribet p-adic partial zeta functions/pseudo-measure, including the algebraicity of negative critical values, integral congruences, smoothing factors and Euler factors. Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof." Confirmed planned, with a correction to the library note: TauCeti does have the ideal Möbius function, `TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.moebius` (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ArithmeticDirichletSeries/Moebius.lean:104, the complex-valued restriction of `UniqueFactorizationMonoid.moebius` to nonzero ideals of 𝓞 K, with Möbius inversion), contrary to the previous note's 'no ideal Möbius function beyond the plan'. That is only one ingredient: W_k(ψ_𝔓,1) = Σ_{𝔪|𝔱} μ(𝔪)ψ(𝔪)N𝔪^k E_k(ψ_𝔓,1)|_𝔪 ∈ M_k(𝔫,ψ) needs Hilbert Eisenstein series with depleted character, the level-raising operator f|_𝔪 on Hilbert forms and the space M_k(𝔫,ψ), none of which exist (rg 'Hilbert modular' empty in both trees; TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Degeneracy.lean V_d operator is F = ℚ). […]

items.name: Definition 8.3: the sets J_𝔪 and J_𝔪^c attached to a cusp
items.statement: Let 𝒜 = (A, λ) with A = (a b; c d) ∈ GL_2^+(F), λ ∈ Cl^+(F), and suppose [𝒜] ∈ C_0(𝔠_0, 𝔫). For 𝔪 | 𝔱𝔓, J_𝔪 is the set of prime divisors 𝔩 | 𝔪 such that [𝒜] ∈ C_0(𝔩, 𝔫), and J_𝔪^c is the set of prime divisors 𝔩 | 𝔪 such that [𝒜] ∈ C_∞(𝔩, 𝔫). items.name: Proposition 8.4 (k > 1): constant terms of E_k(ψ_𝔓,1)|_𝔪
items.statement: In the setting of Definition 8.2, let 𝔪 | 𝔱 and let k > 1 be odd. View E_k(ψ_𝔓,1)|_𝔪 ∈ M_k(𝔫, ψ). Its normalized constant term c_𝒜(0) at a cusp 𝒜 = (A, λ), A = (a b; c d), is zero if [𝒜] ∉ C_0(𝔠, 𝔫); if [𝒜] ∈ C_0(𝔠,𝔫) it equals (equation (103)) (τ(ψ)/N𝔠_0^k) · sgn(N(−c)) · ψ(𝔠_𝒜) · (L(ψ^{-1},1−k)/2^n) · ∏_{𝔭|𝔓}(1 − ψ(𝔭)/N𝔭^k) · ∏_{𝔩∈J_𝔪} N𝔩^{-k} · ∏_{𝔩∈J_𝔪^c} ψ^{-1}(𝔩). Convention (Remark 8.5): [𝒜] ∈ C_0(𝔠,𝔫) implies gcd(𝔠_𝒜, 𝔠) = 1, and c = 0 can occur only if 𝔠 = 1; in that case sgn(N c)ψ(𝔠_𝒜) denotes ψ^{-1}(𝔱_λ𝔡𝔟_𝒜) = ψ^{-1}(𝔱_λ𝔡(a)), the value obtained by replacing A by a left Γ_{1,λ}(𝔫)-equivalent matrix with c ≠ 0; more generally, for ψ totally odd of conductor 1 any expression sgn(N x)ψ(x𝔪) is interpreted as ψ(𝔪) even when x = 0. This convention is in force in all later constant-term formulas.

items.name: Theorem 8.8 (Hida, Silliman): level-1 forms V_k ≡ 1 mod p^m
items.statement: Fix a positive integer m. For positive integers k ≡ 0 (mod (p−1)p^N) with N sufficiently large (depending on m), there is a Hilbert modular form V_k ∈ M_k(1, Z_p, 1) (level 1, trivial nebentypus, Z_p-coefficients) such that V_k ≡ 1 (mod p^m), meaning c(𝔪, V_k) ≡ 0 (mod p^m) for all nonzero ideals 𝔪 and c_λ(0, V_k) ≡ 1 (mod p^m) for all λ ∈ Cl^+(F), and such that the normalized constant term c_𝒜(0, V_k) at each cusp [𝒜] ∈ cusps(1) is ≡ 1 (mod p^m). (Existence of a form ≡ 1 mod p is Hida's, cited as Wiles, Lemma 1.4.2; the refined statement at all cusps is Silliman, Theorem 10.7.)

items.name: Level 𝔫 = cond(H/F)∏_{𝔩∈T}𝔩 and its p-part 𝔓
items.statement: For an integral ideal 𝔫 of F, 𝔓 denotes the p-part of 𝔫, 𝔓 = gcd(p^∞, 𝔫), the largest divisor of 𝔫 supported on primes above p. From §8.3 on (and already in Theorems 8.9 and 8.15, which are stated for the group ring data): R is the trivial-zero-free quotient (§7.1) of the connected component 𝒪[G_p]_χ associated to a totally odd faithful character χ of G' (G = G_p × G', G_p the p-Sylow subgroup); 𝛙: G_𝔫^+ → G → R^* is the canonical character; the level is 𝔫 = cond(H/F)·∏_{𝔩∈T}𝔩 and 𝔓 = gcd(p^∞, 𝔫).
items.locator: §8.2, sentence before Theorem 8.9, the source 2200; §8.3 opening paragraph, the source 2289–2295; recalled in §8.4 display, 2443–2447
items.note: Fixes the level of the group ring family and the cusps C_∞(𝔓,𝔫) at which Silliman's constant-term results apply. Evidence: the layer extract lines 1403–1406 (ClassFieldTheory Layer 12): "`IsAdmissibleModulus K L 𝔪` says that the ray subgroup of `𝔪` lies in the idele-class norm subgroup of `L/K`, i.e. that the conductor divides `𝔪`; `abelianConductor` is the smallest admissible modulus and `isAdmissibleModulus_iff_abelianConductor_dvd` its characterization" — this is cond(H/F), the only non-trivial ingredient of 𝔫 = cond(H/F)·∏_{𝔩∈T}𝔩. Audit at line 1454: "Admissible moduli, abelianConductor ... library: absent". Library check (verified): rg 'abelianConductor|IsAdmissibleModulus' over Mathlib/ and TauCeti/ returns nothing; the only conductors are Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean:246 `DirichletCharacter.conductor` and the ring conductor Mathlib/RingTheory/Conductor.lean; rg 'pPart|primaryPart' finds only TauCeti's `AddSubgroup.primaryPart` (TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Primary/Subgroup.lean:25, abelian groups, not ideals); Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/Ideal/Lemmas.lean:326 gives `StrongNormalizedGCDMonoid (Ideal A)` (ideal gcds) but no gcd with p^∞. IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract line 48) says only "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences" and does not name the level. Confirmed planned, but the owner list is corrected: the item's substantive content is the conductor of the abelian extension H/F, which Class Field Theory Layer 12 names as `abelianConductor` (the most foundational owner); the T-primes factor and the p-part gcd(p^∞,𝔫) are elementary ideal arithmetic on top of it (Mathlib has ideal gcds but no p-part).
