items.name: Theorem 8.9 (Silliman): group ring forms G_k(𝛙) with prescribed constant terms
items.statement: Let R, 𝛙: G_𝔫^+ → G → R^* and the level 𝔫 (with cond(H/F) | 𝔫) be as in §7.1/§8.3 and 𝔓 = gcd(p^∞,𝔫). For all sufficiently large odd positive integers k there exists a group ring valued form G_k(𝛙) ∈ M_k(𝔫, R, 𝛙) whose normalized constant term at 𝒜 = (A, λ), A = (a b; c d), for [𝒜] ∈ C_∞(𝔫) equals sgn(N a)·𝛙^{-1}(a𝔟_𝒜^{-1}), and whose constant term at every cusp [𝒜] ∈ C_∞(𝔓,𝔫) ∖ C_∞(𝔫) equals 0. Convention (Remark 8.10): if 𝔫 = 1 the expression sgn(N a)𝛙^{-1}(a𝔟_𝒜^{-1}) is understood to equal 𝛙(𝔟_𝒜) even if a = 0. (Proved by Silliman, Theorem 10.9, via surjectivity of the total constant term map.)
items.locator: §8.2, Theorem 8.9 (label t:auxforms), the source 2203–2207; Remark 8.10 at 2209–2210
items.note: External input (dks, Theorem 10.9 (J. Silliman, Group ring valued Hilbert modular forms)). G_k(𝛙) is subtracted (with coefficient L_{S_𝔓,T}(ψ,0)/2^n, i.e. Θ^#/2^n in the family) to kill the constant terms at cusps in C_∞ in Propositions 8.11, 8.12 and Theorems 8.17, 8.18. Evidence: Verified: rg -il 'hilbert ?modular|HilbertModular|group.?ring.?valued' over Mathlib/ and TauCeti/ returns no file. Atlas: rg -il 'group.?ring.?valued|prescribed constant|cuspidalis' over atlas/areas/*.json, roadmaps/*.json and packets returns nothing; 'Silliman' hits only atlas/areas/modular-1.json stage IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.6 ("Prove the reusable GL₂ extension theorem of Dasgupta–Kakde–Silliman–Wang ... Theorems 1.1 and 2.1"), the Ribet lemma, not the modular-forms theorem. Nearest descriptions read: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract line 48: "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences"), AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 (line 169: "Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof", i.e. for Deligne–Ribet), the KU-hilberteisenstein checkpoint (line 188: "Owns any missing modular-form and q-expansion prerequisites", an aggregation checkpoint, "not a new proof construction"). Confirmed missing. Silliman's Theorem 10.9 (existence of a group ring valued Hilbert modular form with prescribed constant terms on C_∞(𝔫), zero on C_∞(𝔓,𝔫)∖C_∞(𝔫), via surjectivity of the total constant term map) is named by no stage: L3/I.3 plan Hilbert Eisenstein series and a constant-term argument for the Deligne–Ribet measure, not forms with prescribed constant terms; I.7 names only the resulting congruences; the KU checkpoint's catch-all "any missing modular-form prerequisites" is vocabulary, not a named plan. items.name: Cases 1, 1a, 1b, 2: the ideals 𝔓', 𝔓'' and the case trichotomy
items.statement: With 𝔫 = cond(H/F)∏_{𝔩∈T}𝔩 and 𝔓 = gcd(p^∞, 𝔫), define 𝔓' = ∏_{𝔭 | p, 𝔭 ∤ 𝔓} 𝔭 (the product of the primes above p not dividing 𝔫) and 𝔓'' = ∏_{𝔭 | 𝔓', χ(𝔭) ≠ 1} 𝔭. Case 1: cond(H/F) is not divisible by any prime above p, i.e. 𝔓 = 1 (gcd(𝔫,p) = 1; then 𝔓' is the product of all primes above p). Case 2: cond(H/F) is divisible by some prime above p, i.e. 𝔓 ≠ 1; in case 2 (§8.2.2) ψ has conductor 𝔠_0 possibly divisible by primes above p, 𝔩_1,…,𝔩_d are distinct primes not dividing 𝔠_0p, 𝔫 = 𝔠_0𝔩_1⋯𝔩_d𝔓' with 𝔓' (there) a product of powers of some but not necessarily all primes above p, 𝔠 = lcm(𝔠_0,𝔓), and S_𝔓 = S_∞ ∪ {primes dividing 𝔓}. Trichotomy (§8.4): Case 1a: 𝔓 = 1 and 𝔓' ≠ 𝔓'' (χ(𝔭) = 1 for some 𝔭 | p); Case 1b: 𝔓 = 1 and 𝔓' = 𝔓'' (χ(𝔭) ≠ 1 for all 𝔭 | p); Case 2: 𝔓 ≠ 1.
items.locator: §8.2.1 heading (the source 2212), §8.2.2 opening paragraph (2262–2263), §8.4 opening displays (2443–2456)
items.note: The cases require different cuspidalisation arguments (Propositions 8.11 vs 8.12, Theorems 8.17 vs 8.18) and different ordinary projections and moduli xΘ^# vs Θ^# (Corollaries 8.19, 8.21, Theorem 8.23). Evidence: Verified: python scan of every stage description in atlas/areas/*.json and roadmaps/*.json for 'trivial zero' hits only AnalyticNumberTheory AN.1/AN.3 (trivial zeros of L-functions) and QuadraticFormInvariants (nontrivial zero of a quadratic form); 'p-part' hits only BSD stages; no stage names 𝔓', 𝔓'', χ(𝔭) ≠ 1 or a case split on primes above p dividing the conductor. IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract line 48) reads: "The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations. Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma ..." — no case trichotomy. Libraries: rg 'hilbert ?modular' empty in both trees; no conductor of H/F (only DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean:246 and RingTheory/Conductor.lean); Mathlib `Ideal.primesOver` and `StrongNormalizedGCDMonoid (Ideal A)` (DedekindDomain/Ideal/Lemmas.lean:326) are the only related carriers. Confirmed missing. Proof-internal bookkeeping of DK §8 (𝔓', 𝔓'', Cases 1a/1b/2); the layer that would host it, I.7, names neither the ideals nor the trichotomy, and no other stage does. Nothing in either library concerns it beyond generic Dedekind ideal arithmetic.

items.name: Proposition 8.11: constant terms of f_k(ψ) divisible by p^m (case 1)
items.statement: Suppose 𝔫 is not divisible by any prime above p (case 1, so 𝔓 = 1 and 𝔠 = 𝔠_0 = cond(ψ)). Fix a positive integer m. For positive k ≡ 1 (mod (p−1)p^N) with N sufficiently large, and for each character ψ of R, the form f_k(ψ) := W_1(ψ,1)·V_{k−1} − (L(ψ^{-1},0)/L(ψ^{-1},1−k))·W_k(ψ,1) − (L_{S_∞,T}(ψ,0)/2^n)·G_k(ψ) ∈ M_k(𝔫, ψ) has normalized constant terms at all cusps of level 𝔫 divisible by p^m. Here V_{k−1} is Hida's form (Theorem 8.8) and G_k(ψ) is the specialization at ψ of the group ring form G_k(𝛙) of Theorem 8.9. Proof: constant terms vanish outside C_0(𝔠,𝔫) ∪ C_∞(𝔠,𝔫); on C_∞(𝔫) the W_1 term sgn(N a)ψ^{-1}(a𝔟_𝒜^{-1})L_{S_∞,T}(ψ,0)/2^n times c_𝒜(0,V_{k−1}) ≡ 1 cancels the G_k term mod p^m; for [𝒜] ∈ C_0(𝔠,𝔫) with J = {𝔩 ∈ T : [𝒜] ∈ C_0(𝔩,𝔫)} the constant term is (equation (104)) τ(ψ) sgn(N(−c)) ψ(𝔠_𝒜) (L(ψ^{-1},0)/2^n) ∏_{𝔩∈J}(1 − ψ(𝔩)) · (∏_{𝔩∉J}(1 − N𝔩)/N𝔠_0) · [c_𝒜(0,V_{k−1}) − N𝔠_0^{1−k}∏_{𝔩∉J}(1 − N𝔩^k)/(1 − N𝔩)], plus, when 𝔠 = 1 and [𝒜] ∈ C_∞(𝔫), ψ(𝔟_𝒜)(L_{S_∞,T}(ψ,0)/2^n)[c_𝒜(0,V_{k−1}) − 1]; the bracketed expressions tend p-adically to 0 as N → ∞ since c_𝒜(0,V_{k−1}) → 1 and N𝔠_0^{1−k}∏(1 − N𝔩^k)/(1 − N𝔩) → 1.
items.locator: §8.2.1, Proposition 8.11 (label p:wnop), the source 2216–2258; equation (104) (label e:jprod) at 2242–2258
items.note: Supplies the hypothesis of Theorem 8.15 (p^m-divisible constant terms) to produce the cusp form of Theorem 8.17 in case 1. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7, the layer extract line 48 (and atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json stage 94): "Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma" — Proposition 8.11 (f_k(ψ) has all normalized constant terms ≡ 0 mod p^m for k ≡ 1 mod (p−1)p^N) is one of these Hilbert modular congruences in the DK proof. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3, the layer extract line 169: "Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof"; IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3, line 7: "Hilbert modular Eisenstein series, their algebraic Fourier coefficients, q-expansion principles, the relevant congruences" — these own the Eisenstein constant terms (104). The congruence is a named obligation of I.7 ("the necessary Hilbert modular congruences" of the Dasgupta–Kakde odd-prime proof) with the Eisenstein constant-term computation owned by L3/I.3; no more foundational or more exact owner exists (no stage names f_k(ψ), Hida's V_{k−1} or Silliman's G_k). Not library: neither tree has Hilbert modular forms.

items.name: Proposition 8.12: constant terms at C_∞(𝔓,𝔫) divisible by p^m (case 2)
items.statement: In the setting of case 2 (§8.2.2): ψ a totally odd character of conductor 𝔠_0 (possibly divisible by primes above p), 𝔩_1,…,𝔩_d distinct primes not dividing 𝔠_0p, 𝔫 = 𝔠_0𝔩_1⋯𝔩_d𝔓' with 𝔓' a product of powers of some primes above p, 𝔓 = gcd(𝔫,p^∞) ≠ 1, 𝔠 = lcm(𝔠_0,𝔓), S_𝔓 = S_∞ ∪ {𝔭 | 𝔓}, m fixed. For positive integers k ≡ 1 (mod (p−1)p^N) with N sufficiently large, the form W_1(ψ_𝔓,1)·V_{k−1} − (L_{S_𝔓,T}(ψ,0)/2^n)·G_k(ψ) ∈ M_k(𝔫,ψ) has normalized constant terms at all cusps in C_∞(𝔓,𝔫) divisible by p^m (V_{k−1} from Theorem 8.8, G_k(ψ) the specialization of G_k(𝛙) from Theorem 8.9). Proof: by Proposition 8.7 the constant terms of W_1(ψ_𝔓,1) are supported on C_∞(𝔠_0𝔱,𝔫) ∪ C_0(𝔠,𝔫), and since 𝔓 ≠ 1, (C_∞(𝔠_0𝔱,𝔫) ∪ C_0(𝔠,𝔫)) ∩ C_∞(𝔓,𝔫) = C_∞(𝔫); G_k(ψ) vanishes on C_∞(𝔓,𝔫) ∖ C_∞(𝔫); at [𝒜] ∈ C_∞(𝔫) the normalized constant term of W_1(ψ_𝔓,1) is sgn(N a)ψ^{-1}(a𝔟_𝒜^{-1})L_{S_𝔓,T}(ψ,0)/2^n, that of V_{k−1} is ≡ 1 mod p^m, and that of G_k(ψ) is sgn(N a)ψ^{-1}(a𝔟_𝒜^{-1}).
items.locator: §8.2.2, Proposition 8.12 (label p:cuspw), the source 2266–2285
items.note: Supplies the hypothesis of Theorem 8.15 in case 2, giving Theorem 8.18. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7, the layer extract line 48: "The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences" — Proposition 8.12 (W_1(ψ_𝔓,1)·V_{k−1} − (L_{S_𝔓,T}(ψ,0)/2^n)·G_k(ψ) has normalized constant terms divisible by p^m on C_∞(𝔓,𝔫), case 𝔓 ≠ 1) is the case-2 congruence of that proof. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3, line 169: "Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle and constant-term argument required for that proof" owns the constant terms of the Eisenstein series W_1(ψ_𝔓,1) (Proposition 8.7) used in the proof. Library: rg 'hilbert ?modular' over Mathlib/ and TauCeti/ empty (verified). Confirmed planned, for the same reasons as Proposition 8.11: a Hilbert modular congruence named as an obligation of I.7, with Eisenstein constant terms supplied by L3/I.3. The cusp sets C_∞(𝔓,𝔫) and Silliman's G_k are not named by any layer, and both libraries lack Hilbert modular forms.

items.name: Lemma 8.13: factorisation of the level relative to cond(ψ)
items.statement: Let ψ be a character of R (i.e. ψ ∈ Ψ, ψ|_{G'} = χ) and 𝔠_0 = cond(ψ). Then 𝔫 = cond(H/F)∏_{𝔩∈T}𝔩 can be written 𝔫 = 𝔠_0𝔩_1⋯𝔩_d𝔓' where the 𝔩_i are distinct primes not dividing 𝔠_0p and 𝔓' is divisible only by primes above p. Equivalently: if 𝔩 ∤ p and 𝔩^r | cond(H/F) with r ≥ 2 then 𝔩^r | cond(ψ). Proof: with H_p = fixed field of G' (Gal(H_p/F) = G_p) and H' = fixed field of G_p (Gal(H'/F) = G'), H = H_pH'; G_p is a p-group and 𝔩 ∤ p so 𝔩 is at most tamely ramified in H_p; hence 𝔩^r | cond(H'/F), and χ faithful on G' gives 𝔩^r | cond(χ); writing ψ = ψ_pχ with ψ_p a character of G_p, the 𝔩-part of cond(ψ_p) is at most 𝔩, so 𝔩^r | cond(ψ).
items.locator: §8.3, Lemma 8.13 (label l:conductor), the source 2297–2312
items.note: Ensures every specialization W_k(ψ_𝔓,1) is of the shape treated in §8.1–8.2 at the fixed level 𝔫, so a single group ring form can interpolate them (Proposition 8.14). Evidence: Libraries (verified): rg -il 'tamely|IsTame|tame ramif|TamelyRamified' over Mathlib/ and TauCeti/ returns no file; conductors are only `DirichletCharacter.conductor` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/DirichletCharacter/Basic.lean:234–246) and the ring `conductor` (Mathlib/RingTheory/Conductor.lean); no conductor of an abelian extension or of a ray-class character. Atlas: 'tamely' hits LocalFieldsRamification Layer 3 (atlas/areas/classical-1.json stage 168: "Define `IsTamelyRamified K L` by `p ∤ e` ... If L/K is finite, totally ramified, and tamely ramified of degree e, then there are a uniformizer π of K and α ∈ L with α^e = π"), NumberFieldArithmetic 6.4 (the layer extract line 3473: "`v_P(𝔡) = e − 1` if and only if the completed local extension is tamely ramified", the different, not the conductor) and unrelated stages; ClassFieldTheory Layer 7 (line 1086–1087) plans `conductorExponent`, `characterConductorExp` "with minimality and the unramified criterion"; Layer 13 (line 1497–1499) plans the "abelian conductor–discriminant formula for `abelianConductor`" and "`IsAdmissibleModulus.mem_support_of_ramified`"; GlobalNumberFields Layer 9 (line 1946–1947) plans "the finite conductor ideal ... the least ray conductor modulus" for Hecke/ray class characters. Confirmed missing. The content of Lemma 8.13 is the bound 'conductor exponent ≤ 1 at a prime 𝔩 ∤ p for a character of the p-group G_p' (tame ramification of p-power extensions away from p) and the resulting factorisation 𝔫 = 𝔠_0𝔩_1⋯𝔩_d𝔓'. […]

items.name: Inertia subgroups I_𝔪, norm elements N I_𝔪 and the characters 𝛙^𝔪
items.statement: Let 𝔱 be the product of the primes dividing 𝔫/𝔓. For 𝔪 | 𝔱, I_𝔪 ⊂ G is the subgroup generated by the inertia groups I_v for v | 𝔪, and N I_𝔪 = Σ_{g∈I_𝔪} g ∈ 𝒪[G]. 𝛙^𝔪: G_{𝔫/𝔪}^+ → G/I_𝔪 → 𝒪[G/I_𝔪]^* is the canonical character corresponding to the maximal subextension of H/F in which the primes dividing 𝔪 are unramified, and E_k(𝛙^𝔪,1) ∈ M_k(𝔫/𝔪, Frac(𝒪[G/I_𝔪]), 𝛙^𝔪) is the group ring Eisenstein series (102) attached to 𝛙^𝔪; if ψ is a character of G unramified at all primes dividing 𝔪, the specialization of E_k(𝛙^𝔪,1) at ψ is E_k(ψ_{𝔫/𝔪},1). Fact used: #I_𝔪 divides ∏_{v|𝔪}(1 − N v^k) in Z_p.
items.locator: §8.3, proof of Proposition 8.14, first paragraphs, the source 2320–2328
items.note: Auxiliary data entering the definition (105) of the group ring form W_k(𝛙,1). Evidence: Verified near misses: Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Defs.lean:154 `abbrev inertia : Subgroup G := I.toAddSubgroup.inertia G` with `mem_inertia` (line 157: σ ∈ I.inertia G ↔ ∀ x, σ • x − x ∈ I) is the inertia group of one ideal, not the subgroup I_𝔪 generated by inertia groups of all v | 𝔪; Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Basic.lean:284 `def norm : Module.End k V := ∑ g : G, ρ g` and TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/RelativeNorm.lean:75 `def relNorm : Module.End R V := ∑ q : G ⧸ H, ρ q.out` are norm operators on representations, not the element N I_𝔪 ∈ 𝒪[G]. rg 'hilbert ?modular|group.?ring.?valued' over both trees empty, so E_k(𝛙^𝔪,1) and 𝛙^𝔪 have no carrier. Atlas: rg 'group.?ring.?valued|norm element' over areas/*.json, roadmaps/*.json, packets returns nothing; 'inertia' hits in iwasawa-1.json are IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.1 ("decomposition and inertia groups" of the cyclotomic Z_p-extension) and L1/L2 (inertia part of Galois groups of Z_p-extensions), not inertia subgroups of a finite abelian CM extension; L3 (the layer extract line 169) and I.3 (line 7) plan only scalar Hilbert Eisenstein series for Deligne–Ribet. Confirmed missing. The item bundles the DK-specific data I_𝔪, N I_𝔪, the canonical character 𝛙^𝔪 of the maximal 𝔪-unramified subextension, the lower-level group-ring Eisenstein series E_k(𝛙^𝔪,1) with its specialisation property, and #I_𝔪 | ∏_{v|𝔪}(1 − Nv^k). The group-theoretic pieces have near-miss carriers (`Ideal.inertia`, `Representation.norm`/`relNorm`), but the group-ring-valued Eisenstein series is absent from both libraries and from every layer description; no stage names group-ring-valued Hilbert modular forms.

items.name: Norm-lift map 𝒪[G/I_𝔪] → R and the forms N I_𝔪·Ẽ_k(𝛙^𝔪,1)
items.statement: There is a canonical 𝒪[G]-module map 𝒪[G/I_𝔪] → 𝒪[G] → R, x ↦ N I_𝔪·x̃, where x̃ is an arbitrary lift of x to 𝒪[G]; it is independent of the choice of lift. Applying it coefficientwise to E_k(𝛙^𝔪,1) gives a form N I_𝔪·Ẽ_k(𝛙^𝔪,1) ∈ M_k(𝔫/𝔪, Frac(R)) all of whose non-constant q-expansion coefficients lie in R. If a character ψ of R is nontrivial on I_𝔪 then ψ(N I_𝔪) = 0.
items.locator: §8.3, proof of Proposition 8.14, the source 2329–2336
items.note: Transports the lower-level group ring Eisenstein series into R-valued forms of level 𝔫 for the interpolation (105). items.name: Equation (105): the group ring form W_k(𝛙,1)
items.statement: W_k(𝛙,1) := Σ_{𝔪|𝔱} N I_𝔪·Ẽ_k(𝛙^𝔪,1)|_𝔪 · 𝛙^𝔪(𝔪) · (1/#I_𝔪) · ∏_{v|𝔪}(1 − N v^k) ∈ M_k(𝔫, Frac(R), 𝛙), with 𝔱 the product of the primes dividing 𝔫/𝔓 and I_𝔪, 𝛙^𝔪, Ẽ_k as above; its non-constant q-expansion coefficients lie in R. Variants: W_k(𝛙,1_p) and W_1(𝛙_p,1) are defined in the same way with the pair of characters (𝛙,1) replaced by (𝛙,1_p), resp. (𝛙_p,1), the subscript p meaning depletion at all primes above p; W_1(𝛙_𝔓,1) and W_1(𝛙_{𝔓𝔓''},1) are defined likewise with 𝛙 depleted at the primes dividing 𝔓, resp. 𝔓𝔓''.

items.name: Proposition 8.14: W_k(𝛙,1) interpolates W_k(ψ_𝔓,1) with integral non-constant coefficients
items.statement: For all odd k ≥ 1, the unique form W_k(𝛙,1) ∈ M_k(𝔫, Frac(R), 𝛙) that specializes to W_k(ψ_𝔓,1) for every character ψ of R (𝔫 = cond(H/F)∏_{𝔩∈T}𝔩, 𝔓 = gcd(p^∞,𝔫)) has all non-constant q-expansion coefficients c(𝔪, W_k(𝛙,1)), 𝔪 ≠ 0, lying in R; it is given explicitly by (105). Proof: integrality of (105) is clear from the construction; for the specialization at ψ, let 𝔠_0 = cond(ψ) and 𝔱' the product of the primes dividing 𝔱 not dividing 𝔠_0, so 𝔫 = 𝔠_0𝔱'𝔓' by Lemma 8.13; terms with ψ nontrivial on I_𝔪 vanish, and the sum becomes Σ_{𝔪'|𝔱'} μ(𝔪')N𝔪'^kψ(𝔪')·(Σ_{𝔪|𝔱'/𝔪'} ψ(𝔪)E_k(ψ_{(𝔱'/(𝔪'𝔪))𝔓},1)|_𝔪)|_{𝔪'}, and the inner sum equals E_k(ψ_𝔓,1) by induction on the number of prime factors of 𝔱'/𝔪' using E_k(ψ_{𝔞𝔩},1)|_𝔪 + ψ(𝔩)E_k(ψ_𝔞,1)|_{𝔪𝔩} = E_k(ψ_𝔞,1)|_𝔪; hence the specialization is W_k(ψ_𝔓,1).

items.name: Theorem 8.15 (Silliman): group ring correction making forms cuspidal at C_∞(𝔓,𝔫)
items.statement: Fix a positive integer m ≥ ord_p(#G_p). The following holds for all sufficiently large odd integers k. Let {f_ψ ∈ M_k(𝔫, E, ψ)} be a collection of modular forms indexed by the characters ψ of G belonging to χ (ψ|_{G'} = χ), such that the normalized constant terms of each f_ψ at representatives of each cusp A ∈ C_∞(𝔓,𝔫) are divisible by p^m. Then there exists a group ring family h(𝛙) ∈ M_k(𝔫, R, 𝛙) such that for every such ψ the specialization h(ψ) satisfies: f̃_ψ := f_ψ − (p^m/#G_p)·h(ψ) has constant term 0 at all cusps A ∈ C_∞(𝔓,𝔫). If 𝔓 = 1 (so C_∞(𝔓,𝔫) = cusps(𝔫)) then f̃_ψ is cuspidal; if 𝔓 ≠ 1 then e_𝔓^ord(f̃_ψ) is cuspidal, where e_𝔓^ord = ∏_{𝔭|𝔓} e_𝔭^ord is the ordinary projector of §7.2. (Silliman, Theorem 10.10.)
items.locator: §8.3, Theorem 8.15 (label p:minuspm), the source 2369–2372

Converts the p^m-divisibility of constant terms (Propositions 8.11, 8.12) into an honest group ring cusp form (Theorems 8.17, 8.18). Near misses checked and rejected: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 line 169 "constant-term argument required for that proof" (Deligne–Ribet's constant-term argument, a different statement); AutomorphicBundles:B5 "Construct q-expansions at modular and Hilbert cusps ... Identify cuspidality with the appropriate boundary vanishing condition" (the cusp/q-expansion carrier, not a constant-term-killing family); AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups:AF.3 (adelic constant terms along parabolics). Library: rg -il 'group.ring.valued|Silliman|hilbert modular|ordinary projector' over both pinned trees: no hit; Mathlib's cusp forms (NumberTheory/ModularForms/CuspFormSubmodule.lean) are over SL₂(ℤ)/congruence subgroups only. items.name: The element x = Θ_{S_∞}(1−k)/Θ_{S_∞}(0)
items.statement: In case 1 (gcd(𝔫,p) = 1), x := Θ_{S_∞}(1−k)/Θ_{S_∞}(0) ∈ Frac(R), where Θ_S(s) denotes the image in Frac(R) of the S-depleted Stickelberger element of H_𝔫/F at s (§7.2), so that ψ(Θ_{S_∞}(s)) = L(ψ^{-1}, s) for characters ψ of R; x is well defined because the specializations L(ψ^{-1},0) of the denominator are nonzero. In the statement of Theorem 8.23, x is this element in case 1a and x = 1 in cases 1b and 2.

items.name: Lemma 8.16: x lies in R, is a non-zerodivisor, and x ≡ ∏_{𝔭|p}(1 − χ(𝔭)^{-1}) mod 𝔪_R
items.statement: Suppose we are in case 1, gcd(𝔫,p) = 1. For N sufficiently large and positive k ≡ 1 (mod (p−1)p^N), the element x = Θ_{S_∞}(1−k)/Θ_{S_∞}(0) ∈ Frac(R) lies in R and is a non-zerodivisor satisfying (equation (106)) x ≡ ∏_{𝔭|p}(1 − χ(𝔭)^{-1}) (mod 𝔪_R), 𝔪_R the maximal ideal of the local ring R. Proof: numerator and denominator have nonzero specializations, so x ∈ R implies x is a non-zerodivisor; with S_p = S_∞ ∪ {𝔭 | p}, Θ_{S_p}(1−k) = ∏_{𝔭|p}(1 − σ_𝔭^{-1}N𝔭^{k−1})Θ_{S_∞}(1−k) (σ_𝔭 the Frobenius, each 𝔭 | p unramified in H/F in case 1); y(k) := Θ_{S_p}(1−k) − Θ_{S_p}(0) tends p-adically to 0 as N → ∞ (p-adic L-functions), so y(k) ∈ p^m R for N large; choosing m with p^m/Θ_{S_∞}(0) ∈ R gives (equation (107)) y(k)/Θ_{S_∞}(0) = x∏_{𝔭|p}(1 − σ_𝔭^{-1}N𝔭^{k−1}) − ∏_{𝔭|p}(1 − σ_𝔭^{-1}) ∈ R; the Euler factors 1 − σ_𝔭^{-1}N𝔭^{k−1} are units in R for k > 1, so x ∈ R; increasing m by 1 puts y(k)/Θ_{S_∞}(0) in 𝔪_R, giving (106).
items.locator: §8.3, Lemma 8.16 (label l:xdef), equations (106) (label e:xcong) and (107) (label e:buty), the source 2375–2401

items.name: p-adic continuity of the depleted Stickelberger element: Θ_{S_p}(1−k) → Θ_{S_p}(0)
items.statement: For the p-depleted Stickelberger element Θ_{S_p}(s) of H_𝔫/F (S_p = S_∞ ∪ {𝔭 | p}) with image in Frac(R), the element y(k) = Θ_{S_p}(1−k) − Θ_{S_p}(0) tends p-adically to 0 for positive integers k ≡ 1 (mod (p−1)p^N) as N → ∞; in particular y(k) ∈ R for N large and, for any m, y(k) ∈ p^m R for N sufficiently large. Invoked as 'the theory of p-adic L-functions' (the Deligne–Ribet / Cassou-Noguès p-adic L-function interpolating L_{S_p}(ψ^{-1},1−k)); no citation key is given at this point of the paper.

items.name: Theorem 8.17: cuspidal group ring form F̃_k(𝛙) in case 1
items.statement: In case 1 (gcd(𝔫,p) = 1), for positive k ≡ 1 (mod (p−1)p^N) and N sufficiently large, there exists a group ring form H_k(𝛙) ∈ M_k(𝔫, R, 𝛙) such that F̃_k(𝛙) := x·W_1(𝛙,1)·V_{k−1} − W_k(𝛙,1) − xΘ^#·H_k(𝛙) lies in S_k(𝔫, R, 𝛙) (cuspidal, all q-expansion coefficients in R), where x = Θ_{S_∞}(1−k)/Θ_{S_∞}(0) ∈ R is as in Lemma 8.16, V_{k−1} is Hida's form (Theorem 8.8) and W_k(𝛙,1), W_1(𝛙,1) are the forms (105). Proof: f_k(𝛙) := W_1(𝛙,1)V_{k−1} − x^{-1}W_k(𝛙,1) − (Θ^#/2^n)G_k(𝛙) ∈ M_k(𝔫, Frac(R), 𝛙) specializes at ψ to f_k(ψ) of Proposition 8.11, whose constant terms are divisible by p^m; Theorem 8.15 gives h_k(𝛙) ∈ M_k(𝔫,R,𝛙) with f̃_k(𝛙) = f_k(𝛙) − (p^m/#G_p)h_k(𝛙) cuspidal; choosing m with #G_p·Θ^# | p^m in R, put H_k(𝛙) := G_k(𝛙)/2^n + (p^m/(#G_p·Θ^#))h_k(𝛙) ∈ M_k(𝔫,R,𝛙), and F̃_k(𝛙) = x·f̃_k(𝛙). Integrality of the non-constant coefficients of xW_1(𝛙,1)V_{k−1} holds because the non-constant coefficients of V_{k−1} are highly divisible by p (the constant terms of W_1(𝛙,1) lie only in Frac(R)); there is nothing to check for constant terms since F̃_k(𝛙) is cuspidal.
items.locator: §8.3, Theorem 8.17 (label t:fk1), the source 2404–2431 (auxiliary forms f_k(𝛙), h_k(𝛙), H_k(𝛙) in the proof at 2412–2428)

Confirmed. Its inputs Hida's V_{k−1} (Theorem 8.8) and Silliman's Theorem 8.15 are separate items. Absent from both libraries.

items.name: Theorem 8.18: cuspidal group ring form F̃_k(𝛙) in case 2
items.statement: Suppose we are in case 2, gcd(𝔫,p) ≠ 1 (so 𝔓 ≠ 1). For positive integers k ≡ 1 (mod (p−1)p^N) and N sufficiently large, there exists a group ring form H_k(𝛙) ∈ M_k(𝔫, R, 𝛙) such that F̃_k(𝛙) := e_𝔓^ord(W_1(𝛙,1)·V_{k−1} − Θ^#·H_k(𝛙)) lies in S_k(𝔫, R, 𝛙); here W_1(𝛙,1) is the form (105) (specializing to W_1(ψ_𝔓,1)), V_{k−1} is Hida's form and e_𝔓^ord = ∏_{𝔭|𝔓} e_𝔭^ord. Proved exactly as Theorem 8.17, using Theorem 8.15 and Proposition 8.12 in place of Proposition 8.11.
items.locator: §8.3, Theorem 8.18 (unlabelled), the source 2434–2438
items.note: Case-2 analogue of Theorem 8.17; input to Corollary 8.21. Evidence: Verified the layer extract line 48 (I.7): "The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences"; audit line 53 "Hilbert modular congruences ... for the Hilbert/Eisenstein representation | library: absent". Line 225 (L5): "Instantiate L0a on the integral Hilbert automorphic/cohomology modules furnished by the Shimura and general automorphic owners, proving their finite quotient hypotheses ... Establish Hida control on the actual ordinary loci"; L5 audit (line 228): "Instantiation of the ordinary projector on integral Hilbert automorphic/cohomology modules ... library: absent". Library: rg -il 'Hida|ordinary projector|OrdinaryProjector|hilbert modular|group.ring.valued' over both pinned trees gives only unrelated substring hits (e.g. Mathlib/GroupTheory/Exponent.lean, TauCeti/GroupTheory/Elementary.lean); no ordinary projector or Hilbert modular forms exist. Confirmed. Theorem 8.18 is the case-2 (p | 𝔫) analogue of Theorem 8.17, F̃_k(𝛙) = e_𝔓^ord(W_1(𝛙,1)V_{k−1} − Θ^#H_k(𝛙)) ∈ S_k(𝔫,R,𝛙), from Theorem 8.15 and Proposition 8.12; it is contained in I.7's DK Hilbert modular congruences, with the ordinary projector e_𝔓^ord on Hilbert modular forms owned by PadicFamilies:L5 (abstract projector from L0a). No layer names the theorem. Absent from both libraries.

items.name: The p-ordinary cuspidal family F_k(𝛙)
items.statement: With F̃_k(𝛙) from Theorem 8.17 (case 1) or Theorem 8.18 (case 2) and e_p^ord = ∏_{𝔭|p} e_𝔭^ord: Case 1a: F_k(𝛙) := z^{-1}·e_p^ord(F̃_k(𝛙)), where z := ∏_{𝔭|p} 𝛙(𝔭)/(𝛙(𝔭) − N𝔭^{k−1}) ∈ R (≡ 1 mod p^m for k ≡ 1 mod (p−1)p^N, N large). Case 1b: F_k(𝛙) := x^{-1}·e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|p}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭))(F̃_k(𝛙)) (x ∈ R^* in this case). Case 2: F_k(𝛙) := e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|𝔓''}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭))(F̃_k(𝛙)). In all cases F_k(𝛙) ∈ S_k(𝔫𝔓', R, 𝛙)^{p-ord} = e_p^ord S_k(𝔫𝔓', R, 𝛙), 𝔓' the product of the primes above p not dividing 𝔫.
items.locator: §8.4, proof of Corollary 8.19 (the source 2485, 2493) and display before Corollary 8.21 (2497)

Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation"; audit target "Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations ... for the Hilbert/Eisenstein representation | library: absent". Establish Hida control on the actual ordinary loci" (the ordinary projector e_p^ord on Hilbert modules). Confirmed the previous verdict. F_k(ψ) is the cusp-form side of the DK Hilbert modular congruences that I.7 names explicitly (Dasgupta–Kakde odd-prime obligations); the Hilbert ordinary projector is owned by PadicFamilies:L5 via L0a. No stage names group-ring-valued Hilbert forms, Silliman or Wiles's construction (atlas-wide rg for 'group ring valued', 'Silliman' returns no stage). items.name: Remark 8.20: congruence of group ring forms means congruence of Fourier coefficients
items.statement: A congruence F ≡ G (mod I) between group ring valued forms (such as (108), (110), (111), (112)) means a congruence of Fourier coefficients c(𝔪, F) ≡ c(𝔪, G) (mod I) in R for all (nonzero) ideals 𝔪. For (108) in case 1a this reads (equation (109)): c(𝔪, F_k(𝛙)) ≡ x·c(𝔪, W_1(𝛙,1)) − c(𝔪, W_k(𝛙,1_p)) (mod xΘ^#) for all ideals 𝔪, and similarly in the second case.
items.locator: §8.4, Remark 8.20 (label r:cong), equation (109) (label e:case1cong), the source 2473–2478
items.note: Fixes the meaning of every congruence of forms used in §8.4–8.5 and §9. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract line 48): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences"; audit target "Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations and the hypotheses of the generalised Ribet lemma ... | library: absent". The Eisenstein-side convention is also inside IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.3 (line 7): "Hilbert modular Eisenstein series, their algebraic Fourier coefficients, q-expansion principles, the relevant congruences". Paper: the source 2473–2478 (Remark 8.20, equation (109)). Library: no Hilbert modular forms or group-ring-valued q-expansions in either tree (rg as for item 249); Tau Ceti's QExpansion/Basic.lean is over Q with complex coefficients and has no congruence-mod-ideal notion. Confirmed the previous verdict (planned, I.7). Remark 8.20 fixes what 'F ≡ G mod I' means for group-ring-valued Hilbert forms (coefficientwise in R); this convention is part of the 'Hilbert modular congruences' I.7 plans for the DK proof, and no stage states the convention separately, so medium confidence stands. I.3 names 'the relevant congruences' only for Eisenstein q-expansions in the Deligne–Ribet context, so I.7 remains the owner of the cusp-form congruence convention. Library absent.

items.name: Corollary 8.19, case 1a: F_k(𝛙) ≡ xW_1(𝛙,1) − W_k(𝛙,1_p) mod xΘ^#
items.statement: Suppose we are in case 1 (𝔓 = 1, 𝔓' = product of all primes above p) and χ(𝔭) = 1 for some 𝔭 | p (case 1a). For positive k ≡ 1 (mod (p−1)p^N) and N sufficiently large there exists a cuspidal group ring family F_k(𝛙) ∈ S_k(𝔫𝔓', R, 𝛙)^{p-ord} such that (equation (108), first line) F_k(𝛙) ≡ x·W_1(𝛙,1) − W_k(𝛙,1_p) (mod xΘ^#), as a congruence of Fourier coefficients (Remark 8.20), where W_k(𝛙,1_p) is defined like W_k(𝛙,1) with the trivial character replaced by its p-depletion 1_p and x is as in Lemma 8.16. Proof: with z = ∏_{𝔭|p} 𝛙(𝔭)/(𝛙(𝔭) − N𝔭^{k−1}) ≡ 1 (mod p^m) one has e_p^ord W_k(𝛙,1) = z·W_k(𝛙,1_p), hence z^{-1}x ≡ x (mod xΘ^#), and F_k(𝛙) := z^{-1}e_p^ord(F̃_k(𝛙)) works. (Related identities used for the other cases: e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|p}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭))(W_k(𝛙,1)) = 0, e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|p}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭))(W_1(𝛙,1)) = W_1(𝛙_p,1), and in case 2 e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|p}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭))(W_1(𝛙_𝔓,1)) = W_1(𝛙_{𝔓𝔓''},1).)
items.locator: §8.4, Corollary 8.19 (label c:fcong), equation (108) (label e:case1f), first case, the source 2462–2470, proof 2481–2486 (ordinary-projection identities at 2481–2494 and 2496–2501)
items.note: The Eisenstein congruence modulo the strengthened modulus xΘ^# used to define the maximal Eisenstein ideal and the homomorphism φ in Theorem 8.23 (case 1a); the factor x is essential in §9. Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations ... Library: no Hilbert Eisenstein series, no ordinary projector, no U_p over F in either tree (rg for 'Hilbert', 'ordinary', 'stabili' in both ModularForms directories). Confirmed the previous verdict. The case-1a congruence is one of the DK Hilbert modular (Eisenstein) congruences I.7 names. The ordinary-projection identities on W_k (e_p^ord W_k(ψ,1) = z·W_k(ψ,1_p)) concern Hilbert Eisenstein series, whose construction is owned by AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 / I.3 ('Build the Hilbert Eisenstein series, integral q-expansion principle'), but neither of those layers names ordinary projection or U_p action on them, so the congruence and its proof stay with I.7. items.name: Corollary 8.19, case 1b: F_k(𝛙) ≡ W_1(𝛙_p,1) mod Θ^#
items.statement: Suppose we are in case 1 (𝔓 = 1) and χ(𝔭) ≠ 1 for all 𝔭 | p (case 1b). For positive k ≡ 1 (mod (p−1)p^N) and N sufficiently large there exists a cuspidal group ring family F_k(𝛙) ∈ S_k(𝔫𝔓', R, 𝛙)^{p-ord} such that (equation (108), second line) F_k(𝛙) ≡ W_1(𝛙_p,1) (mod Θ^#), as a congruence of Fourier coefficients, where W_1(𝛙_p,1) is defined like W_1(𝛙,1) with 𝛙 replaced by its p-depletion 𝛙_p. Proof: by the congruence (106), x ≡ ∏_{𝔭|p}(1 − χ(𝔭)^{-1}) mod 𝔪_R, so in case 1b x is a unit of the local ring R (and x is a unit exactly when χ(𝔭) ≠ 1 for all 𝔭 | p, i.e. exactly in case 1b); since e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|p}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭))(W_k(𝛙,1)) = 0 and e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|p}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭))(W_1(𝛙,1)) = W_1(𝛙_p,1), the form F_k(𝛙) := x^{-1}e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|p}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭))(F̃_k(𝛙)) works.
items.locator: §8.4, Corollary 8.19 (label c:fcong), equation (108) (label e:case1f), second case, the source 2462–2470, proof 2488–2494; x a unit iff case 1b at 2458–2460

We then apply U_p − ψ(p) for each p | p") and 2462–2470 (equation (108) second line: W_1(ψ_p,1) mod Θ^# when χ(p) ≠ 1 for all p|p). items.name: Corollary 8.21: F_k(𝛙) ≡ W_1(𝛙_{𝔓𝔓''},1) mod Θ^# (case 2)
items.statement: Suppose we are in case 2 (𝔓 ≠ 1); 𝔓' is the product of the primes above p not dividing 𝔫 and 𝔓'' the product of the primes 𝔭 | 𝔓' with χ(𝔭) ≠ 1. For positive k ≡ 1 (mod (p−1)p^N) and N sufficiently large there exists a cuspidal group ring family F_k(𝛙) ∈ S_k(𝔫𝔓', R, 𝛙)^{p-ord} such that (equation (110)) F_k(𝛙) ≡ W_1(𝛙_{𝔓𝔓''},1) (mod Θ^#), as a congruence of Fourier coefficients. Proof: apply e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|𝔓''}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭)) to F̃_k(𝛙) of Theorem 8.18 and use e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|p}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭))(W_1(𝛙_𝔓,1)) = W_1(𝛙_{𝔓𝔓''},1).
items.locator: §8.4, Corollary 8.21 (label c:fcong2), equation (110) (label e:case2f), the source 2503–2507

items.name: Hecke algebras T̃ and T of p-ordinary group ring cusp forms
items.statement: T̃ ⊂ End_R(S_k(𝔫𝔓', R, 𝛙)^{p-ord}) is the R-subalgebra generated by the Hecke operators T_𝔩 for 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫𝔓', U_𝔭 for 𝔭 | p, and the diamond operators S(𝔪) (which act by 𝛙(𝔪) ∈ R^*). T ⊂ T̃ is the sub-R-algebra generated by T_𝔩 for 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫𝔓', U_𝔭 for 𝔭 | 𝔓 only, and the S(𝔪); i.e. the operators U_𝔭 for 𝔭 | 𝔓' are excluded from T.
items.locator: §8.5, opening paragraph, the source 2511–2515
items.note: The Hecke algebras on which the Eisenstein homomorphism of Theorem 8.23 is defined; T is where φ takes values in R/xΘ^#, and §9 builds Galois representations over T̃_𝔐. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract line 48): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations" (the algebras T, T̃ on which the Eisenstein homomorphism of Theorem 8.23 and the §9 T̃_M-valued representation live). The proof programme includes Hecke algebras at the needed levels and weights, Eisenstein ideals, congruence modules"; audit: "Tau Ceti's Hecke operators on classical modular forms are the only related material". PadicFamilies:L5 (line 225): "Establish Hida control on the actual ordinary loci and integral weight algebras used by OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting" (the ordinary Hecke algebra over totally real fields; R21.2 says it 'Import[s] ordinary families, the ordinary Hecke algebra and Hida control from PadicFamilies', so PadicFamilies is the owner). items.name: The set M of ordinary newforms, their p-stabilizations f_p, and M̄
items.statement: M is the set of p-ordinary cuspidal newforms of weight k, level dividing 𝔫𝔓', and nebentypus ψ for some character ψ ∈ Ψ (R = R_Ψ). For f ∈ M, f_p is its ordinary stabilization with respect to all primes 𝔭 | p. The field E (ring of integers 𝒪, residue field k_E, uniformizer π_E) is assumed large enough that all normalized Fourier coefficients c(𝔞, f_p) lie in 𝒪. M̄ ⊂ M is the subset of f ∈ M such that c(1, (f_p)|_t) ≡ φ̄(t) (mod π_E) for all t ∈ T, with φ̄ as in Lemma 8.22.
items.locator: §8.5, second paragraph (the source 2518–2520) and paragraph after Lemma 8.22 (2558–2560)
items.note: Indexes the product of DVRs into which T and T̃ embed, showing they are reduced and giving the local description at 𝔐. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract line 48): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations" (the subset M̄ of newforms congruent to the Eisenstein character φ̄ mod π_E, the source 2558–2560). PadicFamilies:L5 (line 225): "Instantiate L0a on the integral Hilbert automorphic/cohomology modules ... Establish Hida control on the actual ordinary loci ... Export period modules ... under proved freeness/multiplicity-one hypotheses, and compare with the rational modular-curve case" (p-ordinary Hilbert forms and their ordinary stabilizations as the totally real instance of PadicFamilies:L0's "specialization to the correct classical ordinary space, with nebentypus, p-stabilization and multiplicity recorded"). GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.6 (areas/modular-1.json): "Define the Hilbert cohomological weights ... Export the local newvector and global multiplicity results" (Hilbert newforms of given weight/level/nebentypus). Paper: the source 2518–2520. Changed: dropped PadicFamilies:L0 from the planned list. L0 is the Q-case (ordinary tower over Q) and the item is over a totally real field; […]

items.name: T ↪ T̃ ↪ ∏_{f∈M} 𝒪 are injective with finite cokernel; T, T̃ reduced
items.statement: The 𝒪-algebra maps T → T̃ → ∏_{f∈M} 𝒪 given by t ↦ (c(1, (f_p)|_t))_{f∈M} (so T_𝔩 ↦ (c(𝔩,f_p))_f, U_𝔭 ↦ (c(𝔭,f_p))_f) are injective with finite cokernels; in particular T and T̃ are reduced. Proof: every p-ordinary form g of level 𝔫𝔓' is a linear combination g = Σ_{f∈M} Σ_𝔟 c_{f,𝔟}(f_p)|_𝔟 over divisors 𝔟 of 𝔫 prime to p such that (f_p)|_𝔟 has level dividing 𝔫𝔓', so an operator of T or T̃ annihilating every f_p annihilates every g; finite cokernel follows from multiplicity one: for distinct f, f' ∈ M there is 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫𝔓' with c(𝔩,f_p) ≠ c(𝔩,f'_p).
items.locator: §8.5, paragraph 'Let us be more explicit about this fact', the source 2517–2533
items.note: Reducedness and the embedding into a product of DVRs are used in §9 to construct Galois representations over T̃_𝔐 from those of the individual newforms. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (the layer extract line 48): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations" (the embedding T̃ ↪ ∏_M 𝒪 is how §9 constructs the T̃_M-valued Galois representation from those of the individual newforms). IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.5 (line 20): "Hecke algebras at the needed levels and weights, Eisenstein ideals, congruence modules, Galois representations and stable lattices". GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R16.4 (areas/modular-1.json, 'Global cuspidal decomposition and multiplicity'): "Prove GL₂ global multiplicity one ... Prove strong multiplicity one with a precise set of places where equality is required" (the multiplicity-one input giving the finite cokernel: distinct f, f' ∈ M differ at some l ∤ nP'). Paper: the source 2517–2533. Library near miss (Q only): tauceti:HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.eq_of_forall_notMem_qExpansion_coeff_eq (TauCeti/NumberTheory/ModularForms/Newforms/StrongMultiplicityOne.lean:115, two newforms of level N with the same nebentypus agreeing at all but finitely many good coefficients are equal) and tauceti:HeckeRing.GL2.finrank_cuspFormsNewEigenspace_le_one (Newforms/MultiplicityOne.lean:175); both over Q with complex coefficients, no Hecke algebra over 𝒪, no ordinary forms, no Hilbert forms. rg for 'IsReduced' in TauCeti/NumberTheory and Mathlib HeckeRing/ModularForms finds nothing about Hecke algebras. Changed: replaced GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer:R17.3 by R16.4 as the owner of the multiplicity-one input. […]

items.name: Newform theory and multiplicity one for p-ordinary Hilbert cusp forms (as used)
items.statement: As used in §8.5 (uncited): (a) every p-ordinary cusp form g of weight k and level 𝔫𝔓' with nebentypus in Ψ is a linear combination g = Σ_{f∈M} Σ_𝔟 c_{f,𝔟}(f_p)|_𝔟, 𝔟 ranging over divisors of 𝔫 prime to p such that (f_p)|_𝔟 has level dividing 𝔫𝔓', where M is the set of p-ordinary newforms of level dividing 𝔫𝔓' and f_p the ordinary p-stabilization; (b) (multiplicity one) for distinct f, f' ∈ M there exists a prime 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫𝔓' with c(𝔩, f_p) ≠ c(𝔩, f'_p).

items.name: The p-adic cyclotomic character ε_cyc on ideals
items.statement: ε_cyc is the p-adic cyclotomic character, viewed as a character on ideals prime to p by ε_cyc(𝔩) = ⟨N𝔩⟩ ∈ Z_p^* for 𝔩 ∤ p (the projection of N𝔩 to the principal units). For k ≡ 1 (mod (p−1)p^N) one has N𝔩^{k−1} ≡ ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩) modulo high powers of p, which is how ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩) enters the Eisenstein eigenvalues.
items.locator: §8.5, sentence after equation (111), the source 2543–2545
items.note: Appears in the Eisenstein eigenvalue ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩) + 𝛙(𝔩) of T_𝔩 in (111) and Theorem 8.23, and as the determinant character in §9. Evidence: the layer extract:418–423 (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L0, 'Ray-class character spaces and evaluation', also atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json): "Develop locally algebraic Hecke characters, their algebraic and p-adic avatars through chosen embeddings, conductors, infinity types and local factors. ... Prove descent, finite-level evaluation, norm relations, character twists and change of tame modulus." Library: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean:307 `noncomputable def cyclotomicCharacter (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : (L ≃+* L) →* ℤ_[p]ˣ` with spec at :323 (g t = t ^ ((cyclotomicCharacter L p g).val.toZModPow n).val) — a character of ring automorphisms of a field, no ideal-side version. Changed from missing to planned. items.name: Equations (111)–(112): F_k(𝛙) is a Hecke eigenvector modulo xΘ^# (case 1) or Θ^# (case 2)
items.statement: Let F_k(𝛙) be the cuspidal family of Corollary 8.19 (case 1) or 8.21 (case 2); congruences are coefficientwise (Remark 8.20). For 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫𝔓' (equation (111)): F_k(𝛙)|_{T_𝔩} ≡ (𝛙(𝔩) + ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩))·F_k(𝛙) (mod xΘ^#) in case 1, and F_k(𝛙)|_{T_𝔩} ≡ (𝛙(𝔩) + 1)·F_k(𝛙) (mod Θ^#) in case 2. For all 𝔭 | 𝔓𝔓'' (equation (112)): F_k(𝛙)|_{U_𝔭} ≡ F_k(𝛙) (mod xΘ^#) in case 1b and (mod Θ^#) in case 2. Moreover S(𝔪) acts on F_k(𝛙) by 𝛙(𝔪). (These follow from the Eisenstein congruences (108), (110) and the Hecke eigenvalues of the Eisenstein families W_1(𝛙,1), W_k(𝛙,1_p), W_1(𝛙_p,1), W_1(𝛙_{𝔓𝔓''},1).)

items.name: Lemma 8.22: the mod-𝔪_R Eisenstein homomorphism φ̄: T → k_E
items.statement: Let k_E be the residue field of the p-adic local ring 𝒪 = 𝒪_E. There is an 𝒪-algebra homomorphism φ̄: T → k_E with φ̄(T_𝔩) = 1 + χ(𝔩) for 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p, φ̄(U_𝔭) = 1 for 𝔭 | 𝔓, and φ̄(S(𝔪)) = χ(𝔪). Proof: F_k(𝛙) is an eigenform for these operators modulo the maximal ideal 𝔪_R of R (by (111), (112), since xΘ^#, Θ^# ⊂ 𝔪_R); 𝔪_R is generated by the uniformizer π_E and the images of [g] − χ(g), g ∈ G, and R/𝔪_R ≅ k_E; φ̄ sends each operator to its mod 𝔪_R eigenvalue.
items.locator: §8.5, Lemma 8.22 (label t:modp), the source 2549–2556

Evidence: the layer extract:46–48 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma for residually indistinguishable characters ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation". Paper check: the source 2549–2556 (Lemma 8.22, label t:modp) matches the item. For comparison the layer extract:20 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.5): "Prove Wiles's totally real main conjecture at odd primes. The proof programme includes Hecke algebras at the needed levels and weights, Eisenstein ideals, congruence modules ..." and its audit (the layer extract:29): 'There are no Eisenstein ideals, congruence modules or Galois representations attached to modular forms.' Library: rg 'Eisenstein ideal|EisensteinIdeal|HeckeAlgebra|Hecke algebra' over both trees gives only Mathlib/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/Defs.lean and TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/* (abstract Hecke rings / GL₂ over ℚ), no Hecke algebra of Hilbert forms. Confirmed planned, but I removed I.5 from the list: the residual Eisenstein homomorphism φ̄ : T → k_E (T_𝔩 ↦ 1+χ(𝔩), U_𝔭 ↦ 1, S(𝔪) ↦ χ(𝔪)) is defined from the DK congruences (111)–(112) and the specific maximal ideal 𝔪_R of the group-ring quotient R, so it is part of I.7's 'Hilbert modular congruences ... for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation'. I.5's Eisenstein ideals are Wiles's, in the Λ-adic Hecke algebra for the main conjecture: a related construction but a different object, and PROTOCOL §15 asks for one owner. items.name: Maximal Eisenstein ideal 𝔐 and the completions T_𝔐, T̃_𝔐, ∏_{f∈M̄} 𝒪
items.statement: 𝔐 := ker(φ̄) ⊂ T, a maximal ideal (the maximal Eisenstein ideal). T_𝔐 is the 𝔐-adic completion of T and T̃_𝔐 := T̃ ⊗_T T_𝔐 the 𝔐-adic completion of T̃. The 𝔐-adic completion of ∏_{f∈M} 𝒪 is (∏_{f∈M} 𝒪)_𝔐 = ∏_{f∈M̄} 𝒪, with M̄ the set of f ∈ M such that c(1,(f_p)|_t) ≡ φ̄(t) (mod π_E) for all t ∈ T.
items.locator: §8.5, paragraph after Lemma 8.22, the source 2558–2561
items.note: The local Hecke algebras over which the Galois representation and the Ritter–Weiss comparison of §9 are carried out. Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation and compare the resulting arithmetic class and Fitting ideal." Comparison stages read: AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6 ('representability by a continuous representation over the localised completed Hecke algebra under absolute residual irreducibility') is for classical forms and a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal; OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.2 ('Eisenstein/residually reducible control statements needed by Skinner–Wiles, specifying ... localizations') is Hida control for Skinner–Wiles. The maximal Eisenstein ideal 𝔐 = ker φ̄ of the Hilbert Hecke algebra T of the DK set-up, the completions T_𝔐, T̃_𝔐 and the identification (∏_M 𝒪)_𝔐 = ∏_{M̄} 𝒪 over residually Eisenstein newforms are the Hecke-side data over which I.7 constructs the integral Galois representation; R19.6 (residually irreducible, classical) and R21.2 (Skinner–Wiles control) are near neighbours that do not contain this object. Mathlib's AdicCompletion is the generic completion only.

items.name: T_𝔐 ↪ T̃_𝔐 ↪ ∏_{f∈M̄} 𝒪 are injective with finite cokernel
items.statement: The 𝔐-adic completions satisfy: the induced maps T_𝔐 → T̃_𝔐 → ∏_{f∈M̄} 𝒪 are injective with finite cokernel. This follows from the injections with finite cokernel T → T̃ → ∏_{f∈M} 𝒪 before completion by the Artin–Rees Lemma (Atiyah–Macdonald, Proposition 10.12: 𝔐-adic completion is exact on finitely generated modules over the Noetherian ring T), together with (∏_{f∈M} 𝒪)_𝔐 = ∏_{f∈M̄} 𝒪.

items.name: Theorem 8.23 (i): the Eisenstein quotient W and surjection φ: T̃_𝔐 → W with R/xΘ^# ↪ W
items.statement: In both cases 1 and 2, with x as in Lemma 8.16 in case 1a and x = 1 in cases 1b and 2, there exist a non-zerodivisor x ∈ R, an R/xΘ^#-algebra W, and a surjective R-algebra homomorphism φ: T̃_𝔐 → W such that the structure map R/xΘ^# → W is injective. Construction (case 1a; the other cases are identical with x = 1): 𝒞 := ∏_{𝔞 ⊂ 𝒪_F, 𝔞 ≠ 0} R/xΘ^#; c: S_k(𝔫𝔓', R, 𝛙) → 𝒞 sends a cusp form to (c(𝔞,f) mod xΘ^#)_𝔞; Hecke operators act on 𝒞 by the coefficient formula (100) and c is Hecke equivariant; ℱ := c(T̃·F_k(𝛙)), the image of the T̃-span of F_k(𝛙), a finite-type R/xΘ^#-module; W := image of the canonical R-algebra map T̃ → End_{R/xΘ^#}(ℱ), and φ: T̃ → W the resulting surjection; by (111), (112) and the S(𝔪)-eigenvalue 𝛙(𝔪), W viewed as a T-module through φ is 𝔐-adically complete, so φ factors through T̃_𝔐 → W. Injectivity: if α ∈ R maps to 0 in W then αF_k(𝛙) ≡ 0 (mod xΘ^#); the coefficients 𝔪 = 1 and 𝔪 = 𝔭 (𝔭 | p) of (109) give (x − 1)α ≡ 0 and ((1 + 𝛙(𝔭))x − 𝛙(𝔭))α ≡ 0 (mod xΘ^#); multiplying the first by −(1 + 𝛙(𝔭)) and adding gives α ≡ 0 (mod xΘ^#).
items.locator: §8.5, Theorem 8.23 (label t:yxt), first bullet, the source 2572–2585; construction of 𝒞, c, ℱ, W, φ in the proof at 2587–2601; injectivity at 2604–2610

Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma for residually indistinguishable characters, the Fitting-ideal comparison"; audit the layer extract:56: 'Hilbert modular congruences ... for the Hilbert/Eisenstein representation | library: absent | Absent.' IHG.6 (the layer extract:119–122, 154–157): takes as input a rank-two representation over 'T ⊂ Ttilde, T local ... a nontrivial ideal Itilde' and states "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses; no arithmetic Brumer–Stark conclusion is part of this abstract supplier." Paper check: the source 2572–2610 (Theorem 8.23, label t:yxt, first bullet and the construction 𝒞, c, ℱ, W, φ and the injectivity argument via the 𝔪 = 1 and 𝔪 = 𝔭 coefficients of (109)) match the item. Library: rg over both trees finds no Hilbert cusp forms, no coefficient map c(𝔞,f) on Hilbert forms, no group-ring-valued forms. Confirmed planned. Theorem 8.23(i) — the Eisenstein quotient W of T̃_𝔐 built from the T̃-span of F_k(𝛙) in ∏_𝔞 R/xΘ^#, the surjection φ and injectivity of R/xΘ^# → W — is the central Hilbert modular congruence of Dasgupta–Kakde and produces the ideal Ĩ = ker φ consumed by IHG.6's abstract generalised Ribet lemma; the IHG.6 text explicitly assigns the verification of these Hilbert/Eisenstein hypotheses to I.7, so I.7 is the owner. items.name: Theorem 8.23 (ii): values of φ on T_𝔐 (the Eisenstein character)
items.statement: With W, φ as in Theorem 8.23 (i), the restriction of φ: T̃_𝔐 → W to T_𝔐 takes values in R/xΘ^# ⊂ W; precisely φ(S(𝔪)) = 𝛙(𝔪) for 𝔪 ∈ G_𝔫^+, φ(U_𝔭) = 1 for 𝔭 | 𝔓, and φ(T_𝔩) = ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩) + 𝛙(𝔩) for 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p. (Proof: from (111), (112) and the S(𝔪)-eigenvalue 𝛙(𝔪) of W_1(𝛙,1) and W_k(𝛙,1_p). In cases 1b and 2, ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩) = 1 in W, because Θ^# divides ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩) − 1 in R for k − 1 divisible by (p−1)p^m and m sufficiently large; this uses that Θ^# is a non-zerodivisor in the trivial-zero-free quotient R.)
items.locator: §8.5, Theorem 8.23 (label t:yxt), second bullet, the source 2577–2582; proof 2594–2597 and 2618
items.note: Identifies the Eisenstein character of the Hecke algebra; in §9 the Galois representation reduced modulo ker φ has semisimplification 𝛙 ⊕ ε_cyc^{k−1} (resp. 𝛙 ⊕ 1). Evidence: the layer extract:46–48 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma for residually indistinguishable characters ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation and compare the resulting arithmetic class and Fitting ideal." Theorem 8.23(ii) identifies the Eisenstein character φ|_{T_𝔐} (S(𝔪) ↦ 𝛙(𝔪), U_𝔭 ↦ 1, T_𝔩 ↦ ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩)+𝛙(𝔩)), which is exactly the 'T-valued character polynomials modulo I' hypothesis of IHG.6 (semisimplification 𝛙 ⊕ ε_cyc^{k−1}, resp. 𝛙 ⊕ 1) that IHG.6 delegates to I.7; it is part of I.7's Hilbert modular congruences. The ideal-side ε_cyc it uses is item 258 (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L0). Nothing in Mathlib or Tau Ceti is close.

items.name: Theorem 8.23 (iii): φ(U)·y = 0 forces y ∈ (Θ^#)
items.statement: With W, φ as in Theorem 8.23 (i), let U := ∏_{𝔭|𝔓'}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭)) ∈ T̃_𝔐. If y ∈ R and φ(U)·y = 0 in W, then y ∈ (Θ^#) ⊂ R. Proof (case 1a): (108) gives F_k(𝛙)|_U ≡ x·W_1(𝛙_p,1) (mod xΘ^#) (the source prints W_1(1,ψ_p)); if yF_k(𝛙)|_U ≡ 0 (mod xΘ^#) then the Fourier coefficient at 𝔪 = 1 gives xy ∈ (xΘ^#), hence y ∈ (Θ^#) since x is a non-zerodivisor in R. Cases 1b and 2 are analogous with x = 1.

items.name: Hida–Wiles Galois representation ρ_f: existence, unramified outside 𝔫p, Frobenius characteristic polynomial
items.statement: Standing setting of §9 (inherited from §7–8): p an odd prime; F totally real, H/F finite abelian CM, G = Gal(H/F); χ a totally odd character of G of order prime to p; R = R_Ψ the trivial-zero-free character group ring quotient of the component 𝒪[G_p]_χ (§7.1), in which Θ^# = Θ_{Σ,Σ'}^# is a non-zerodivisor; 𝛙 : G → R^* the group-ring character; E/ℚ_p finite with ring of integers 𝒪 = 𝒪_E, uniformiser π_E, residue field k_E; 𝔫 the level, 𝔓 = gcd(𝔫, p^∞), 𝔓' = ∏_{𝔭|p, 𝔭∤𝔓} 𝔭; 𝕋 ⊂ \tilde{𝕋} the p-ordinary group-ring Hecke algebras of level 𝔫𝔓' (§8.7), 𝔐 = ker(\overline{φ} : 𝕋 → k_E) (Lemma 8.22), 𝕋_𝔐 ⊂ \tilde{𝕋}_𝔐 ⊂ ∏_{f∈\overline{M}} 𝒪 their 𝔐-adic completions (injections with finite cokernel); \overline{M} the finite set of p-ordinary cuspidal newforms f of weight k > 1, level dividing 𝔫𝔓', nebentypus ψ ∈ Ψ, whose ordinary p-stabilisation f_p has all c(𝔞, f_p) ∈ 𝒪 and satisfies c(1,(f_p)|_t) ≡ \overline{φ}(t) mod π_E for all t ∈ 𝕋; m with Θ^# | p^m in R (Lemma 8.1), N > m, k ≡ 1 mod (p−1)p^N; φ : \tilde{𝕋}_𝔐 → W the surjective R-algebra map of Theorem 8.23. Statement (Hida, Wiles): for f ∈ \overline{M} with nebentypus ψ there is a continuous representation ρ_f : G_F → GL_2(E) such that (1) ρ_f is unramified outside 𝔫p, and (2) for every prime 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p of F the characteristic polynomial of ρ_f(Frob_𝔩) is χr(ρ_f(Frob_𝔩))(x) = x² − c(𝔩, f) x + ψ(𝔩) ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩), where ε_cyc is the p-adic cyclotomic character (ε_cyc(𝔩) = ⟨N𝔩⟩ ∈ ℤ_p^* for 𝔩 ∤ p).
items.locator: §9.1 (label s:galrepf), properties (1)–(2) of ρ_f, the source lines 2623–2636; the Hecke algebras 𝕋 ⊂ 𝕋̃ and their completions are those of §8.5 'Homomorphism on the Hecke Algebra' (lines 2512–2568)

items.name: Ordinary local shape (113) of ρ_f at primes above p (Wiles)
items.statement: Let f ∈ \overline{M}, ρ_f as above, 𝔭 | p a prime of F and G_𝔭 ⊂ G_F a decomposition group at 𝔭. Then ρ_f|_{G_𝔭} ∼ [[ψ η_𝔭^{−1} ε_cyc^{k−1}, *],[0, η_𝔭]] (equation (113)): there is a basis of E² in which every ρ_f(σ), σ ∈ G_𝔭, is upper triangular with diagonal entries ψη_𝔭^{−1}ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ) and η_𝔭(σ). Here η_𝔭 : G_𝔭 → E^* is the unramified character with η_𝔭(rec(ϖ^{−1})) = c(𝔭, f_p), where ϖ ∈ F_𝔭 is a uniformiser and rec : F_𝔭^* → G_𝔭^{ab} is the local Artin reciprocity map in Serre's convention (\cite{serre}), so that rec(ϖ^{−1}) is a lift to G_𝔭^{ab} of the Frobenius of the maximal unramified extension of F_𝔭.
items.locator: §9.1, property (3) of ρ_f, equation (113) (label e:locbasis), the source lines 2636–2641
items.note: External input (\cite{wilesrep} Theorem 2 (Wiles, Invent. Math. 94 (1988)); reciprocity conventions from \cite{serre} (Serre, Corps locaux, 1962)). The upper-triangular ordinary shape at 𝔭 | p is what 'Ribet's wrench' compares with the global basis of eigenvectors of ρ_f(τ); it yields the change-of-basis matrices M_{f,𝔭} and, through (119), the control of b on decomposition groups at p. Include the cases required for Barsotti–Tate, ordinary and endpoint-weight lifting". items.name: Local eigenspace V_{𝔭,f}
items.statement: For f ∈ \overline{M} and 𝔭 | p, V_{𝔭,f} ⊂ E² is the eigenspace of ρ_f|_{G_𝔭}: the E-line spanned by the vector (1,0)^T in a basis for which (113) holds, i.e. the G_𝔭-stable line on which G_𝔭 acts through the character ψη_𝔭^{−1}ε_cyc^{k−1}.

Construct ordinary deformation rings with the filtration data". rg over all stage descriptions for "Ribet's wrench", 'V_{p,f}', 'local eigenspace' returns nothing; PadicFamilies:L5 audit: "No Galois or automorphic filtration theory in either library". items.name: Čebotarev density theorem (as used)
items.statement: Let F be a number field and S a finite set of places. The Frobenius elements Frob_𝔩 ∈ G_F (𝔩 ∉ S, well defined up to conjugacy) are dense in G_F: every element of every finite quotient Gal(K/F) with K/F unramified outside S is Frob_𝔩 for infinitely many primes 𝔩. As used in §9: if ρ : G_F → GL_2(A) is continuous (A = E, or A = K = ∏_{f∈\overline{M}} E with its 𝔐-adic topology), then a closed condition on ρ(σ) — its characteristic polynomial or trace lying in a closed subring (𝒪[x], 𝕋_𝔐[x]) or satisfying a congruence modulo π_E, 𝔐 or I — that holds for all σ = Frob_𝔩 with 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p holds for all σ ∈ G_F.
items.locator: §9.1 line 2644 ('By Čebotarev and property (2)'), §9.2 line 2734, §9.3 line 2763; the source lines 2644–2647, 2734–2735, 2763–2766
items.note: External input (no \cite key given; standard (Čebotarev density theorem)). Propagates the Frobenius formulae (2)/(116) and the values φ(T_𝔩) to all σ ∈ G_F, giving integrality and residual Eisenstein shape of characteristic polynomials and the trace congruence (120). Derive, rather than reprove, the density of split-completely primes, the non-Galois statement via a Galois closure, infinitude of every Frobenius class, and the rational arithmetic-progression case." Pinned Mathlib 082e2d3: rg -i 'chebotarev' Mathlib returns nothing; Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/DirichletDensity.lean:82 defines `HasDirichletDensity` only; Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean:437 `infinite_setOf_prime_and_eq_mod` is Dirichlet's theorem over ℚ. items.name: Integrality and residual Eisenstein factorisation of χr(ρ_f(σ))
items.statement: For f ∈ \overline{M} and every σ ∈ G_F, the characteristic polynomial χr(ρ_f(σ))(x) lies in 𝒪[x] and satisfies χr(ρ_f(σ))(x) ≡ (x − 1)(x − χ(σ)) mod π_E. (Proof: Čebotarev and property (2) of ρ_f, using that ψ ≡ χ mod π_E and that f ∈ \overline{M} gives c(𝔩, f) ≡ \overline{φ}(T_𝔩) = 1 + χ(𝔩) mod π_E for 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p.)
items.locator: §9.1, unnumbered display after property (3), the source lines 2644–2646
items.note: Gives the two distinct residual eigenvalues 1 and χ(σ) used to diagonalise ρ_f(τ) via Hensel's lemma. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json; the layer extract lines 45-50): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation"; audit target "Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations and the hypotheses of the generalised Ribet lemma ... | library: absent". The hypothesis verified is IHG.6's "Assume its characteristic polynomials lie in T[X], reduce to the product of two T-valued character polynomials modulo I" (modular-1.json), and IHG.6 states "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses". Libraries: no Hilbert-form Galois representations in either pinned tree (see n=266). Confirmed. χr(ρ_f(σ)) ∈ 𝒪[x] with χr ≡ (x−1)(x−χ(σ)) mod π_E for all σ is the 'integral Galois representation'/character-polynomial hypothesis of the generalised Ribet lemma for the actual Hilbert eigenform, which I.7 is charged with proving (IHG.6 explicitly delegates it to I.7). Its inputs (ρ_f, n=266; Chebotarev, n=269) are themselves only planned.

items.name: Hensel's lemma for a quadratic with distinct residual roots (as used)
items.statement: Let A be a complete local ring with maximal ideal 𝔪 (A = 𝒪 with 𝔪 = (π_E), or A = 𝕋_𝔐, a finite local 𝒪-algebra complete for its maximal ideal 𝔐). If a monic polynomial P ∈ A[x] of degree 2 reduces modulo 𝔪 to (x − ā)(x − b̄) with ā ≠ b̄ in A/𝔪, then P has exactly two roots a, b ∈ A, with a ≡ ā, b ≡ b̄ mod 𝔪, and a − b ∈ A^*.
items.locator: §9.1 line 2650 ('Hensel's Lemma implies that ρ_f(τ) has two distinct eigenvalues'), §9.2 lines 2737–2738; the source lines 2648–2650 and 2736–2738
items.note: External input (no \cite key given; standard (Hensel's lemma)). Produces the distinct eigenvalues λ_{1,f}, λ_{2,f} ∈ 𝒪 of ρ_f(τ) and λ_1, λ_2 ∈ 𝕋_𝔐^* of ρ(τ), hence the global bases in Ribet's wrench. Evidence: Verified in the pinned Mathlib tree (git HEAD 082e2d37): Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.lean:94-99 `class HenselianRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) : Prop where jac : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥; is_henselian : ∀ (f : R[X]) (_ : f.Monic) (a₀ : R) (_ : f.eval a₀ ∈ I) (_ : IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (f.derivative.eval a₀))), ∃ a : R, f.IsRoot a ∧ a - a₀ ∈ I`; line 170-171 `instance (priority := 100) IsAdicComplete.henselianRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) [IsAdicComplete I R] : HenselianRing R I`; line 266-269 `theorem IsLocalRing.eq_of_eval_eq_zero_of_not_isUnit_sub {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] {f : Polynomial R} {a b : R} (ha : f.eval a = 0) (hb : f.eval b = 0) (h : ¬ IsUnit (a - b)) (h' : IsUnit (f.derivative.eval a)) : a = b`. Also line 108 `class HenselianLocalRing` and TauCeti/NumberTheory/LocalField/Henselian.lean:34 `instance henselianLocalRing_integer : HenselianLocalRing 𝒪[K]` (the A = 𝒪_E case). Near miss: Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Hensel.lean:461 `hensels_lemma` (ℤ_p only). Confirmed library, with the previous agent's caveat retained. The mathematical content used ('Hensel's lemma' for a complete local ring A and a monic P with a simple residual root) is HenselianRing.is_henselian for I = 𝔪 via IsAdicComplete.henselianRing, whose hypotheses (any commutative ring I-adically complete, any monic polynomial, derivative a unit mod I) are weaker than the item's (complete local ring, quadratic with distinct residual roots: P'(ā) ≡ ā−b̄ is a unit). items.name: Distinct eigenvalues λ_{1,f}, λ_{2,f} of ρ_f(τ) for χ(τ) ≠ 1
items.statement: Let f ∈ \overline{M} and τ ∈ G_F with χ(τ) ≠ 1 (for instance any τ restricting to the complex conjugation of H, for which χ(τ) = −1). Since χ has order prime to p, χ(τ) ≢ 1 mod π_E; hence χr(ρ_f(τ)) ≡ (x − 1)(x − χ(τ)) mod π_E has distinct residual roots and by Hensel's lemma ρ_f(τ) has two distinct eigenvalues λ_{1,f}, λ_{2,f} ∈ 𝒪 with λ_{1,f} ≡ 1 mod π_E and λ_{2,f} ≡ χ(τ) mod π_E. In particular ρ_f(τ) is diagonalisable over E with eigenvalues λ_{1,f}, λ_{2,f}.
items.locator: §9.1, display 'Suppose that τ ∈ G_F such that χ(τ) ≠ 1', the source lines 2648–2650
items.note: Supplies the 'global' basis of eigenvectors of ρ_f(τ) in Ribet's wrench. Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7 (atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json; the layer extract lines 45-50): "Import the general representation/lattice/extension-class/annihilator theorem from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.6 ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation". IHG.6 (modular-1.json) is explicitly the abstract supplier: "For a finite collection of local subgroups, choose triangularizations with diagonal characters eta_v, xi_v ... IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses; no arithmetic Brumer–Stark conclusion is part of this abstract supplier." Libraries: the Hensel input is in Mathlib (n=271) but ρ_f and its eigenvalues are in neither pinned tree (see n=266). Confirmed planned, owner narrowed to I.7 only. The statement is an arithmetic fact about the actual representation ρ_f (distinct eigenvalues λ_{1,f} ≡ 1, λ_{2,f} ≡ χ(τ) mod π_E for χ(τ) ≠ 1, using that χ has prime-to-p order), i.e. one of the 'hypotheses for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation' that I.7 must prove. I dropped IHG.6: it plans the abstract theorem taking such triangularisation data as hypotheses and expressly disclaims the arithmetic verification, so listing it was shared vocabulary rather than planning of this item.

items.name: CM form
items.statement: A cuspidal eigenform f (with Galois representation ρ_f) is a CM form if ρ_f = Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} α for some quadratic CM extension L of F and some p-adic Hecke character α of L (a continuous character α : G_L → E^*).

items.name: Ribet: reducible restriction to a finite index subgroup forces induced (dihedral) representation
items.statement: Let f be a cuspidal eigenform of weight k > 1 with p-adic Galois representation ρ_f. If the restriction of ρ_f to some finite index subgroup of G_F is reducible, then ρ_f is induced from a character of an index-two subgroup of G_F (so the image of ρ_f is projectively dihedral). (Stated by Ribet for classical modular forms; applied by the paper to Hilbert modular eigenforms over F.)
items.locator: §9.1, proof of Lemma 9.1, the source lines 2659–2663
items.note: External input (\cite{ribetrep} Theorem 2.3 (K. Ribet, On l-adic representations attached to modular forms, Invent. Math. 28 (1975))). First step of Lemma 9.1: reducibility on a finite index subgroup implies ρ_f is induced from an index-two subgroup. Evidence: rg over both pinned trees for 'Ribet', 'projectively dihedral', 'dihedral', 'induced from', 'finite index' + representation finds nothing relevant: Mathlib RepresentationTheory/FiniteIndex.lean:23 `Rep.indCoindIso` is only Ind ≅ Coind for a finite-index subgroup (read); Tau Ceti hits for 'dihedral' are DihedralGroup examples in character-table/Belyi files. items.name: Balasubramanyam–Ghate–Vatsal: an induced ρ_f comes from a CM field
items.statement: If the p-adic Galois representation ρ_f of a (p-ordinary) Hilbert cuspidal eigenform f of weight k > 1 over the totally real field F is induced from an index-two subgroup of G_F (equivalently has projectively dihedral image), then the quadratic extension L/F fixed by that subgroup is a CM field; hence f is a CM form in the sense above.

Second step of Lemma 9.1: the fixed field of the index-two subgroup is CM, so ρ_f induced implies f is a CM form. Evidence: rg over both pinned trees for 'Balasubramanyam|Ghate|Vatsal|Hilbert modular|projectively|dihedral' + CM finds nothing beyond Mathlib NumberTheory/NumberField/CMField.lean:71 `IsCMField` (read). Nearly ordinary filtrations at each place above p') and OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.2 ('Hida control and finite flatness') plan ordinary Hilbert families with no statement about induced rho_f. items.name: Lemma 9.1 (Ribet): restrictions of a non-CM ρ_f to finite index subgroups are irreducible
items.statement: Let f be a cuspidal eigenform of weight k > 1 that is not a CM form. Then the restriction of ρ_f to any finite index subgroup of G_F is irreducible. (Proof: if some restriction were reducible, \cite{ribetrep} Theorem 2.3 gives that ρ_f is induced from an index-two subgroup, so its image is projectively dihedral, and by \cite{bgv} Remark (ii) the fixed field of that subgroup is a CM field, i.e. f is CM.)

items.name: Hara–Ochiai: p-ordinary CM forms have p split in the CM field
items.statement: Let f be a p-ordinary Hilbert cuspidal eigenform which is a CM form with respect to the quadratic CM extension L/F, i.e. ρ_f = Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} α. Then every prime 𝔭 | p of F splits in L; consequently a decomposition group G_𝔭 ⊂ G_F at 𝔭 is contained in G_L.
items.locator: §9.1, proof of Lemma 9.2, the source line 2669
items.note: External input (\cite{ho} Proposition A.3 (T. Hara, T. Ochiai, The cyclotomic Iwasawa main conjecture for Hilbert cusp forms with complex multiplication, Kyoto J. Math. 58)). Gives G_𝔭 ⊂ G_L in the proof of Lemma 9.2, so that V_{𝔭,f} is one of the two G_L-stable lines of the induced representation. items.name: Irreducibility of ρ_f for cuspidal eigenforms (as used)
items.statement: For every cuspidal eigenform f of weight k > 1 (in particular every f ∈ \overline{M}) the representation ρ_f : G_F → GL_2(E) is irreducible. As used: (i) in Lemma 9.2, a line stable under all of G_F would contradict irreducibility of ρ_f; (ii) in Lemma 9.9, for each factor E_j of K the projections of the b(σ) to E_j are not all zero, because ρ_{f_j} is irreducible (a basis vector of the global basis cannot span a G_F-stable line).
