Libraries: rg over both pinned trees finds no Galois representation attached to any modular or Hilbert form (Mathlib hits for 'Galois representation' are none; Tau Ceti hits are torus/cocharacter and GaloisLattice files). Confirmed planned. R19.2 owns the theorem: it constructs rho_f for cohomological Hilbert forms (the paper's parallel-weight-k > 1 cuspidal eigenforms are cohomological) and proves 'the required irreducibility'. […]

items.name: Lemma 9.2: V_{𝔭,f} is moved by complex conjugation for CM forms
items.statement: Let f ∈ \overline{M} be a CM form associated to the quadratic CM extension L/F, and let 𝔭 | p. Then the subspace V_{𝔭,f} is not stable under ρ_f(τ) for any τ ∈ G_F that restricts to the complex conjugation of L. (Proof: since f is p-ordinary, 𝔭 splits in L by \cite{ho} Proposition A.3, so G_𝔭 ⊂ G_L; ρ_f = Ind_{G_L}^{G_F} α has exactly two G_L-stable lines, and V_{𝔭,f} is one of them because ρ_f|_{G_𝔭} is not scalar (the two characters of its semisimplification are distinct, one ramified and the other unramified); if that line were stable under a τ restricting to complex conjugation of L it would be stable under all of G_F = G_L ∪ τG_L, contradicting irreducibility of ρ_f.)
items.locator: §9.1, Lemma 9.2 (label l:cm), the source lines 2665–2671
items.note: Handles the CM eigenforms in the construction of τ (Proposition 9.3): any τ inducing complex conjugation on the compositum H_0 works for them. Evidence: the layer extract lines 45-50 (atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json), IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7: 'Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde ... Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations ...'; 'Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation'. Libraries: rg over both pinned trees for 'CM form', 'complex conjugation' near representation, 'Hilbert modular', 'induced' finds only Mathlib RepresentationTheory/Induced.lean:55-76 `Representation.IndV`/`Representation.ind` (abstract, read) and NumberField/CMField.lean:71 `IsCMField`. Atlas scan for 'CM form|CM eigenform|complex multiplication|Ochiai': no stage names Lemma 9.2 or CM Hilbert forms; ModularForms Layer 9 (Q, self-twists) and ShimuraVarieties:V5 / HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.1 (main theorem of complex multiplication) are unrelated. Confirmed planned, by containment only. Lemma 9.2 (V_{p,f} not stable under rho_f(tau) for CM f in \overline{M} and tau restricting to complex conjugation of L) is an internal step of the DK odd-prime proof fixing the global basis of the integral Galois representation, which I.7 commits to formalising; no layer names it. Its inputs are the unplanned Hara–Ochiai Prop. A.3 (item 277) and the planned irreducibility of rho_f (item 278, R19.2), so as with item 276 the containment rests on the DK proof target alone.

items.name: Proposition 9.3: a τ moving every local eigenspace V_{𝔭,f}
items.statement: There exists τ ∈ G_F such that τ restricts to the complex conjugation of G = Gal(H/F) and such that for all f ∈ \overline{M} and all 𝔭 | p the subspace V_{𝔭,f} is not stable under ρ_f(τ). (Proof, a modification of \cite{dkv} Lemma 4.3: let H_0 be the compositum of H with the CM fields L of the CM forms f ∈ \overline{M}, a finite CM abelian extension of F, and τ_0 ∈ Gal(H_0/F) its complex conjugation; by Lemma 9.2 any τ restricting to τ_0 works for the CM forms. Enumerate the V_{𝔭,f} for non-CM f ∈ \overline{M} and 𝔭 | p as V_1, …, V_n, with stabilisers G_i ⊂ G_F, of infinite index by Lemma 9.1; inductively choose α_i ∈ \overline{F} fixed by G_i and not in H_{i−1}, let H_i be the Galois closure of H_{i−1}(α_i) over F and τ_i ∈ Gal(H_i/F) restricting to τ_{i−1} with τ_i(α_i) ≠ α_i; any τ ∈ G_F restricting to τ_n on H_n moves every α_i, so lies in no G_i.)
items.locator: §9.1, Proposition 9.3 (label p:tau), the source lines 2674–2684
items.note: Fixes once and for all the element τ used to define the global bases of all ρ_f and of ρ, guaranteeing the non-degeneracy (114) of Ribet's wrench. Evidence: the layer extract lines 45-50 (atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json), IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7: 'Formalise the proof of the integral Brumer–Stark theorem ... The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations. Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma ...'; audit target 'Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations and the hypotheses of the generalised Ribet lemma ... for the Hilbert/Eisenstein representation | library: absent'. Libraries: rg over both pinned trees for 'complex conjugation', 'Galois closure', 'Hilbert modular', 'eigenspace' near Galois finds nothing relevant. Atlas scan for 'Ventullo', 'Dasgupta.Kakde.Ventullo', 'DKV', 'Gross.Stark', 'wrench', 'stabiliser': no stage names DKV Lemma 4.3, the Gross–Stark conjecture, or the choice of tau; 'Dasgupta'/'Kakde' occur only in IHG.6 (DKSW extension theorem, the layer extract lines 109-125, which assumes field-factor irreducibility and does not use such a tau), I.7, and NoncommutativeAndEquivariantIwasawa NE.4/NE.6 (Kakde's noncommutative main conjecture). Confirmed planned, by containment only. Proposition 9.3 (a tau in G_F restricting to complex conjugation of G with V_{p,f} not rho_f(tau)-stable for all f in \overline{M} and p | p) is the non-degeneracy input for the global bases of the integral Galois representation rho over the Hecke algebra in the DK odd-prime proof, which I.7 commits to formalising under 'integral Galois representations'; no layer names the proposition or its DKV Lemma 4.3 model. […]

items.name: Global basis for ρ_f and change-of-basis matrices M_{f,𝔭}
items.statement: Fix τ as in Proposition 9.3. For each f ∈ \overline{M} choose the basis of E² in which ρ_f(τ) = diag(λ_{1,f}, λ_{2,f}) with λ_{1,f} ≡ 1 and λ_{2,f} ≡ χ(τ) ≡ −1 mod π_E, and write ρ_f(σ) = [[a_f(σ), b_f(σ)],[c_f(σ), d_f(σ)]] for σ ∈ G_F. For each 𝔭 | p let M_{f,𝔭} = [[A_{f,𝔭}, B_{f,𝔭}],[C_{f,𝔭}, D_{f,𝔭}]] ∈ GL_2(E) be a change-of-basis matrix from this basis to a basis giving the local form (113), i.e. such that [[a_f(σ), b_f(σ)],[c_f(σ), d_f(σ)]] M_{f,𝔭} = M_{f,𝔭} [[ψη_𝔭^{−1}ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ), *],[0, η_𝔭(σ)]] for all σ ∈ G_𝔭 (so the first column of M_{f,𝔭} spans V_{𝔭,f}).
items.locator: §9.1, text after Proposition 9.3, the source lines 2686–2698
items.note: Sets up the matrix entries a_f, b_f, c_f, d_f and the local constants A_{f,𝔭}, C_{f,𝔭} which, assembled over f ∈ \overline{M}, give the entries of ρ and the elements A_𝔭/C_𝔭 adjoined to form B. Evidence: the layer extract:44-50 (atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json, IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7): "The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations. Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation". the layer extract:110-158 (IHG.6) ends: "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses; no arithmetic Brumer–Stark conclusion is part of this abstract supplier." Paper: the source 2686-2698 (basis with rho_f(tau) diagonal, entries a_f,b_f,c_f,d_f, matrices M_{f,p} conjugating to the local form (113)). Library: rg over Mathlib and TauCeti for HilbertModular|Hecke algebra|GaloisRep|eigenform|Ribet finds only the abstract double-coset Hecke ring (Mathlib/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/Defs.lean) and unrelated algebraic-group files; no Galois representation of a Hilbert eigenform, no ordinary local shape. Confirmed planned; narrowed the planner list to I.7 alone. IHG.6 is the abstract supplier: it takes triangularizations (eta_v, xi_v) as hypotheses and explicitly delegates everything about the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein representation to I.7, and the classical Ribet-wrench basis comparison for rho_f is part of Dasgupta–Kakde's odd-prime proof obligations that I.7 names. Neither library has rho_f, so not library. Nearest other layer R19.2 (Hilbert Galois representations themselves) constructs rho_f but not this basis bookkeeping.

items.name: Key point (114): A_{f,𝔭} ≠ 0 and C_{f,𝔭} ≠ 0
items.statement: For every f ∈ \overline{M} and every 𝔭 | p, the entries A_{f,𝔭} and C_{f,𝔭} of the change-of-basis matrix M_{f,𝔭} are nonzero. (Equivalently: the line V_{𝔭,f}, spanned by the first column (A_{f,𝔭}, C_{f,𝔭})^T of M_{f,𝔭}, is neither of the two eigenlines E·(1,0)^T, E·(0,1)^T of ρ_f(τ); this is exactly the conclusion of Proposition 9.3.)
items.locator: §9.1, equation (114) (label e:keypoint), the source lines 2699–2703
items.note: Makes A_𝔭 and C_𝔭 invertible in K = ∏E, so that A_𝔭/C_𝔭 and the formula (119) make sense, and allows the column factors A_j/C_j to be cancelled in the determinant argument of Theorem 9.10. Evidence: the layer extract:44-50 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7): "The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation". Paper: the source 2699-2703, equation (114) (label e:keypoint): for every f in Mbar and p | p, A_{f,p} ≠ 0 and C_{f,p} ≠ 0, the restatement of Proposition 9.3 (line 2673-2684, built on Lemmas 9.1/9.2, CM vs non-CM). Library search (rg 'CM form|non-CM|eigenline|Ribet' in both trees) finds nothing relevant; the atlas scan for 'non-CM' hits only HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.7/HE.8 and ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.3 (elliptic-curve/CM contexts unrelated to Hilbert eigenforms above an Eisenstein ideal). Confirmed planned with I.7 as sole owner, as in the previous verdict. In DKSW's generalised lemma (IHG.6) this non-degeneracy is replaced by the field-factor irreducibility hypothesis, so IHG.6 does not plan (114); I.7 explicitly owns the Dasgupta–Kakde odd-prime proof obligations for the actual representation. No library declaration is near.

items.name: Total quotient ring K = Frac(𝕋_𝔐) = ∏_{f∈\overline{M}} E
items.statement: K = Frac(𝕋_𝔐) = Frac(∏_{f∈\overline{M}} 𝒪) = ∏_{f∈\overline{M}} E (equation (115)), via the 𝒪-algebra injections with finite cokernel 𝕋_𝔐 → \tilde{𝕋}_𝔐 → ∏_{f∈\overline{M}} 𝒪 of §8.7 (which become isomorphisms after inverting p). Elements of K are indexed by f ∈ \overline{M}; K carries the p-adic topology and the (equivalent for finitely generated submodules) 𝔐-adic topology.
items.locator: §9.2 (label s:galrepphi), equation (115) (label e:kdef), the source lines 2707–2710; the injections 𝕋_𝔐 → 𝕋̃_𝔐 → ∏_{f∈M̄} 𝒪 with finite cokernel are from §8.5 (lines 2562–2568)
items.note: Coefficient ring of the product representation ρ; the modules B_0, B, B' live inside K, and its product structure underlies the non-zerodivisor arguments of Lemma 9.9 and Theorem 9.10. Evidence: the layer extract:44-50 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation"; the layer extract:110-158 (IHG.6) takes "K=Frac(Ttilde) a product of local rings with principal maximal ideals" as an abstract hypothesis and says "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses". Paper: the source 2707-2710, equation (115) K = Frac(T_M) = Frac(∏_{f∈Mbar} O) = ∏ E, using the finite-cokernel injections at the source 2563-2567. Mathlib near misses verified in the pinned tree: Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/Pi.lean:78 bijective_lift_piRingHom_algebraMap_comp_piEvalRingHom (localization of a finite product is the product of localizations) and Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean:633 IsArtinianRing.equivPi (reduced Artinian ring ≅ ∏ R/m); neither identifies Frac of the p-ordinary Hecke algebra T_M with ∏_{f∈Mbar} E. Confirmed planned; dropped IHG.6 from the planner list because it assumes the product structure of K abstractly and explicitly assigns the arithmetic instance to I.7. Not library: the ingredient lemmas are generic (and equivPi does not even apply, T_M being O-torsion-free, not Artinian); the item needs the Hecke algebra T_M of §8.7 and its finite-index embedding into ∏O, absent from both trees.

items.name: Product Galois representation ρ = ∏_f ρ_f : G_F → GL_2(K)
items.statement: ρ = ∏_{f∈\overline{M}} ρ_f : G_F → GL_2(K), with K = ∏_{f∈\overline{M}} E as in (115). It is continuous for the p-adic topology on K (each ρ_f is continuous), hence continuous for the 𝔐-adic topology on K, since every ideal 𝔐^n of 𝕋_𝔐 is finitely generated over 𝒪.
items.locator: §9.2, display after (115) and following sentence, the source lines 2711–2717
items.note: The single representation over the Hecke algebra whose off-diagonal entries b(σ) generate B_0 and define the cohomology class κ. Evidence: the layer extract:44-50 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation"; the layer extract:110-158 (IHG.6): "a continuous rank-two representation over the total quotient ring K of T" is the INPUT of the abstract theorem, and "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses". Paper: the source 2711-2717, rho = ∏_f rho_f : G_F → GL_2(K), continuous for the p-adic hence M-adic topology. Alternatives checked: OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.3 ("Construct the Galois representation or determinant law over the ordinary Hecke algebra and prove its ordinary local structure") concerns the Hida ordinary Hecke algebra of Skinner–Wiles, not the finite weight-k algebra T_M and its total quotient ring; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.6 requires absolute residual irreducibility, which fails here (residually Eisenstein). rg in both libraries for Galois representations attached to modular forms finds none. Confirmed planned; planner narrowed to I.7, which the atlas itself (IHG.6's closing sentence) names as the layer that supplies the actual representation and its hypotheses. R21.3 is the nearest more foundational alternative but its object is the Λ-adic ordinary Hecke algebra representation, a different construction; noted, not cited. Nothing in either library.

items.name: ρ is unramified outside 𝔫p and satisfies the Hecke characteristic polynomial (116)
items.statement: (1) ρ is unramified outside 𝔫p. (2) For every prime 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p of F, χr(ρ(Frob_𝔩))(x) = x² − T_𝔩 x + 𝛙(𝔩) ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩) (equation (116)), where T_𝔩 ∈ 𝕋_𝔐 ⊂ K is the Hecke operator (mapping to (c(𝔩, f))_f under (115)), 𝛙(𝔩) ∈ R^* ⊂ 𝕋_𝔐 is the value of the group-ring character (which maps to (ψ_f(𝔩))_f), and ε_cyc is the p-adic cyclotomic character. (Immediate from properties (1)–(2) of each ρ_f.)
items.locator: §9.2, properties (1)–(2) of ρ and equation (116) (label e:char), the source lines 2718–2725
items.note: Transfers the Hida–Wiles properties of each ρ_f to ρ with Hecke operators as coefficients; (116) with φ(T_𝔩) = ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩) + 𝛙(𝔩) gives the trace congruence (120), and (1) gives Proposition 9.4. Evidence: the layer extract:44-50 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7): "Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation"; the layer extract:110-158 (IHG.6): "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses" (property (1) is the ramification hypothesis; (116) is the T[X] characteristic-polynomial hypothesis 'Assume its characteristic polynomials lie in T[X]'). Paper: the source 2718-2725, properties (1)-(2) and equation (116) chr(rho(Frob_l)) = x² − T_l x + psi(l) eps_cyc^{k−1}(l). the layer extract:523-537 (R19.6): "Construct the determinant law from Hecke operators and Frobenius polynomials, then prove representability ... under absolute residual irreducibility" — for the localised completed Hecke algebra of the modularity-lifting programme. Library: no Hecke operators T_l on Hilbert forms over O and no Galois representations of eigenforms in either tree (rg 'Hecke|GaloisRep|Frob' in TauCeti and Mathlib/NumberTheory). Confirmed planned; removed R19.6 as co-planner. R19.6's object is a determinant law over a completed Hecke algebra under residual irreducibility (representability), whereas this item is the transfer of the per-form Hida–Wiles properties to the product rho over Frac(T_M), which the atlas assigns to I.7 by name ('ramification hypotheses'). The per-form inputs are separate items (R19.2/R19.4). Not library.

items.name: Ordinary local shape (117) of ρ at primes above p with η_𝔭(rec(ϖ^{−1})) = U_𝔭
items.statement: For every 𝔭 | p and decomposition group G_𝔭 ⊂ G_F, ρ|_{G_𝔭} ∼ [[𝛙 η_𝔭^{−1} ε_cyc^{k−1}, *],[0, η_𝔭]] (equation (117)), where η_𝔭 : G_𝔭 → \tilde{𝕋}^* (⊂ K^*) is the unramified character with η_𝔭(rec(ϖ^{−1})) = U_𝔭, the Hecke operator at 𝔭 (mapping to (c(𝔭, f_p))_f under (115)); ϖ and rec as in (113). That is, there is a basis of K² in which every ρ(σ), σ ∈ G_𝔭, is upper triangular with diagonal entries 𝛙η_𝔭^{−1}ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ) and η_𝔭(σ). (Immediate from (113) for each f ∈ \overline{M}, taking the product of the local bases.)
items.locator: §9.2, property (3) of ρ and equation (117) (label e:localrho), the source lines 2726–2732
items.note: Yields the change-of-basis matrices M_𝔭 of (118) and hence the local formula (119) for b on G_𝔭. Evidence: the layer extract:44-50 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7): "integral Galois representations ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation"; the layer extract:110-158 (IHG.6): "For a finite collection of local subgroups, choose triangularizations with diagonal characters eta_v, xi_v" is a hypothesis of the abstract theorem, and "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses". Paper: the source 2726-2732, equation (117) rho|_{G_p} ~ [[psi eta_p^{-1} eps_cyc^{k−1}, *],[0, eta_p]] with eta_p unramified, eta_p(rec(ϖ^{-1})) = U_p; the Hecke algebra is that of p-ordinary forms (the source 2514). Alternative checked: R21.3 (key text quoted under n=284) proves 'ordinary local structure' over the Hida ordinary Hecke algebra, a different object; R19.5 (the layer extract:507-515) plans the per-form ordinary local case. Library: no ordinary local shape of any Galois representation in either tree. Confirmed planned; planner narrowed to I.7. IHG.6 chooses the local triangularizations abstractly and disclaims the arithmetic instance; the per-form input (113) (Wiles) is an earlier item owned elsewhere (R19.5). Not library.

items.name: χr(ρ(σ)) ∈ 𝕋_𝔐[x], residual factorisation, and the distinct eigenvalues λ_1, λ_2 of ρ(τ)
items.statement: For all σ ∈ G_F, the characteristic polynomial χr(ρ(σ))(x) lies in 𝕋_𝔐[x] and χr(ρ(σ))(x) ≡ (x − 1)(x − χ(σ)) mod 𝔐 (by Čebotarev and (116), since T_𝔩 ≡ 1 + χ(𝔩) and 𝛙(𝔩) ≡ χ(𝔩) mod 𝔐). For the τ fixed in §9.1 (χ(τ) = −1), χr(ρ(τ)) has two distinct roots modulo 𝔐, hence by Hensel's lemma two distinct roots λ_1, λ_2 ∈ 𝕋_𝔐^* with λ_1 ≡ 1 and λ_2 ≡ −1 mod 𝔐; under (115), λ_i = (λ_{i,f})_{f∈\overline{M}}.
items.locator: §9.2, text after (117), the source lines 2734–2738
items.note: Allows a global basis for ρ over K diagonalising ρ(τ); the unit λ_1 − λ_2 (λ_1 ≢ λ_2 mod 𝔐) is what solves the congruences (120)–(123). Evidence: the layer extract:44-50 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7): "Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation"; the layer extract:110-158 (IHG.6): "Assume its characteristic polynomials lie in T[X], reduce to the product of two T-valued character polynomials modulo I" (an assumption of the abstract theorem) and "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein ... hypotheses". Paper: the source 2734-2738: chr(rho(sigma)) ∈ T_M[x], ≡ (x−1)(x−chi(sigma)) mod M by Čebotarev and (116); Hensel gives distinct roots lambda_1 ≡ 1, lambda_2 ≡ −1 in T_M^*. Mathlib ingredients verified in the pinned tree: Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.lean:108 class HenselianLocalRing (simple residual roots of monic polynomials lift) and line 170 instance IsAdicComplete.henselianRing; Čebotarev density is planned by tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev (layers 9-14) and R01.5 'Chebotarev recognition' for semisimple representations over a field, not over T_M. Confirmed planned with I.7 as sole owner (IHG.6 dropped: it states this as a hypothesis and delegates its verification to I.7). Not library: Hensel lifting over a complete local ring is only an ingredient; the integrality of chr(rho(sigma)) in T_M[x] for all sigma needs Čebotarev plus the Hecke-algebra representation, absent from both trees.

items.name: Global basis for ρ, matrix entries a, b, c, d, and change-of-basis matrices M_𝔭 (118)
items.statement: Choose the basis of K² in which ρ(τ) = diag(λ_1, λ_2) (the product over f of the bases chosen in §9.1), and write ρ(σ) = [[a(σ), b(σ)],[c(σ), d(σ)]] with a, b, c, d : G_F → K, so that a = (a_f)_f, b = (b_f)_f, etc. For each 𝔭 | p let M_𝔭 = [[A_𝔭, B_𝔭],[C_𝔭, D_𝔭]] ∈ GL_2(K) be a change-of-basis matrix with [[a(σ), b(σ)],[c(σ), d(σ)]] M_𝔭 = M_𝔭 [[𝛙η_𝔭^{−1}ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ), *],[0, η_𝔭(σ)]] for all σ ∈ G_𝔭 (equation (118)); under (115), A_𝔭 = (A_{f,𝔭})_{f∈\overline{M}} and similarly for B_𝔭, C_𝔭, D_𝔭. By (114), A_𝔭 and C_𝔭 are invertible in K, so A_𝔭/C_𝔭 ∈ K^* is defined.
items.locator: §9.2, equation (118) (label e:plocal) and surrounding text, the source lines 2740–2749
items.note: Defines the function b(σ) whose values generate B_0 and the elements A_𝔭/C_𝔭 adjoined in the definition of B. Evidence: the layer extract:44-50 (IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.7): "The odd-prime result of Dasgupta–Kakde and the integral DKSW refinement have distinct proof obligations ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation"; the layer extract:110-158 (IHG.6): "compare the distinguishable case with the separate classical construction" and "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses". Paper: the source 2740-2749, equation (118) (label e:plocal): basis with rho(tau) = diag(lambda_1, lambda_2), entries a,b,c,d : G_F → K, matrices M_p = [[A_p,B_p],[C_p,D_p]] ∈ GL_2(K) with A_p = (A_{f,p})_f, and A_p, C_p invertible in K by (114). Library: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Block.lean is generic block-triangular linear algebra; no representation over a Hecke algebra's total quotient ring in either tree (rg 'Hecke|GaloisRep|Ribet' as above). Confirmed planned; planner narrowed to I.7, which owns the classical (residually distinguishable) Ribet-wrench construction of Dasgupta–Kakde's odd-prime proof; IHG.6 only compares its distinguishable case with that 'separate classical construction' and takes the triangularization data as input. Not library.

items.name: Local formula (119) for b on decomposition groups at p
items.statement: For every 𝔭 | p and every σ ∈ G_𝔭, b(σ) = (A_𝔭/C_𝔭)·(𝛙η_𝔭^{−1}ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ) − a(σ)) in K. (Proof: compare the top-left entries of the two sides of (118): a(σ)A_𝔭 + b(σ)C_𝔭 = A_𝔭·𝛙η_𝔭^{−1}ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ), and divide by the unit C_𝔭.)
items.locator: §9.2, equation (119) (label e:beq), the source lines 2750–2755
items.note: The central local input: it gives the coboundary formula (126) at 𝔭 ∈ Σ, the inclusion b(I_𝔭) ⊂ (A_𝔭/C_𝔭)I at unramified 𝔭 | p, and the expression of the auxiliary generators c_i in Theorem 9.10. Evidence: Verified in the layer extract lines 110–158 (IHG.6): "For a finite collection of local subgroups, choose triangularizations with diagonal characters eta_v, xi_v and a partition Sigma disjoint-union P" and "Construct N and the cocycle, zero on a chosen subgroup in nonempty Sigma and on the specified inertia groups, with explicit coboundary vectors y_v on the remaining Sigma subgroups." I.7 (the layer extract lines 48–50): "Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation"; IHG.6 closing sentence: "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses". Paper checked: the source 2745–2755, (118) M_𝔭-triangularisation on G_𝔭 and (119) b(σ) = (A_𝔭/C_𝔭)(𝛙η_𝔭^{-1}ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ) − a(σ)). Library search: rg -i 'pseudo-?represent|PseudoRep|Eisenstein ?ideal|Ribet' is empty in both pinned trees; Mathlib's only Hecke-algebra files are NumberTheory/HeckeRing/Defs.lean and FLT/Basic.lean (abstract Hecke rings, no Galois side). Confirmed the previous verdict. (119) is the entry-wise consequence of the local triangularisation (118): the vector y_𝔭 = A_𝔭/C_𝔭 with b(σ) = y_𝔭·(ξ_𝔭(σ) − a(σ)) on G_𝔭 is exactly IHG.6's 'explicit coboundary vector y_v' at a Sigma subgroup, derived from its 'triangularizations with diagonal characters eta_v, xi_v'; (118) itself for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein ρ is an I.7 hypothesis. No more foundational owner names this: R19.6 (representations over Hecke algebras) requires absolute residual irreducibility and never mentions triangularisation on decomposition groups. […]

items.name: Eisenstein ideals Ĩ = ker φ ⊂ \tilde{𝕋}_𝔐 and I = Ĩ ∩ 𝕋_𝔐
items.statement: Ĩ ⊂ \tilde{𝕋}_𝔐 is the kernel of the surjective R-algebra homomorphism φ : \tilde{𝕋}_𝔐 → W of Theorem 8.23, and I = Ĩ ∩ 𝕋_𝔐 is the kernel of φ|_{𝕋_𝔐} : 𝕋_𝔐 → R/xΘ^# ⊂ W. One has I ⊂ 𝔐 (since \overline{φ} = φ mod 𝔪_R on 𝕋), and, φ|_{𝕋_𝔐} having values in the image of R, every element of 𝕋_𝔐 is congruent modulo I to an element of R.
items.locator: §9.3, opening paragraph, the source lines 2760–2761
items.note: The ideal modulo which the traces of ρ are Eisenstein; B/IB and its quotients carry the class κ, and φ(det M'') = 0 in W is what converts relations in \overline{B}_p into divisibility by Θ^#. Evidence: Verified: I.7 (the layer extract line 48) "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma for residually indistinguishable characters" with audit target "Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations and the hypotheses of the generalised Ribet lemma ... for the Hilbert/Eisenstein representation | library: absent". IHG.6 (the layer extract lines 126–130): "the full local-condition version for a Noetherian inclusion T ⊂ Ttilde, T local, with both rings complete for the maximal ideal of T, a nontrivial ideal Itilde, I=Itilde∩T". Paper checked: the source 2760–2761, Ĩ = ker φ ⊂ \tilde𝕋_𝔐, I = Ĩ ∩ 𝕋_𝔐 = ker φ|_{𝕋_𝔐}. Atlas scan of areas/*.json and roadmaps/*.json for 'Eisenstein ideal' hits only ModularCurves layer 10 (Mazur), AutomorphicCongruences L2/L2s (GU(3,1) Klingen–Eisenstein) and IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.5 (Wiles's Λ-adic Hecke algebras for the main conjecture) — different objects. Library: rg 'Eisenstein ?ideal' empty in both trees. Confirmed the previous verdict. The Eisenstein ideal is the kernel of the group-ring-valued Hecke homomorphism φ of Theorem 8.23, i.e. the output of I.7's 'Hilbert modular congruences'; its abstract shape (Ĩ ⊂ T̃ nontrivial, I = Ĩ ∩ T) is verbatim the input datum of IHG.6's local-condition theorem. I.5's 'Eisenstein ideals' belong to Wiles's Λ-adic main-conjecture Hecke algebra and are not this finite-level, group-ring-valued ideal, so I.5 is not a more exact owner. No library object exists.

items.name: Trace congruence (120): Tr ρ(σ) ≡ ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ) + 𝛙(σ) mod I
items.statement: For all σ ∈ G_F, Tr ρ(σ) = a(σ) + d(σ) lies in 𝕋_𝔐 and a(σ) + d(σ) ≡ ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ) + 𝛙(σ) mod I (equation (120)). (Proof: by (116) and Theorem 8.23, φ(Tr ρ(Frob_𝔩)) = φ(T_𝔩) = ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩) + 𝛙(𝔩) for 𝔩 ∤ 𝔫p, so the congruence holds on Frobenii and extends to G_F by Čebotarev and continuity.)
items.locator: §9.3, equation (120) (label e:trmodi), the source lines 2763–2766
items.note: The pseudo-representation input: with the diagonalisation of ρ(τ) it yields the diagonal congruences (123). Evidence: Verified: IHG.6 (the layer extract lines 116–120) "Assume its characteristic polynomials lie in T[X], reduce to the product of two T-valued character polynomials modulo I" and (line 130) "Require irreducibility on reduced field factors and the source's character-polynomial congruence"; I.7 (line 50) "Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation". Paper checked: the source 2762–2766, Tr ρ(σ) = a(σ)+d(σ) ≡ ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ) + 𝛙(σ) mod I for all σ ∈ G_F, from φ(T_𝔩) = ε_cyc^{k−1}(𝔩)+𝛙(𝔩) and Čebotarev. Library: Mathlib has no Chebotarev (rg -i chebotarev empty); Tau Ceti has NumberTheory/Chebotarev/FrobeniusPrimeSet.lean (`NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet`, the prime sets whose density the theorem computes) but not the density theorem itself, and neither tree has a Galois representation over a Hecke algebra. Confirmed the previous verdict. The trace congruence (120) is the trace half of IHG.6's hypothesis that char ρ reduces mod I to (x − ε_cyc^{k−1})(x − 𝛙) ('the source's character-polynomial congruence'); establishing it for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein ρ from Theorem 8.23 plus Čebotarev is I.7's stated job. Correction to the previous note only: Tau Ceti does contain Chebotarev preliminaries (Frobenius prime sets, ramified primes, auxiliary primes), though not the density theorem, so the Čebotarev input is 'in progress' rather than wholly absent; this does not change the status.

items.name: Diagonal congruences (123): a(σ) ≡ ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ), d(σ) ≡ 𝛙(σ) mod I
items.statement: For all σ ∈ G_F, a(σ) ≡ ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ) mod I and d(σ) ≡ 𝛙(σ) mod I (equation (123)); in particular a(σ), d(σ) ∈ 𝕋_𝔐. (Proof: from (120) at σ = τ, λ_1 + λ_2 ≡ ε_cyc^{k−1}(τ) + 𝛙(τ) mod I, so λ_1, λ_2 are roots of (x − ε_cyc^{k−1}(τ))(x − 𝛙(τ)) mod I (equation (121)); since λ_1 ≡ 1 ≡ ε_cyc^{k−1}(τ) and λ_2 ≡ χ(τ) ≡ 𝛙(τ) mod 𝔐 and λ_1 ≢ λ_2 mod 𝔐, one gets λ_1 ≡ ε_cyc^{k−1}(τ) and λ_2 ≡ 𝛙(τ) mod I. Applying (120) to στ gives a(σ)λ_1 + d(σ)λ_2 ≡ ε_cyc^{k−1}(στ) + 𝛙(στ) ≡ ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ)λ_1 + 𝛙(σ)λ_2 mod I (equation (122)); solving (120) and (122), using that λ_1 − λ_2 is a unit of 𝕋_𝔐, yields (123).)
items.locator: §9.3, equations (121) (label e:charmodi), (122) (label e:trtau) and (123) (label e:adcong), the source lines 2767–2786
items.note: Turns the multiplicativity of ρ into the cocycle relation defining κ; also used in (126), in b(I_𝔭) ⊂ (A_𝔭/C_𝔭)I, and in the expression of c_i. Evidence: Verified: IHG.6 (the layer extract lines 132–134) "Prove the theorem in its residually indistinguishable case, and compare the distinguishable case with the separate classical construction"; IHG.1 (the layer extract lines 161–163) "generalized matrix algebra decompositions under residually multiplicity-free hypotheses ... Develop reducibility ideals, extension modules and the lattice constructions used by congruence arguments"; I.7 (line 50) "Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation". Paper checked: the source 2767–2786: λ_1 ≢ λ_2 mod 𝔐 (residually distinct), (121) λ_i roots of (x − ε_cyc^{k−1}(τ))(x − 𝛙(τ)) mod I, (122) from (120) at στ, solve to get (123). Library: rg 'pseudo-?represent|PseudoRep|reducibility' empty in both trees; no GMA/Cayley–Hamilton algebra objects in Mathlib or Tau Ceti. Confirmed planned, with the owner refined. The diagonal congruences use λ_1 ≢ λ_2 mod 𝔐, i.e. the residually distinguishable (multiplicity-free) case; the abstract statement 'diagonal entries of a GMA decomposition are congruent to the two characters modulo the reducibility ideal' is IHG.1's 'generalized matrix algebra decompositions under residually multiplicity-free hypotheses ... reducibility ideals', which is the more foundational stage of the same roadmap, while IHG.6 names it as the 'separate classical construction' it compares against and I.7 applies it to the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein ρ. Since IHG.1 does not spell out the congruence itself, IHG.6 is listed first as the safer owner. Nothing in either library.

items.name: Modules B_0, B, B' and \overline{B} = B/B' (general setting)
items.statement: B_0 is the 𝕋_𝔐-submodule of K generated by {b(σ) : σ ∈ G_F}; B is any 𝕋_𝔐-submodule of K containing B_0; B' ⊂ B is any 𝕋_𝔐-submodule containing IB_0; \overline{B} = B/B', and for σ ∈ G_F, \overline{b}(σ) denotes the image of b(σ) in \overline{B}.
items.locator: §9.3, text after (123), the source lines 2787–2788
items.note: The general framework in which the cocycle κ is defined; specialised in §9.4 to B = (B_0, A_𝔭/C_𝔭 : 𝔭 ∈ Σ − S_∞) and B' = (IB, B(I_p), p^mB). Evidence: Verified: IHG.6 (the layer extract lines 118–120) "Construct a finite T-module M and a continuous class in H¹(G,M(chi/psi)) whose every representative cocycle generates M, and prove Fitt₀_T(M) is contained in I" and (lines 136–139) "Construct N and the cocycle, zero on a chosen subgroup in nonempty Sigma and on the specified inertia groups, with explicit coboundary vectors y_v on the remaining Sigma subgroups. Prove N is generated by the cocycle image together with those vectors." Paper checked: the source 2787–2788, B_0 = 𝕋_𝔐⟨b(σ) : σ ∈ G_F⟩ ⊂ K, B ⊇ B_0 any submodule, B' ⊇ IB_0, \overline B = B/B'. Library: no module generated by matrix entries of a Galois representation over a Hecke algebra in either tree (rg for 'Ribet|pseudo-?represent|Eisenstein ?ideal' empty). Confirmed the previous verdict. B_0 (span of the off-diagonal entries), the enlargement B by local vectors and the quotient \overline B = B/B' are exactly IHG.6's M and N ('generated by the cocycle image together with those vectors'), and the general (B, B') framework is the abstract DKSW module; IHG.6 is the most foundational owner. No library object.

items.name: Cohomology class κ ∈ H^1(G_F, \overline{B}(𝛙^{−1}ε_cyc^{k−1})), and κ ∈ H^1(G_F, \overline{B}(𝛙^{−1})) when p^mB ⊂ B'
items.statement: With B_0 ⊂ B, B' ⊇ IB_0 and \overline{B} = B/B' as above: since ρ is a homomorphism, b(σσ') = a(σ)b(σ') + b(σ)d(σ') for σ, σ' ∈ G_F, and by (123) \overline{b}(σσ') = ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ)\overline{b}(σ') + 𝛙(σ')\overline{b}(σ) in \overline{B}. Hence the function σ ↦ \overline{b}(σ)𝛙(σ)^{−1} (equation (124)) is a continuous 1-cocycle on G_F with values in \overline{B}(𝛙^{−1}ε_cyc^{k−1}) (the module \overline{B} with G_F acting through the character 𝛙^{−1}ε_cyc^{k−1}), and κ ∈ H^1(G_F, \overline{B}(𝛙^{−1}ε_cyc^{k−1})) denotes its class. If moreover p^mB ⊂ B' and k ≡ 1 mod (p−1)p^N with N ≥ m (so that ε_cyc^{k−1} ≡ 1 mod p^m), then ε_cyc^{k−1} acts trivially on \overline{B} and κ is a class in H^1(G_F, \overline{B}(𝛙^{−1})) (equation (125)).
items.locator: §9.3, displays between (123) and (124), equations (124) (label e:kappadef) and (125) (label e:kappaspace), the source lines 2789–2801
items.note: The Galois cohomology class of Ribet's method; its restriction to G_H cuts out an abelian extension of H whose ramification is controlled by Propositions 9.4–9.5, giving the surjection α from the class group and ultimately β from ∇. Evidence: Verified: IHG.6 (the layer extract lines 118–121) "Construct a finite T-module M and a continuous class in H¹(G,M(chi/psi)) whose every representative cocycle generates M ... Residual equality of chi and psi is allowed. ArithmeticGaloisDuality owns the continuous cochain/class API." I.7 (line 50): "Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation and compare the resulting arithmetic class". Paper checked: the source 2789–2801: b(σσ') = a(σ)b(σ') + b(σ)d(σ'), (123) gives \overline b(σσ') = ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ)\overline b(σ') + 𝛙(σ')\overline b(σ), so (124) σ ↦ \overline b(σ)𝛙(σ)^{-1} is a 1-cocycle with κ ∈ H^1(G_F, \overline B(𝛙^{-1}ε_cyc^{k−1})), and (125) κ ∈ H^1(G_F, \overline B(𝛙^{-1})) when p^mB ⊂ B', k ≡ 1 mod (p−1)p^N, N ≥ m. Library carrier only: Tau Ceti `TauCeti.ContCohomology.H1` (abbrev at RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/LowDegree.lean:674, Z1 at :485, B1 at :174) with Mathlib's `groupCohomology.IsCocycle₁` used at Corestriction.lean:282; no construction of κ. Confirmed planned; added I.7 as co-owner because the previous note itself assigned the k ≡ 1 mod (p−1)p^N passage to \overline B(𝛙^{-1}) to I.7 ('compare the resulting arithmetic class') without listing it. κ is IHG.6's 'continuous class in H¹(G, M(chi/psi))' with chi = ε_cyc^{k−1}, psi = 𝛙. The libraries supply only the continuous-H¹ carrier (Tau Ceti explicit H1 for a topological group on a topological abelian group), not the class.

items.name: Vanishing of H^1 of a pro-v group with pro-p coefficients, v ≠ p (as used)
items.statement: Let P be a pro-ℓ group for a rational prime ℓ ≠ p and let M be a pro-p group (e.g. a finite abelian p-group, or a finitely generated 𝒪-module with its p-adic topology) with a continuous P-action. Then the continuous cohomology H^1(P, M) vanishes. As used: for a place v of F with v ∤ p, the wild inertia subgroup I_{v,1} ⊂ I_v is pro-ℓ (ℓ the residue characteristic of v) while \overline{B} is pro-p, so H^1(I_{v,1}, \overline{B}(𝛙^{−1})) = 0 by continuity of cocycles.
items.locator: §9.3, proof of Proposition 9.4, the source lines 2811–2814
items.note: External input (no \cite key given; standard (cohomology of profinite groups: continuity of cocycles, pro-ℓ group versus p-primary module)). Gives the tame ramification of κ at v | 𝔫, v ∤ p, in Proposition 9.4. Evidence: Verified in atlas/areas/algebra-1.json. ProfiniteCohomology layer 11: "`cd_p G = 0` if and only if `Hⁱ(G, M) = 0` in positive degrees for every `p`-primary `M`" and "`cd_p_eq_of_index_not_dvd`, equality when `H` is open of index prime to `p`, from Layer 10's `cor ∘ res`"; "The `p`-Sylow equality `cd_p G = cd_p G_p` (NSW (3.3.6)) belongs to the Profinite Pro-`p` Groups roadmap". ProfiniteProPGroups layer 6: "**The Sylow equality.** Let `G` be profinite, and let `G_p` be a `p`-Sylow subgroup of `G` ... Then `cd_p G = cd_p G_p` ... for open `U ⊇ G_p` the composite of corestriction after restriction is multiplication by `[G : U]`, and the Sylow property makes those indices prime to `p`. With the colimit, restriction to `G_p` is therefore injective on the cohomology of every discrete `p`-primary module ... named `cd_p_eq_of_isProPSylow`." Paper checked: the source 2811–2814 (I_{v,1} pro-v, \overline B pro-p, H^1(I_{v,1}, \overline B(𝛙^{-1})) = 0 'from continuity of cocycles'). Library: Tau Ceti has the ingredients but not the vanishing — `TauCeti.ContCohomology.explicitCor1_comp_res1 : explicitCor1 G M U hU (explicitRes1 G M U x) = U.index • x` (RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Corestriction.lean:496–498), `ProfiniteProPGroups.IsProPSylow` (Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Sylow/Basic.lean:57) and `IsProP` (Profinite/ProP/Basic.lean:53), and the finite-quotient colimit description (ContCohomology/FiniteQuotient/Colimit.lean); […]

items.name: Proposition 9.4: κ is unramified away from 𝔫p and tamely ramified at v | 𝔫, v ∤ p
items.statement: Let \overline{B} = B/B' be as above with p^mB ⊂ B' and k ≡ 1 mod (p−1)p^N, N ≥ m, so that κ ∈ H^1(G_F, \overline{B}(𝛙^{−1})) is defined by (124). Then κ is unramified away from 𝔫p: its restriction to H^1(I_v, \overline{B}(𝛙^{−1})) vanishes for every place v ∤ 𝔫p of F (I_v an inertia subgroup at v). Furthermore, for v | 𝔫 with v ∤ p, κ is at most tamely ramified: its restriction to H^1(I_{v,1}, \overline{B}(𝛙^{−1})) vanishes, where I_{v,1} ⊂ I_v is the wild inertia subgroup. (Proof: ρ is unramified outside 𝔫p, so b(σ) = 0 for σ ∈ I_v, v ∤ 𝔫p, and the cocycle itself vanishes on I_v; for v ∤ p, I_{v,1} is pro-ℓ (ℓ ≠ p) and \overline{B} is pro-p, so H^1(I_{v,1}, \overline{B}(𝛙^{−1})) = 0.)
items.locator: §9.3, Proposition 9.4 (label p:easyur), the source lines 2803–2814
items.note: Supplies the away-from-p ramification properties of κ used in Proposition 9.5 to show that κ_H cuts out a subextension of L/H. Evidence: Verified: IHG.6 (the layer extract lines 136–137) "Construct N and the cocycle, zero on a chosen subgroup in nonempty Sigma and on the specified inertia groups" and (lines 156–158) "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses"; I.7 (line 50) "Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation and compare the resulting arithmetic class". LocalFieldsRamification layer 4 (atlas/areas/classical-1.json): "**Wild inertia.** Define `P_K = Gal(Kˢ/K^{t})` ... Prove that it is a closed normal pro-`p` subgroup of `G_K`. Prove that it is the unique maximal such subgroup of `I_K`, that is, its pro-`p` Sylow subgroup." Paper checked: the source 2803–2814, Proposition 9.4 (p:easyur): κ|_{I_v} = 0 for v ∤ 𝔫p since ρ is unramified outside 𝔫p so b(I_v) = 0; κ|_{I_{v,1}} = 0 for v | 𝔫, v ∤ p since I_{v,1} is pro-v and \overline B is pro-p. Library: Mathlib's `Ideal.inertia` / `ker_stabilizerHom` (RingTheory/Ideal/Over.lean:354) and `ValuationSubring.inertiaSubgroup` (RingTheory/Valuation/RamificationGroup.lean:50) give inertia of a finite extension only, with no wild inertia and no action on cohomology; Tau Ceti's wild/tame ramification is for function fields only (rg 'wildInertia|WildInertia|inertiaGroup' outside FunctionField hits only the Clifford-theory `inertia` in RepresentationTheory/Induction/Inertia.lean:83); neither tree restricts a class to an inertia subgroup of G_F for a number field. Confirmed planned; […]

items.name: The module B = (B_0, A_𝔭/C_𝔭 : 𝔭 ∈ Σ − S_∞)
items.statement: Recall (from §5, equations (bigsigmadef)/(sigmapdef), and §1 (20)) Σ = {v ∈ S_ram : v | p} ∪ S_∞ and Σ' = {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p} ∪ T, where S_ram is the set of finite primes of F ramified in H/F and T the smoothing set; by §4.1 (label s:nop) one may and does assume that T contains no primes above p. Thus the finite places of Σ are the primes above p dividing 𝔓 (ramified in H/F), the primes 𝔭 | p not in Σ are those dividing 𝔓', and Σ ∪ Σ' ∪ {𝔭 | p} is the set of primes dividing 𝔫p together with S_∞. Definition: B is the 𝕋_𝔐-submodule of K generated by B_0 = (b(σ) : σ ∈ G_F) together with the elements A_𝔭/C_𝔭 of (118)–(119) for all finite 𝔭 ∈ Σ: B = (B_0, A_𝔭/C_𝔭 : 𝔭 ∈ Σ − S_∞). In case 1 (𝔓 = 1, i.e. Σ = S_∞) one has B = B_0.
items.locator: §9.4 'Surjection from ∇', opening displays and definition of B, the source lines 2818–2830
items.note: Adjoining A_𝔭/C_𝔭 makes κ locally trivial at 𝔭 ∈ Σ (coboundary (126)) and produces the quotient \overline{B}_1 receiving the surjection γ from (X_{H,Σ})_{R^#}. Evidence: the layer extract:110-158 (IHG.6, verified): "Construct N and the cocycle, zero on a chosen subgroup in nonempty Sigma and on the specified inertia groups, with explicit coboundary vectors y_v on the remaining Sigma subgroups. Prove N is generated by the cocycle image together with those vectors." and "IntegralIwasawaTheory I.7 verifies the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein and ramification hypotheses". the layer extract:46-52 (I.7, verified): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma ... Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation". Library: rg for Ribet/EisensteinIdeal/HeckeAlgebra/Fitting in Tau Ceti f790474 hits only Fitting's lemma (TauCeti/RingTheory/KrullSchmidt/Uniqueness.lean:28) and GL2 Hecke rings; Mathlib 082e2d3 has no Ribet/Fitting-ideal file and only HeckeRing/Defs.lean. Confirmed the previous verdict. B = (B_0, A_p/C_p : p in Sigma - S_inf) is the paper's instance of DKSW's module N generated by the cocycle image plus coboundary vectors y_v on the Sigma subgroups, which IHG.6 names explicitly; the instantiation for the Hilbert/Eisenstein representation is delegated by IHG.6 to I.7. The only other atlas stage naming Ribet/Brumer-Stark, IntegralIwasawaTheory:KU-brumerstark, is by its own text a readiness checkpoint aggregating I.6/I.7, not an owner. Nothing in either pinned tree builds Hecke-algebra-valued cocycle modules.

items.name: The submodule B' = B(I_p) generated by inertia at primes above p not in Σ
items.statement: B' is the 𝕋_𝔐-submodule of B generated by the elements b(σ) for σ ∈ I_𝔭 (an inertia subgroup of the decomposition group G_𝔭 ⊂ G_F), as 𝔭 ranges over the primes dividing 𝔓', i.e. the primes above p that do not ramify in H/F (equivalently 𝔭 | p with 𝔭 ∉ Σ). (This is the module written B(I_p) in the introduction.)
items.locator: §9.4, sentence 'Let B' be the 𝕋_𝔐-submodule of B generated by b(σ) for σ ∈ I_𝔭…', the source line 2832
items.note: Killing B' makes κ unramified at the primes above p outside Σ; Theorem 9.10 relates this quotient to the operators U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭) and so to the extra congruences of Theorem 8.23. Evidence: the layer extract:110-158 (IHG.6, verified): "a partition Sigma disjoint-union P. On Sigma impose xi_v congruent to psi modulo Itilde; on the specified inertia subgroups for P impose xi_v congruent to chi ... Construct N and the cocycle, zero on a chosen subgroup in nonempty Sigma and on the specified inertia groups". the layer extract:46-52 (I.7): "Here prove every hypothesis for the actual Hilbert/Eisenstein Galois representation". Library search (rg Ribet|EisensteinIdeal|HeckeAlgebra|Fitting, inertia-generated submodules) finds nothing in Tau Ceti f790474 or Mathlib 082e2d3. Confirmed. B' = B(I_p), the submodule generated by cocycle values on the inertia groups of the primes above p outside Sigma, is what makes the cocycle "zero ... on the specified inertia groups" for the P-primes in IHG.6's local-condition theorem; the concrete B' for the Hilbert/Eisenstein representation is I.7's. No library declaration: neither tree has the Galois representation, the Hecke algebra T_M, or the cocycle b.

items.name: The quotient \overline{B}_p = B/(IB, B', p^mB) and its submodule \overline{B}_0
items.statement: \overline{B}_p = B/(IB, B', p^mB), the quotient of B by the 𝕋_𝔐-submodule generated by IB, B' = B(I_p) and p^mB, where m is the integer with Θ^# | p^m fixed in §8 (Lemma 8.1) and N > m, k ≡ 1 mod (p−1)p^N. \overline{B}_0 ⊂ \overline{B}_p is the image of B_0 in \overline{B}_p. This is the instance B' := (IB, B(I_p), p^mB) ⊇ IB_0 of the general setting with p^mB ⊂ B', so by (125) κ ∈ H^1(G_F, \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1})). \overline{B}_p is a finite p-group (a finitely generated 𝒪-module killed by p^m), and since it is killed by I it is an R-module through R → 𝕋_𝔐 (with 𝕋_𝔐 = R + I).
items.locator: §9.4, display defining \overline{B}_p and the following sentence, the source lines 2833–2836
items.note: The module whose Fitting ideal over R is computed in Theorem 9.10 and which receives the surjection β from ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#} in Theorem 9.8. Audit note the layer extract:42: "neither library has Fitting ideals" (confirmed: rg FittingIdeal in Mathlib 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti f790474 returns nothing). Confirmed. B-bar_p = B/(IB, B', p^m B), a finite p-group killed by the Eisenstein ideal and hence an R-module, is the paper's instance of the finite T-module N (killed by I, finite over T) of DKSW's local-condition theorem planned in IHG.6; the p^m truncation and the concrete inertia submodule are I.7's instantiation. No library counterpart: no Hecke algebra T_M, no Eisenstein ideal, no cocycle module in either pinned tree.

items.name: Proposition 9.5: κ ∈ H^1(G_F, \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1})) is unramified away from Σ', tamely ramified at Σ', locally trivial at Σ
items.statement: The class κ ∈ H^1(G_F, \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1})) of (125) (for B, B' = (IB, B(I_p), p^mB) as in §9.4) is unramified away from Σ' (its restriction to H^1(I_v, \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1})) vanishes for every place v ∉ Σ'), tamely ramified at Σ' (its restriction to the wild inertia I_{v,1} vanishes for v ∈ Σ'), and locally trivial at Σ (its restriction to H^1(G_{F,v}, \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1})) vanishes for every v ∈ Σ, archimedean places included). (Proof: Proposition 9.4 gives unramifiedness away from Σ ∪ Σ' ∪ {𝔭 | p} and tameness at Σ'; at 𝔭 | p, 𝔭 ∉ Σ, κ is unramified because \overline{B}_p is a quotient by the image b(I_𝔭) = B'; at infinite places local triviality is automatic since p is odd and \overline{B}_p is a p-group; at finite 𝔭 ∈ Σ, (126) exhibits κ|_{G_𝔭} as the coboundary of A_𝔭/C_𝔭.)

items.name: R^#-module structure on \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1}), \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1}), \overline{B}_1(𝛙^{−1})
items.statement: Let R^# = R_{Ψ^#} with the involution # : R^# → R induced by g ↦ g^{−1} on 𝒪[G] (§6.1). \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1}) is the module \overline{B}_0 regarded as an R^#-module via (r, b) ↦ r^#·b, where r^#·b is the usual action of R (through R → 𝕋_𝔐) on \overline{B}_0; the same recipe makes \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1}) and \overline{B}_1(𝛙^{−1}) R^#-modules. With this structure the G-action on \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1}) through the character 𝛙^{−1} (g ↦ 𝛙(g)^{−1}) agrees with the R^#-module action via the projection 𝒪[G] → R^#, g ↦ [g].
items.locator: §9.4, paragraph 'It is natural to consider \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1}) as an R^#-module', the source lines 2861–2864
items.note: Makes α, γ, β R^#-linear so that ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#} can surject onto \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1}) and Fitting ideals over R and R^# can be compared (Corollary 9.11). Evidence: the layer extract:46-52 (I.7, verified): "Include the necessary Hilbert modular congruences, integral Galois representations, the generalised Ribet lemma for residually indistinguishable characters, the Fitting-ideal comparison, and the passage from modified to unmodified data" and "compare the resulting arithmetic class and Fitting ideal". Generic mechanism verified: Mathlib/Algebra/Module/RingHom.lean:57 `abbrev Module.compHom [Semiring S] (f : S →+* R) : Module S M`. Checked the layer extract:71 (I.8): "Construct the involution and cyclotomic twist τ on the coefficient ring" is the Iwasawa-algebra involution of the compactly supported complex C_{F_inf,S} for the all-prime main conjecture, not the R^# = R_{Psi^#} structure on the B-bar modules. Confirmed. The item is the R^#-module structure on the specific modules B-bar_0, B-bar_p, B-bar_1 via the involution # on R_Psi and the compatibility with the G-action through psi^{-1}; Module.compHom is only the generic restriction of scalars and R_Psi, T_M, # do not exist in either pinned tree, so not library. No atlas layer names the # twist of the Ribet modules; the I.8 involution is a different object on a different ring. I.7's "Fitting-ideal comparison" (Corollary 9.11 compares Fitt over R and R^#, which is the purpose of this structure) is the containing target; no more exact owner found in areas/*.json or roadmaps/*.json.

items.name: Corollary 9.6: canonical R^#-surjection α : Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#} ↠ \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1})
items.statement: There is a canonical R^#-module surjection α : Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#} = Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) ⊗_{ℤ[G]} R^# → \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1}), induced by α(𝔞) = \overline{b}(σ) for 𝔞 ∈ Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H), where σ ∈ G_H ⊂ G_F is any lift of rec_{L/H}(𝔞) ∈ Gal(L/H). (Proof: 𝛙 is trivial on G_H, so κ_H = res^{G_F}_{G_H} κ ∈ H^1(G_H, \overline{B}_p)^{G=𝛙^{−1}} = Hom_cont(G_H^{ab}, \overline{B}_p)^{G=𝛙^{−1}} is a G-equivariant homomorphism, G acting on G_H^{ab} by conjugation and on \overline{B}_p through 𝛙^{−1}; by Proposition 9.5 the fixed field L' of ker κ_H is unramified outside Σ'_H, tamely ramified at Σ'_H and split completely at Σ_H, so L' ⊂ L and one gets the G-equivariant composite (127) Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^− →(rec_{L/H}) Gal(L/H) ↠ Gal(L'/H) →(κ_H) \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1}), which is 𝔞 ↦ \overline{b}(σ) and has image in \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1}); extending scalars gives α. Surjectivity: let B_α = im α and \overline{B}^α = \overline{B}_0/B_α; the image of κ_H in H^1(G_H, \overline{B}^α) is trivial, so by Lemma 6.3 the image κ^α of κ in H^1(G_F, \overline{B}^α(𝛙^{−1})) is trivial; writing κ^α(σ) = (1 − 𝛙^{−1}(σ))t with t ∈ \overline{B}^α and evaluating at σ = τ (κ(τ) = 0 since b(τ) = 0, and 𝛙(τ) = −1) gives 2t = 0, so t = 0 and κ^α = 0 as a cocycle; since the values b(σ) generate B_0, \overline{B}^α = 0.)
items.locator: §9.4, Corollary 9.6 (label c:cb) and equation (127) (label e:clb), the source lines 2866–2895

Prove N is generated by the cocycle image together with those vectors." the layer extract:46-52 (I.7): "integral Galois representations ... the Fitting-ideal comparison". the layer extract:37 (I.6): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations" (source of the X_{H,Sigma} surjection gamma that this quotient receives, not the item itself). items.name: \overline{B}_1 is generated over R by the images of A_𝔭/C_𝔭, 𝔭 ∈ Σ finite
items.statement: \overline{B}_1 is generated as a 𝕋_𝔐-module by the images of the elements A_𝔭/C_𝔭 for finite 𝔭 ∈ Σ (since B is generated by B_0 and these elements). Moreover, since by the definition of φ (Theorem 8.23: φ|_{𝕋_𝔐} takes values in R/xΘ^#, the image of R) every element of 𝕋_𝔐 is congruent modulo I to an element of R, and I kills \overline{B}_1, \overline{B}_1 is generated over R by the images of the A_𝔭/C_𝔭, 𝔭 ∈ Σ − S_∞. Consequently there is a canonical R^#-module surjection ⊕_{𝔭∈Σ−S_∞} R^# → \overline{B}_1(𝛙^{−1}).

items.name: Proposition 9.7: canonical R^#-surjection γ : (X_{H,Σ})_{R^#} ↠ \overline{B}_1(𝛙^{−1})
items.statement: There is a canonical R^#-module surjection γ : (X_{H,Σ})_{R^#} = X_{H,Σ} ⊗_{ℤ[G]} R^# → \overline{B}_1(𝛙^{−1}). (Construction and proof: the R^#-surjection ⊕_{𝔭∈Σ} R^# → \overline{B}_1(𝛙^{−1}) sending the basis vector at a finite 𝔭 ∈ Σ to −A_𝔭/C_𝔭 (and the archimedean summands to 0, \overline{B}_1 being generated by the finite 𝔭) factors through (X_{H,Σ})_{R^#}: since R^# is a quotient of the component of 𝒪[G] of the odd, hence nontrivial, character χ^{−1}, one has (X_{H,Σ})_{R^#} ≅ (Y_{H,Σ})_{R^#} = ⊕_{𝔭∈Σ}(ℤ[G/G_𝔭] ⊗_{ℤ[G]} R^#) ≅ ⊕_{𝔭∈Σ} R^#/ΔG_𝔭, where Y_{H,Σ} is the free abelian group on the places of H above Σ, X_{H,Σ} ⊂ Y_{H,Σ} its degree-zero submodule, G_𝔭 ⊂ G the decomposition group at 𝔭 and ΔG_𝔭 ⊂ R^# the ideal generated by 𝛙(g) − 1, g ∈ G_𝔭; so it suffices that (𝛙(g) − 1)·A_𝔭/C_𝔭 ≡ 0 in \overline{B}_1(𝛙^{−1}) for g ∈ G_𝔭, which follows from (126) because its left-hand side b(σ)𝛙^{−1}(σ) ∈ \overline{B}_0 vanishes in the quotient \overline{B}_1 of \overline{B}_p.)

items.name: Ext^1 classification of extensions, pushout and pullback (as used)
items.statement: For a commutative ring A (here A = R^#) and A-modules X, C, Ext^1_A(X, C) classifies short exact sequences 0 → C → Z → X → 0 up to isomorphism of Z inducing the identity on C and on X. A homomorphism α : C → C' induces the pushout α_* : Ext^1_A(X, C) → Ext^1_A(X, C'), realised by an extension Z' with a map Z → Z' compatible with α and id_X (surjective when α is); a homomorphism γ : X' → X induces the pullback γ^* : Ext^1_A(X, C) → Ext^1_A(X', C), realised by the fibre product Z ×_X X' with a map Z ×_X X' → Z compatible with id_C and γ (surjective when γ is). If α_*η_1 = γ^*η_2 in Ext^1_A(X, C'), then the extensions Z_1 (representing α_*η_1) and Z_2 (representing γ^*η_2) are isomorphic compatibly with the identities on C' and X. As used: for the rows of (128), with α : \overline{Cl_Σ^{Σ'}}(H)_{R^#} ↠ \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1}) and γ : (X_{H,Σ})_{R^#} ↠ \overline{B}_1(𝛙^{−1}), this yields the four-row diagram (129) and the surjection β = (Z_2 ↠ \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1})) ∘ (Z_1 ≅ Z_2) ∘ (∇_{R^#} ↠ Z_1).
items.locator: §9.4, proof of Theorem 9.8, text around (129) (label e:commdiag2), the source lines 2943–2967

Reduces Theorem 9.8 to the equality of extension classes α_*η_1 = γ^*η_2. Tau Ceti: TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/Ext/Basic.lean is transport/vanishing/exactness API only (extAddEquivOfIso, exact_postcomp, exact_precomp₃). Atlas: rg over atlas/areas/*.json, roadmaps/*.json and packets for 'Yoneda Ext', 'Baer sum', 'classif.* extensions', 'Ext^1'/'Ext¹' finds only the group-extension H² bijection in algebra-1.json ("The Baer sum is not needed and is not a target"), Koszul Ext-algebras and Ext-Euler forms; no stage names the Ext¹/extension correspondence for modules. It gives neither that every class in Ext¹_A(X,C) is represented by an extension nor the fact actually used, that α_*η₁ = γ^*η₂ forces Z₁ ≅ Z₂ compatibly with the identities on C' and X. […]

items.name: Theorem 9.8: R^#-surjection β : ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#} ↠ \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1}) completing diagram (128)
items.statement: Let ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H) be the Ritter–Weiss module of §6/Appendix A for the sets Σ, Σ' of §9.4, with its exact sequence (79) 0 → Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → X_{H,Σ} → 0 (property (P1)); tensoring with R^# over ℤ[G] gives the exact top row 0 → \overline{Cl_Σ^{Σ'}}(H)_{R^#} → ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#} → (X_{H,Σ})_{R^#} → 0, where \overline{Cl_Σ^{Σ'}}(H)_{R^#} denotes the image of Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#} in ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#} (through which α of Corollary 9.6 factors). Diagram (128) has this top row, bottom row 0 → \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1}) → \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1}) → \overline{B}_1(𝛙^{−1}) → 0, and vertical surjections α (Corollary 9.6) on the left and γ (Proposition 9.7) on the right. Statement: there exists an R^#-module surjection β : ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#} ↠ \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1}) making (128) commute. (Proof: let η_1 ∈ Ext^1_{R^#}((X_{H,Σ})_{R^#}, \overline{Cl_Σ^{Σ'}}(H)_{R^#}) and η_2 ∈ Ext^1_{R^#}(\overline{B}_1(𝛙^{−1}), \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1})) be the classes of the two rows; it suffices to show α_*η_1 = γ^*η_2 in Ext^1_{R^#}((X_{H,Σ})_{R^#}, \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1})), for then the representing modules Z_1 ≅ Z_2 give the four-row diagram (129) and β is the composite of the middle vertical arrows ∇_{R^#} ↠ Z_1 ≅ Z_2 ↠ \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1}), surjective since α and γ are. To compare the classes use the isomorphism (130) Ext^1_{R^#}((X_{H,Σ})_{R^#}, \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1})) ≅ ⊕_{v∈Σ} H^1(G_v, \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1})) (the isomorphism (85) of §6.2 base-changed to R^#; G_v ⊂ G the decomposition group at v). For α_*η_1: by Lemma 6.4, α_*η_1 = (α_*λ_v)_{v∈Σ} where λ_v ∈ H^1(G_v, Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^−) is the canonical class of (84); by the explicit formula of Corollary 9.6 the composite G_H → Gal(L/H) →(rec^{−1}) Cl_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^− →(α) \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1}) is σ ↦ \overline{b}(σ), whose unique lift to H^1(G_F, \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1})) (Lemma 6.3) is κ; hence α_*λ_v is the unique class in H^1(G_v, \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1})) whose inflation to H^1(G_{F,v}, \overline{B}_0(𝛙^{−1})) is res^{G_F}_{G_{F,v}} κ. items.name: Lemma 9.9: B_0 is generated over R by finitely many non-zerodivisors of K
items.statement: The module B_0 can be generated over R by finitely many elements b_1, …, b_n that are non-zerodivisors (equivalently, invertible) in K = Frac(𝕋_𝔐) = ∏_{f∈\overline{M}} E, i.e. each b_i has nonzero projection to every factor E_j (E_j the factor of the eigenform f_j). (Proof: ρ is continuous, so B_0 is a compact 𝒪-submodule of the finite-dimensional E-vector space K, hence finitely generated over 𝒪 and a fortiori over R. Starting from any finite generating set, if b_i has zero projection to E_j, then since ρ_{f_j} is irreducible some b_k has nonzero projection to E_j; replacing b_i by b_i + t b_k with t ∈ 𝒪 ∖ {0} outside a finite set makes the projection to E_j nonzero without creating a zero projection elsewhere and without changing the R-span; induction on the number of zero projections.)

items.name: Theorem 9.10: Fitt_R(\overline{B}_p) ⊂ (Θ^#)
items.statement: With R the trivial-zero-free character group ring quotient of 𝒪[G_p]_χ, Θ = Θ_{Σ,Σ'} ∈ R (§8 convention, Θ^# its image under #), and \overline{B}_p = B/(IB, B(I_p), p^mB) as in §9.4 regarded as an R-module (no twist by 𝛙^{−1}), one has Fitt_R(\overline{B}_p) ⊂ (Θ^#). (Proof: let 𝔭_1, …, 𝔭_r be the primes of F above p not in Σ (those dividing 𝔓'); for each i choose σ_i ∈ G_{𝔭_i} ⊂ G_F lifting rec(ϖ_i) ∈ G_{𝔭_i}^{ab}, ϖ_i a uniformiser of F_{𝔭_i}, and set c_i = b(σ_i)𝛙(𝔭_i)ε_cyc^{1−k}(σ_i); by (119) and (123), with A_i/C_i := A_{𝔭_i}/C_{𝔭_i} and 'y + I' meaning y + z for some z ∈ I, c_i = (A_i/C_i)(U_{𝔭_i} − 𝛙(𝔭_i) + I) ∈ B. Let b_1, …, b_n be R-generators of B that are non-zerodivisors in K (the generators of B_0 from Lemma 9.9 together with A_𝔭/C_𝔭 for finite 𝔭 ∈ Σ). Compute Fitt_R(\overline{B}_p) with the redundant generating set c_1, …, c_r, b_1, …, b_n: it suffices to show det M ∈ (Θ^#) for every M = (W | Z) ∈ M_{(n+r)×(n+r)}(R), W = (w_{ij}) ∈ M_{(n+r)×r}(R), Z = (z_{ij}) ∈ M_{(n+r)×n}(R), whose rows are relations Σ_j w_{ij}c_j + Σ_j z_{ij}b_j ≡ 0 in \overline{B}_p. By (119), since 𝛙 and η_{𝔭_i} are unramified at 𝔭_i and a(σ) ≡ ε_cyc^{k−1}(σ) mod I, b(I_{𝔭_i}) ⊂ (A_i/C_i)I, so B(I_p) ⊂ Σ_j (A_j/C_j)I; and IB = Σ_j I b_j. Hence each relation lifts to an equality in B (equation (131)): Σ_{j=1}^r (A_j/C_j)(w_{ij}(U_{𝔭_j} − 𝛙(𝔭_j)) + I) + Σ_{j=1}^n (z_{ij} + I + p^mR) b_j = 0. The matrix M' ∈ M_{n+r}(K) with these entries has each row summing to zero, so det M' = 0; cancelling the non-zerodivisor column factors A_j/C_j and b_j gives det M'' = 0 for M'' = ((w_{ij}(U_{𝔭_j} − 𝛙(𝔭_j)) + I) | (z_{ij} + I + p^mR)) ∈ M_{n+r}(\tilde{𝕋}_𝔐). With U = ∏_{j=1}^r (U_{𝔭_j} − 𝛙(𝔭_j)) ∈ \tilde{𝕋}_𝔐 as in Theorem 8.23, applying φ gives 0 = φ(det M'') = φ(U)(det M + p^mR) in W; by the last statement of Theorem 8.23, det M + p^mR ∈ (Θ^#) (equation (132)), and since Θ^# | p^m in R, det M ∈ (Θ^#).)

items.name: Corollary 9.11: Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R) ⊂ (Θ^#)
items.statement: Let p be odd, R the trivial-zero-free character group ring quotient R_Ψ of 𝒪[G_p]_χ (§7.1), Σ = {v ∈ S_ram : v | p} ∪ S_∞ and Σ' = {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p} ∪ T with T containing no primes above p, Θ = Θ_{Σ,Σ'} and Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R = Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) ⊗_{ℤ[G]} R. Then Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R) ⊂ (Θ^#). (Proof: Theorem 9.10 gives Fitt_R(\overline{B}_p) ⊂ (Θ^#), hence Fitt_{R^#}(\overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1})) ⊂ (Θ); the surjection β : ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#} ↠ \overline{B}_p(𝛙^{−1}) of Theorem 9.8 gives Fitt_{R^#}(∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#}) ⊂ (Θ); and Corollary 6.2, Fitt_R(Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_R) = Fitt_{R^#}(∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_{R^#})^#, gives the result.)

items.name: Lemma B.1, first assertion: Γ-invariants of V^θ(H) are NΓ·V^θ(H)
items.statement: Assume condition (A2) of App. A (every v ∈ Σ' has inertia group of order prime to the residue characteristic; automatic for Σ' = T, which contains no ramified primes), so that V^θ = V^θ(H) is a projective Z[G]-module of constant rank #S' − 1 (Lemma A.4). items.name: Invariants of a projective module are Z[G]^Γ ⊗ M (Bourbaki, Comm. Alg. Ch. I, Prop. 10)
items.statement: If M is a projective Z[G]-module and Γ ⊂ G a subgroup, then M^Γ = Z[G]^Γ ⊗_{Z[G]} M (flatness of M: the functor − ⊗_{Z[G]} M commutes with the kernel defining invariants); since Z[G]^Γ = (NΓ)Z[G], this gives M^Γ = (NΓ)·M.

items.name: Lemma B.1, second assertion: V^θ(H)^Γ ≅ V^θ(H^Γ)
items.statement: Assume (A2). For any subgroup Γ ⊂ G there is a canonical isomorphism of Z[G/Γ]-modules V^θ(H)^Γ = NΓ·V^θ(H) ≅ V^θ(H^Γ), where V^θ(H^Γ) is the module of App. A formed for the extension H^Γ/F (same S', Σ, Σ'); it sends NΓ·x to the restriction x̄ of x. Proof: (i) V(H)^Γ ≅ V(H^Γ) componentwise: each component of V(H) is Ind_{G_w}^G N_w(H_w), and with Γ_w = Γ ∩ G_w one has (166) (Ind_{G_w}^G N_w(H_w))^Γ ≅ Ind_{G_w/Γ_w}^{G/Γ} N_w(H_w)^{Γ_w} as G/Γ-modules (induced = coinduced, then Hom-adjunction), so it suffices that N_w(H_w)^{Γ_w} ≅ N_w(H_w^{Γ_w}); for v ∉ S' (N_w = H_w^*, O_w^*, U_w^1) this is trivial, and for v ∈ S' the map NΓ_w : V_w(H_w^{Γ_w}) → V_w(H_w)^{Γ_w}, (σ−1) ↦ NΓ_w(σ̃−1) (well defined since W(H_w^ab/(H_w^{Γ_w})^ab) ≅ ker(NΓ_w : H_w^* → (H_w^{Γ_w})^*)) is an isomorphism by the diagram (167) of exact rows 1 → (H_w^{Γ_w})^* → V_w(H_w^{Γ_w}) → Δ(G_w/Γ_w) → 1 and 1 → (H_w^*)^{Γ_w} → V_w(H_w)^{Γ_w} → (ΔG_w)^{Γ_w} → 1 (bottom row exact by Hilbert 90, flanking maps isomorphisms, right square cartesian). (ii) 𝔒(H)^Γ ≅ 𝔒(H^Γ): Γ-invariants of (139) 0 → C_H → 𝔒(H) → ΔG → 0 give (169) 1 → C_H^Γ → 𝔒(H)^Γ → Δ(G)^Γ → 1 (H^1(Γ, C_H) = 1), rewritten via NΓ : Δ(G/Γ) ≅ Δ(G)^Γ and C_H^Γ ≅ C_{H^Γ} as (170) 1 → C_{H^Γ} → 𝔒(H)^Γ → Δ(G/Γ) → 1; its class α ∈ H^2(G/Γ, C_{H^Γ}) satisfies infl(α) = u_G^{#Γ} = infl(u_{G/Γ}) (NΓ acts as #Γ on Γ-invariants; Neukirch I.1.6), and infl is injective, so α = u_{G/Γ} and (171) gives 𝔒(H^Γ) ≅ 𝔒(H)^Γ with right square cartesian. (iii) The square (168) V(H^Γ) ≅ V(H)^Γ, 𝔒(H^Γ) ≅ 𝔒(H)^Γ with vertical maps θ commutes because the right squares of (167) and (171) are cartesian and the diagram Ind_{G_w}^G(ΔG_w/Γ_w) → Δ(G/Γ), Ind_{G_w}^G(ΔG_w)^{Γ_w} → Δ(G)^Γ (vertical NΓ_w, NΓ; horizontal N(Γ/Γ_w)) commutes; taking kernels of θ gives the claim.

items.name: Induced modules equal coinduced modules (Weibel, Lemma 6.3.4)
items.statement: For a subgroup G_w of finite index in G and a G_w-module N, the induced module Ind_{G_w}^G N = Z[G] ⊗_{Z[G_w]} N is naturally isomorphic to the coinduced module Hom_{G_w}(Z[G], N). items.name: Hilbert's Theorem 90 (as used in Lemma B.1)
items.statement: For the finite Galois extension H_w/H_w^{Γ_w} of local fields with group Γ_w, H^1(Γ_w, H_w^*) = 0; hence taking Γ_w-invariants of the exact sequence (133) 0 → H_w^* → V_w(H_w) → ΔG_w → 0 yields the exact bottom row of (167): 1 → (H_w^*)^{Γ_w} → V_w(H_w)^{Γ_w} → (ΔG_w)^{Γ_w} → 1.
items.locator: App. B.1, proof of Lemma B.1, line 3637
items.note: External input (standard (no cite key given)). Exactness of the bottom row of diagram (167). Evidence: Verified at Mathlib 082e2d3. items.name: H^1(Γ, C_H) = 1 for the idele class group (Neukirch, Class Field Theory, Thm. III.4.7)
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension H/H^Γ of number fields with group Γ, the idele class group C_H = A_H^*/H^* satisfies H^1(Γ, C_H) = 1. Hence Γ-invariants of the Ritter–Weiss extension (139) 0 → C_H → 𝔒(H) → ΔG → 0 give the short exact sequence (169).

items.name: Inflation of the fundamental class (Neukirch, Class Field Theory, Prop. I.1.6)
items.statement: Let Γ ⊂ G = Gal(H/F), and let u_G ∈ H^2(G, C_H), u_{G/Γ} ∈ H^2(G/Γ, C_{H^Γ}) be the global fundamental classes of H/F and H^Γ/F. The inflation map infl : H^2(G/Γ, C_{H^Γ}) → H^2(G, C_H) is injective and infl(u_{G/Γ}) = u_G^{#Γ} (i.e. #Γ · u_G). As used: the class α of (170) satisfies infl(α) = u_G^{#Γ} (obtained by pulling (169) back along NΓ : ΔG → (ΔG)^Γ and pushing forward along C_{H^Γ} → C_H, NΓ acting as #Γ on Γ-invariants), hence α = u_{G/Γ}.

items.name: Global component W_v(H) = Ind_{G_w}^G W_w(H_w)
items.statement: For a finite place v of F in S' with chosen w | v, W_v(H) := Ind_{G_w}^G W_w(H_w), the v-component of the Ritter–Weiss module W = W(H) of App. A (W_w(H_w) = ΔW/(ΔW)Δ(W,Z) built from the Weil group of H_w^nr/F_v). items.name: Lemma B.2, first item: α_v commutes with reduction modulo Γ, equation (173)

items.name: Higher Fitting ideals Fitt^i_R(M)
items.statement: For i ≥ 0 and a finitely presented R-module M with presentation R^a →(A) R^g → M → 0 (g generators, a relations; the paper's matrices have rows = relations and columns = generators), Fitt^i_R(M) is the ideal generated by the (g−i)×(g−i) minors of A (R if g − i ≤ 0), independent of the presentation; Fitt_R(M) := Fitt^0_R(M). As used in §B.2: for the presentation V^θ_p (free of rank t = #S' − 1) → B^θ_p (free of rank g = t + s − j) of ∇^T_J(H)_p with t×(t+s−j) matrix A_J, Fitt^{s−j}_R ∇^T_J(H)_p is generated by the determinants of the t×t submatrices obtained by choosing any t = g − (s−j) of the columns of A_J.

items.name: Lemma B.4: Fitt of Cl^T(H)^{∨,-} equals the #-image of Fitt^s of ∇^T_{S_∞}(H)^-
items.statement: Let s = #S_ram and let ∇^T_{S_∞}(H) be the Ritter–Weiss module of Definition A.2 with Σ = S_∞, Σ' = T (T disjoint from S_ram, satisfying (1)). items.name: Presentation matrix A of V^θ_p → B^θ_p and the column description of Fitt^s
items.statement: With R = ℤ_p[G], Σ = S_∞, Σ' = T, an R-basis v_1,…,v_t of V^θ_p (t = #S' − 1) and the basis {f_v}_{v∈S'∖S_ram, v≠∞} ∪ {f_{v,0}, f_{v,1}}_{v∈S_ram} of B^θ_p defined by f_v = e_v − θ_B(e_v)e_∞ (∞ a fixed infinite place of F, θ_B(e_∞) = 1), A ∈ M_{t×(t+s)}(R) is the matrix of V^θ_p → B^θ_p: its (i, f_v)-entry is the e_v-coordinate of the image of v_i, namely β_v(v_i) for finite v ∈ S' ∖ S_ram, the ΔG_w-component (inclusion into ℤ[G_w], induced to R) for infinite v ≠ ∞, and (α_v(v_i), β_v(v_i)) for the pair of columns f_{v,0}, f_{v,1} of v ∈ S_ram. By definition Fitt^s_{R^-} ∇^T_{S_∞}(H)^-_p is generated by the determinants of the t×t submatrices of A (projected to R^-) obtained by selecting any t of its columns.

By definition, Fitt^s_{R^-} ∇^T_{S_∞}(H)_p^- is the ideal generated by the determinants of the submatrices of A determined by selecting any t of its columns. These columns are indexed by the basis vectors of B^θ_p.' items.name: Lemma B.5: the 2×2 determinant of (α_v, β_v)-values vanishes
items.statement: Let v be a finite place of F in S' (in the application v ∈ S_ram) and x_1, x_2 ∈ W_v(H). Then det [[α_v(x_1), β_v(x_1)], [α_v(x_2), β_v(x_2)]] = 0 in Z[G]. Proof: it suffices to take x_1, x_2 ∈ W_w(H_w) and prove the vanishing in Z[G_w]; there det [[α_w(x_1), β_w(x_1)], [α_w(x_2), β_w(x_2)]] = N I_w · det [[\overline{α_w(x_1)}, β_w^0(x_1)], [\overline{α_w(x_2)}, β_w^0(x_2)]] (bar = reduction modulo I_w), and the right-hand determinant vanishes because \overline{α_w(x)} = (σ_w − 1)β_w^0(x) by (145).
items.locator: App. B.2, Lemma B.5 (label l:detz), lines 3770–3785
items.note: Any t × t minor of A_J using both columns f_{v,0}, f_{v,1} of some ramified v vanishes, so only one column per ramified place contributes in (177). Evidence: IntegralIwasawaTheory:I.6 (the layer extract line 37; atlas/areas/iwasawa-1.json): "Build the Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations, the comparison to class/ray-class groups, and their Fitting-ideal functoriality." Lemma B.5 (the source lines 3770–3785, verified) is a property of the columns (α_v(x), β_v(x)) of the Ritter–Weiss presentation matrix: det = N I_w · det of the reduced matrix, which vanishes because ᾱ_w(x) = (σ_w − 1)β_w^0(x) by (145). This lies inside the containing target 'Ritter–Weiss modules and their presentations'. Library re-search (Mathlib 082e2d37e8, TauCeti f79047482): rg -i 'fitting' hits only Mathlib/Algebra/Lie/{TraceForm,Weights/Killing,Weights/Basic}.lean, Mathlib/RingTheory/Artinian/Module.lean and TauCeti Krull–Schmidt/Fitting's-lemma files; rg -i 'stickelberger|ritter.weiss|sinnott|kurihara|brumer' hits only TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Discriminant/Stickelberger.lean (header line 13 '# Stickelberger's congruence', the discriminant ≡ 0,1 mod 4 theorem) and TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/LeibnizPart.lean (unrelated). No W_v(H), α_v, β_v, I_w or Z[G]-presentation data exist in either tree. I.6 audit target: 'Ritter–Weiss modules, their presentations ... | library: absent'. Confirmed the previous verdict (planned, I.6). The nearest library declaration is the generic Matrix.det_fin_two (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Determinant/Basic.lean line 806), which only expands a 2×2 determinant and is not the content of the lemma (proportionality of the Ritter–Weiss local maps). No other atlas stage names the Ritter–Weiss local data; ES.7/L6/IHG.6 only mention generic Fitting APIs.

items.name: Lemma B.6: descent formula for Fitt^{s−j} of ∇^T_J(H)_p
items.statement: Let S_∞ ⊂ J ⊂ S_∞ ∪ S_ram, j = #(J \ S_∞), J̄ = S_ram \ J, s = #S_ram, p any prime, R = Z_p[G] (the result also holds over Z[G]; p odd and minus parts are not needed). Then Fitt^{s−j}_R ∇^T_J(H)_p = (∏_{v∈\overline{J∪J'}} N I_v · Fitt_{Z_p[G/I_{\overline{J∪J'}}]} ∇^T_{J∪J'}(H^{\overline{J∪J'}})_p : J' ⊂ J̄), the right side being the ideal of R generated by the images under multiplication by ∏_{v∈\overline{J∪J'}} N I_v of the 0-th Fitting ideals of the modules ∇^T_{J∪J'}(H^{\overline{J∪J'}})_p (Definition A.2 for H^{\overline{J∪J'}}/F with Σ = J ∪ J', Σ' = T), as J' ranges over all subsets of J̄. Proof: the matrix A_J of the presentation V^θ_p → B^θ_p of ∇^T_J(H)_p is A with the columns f_{v,1} removed for v ∈ J \ S_∞ (size t × (t+s−j); columns partitioned into t − (s−j) columns for v ∈ S' \ J̄, v ≠ ∞, and s − j pairs for v ∈ J̄). By the minor description and Lemma B.5, (177) Fitt^{s−j}_R ∇^T_J(H)_p = (det A_{J,J'} : J' ⊂ J̄), where A_{J,J'} is the t × t matrix of the columns for v ∈ S' \ J̄, the first (α_v) column for v ∈ J', and the second (β_v) column for v ∈ \overline{J∪J'}. Since β_v(x) = N I_v·β_v^0(x), (178) det A_{J,J'} = (∏_{v∈\overline{J∪J'}} N I_v) det A^0_{J,J'}, with A^0_{J,J'} (β_v replaced by β_v^0 for v ∈ \overline{J∪J'}) a well-defined matrix over Z_p[G/I_{\overline{J∪J'}}]. By Lemma B.1, V^θ(H^{\overline{J∪J'}})_p has basis v̄_i = N I_{\overline{J∪J'}}·v_i, and by Lemma B.3 (Γ = I_{\overline{J∪J'}}) A^0_{J,J'} is exactly the square matrix of the presentation V^θ_p → B^θ_p of ∇^T_{J∪J'}(H^{\overline{J∪J'}})_p (H^{\overline{J∪J'}} is unramified at v ∈ \overline{J∪J'}, so that column is (β_v(v̄_i))_i, the others (α_v(v̄_i))_i), whence (179) (det A^0_{J,J'}) = Fitt ∇^T_{J∪J'}(H^{\overline{J∪J'}})_p. Combining (177)–(179) gives the lemma.

items.name: Lemma B.7: Fitt^{s−s_0} of ∇^T_{Σ_0}(H^{Σ\Σ_0})^-_p via Theorem 3.7
items.statement: Let p be an odd prime, Σ = S_∞ ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v | p} as in §3.2 (32), Σ̄ = S_ram \ Σ. Let S_∞ ⊂ Σ_0 ⊂ Σ, s_0 = #(Σ_0 \ S_∞), s = #S_ram, R_0 = Z_p[G/I_{Σ\Σ_0}] = Z_p[Gal(H^{Σ\Σ_0}/F)]. Then Fitt^{s−s_0}_{R_0^-} ∇^T_{Σ_0}(H^{Σ\Σ_0})^-_p = (Θ_{Σ_0∪J_0,T}(H^{\overline{Σ_0∪J_0}}/F) · ∏_{v∈\overline{Σ∪J_0}} N I_v : J_0 ⊂ Σ̄) ⊂ R_0^-, each generator viewed in R_0 via multiplication by ∏_{v∈\overline{Σ∪J_0}} N I_v (no # on Θ). Proof: by the argument of (175) applied to H^{Σ\Σ_0}, Fitt^{s−s_0}_{R_0^-} ∇^T_{Σ_0}(H^{Σ\Σ_0})^-_p = (Fitt_{R_0^-} Sel^T_{Σ_0}(H^{Σ\Σ_0})^-_p)^#, and Theorem 3.7 applied to the extension H^{Σ\Σ_0}/F (whose Σ-set is Σ_0 and whose ramified primes lie in Σ̄ ∪ Σ_0) gives Fitt_{R_0^-}(Sel^T_{Σ_0}(H^{Σ\Σ_0})^-_p) = KS_p^T(H^{Σ\Σ_0}/F)^-, whose #-image is the stated ideal.

items.name: Theorem B.8: Fitt^s of ∇^T_{S_∞}(H)^-_p equals the Sinnott–Kurihara generators, equation (180)
items.statement: For every odd prime p, with R = Z_p[G], s = #S_ram, T disjoint from S_ram satisfying (1): Fitt^s_{R^-} ∇^T_{S_∞}(H)^-_p = (∏_{v∈J̄} N I_v · Θ_{J,T}(H^{J̄}/F) : S_∞ ⊂ J ⊂ S_∞ ∪ S_ram) ⊂ R^- (generators viewed in R via multiplication by ∏_{v∈J̄} N I_v; no # on Θ). Proof: Lemma B.6 with J = S_∞ gives (181) Fitt^s_R ∇^T_{S_∞}(H)_p = (∏_{v∈J̄} N I_v · Fitt_R ∇^T_J(H^{J̄})_p : S_∞ ⊂ J ⊂ S_∞ ∪ S_ram); partitioning J = Σ_0 ∪ J_0 with Σ_0 = J ∩ Σ, J_0 = J \ Σ this is (182) (∏_{v∈\overline{Σ_0∪J_0}} N I_v · Fitt_R ∇^T_{Σ_0∪J_0}(H^{\overline{Σ_0∪J_0}})_p : S_∞ ⊂ Σ_0 ⊂ Σ, J_0 ⊂ Σ̄); applying Lemma B.6 with J = Σ_0 to H^{Σ\Σ_0} (S_ram(H^{Σ\Σ_0}/F) ⊂ Σ̄ ∪ Σ_0; s_0 = #(Σ_0\S_∞), R_0 = Z_p[G/I_{Σ\Σ_0}]) gives Fitt^{s−s_0}_{R_0} ∇^T_{Σ_0}(H^{Σ\Σ_0})_p = (∏_{v∈\overline{Σ∪J_0}} N I_v · Fitt_{R_0} ∇^T_{Σ_0∪J_0}(H^{\overline{Σ∪J_0}})_p : J_0 ⊂ Σ̄), and multiplying by ∏_{v∈Σ\Σ_0} N I_v recovers the terms of (182) for that Σ_0, so (183) Fitt^s_R ∇^T_{S_∞}(H)_p = (∏_{v∈Σ\Σ_0} N I_v · Fitt^{s−s_0}_{R_0} ∇^T_{Σ_0}(H^{Σ\Σ_0})_p : S_∞ ⊂ Σ_0 ⊂ Σ); projecting to the minus side and applying Lemma B.7 yields Fitt^s_{R^-} ∇^T_{S_∞}(H)^-_p = (∏_{v∈Σ\Σ_0} N I_v ∏_{v∈\overline{Σ∪J_0}} N I_v · Θ_{Σ_0∪J_0,T}(H^{\overline{Σ_0∪J_0}}/F) : S_∞ ⊂ Σ_0 ⊂ Σ, J_0 ⊂ Σ̄), which is (180) with J = Σ_0 ∪ J_0. Together with Lemma B.4 and (176) this proves Kurihara's conjecture (165).

items.name: X_{H,Σ}: the degree-zero submodule of the place module Y_{H,Σ}
items.statement: For a finite set Σ of places of F, X_{H,Σ} := ker(Y_{H,Σ} → ℤ), the kernel of the augmentation (degree) map sending every place of H above Σ to 1; it is a ℤ[G]-submodule of Y_{H,Σ} = ⊕_{v∈Σ} ℤ[G/G_v] with Y_{H,Σ}/X_{H,Σ} ≅ ℤ (trivial G-action). It is never defined explicitly in the paper: it first appears as the third term of (79) (property (P1)), and Appendix A identifies it as Z^θ = ker(θ_Z: Z = Y_{H,Σ} → ℤ) when S'_ram = ∅ (assumption (A1)). Over ℤ[1/2], X_{H,Σ}^- ≅ Y_{H,Σ}^- (item 129), and for R^# a component of an odd character (X_{H,Σ})_{R^#} ≅ (Y_{H,Σ})_{R^#} ≅ ⊕_{𝔭∈Σ} R^#/ΔG_𝔭 (Proposition 9.7).

items.name: 0th Fitting ideal Fitt_R(M) (standing convention of the paper)
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and a finitely presented (in the paper: finitely generated) R-module M with a presentation R^a →(A) R^t → M → 0, Fitt_R(M) = Fitt^0_R(M) is the ideal of R generated by the t×t minors of the t×a relation matrix A (equal to R when t = 0 and to 0 when a < t); it is independent of the presentation. Throughout the paper 'Fitt' denotes this 0th Fitting ideal (line 353), computed over ℤ[G]^-, ℤ_p[G]^-, O[G]^-, character group rings R_Ψ, R^# and 𝕋_𝔐-modules regarded over R; the higher Fitting ideals Fitt^i_R(M) of Appendix B (item 326) are the ideals of (t−i)×(t−i) minors and Fitt_R = Fitt^0_R.
items.locator: §1.1, sentence after Theorem 1.3 (line 353: 'Here Fitt denotes the 0th Fitting ideal'); §2.3 Fitting ideals, label s:fitting (lines 652–659); App. B.2, line 3727

items.name: Locally quadratic presentation
items.statement: A presentation P_1 → P_0 → M → 0 of an R-module M is called locally quadratic if P_1 and P_0 are finitely generated projective R-modules of the same constant rank; equivalently, after localisation at every prime (or on every local factor of a semi-local R) it becomes a quadratic presentation R_𝔭^m → R_𝔭^m → M_𝔭 → 0 in the sense of §2.3. Over a ring that is a finite product of local rings (every ℤ_p[G]-algebra of the paper), projective modules of constant rank are free, so a locally quadratic presentation is a quadratic presentation (Remark A.7). The paper uses the notion, without a formal definition, for (155) over ℤ[G] under (A1),(A2) and for (156) over R under (A1),(A2').

items.name: Dual ray class sequence (37): effect of enlarging the smoothing set on Cl^{∨,-}
items.statement: Let T ⊂ Σ' be finite sets of finite primes of F with T (hence Σ') satisfying condition (1), and let S' = Σ' ∖ T. Then there is a short exact sequence of ℤ[G]^-‑modules 0 → Cl^T(H)^{∨,-} → Cl^{Σ'}(H)^{∨,-} → ∏_{w ∈ S'_H} ((O_H/w)^*)^{∨,-} → 0, the Pontryagin dual (minus parts, 2 inverted) of the ray class group sequence ∏_{w∈S'_H}(O_H/w)^* → Cl^{Σ'}(H) → Cl^T(H) → 0, exact on the left on the minus side because (O^*_{H,T})^- = 0 under condition (1) on T. The residue-field terms are computed as follows: for v ∈ S' unramified in H, ∏_{w|v}(O_H/w)^* ≅ ℤ[G]/(σ_v − N v) and its R-dual is R/(σ_v^{-1} − N v) = R/(1 − σ_v N v), quadratically presented with Fitting ideal (1 − σ_v N v); for v ∈ S' ramified with v ∤ p, I_v = I_{v,p} × I_v', τ_v a generator of the cyclic group I_{v,p}, ℤ[G_v]/(τ_v − 1, σ_v − N v, τ − 1 : τ ∈ I_v') ≅ (O_H/w)^*, x ↦ u^x, and (38) ∏_{w|v}((O_H/w)^*)^∨_R ≅ R/(τ_v − 1, σ_v^{-1} − N v) if χ(I_v') = 1 and 0 otherwise. Used with S' = {v ∈ S_ram : v ∤ p} in Theorem 3.7 (giving, with Lemma 3.1 and the snake lemma, (39)–(40)); with S' = {v ∈ T : v | p} in Lemma 4.1 (where the residue groups have prime-to-p order, so the R-component vanishes); and with S' = Σ' − Σ'(χ) (unramified in H_χ) as (53) in Lemma 4.3.

items.name: Change of depletion set: 0 → Y_{H,Σ∖Σ_0} → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → Sel_{Σ_0}^{Σ'}(H) → 0
items.statement: Let S_∞ ⊂ Σ_0 ⊂ Σ be finite sets of places of F and Σ' a finite set of finite primes disjoint from Σ satisfying condition (1). The identity of Hom_ℤ(H^*_{Σ'}, ℤ) induces a surjection Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) = Hom_ℤ(H^*_{Σ'},ℤ)/∏_{w∉Σ_H∪Σ'_H}ℤ ↠ Sel_{Σ_0}^{Σ'}(H) = Hom_ℤ(H^*_{Σ'},ℤ)/∏_{w∉(Σ_0)_H∪Σ'_H}ℤ, and w ↦ ord_w identifies its kernel with the free abelian group Y_{H,Σ∖Σ_0} on the places of H above Σ ∖ Σ_0; i.e. there is a canonical short exact sequence of ℤ[G]-modules 0 → Y_{H,Σ∖Σ_0} → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → Sel_{Σ_0}^{Σ'}(H) → 0 (the paper states it as 'canonical'; injectivity of w ↦ ord_w uses that the ord_w, w ∉ Σ'_H, are ℤ-linearly independent on H^*_{Σ'} modulo the classes of the ord_{w'}, w' ∉ Σ_H ∪ Σ'_H, i.e. no nonzero finite combination of the ord_w for w above Σ ∖ Σ_0 is a combination of ord's at places outside Σ_H ∪ Σ'_H). Instances used: Σ_0 = S_∞, giving 0 → Y_{H,Σ∖S_∞} → Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H) → Sel_{S_∞}^{Σ'}(H) → 0 and, with Y^-_{H,S_∞} = 0, Lemma 3.1; Σ_0 = Σ_p for H_ψ, giving Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_R ≅ Sel_{Σ_p}^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_R since (Y_{H_ψ,Σ−Σ_p})_R = 0 (Lemma 5.5).

items.name: Action of e_p^ord and of ∏(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭)) on the Eisenstein families W_k(𝛙,1), W_1(𝛙,1), W_1(𝛙_𝔓,1)
items.statement: Let k ≡ 1 (mod (p−1)p^N) with N ≥ m, and view the group ring Eisenstein families (105) at level 𝔫𝔓' via level raising. (i) In case 1 put z := ∏_{𝔭|p} 𝛙(𝔭)/(𝛙(𝔭) − N𝔭^{k−1}) ∈ R^*; then z ≡ 1 (mod p^m) and e_p^ord W_k(𝛙,1) = z·W_k(𝛙,1_p), where W_k(𝛙,1_p) is (105) with the trivial character replaced by its p-depletion. (ii) In case 1, e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|p}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭))(W_k(𝛙,1)) = 0 and e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|p}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭))(W_1(𝛙,1)) = W_1(𝛙_p,1), with 𝛙_p the p-depletion of 𝛙. (iii) In case 2, e_p^ord ∏_{𝔭|p}(U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭))(W_1(𝛙_𝔓,1)) = W_1(𝛙_{𝔓𝔓''},1). These are asserted in the text from the U_𝔭-eigenvalues of the Eisenstein constituents (U_𝔭 acts on E_k(ψ,1)|_𝔪 through the eigenvalues ψ(𝔭) and N𝔭^{k−1}, the ordinary projector keeps the unit-root part ψ(𝔭) and U_𝔭 − 𝛙(𝔭) kills it).

items.name: Herbrand–Dirichlet Σ-unit theorem in equivariant form (as used in Lemma A.4)
items.statement: Let Σ ⊃ S_∞ and Σ' be disjoint finite sets of places of F and O^*_{H,Σ,Σ'} the group of Σ-units of H congruent to 1 modulo every prime of H above Σ'. Then O^*_{H,Σ,Σ'} ⊗_ℤ ℚ̄ ≅ X_{H,Σ} ⊗_ℤ ℚ̄ as ℚ̄[G]-modules (the logarithmic embedding identifies the Σ-units modulo torsion with a G-stable lattice in the degree-zero hyperplane of ⊕_{w|Σ} ℝ, and the Σ'-congruence subgroup has finite index); consequently dim_{ℚ̄}(O^*_{H,Σ,Σ'} ⊗_{ℤ[G]} ℚ̄(χ)) = dim_{ℚ̄}(X_{H,Σ} ⊗_{ℤ[G]} ℚ̄(χ)) for every character χ: G → ℚ̄^*.
items.locator: App. A.3, proof of Lemma A.4, sentence before equation (154) (lines 3392–3393: 'the Dirichlet unit theorem implies dim(O^*_{H,Σ,Σ'})_χ = dim(X_{H,Σ})_χ')

items.name: Integral duality Hom_ℤ(M, ℤ) ≅ Hom_{ℤ[G]}(M, ℤ[G])
items.statement: For a finite group G there is a natural isomorphism of functors from ℤ[G]-modules to ℤ[G]-modules, Hom_ℤ(−, ℤ) ≅ Hom_{ℤ[G]}(−, ℤ[G]), given by φ ↦ (m ↦ Σ_{g∈G} φ(gm)[g^{-1}]), compatible with the contragredient actions (82) on both sides. Consequently the transpose ∇_Σ^{Σ'}(H)^{tr} = coker((B^θ)^* → (V^θ)^*) of (157), formed with (·)^* = Hom_{ℤ[G]}(·, ℤ[G]), may be computed with 𝓕 = Hom_ℤ(·, ℤ), which is how it is compared with the presentation (31) of the Selmer module (itself a quotient of Hom_ℤ(O^*_{H,S',Σ'}, ℤ)).

items.name: Fitting ideal of a transpose with s excess generators: Fitt^0_{R^#}(M^{tr}) = (Fitt^s_R(M))^# (equation (175))
items.statement: Let R = ℤ[G] (or ℤ_p[G], or a character group ring with involution #) and let M be an R-module with a presentation P_1 →(A) P_0 → M → 0 by free R-modules (or projectives of constant rank, over a product of local rings) with rank P_0 = rank P_1 + s, t := rank P_1. Then the transpose M^{tr} = coker(P_0^* → P_1^*) (with (·)^* = Hom_R(·, R) carrying the contragredient action) satisfies Fitt^0_{R^#}(M^{tr}) = (Fitt^s_R(M))^#: both ideals are generated by the t×t minors of the t×(t+s) matrix A, resp. of its #-transpose (a_{ji}^#). As used: for Σ = S_∞, Σ' = T (so S'_ram = S_ram, s = #S_ram), the presentation (155) V^θ → B^θ → ∇^T_{S_∞}(H) → 0 has B^θ free of rank #S' + s − 1 and V^θ projective of rank #S' − 1 (Lemmas A.4, (149)), and ∇^{tr} ≅ Sel^T_{S_∞}(H) (Lemma A.8), whence Fitt_{ℤ[G]}(Sel^T_{S_∞}(H)) = (Fitt^s_{ℤ[G]} ∇^T_{S_∞}(H))^#; the same argument for H^{Σ∖Σ_0}, Σ_0 ⊂ Σ, gives Fitt^{s−s_0}_{R_0^-} ∇^T_{Σ_0}(H^{Σ∖Σ_0})^-_p = (Fitt_{R_0^-} Sel^T_{Σ_0}(H^{Σ∖Σ_0})^-_p)^# in Lemma B.7.
